changesets.headline: A mistyped `astryx component` name answers faster on repeat runs: the Core docs its suggestions read are kept between runs, so the answer no longer reads every Core doc again. (#12538)
`astryx add` refuses a named pipe or a device where it writes a file, never opening it.

The agent block that `astryx init` writes ends with one line on how to remove it: run `astryx init --remove-agents`, which removes it from the agent files at the project root and in the folder you run it in, and delete any other copy between its markers. Asked to take Astryx's text out of a project, agents deleted whole agent files or cut one copy by hand and left the others; with the line, they run the command and remove what it leaves.

The agent docs `astryx init` writes, and the computer-level skill, name the Astryx prop names that differ from other libraries in the workflow's third step: buttons, badges, tokens and tabs take their text in `label` (Text, Heading and Link take children), booleans start with `is` or `has`, and every input takes `value` and `onChange`. An agent that writes props before it reads a component now writes these right far more often. Run `astryx upgrade` or `astryx init` to refresh a project's agent docs.

The AI Chat Landing template's keywords name its greeting, its suggestion cards and its composer. `astryx search` now finds it for an idea about a greeting, and `astryx build` lists it as an alternative start for more ideas that name a greeting, suggestions or a composer.

The `ai-chat` page template now gives its dead buttons and menu items a behavior: the composer's send, mention and attach buttons, the document version menu, and the document's share action now show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"), and Copy copies the document to the clipboard (desktop and narrow screens). No layout or styling changes.

AlertDialog: under a finger the alert appears and leaves the way an iOS alert does. It scales down into place from 1.2 while it and the dimming fade in, on the theme's entrance timing. When it closes it fades out with the dimming, on the theme's exit timing, and a close or a reopen midway turns back from where it is. While it appears a touch does nothing, and keys and assistive technology still act. While it leaves nothing reaches it, but a toast its action raised stays live and its words are read. With reduced motion it only cross-fades. On a phone (a compact window under a coarse pointer) the width with no `width` prop goes from 400 px to 320 px in every theme; a `width` you pass still wins. With a mouse nothing changes.

`AppShell`: on a phone, when the theme keeps the standard width points, a server-rendered page no longer shows the inline side navigation for a moment while its script loads. The menu toggle still arrives with the script.

`astryx upgrade` keeps each theme's chat corners now that `--radius-chat` follows the container radius: it adds `--radius-chat` to the tokens of each `defineTheme()` theme (28px, or the page step of its radius scale) and the page step to each adaptation rule with a radius scale. A theme that extends an Astryx theme, or a theme this project defines (a relative or aliased import is trusted to be one), and has no radius scale of its own inherits its base's value; one that extends another theme, such as one from another package, gets a TODO that also covers that theme's adaptation rules. It leaves a TODO where it cannot read the theme, and reports a default-exported object shaped like a theme for manual migration. The token it writes is declared at the theme root, so a value a project sets on an ancestor such as `:root` no longer reaches the theme's chat surfaces: set the token in the theme instead.

`AvatarGroupOverflow` takes a caller's `aria-label` as its name. Before, the translated "{count} more" always replaced it, so a builder could not give the indicator a fuller name such as "Show 5 more teammates". A caller `aria-labelledby` still names it, and with neither the translated count does.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` offers a font asked for on a part as its preset's whole stack ("monospace numbers in tables" gives `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`), so systems without its first family show the next one of its kind. It no longer offers `ui-monospace` alone, which only Apple systems draw.

`astryx experimental theme` pictures (`--png`) say when this machine has no font of the kind a stack names, for example headings set to the serif preset on a system with no serif font, which the picture shows in a sans-serif font. The font dial's help no longer says system presets always show.

The note for an Apple interface face offers its generic once (`system-ui, sans-serif`), and a font name such as `constructor` is no Apple face. `astryx doctor` names the package that loads a family a theme's font stylesheet lacks when it is an open font it knows (`npm install @fontsource/inter`), then the command that writes the stylesheet again; for a self-hosted family (such as `Acme Sans`) it gives the step to add the font stylesheet export or a local `<slug>.fonts.css`.

`astryx theme build` warns, and `astryx experimental theme` refuses, a radius scale with no `base` or `multiplier`, or one Core cannot read as a number (a boolean is read as 1 or 0, so it builds). Core builds every scaled corner from it as NaNpx, which the browser drops. A radius of `0` or `''` is said too: Core skips it and builds no corner token, so the base theme's corners stay (`radius: {base: 0, multiplier: 1}` squares them).
changesets.body:
In the editor:

- A family typed alone that the base theme already uses keeps the base's own fallbacks (Fraunces keeps Georgia and serif).
- Any other family typed alone gets fallbacks of the kind its name says (a Serif name serif ones, a Mono or Code name monospace ones), as the open fonts do.
- A family the base's font stylesheet loads is no longer also named as a font no package loads.

changesets.headline: The `astryx experimental theme` font dial's help names `rounded` as Nunito, an open font that loads once its package is installed, no longer beside the system presets. It also says exactly when a picture names a missing font: a serif, monospace or cursive stack drawn in a font of another kind.
`astryx theme build` and `astryx experimental theme` judge the shape of a typography block by what Core reads:

`astryx theme build` warns, at its line, a typography value Core builds into something no browser uses, as `astryx experimental theme` refuses it: a font stack with a space in one `family` (Core quotes it whole), a quoted family name with a space, a role weight with no type scale, and a `weights` entry that is no heading level. Both judge a family by what Core writes, so a quoted name without a space (`'"Lato"'`) and a list without one (`'Lato,serif'`), which build as written, are taken. On the font dial, a weight number in any form CSS reads (`Inter +500`, `Inter 1e3`) after a known family, or a weight or style word before it (`700 Inter`, `bold Inter`), is that weight or style, never saved as a family of that name.

`astryx theme build` warns a typography value wherever the theme writes it (a const, a role const, a spread, an import, a value computed at run time), at the line that writes it when one does; a role weight that is no font weight (`'semi-bold'`, `'1200'`), which the browser drops; and a heading weight under a number key that is no level (`{7: '800'}`). Both the build and `astryx experimental theme` read a heading level as Core does, so `'01'` and `'1.0'` are level 1. On the font dial, a weight or style word after a name that starts with a family the editor knows (`Inter Tight Bold`) is read as a number there is: a weight where a family goes.

`astryx theme build` and `astryx experimental theme` name a typography weight given as a number (`weight: 600`) as a type mismatch: the field takes the text `'600'`. The message says Core still writes a weight from 1 to 1000, and offers the text form.

`Badge` is as wide as its label. A badge alone in a `Grid` cell or a `VStack` no longer stretches into a bar across the cell or the stack; in a crowded `HStack` it still shrinks and ends its label with an ellipsis.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a whole-theme token the base theme draws past on a part (neutral's neutral badge fills with its own gray, not `--color-neutral`) is no longer reported as reaching it. `set` says that part does not use the token and gives the command that does; `how <token>` lists those parts under `notIn`; and a value question about the part answers what it draws there, the theme's own setting on it first.

A run that loads no project, other than `hook`, and whose `--base` names no other package, such as `astryx --version`, `--help` or `manifest`, no longer loads the base resolver. Core's base declaration reads Core's package name from a small module of its own, so it loads no provider-identity code. Output is unchanged.

The Best Practices section of `astryx component <Name>`, `astryx hook <name>` and an integration component read through `astryx discover <package>/<Component>` puts a `Do:` or `Don't:` label line before each run of items with the same guidance, instead of repeating a bold badge on every item; a blank line separates runs, so each run stays its own Markdown list. Every item keeps its place and its guidance; `--json` is unchanged.

Two example blocks no longer cause a hydration mismatch: `TimestampAutoFormat` and `TimestampRelativeFormat` read the clock once per mount after hydration instead of during render; the server markup shows a fixed placeholder date until hydration. Six example blocks that show several breadcrumbs, outlines, paginations or side navigations side by side now give each one its own accessible name, so screen readers can tell the landmarks apart. No visual change after hydration.

Six chat example blocks (the full-featured composer, the composer drawer with progress, the message bubble with custom content and with metadata, and the message metadata footer and showcase): Copy now copies the message and says so; Retry, the thumbs, Mention, Attach and the report card show a short demo note instead of doing nothing. Other chat examples are unchanged.
Layout header and footer, card and empty state example blocks: their action buttons show a short demo note instead of doing nothing. The general Layout example blocks are not part of this change.

The CommandPaletteGroup basic block, both CommandPaletteList blocks and the DropdownMenuGroup showcase: picking an item shows a short demo note instead of doing nothing. Other command palette and dropdown menu examples are unchanged.

Five nav example blocks (TopNav showcase, centered navigation, enterprise dashboard and mega menu; SideNav with a header menu): Search, Notifications and Profile show a short demo note, and Sign in, Get started, Upgrade and the header-menu side nav's items are links. Other top and side nav examples are unchanged.

Nine example blocks (Toolbar card header, sizes and three slots; Selector and MultiSelector ghost toolbars; Selector option descriptions; Table bulk actions; TabList tabs with actions; Popover hook usage): their action buttons show a short demo note instead of doing nothing, and the three-slot toolbar's Back arrow mirrors in right-to-left. The three-slot toolbar's Back still does nothing on press; the bulk-actions Delete and Archive, and controls in other blocks (such as the toolbar-with-tabs New item), are unchanged.
`astryx build`'s block picker counts every block its doc-side word weights were fitted with as known, so those blocks no longer get the head start the picker gives blocks it has never seen.

The heading truncation, bottom sheet menu, step content, step indicator, step states and grid focus examples lay out with HStack and VStack instead of hand-written flex wrappers, so their gaps follow the theme's spacing steps. They look the same in the default theme; themes with roomier spacing show wider gaps.

BottomSheet's docs say that a modal sheet with no data-autofocus field opens with focus on its panel in Safari on iOS, as in Chromium, and that marking a field data-autofocus opens on it in every browser.
A Breadcrumbs menu crumb's menu keeps its gap below the crumb and slides in from it again in published builds, and keeps the viewport gutter on its far edge.

`astryx build` lists blocks as examples to read, not sections to insert. The kit starts from the template, builds its parts with components, and shows up to three BLOCK EXAMPLES for reference. The JSON `blocks` field keeps its shape and still holds the same blocks, now shown as examples.

`astryx build` ranks blocks also by single words a block's docs use that its fitted word weights do not know (such as a newer Core block's own terms), so a request that uses those words can tie to that block.

`astryx build` calls page or app shell with a refit word table and new blend numbers. The weights file stores that table once: the pick model reads the call model's tables when it carries none of its own.
The `build()` API description says a whole-page idea that would start on the app shell starts from the closest page template.

`astryx build` starts from a family's frame template when the frame holds the page the idea names. "Notification settings in a modal" now starts from the settings dialog template instead of the plain settings page; a modal that holds only a part ("a toggle in a modal on the settings page") keeps the settings page.

`astryx build` treats a frame as evidence for a page template only when the frame holds that template's kind of page. "Saved drafts in a modal with resume and delete row actions" asks for a list of drafts in a modal, not a settings page, so it no longer starts from the settings dialog; it starts from the app shell, with the parts listed in the kit.

`astryx build` no longer starts a part, a change to an existing page, or a page it would put on the app shell from a template kept off the template gallery. The theme showcase, a page of sample product screens, was taken as the app shell; those requests now start from a real shell template.

`astryx build` reads a request that opens with "add" and says where the piece goes ("add a filter row above the table") as a change to a page the builder already has, so it starts from the app shell. "Add a dashboard to the app" and "add a new dashboard" still start from a page template.

`astryx build` keeps "a side panel with an owner, a status, and a history" as one part that starts from the app shell, and reads "a list of planning jobs" as a page. Component categories now declare the page-template family whose records their components hold.

`astryx build` starts a part from a page family's base template only when that template leads the ranking and the family is where the part goes. A part request headed by a word that also names a component, such as "a table filter chip", asks for that piece and starts from the app shell.

`astryx build` picks which page template to start from with a second word model, once the existing model has called a page. The page-or-shell and page-or-block calls are unchanged; only the choice among page templates changes.

`astryx build` with no query now names the exact theme wiring `theme add` prints for your project: the imports and the value `<Theme>` takes (`themes[defaultThemeSlug]` from the generated `astryx-themes` module), the color mode for a theme with one, or the provider to pass it to when an installed package declares one. Before a theme is added, it reads the installed theme's built module the way `theme add` does, so the wiring it names is the one `theme add` then prints. When no theme is added yet, a last step gives the `theme add <slug>` command for your installed theme or the starter theme. The old rule left the value open (`theme={...}`), so pages often passed a theme name such as `"light"` and crashed once script ran.

The `build` API doc and the build kit's comments say that for a whole page the page-pick model chooses the start from the ranker's list and its own word tables, so the start can differ from the ranker's first template.

`astryx build` names a page template that is not ready only when the idea names it, as a reason ("`incident-console` isn't ready yet, so build started from `shell-top-nav`."); otherwise no not-ready template appears in its output, including `pages` and the "Keyword search matched" line.

`astryx build` chooses its start from ready page templates only: a template that is not ready yet, however well its words match, is no longer search's direct match for build and no longer keeps an idea on the app shell.

`astryx build` reads search as if every page template that is not ready yet were absent: search leaves such templates out of what it ranks for build, so the start, the page list, the block suggestions, the components and `matchCount` are exactly what they would be without them. A not-ready template's name typed as the idea no longer empties the kit. When the idea names a not-ready template that search matches directly, the reason still says it is not ready yet. `astryx search` still lists every template.

`astryx build` reports `start.fit` on a page-template start: the page-pick model's probability for that template among the ready page templates, from 0 to 1. At 0.4 or more the choice is clear; below it, several templates fit about as well. It is absent for a template the word tables do not list. `--verbose` text shows it too.

`astryx build` names where its start and each alternative go in the project it runs in, so the scaffold command runs as printed: the path `astryx template` names for that template from the project's layout and the template's own id (not the Core id an integration replacement stands in for): in a Next app, its App Router folder (`app/<name>` or `src/app/<name>`) or, with only the Pages Router, the page file `pages/<name>.tsx` or `src/pages/<name>.tsx`; else `src/pages/<name>`. The path is quoted when a shell would read it otherwise. In a folder with no package.json, the command keeps the `<path>` placeholder.

`astryx build` settles an exact ranker tie by whether a template is its family's base, instead of by how many hyphen-separated parts its id has: a family's base keeps its place ahead of a tied variant. Templates still tied, in the same family or not, are ordered by how strongly each one's own descriptor answers the idea, then by how typical of its family it is, then by name. A template the idea names by its whole name wins a tie. The page-pick model settles an exact tie of its final score the same way, and its rank features give equal values equal ranks, so the order of the weights file never decides.

When page templates of one family tie exactly and the ranker's pick is one the word tables do not list (such as the collapsible and comparison tables, or an integration's template), `astryx build` starts from the tied template whose own description, keywords and page components best match the idea, then the one most typical of its family, instead of the alphabetically first.

When `astryx build`'s ranker picks a template the word tables don't list, it now weighs that template against the pick model's best listed page, the same model that chooses the page everywhere else, instead of against the call model's.

A page template that is not ready yet no longer takes one of the places in the search results `astryx build` reads, so it no longer pushes a page, a block suggestion or a component out of build's kit; `matchCount` still counts it. When the idea names a not-ready template, the reason still says so even if another not-ready template ranks above it.

`astryx build`: a page template named the way code writes it (`CheckoutWizard`, `kanbanBoard`) starts that template, as its plain words do, and so does a name with two neighbouring letters swapped in a word of six or more letters (`dashbaord`). Shorter words are read as written.

Button's docs now list `ref` and say that in link mode (with `href` and not disabled) the ref receives the anchor (or the link component's element), although its type names `HTMLButtonElement`. No runtime or type change.

A Button whose label is cut short in a narrow row shows its full label in a tooltip when keyboard focus reaches it, and a ToggleButton's cut label now shows an ellipsis. Labels that fit look the same and show no tooltip, and screen readers hear the name once.

A long-running CLI process reads a family doc or a theme or icon descriptor again when npm replaces it with a file of the same size and modification time, and reads the theme part data cache again when it is rewritten in place with the same size and modification time.

Calendar's weekday names no longer run into each other when a theme sets a larger text size or smaller element sizes. Each weekday column is at least as wide as its name. In a Calendar wider than its natural width, each weekday name now sits at the centre of its day column; at its natural width the Calendar looks the same.

The `canvas-editor` template draws the corner radius field with the one-rounded-corner icon and the per-corner button with the four-corner icon, and declares each icon with the meaning its picture shows, so a project whose icon set reaches these Lucide icons through reviewed matches also gets the right picture on each control.

The canvas-editor page template fits a phone. When 40% is too wide for the canvas, the artboard opens at the largest zoom step that fits, the tab strip keeps the open tab's close reachable, and the save note leaves the screen when the header is too narrow for it (a screen reader still reads it).

The `canvas-editor` template's flip buttons draw the mirror axis of their action: Flip horizontally shows the vertical axis and Flip vertically the horizontal one. Before, each button showed the other's picture. Each button keeps its meaning, so icon sets that map the flip meanings draw the same icons as before. A main icon set that wraps `lucide-react` and names no variant keeps the template's Lucide imports, so it now shows the corrected pictures too.

A run that keeps many values trims the per-user catalogs folder once, when it ends (a command that fails trims it as it exits), instead of after each value. A first `theme build` on a fresh cache keeps about 270 values and is about 130 ms faster. Every answer is unchanged, and the folder keeps the same size limit.

ChatComposer keeps its send action inside the composer on a narrow screen. When the footer actions are wider than the footer, they wrap onto more lines inside the composer instead of pushing the send button past its edge; an action too wide for a line of its own is shortened with an ellipsis. Wide composers look the same as before.

In development, `ChatToolCalls`, `ChatDictationButton` throw an error that names a missing required prop and shows the fix, instead of a TypeError from inside the component. Production output is unchanged.

Chat surfaces now default to the container radius: `--radius-chat` defaults to `var(--radius-container)` instead of `28px`, a theme that sets `--radius-container` but not `--radius-chat` declares the alias at its root, and a radius scale no longer sets `--radius-chat` (it set the page step), so chat follows the theme's container, also where the theme sets its container over the scale. This changes the corners of ChatComposer, its drawer and status bar, and ChatMessageBubble, and the buttons inside the composer take their normal corners. The send button stays circular inside a composer, as it is outside one: a theme whose composer corner made the send button a rounded square (controls taller than 32px, or a chat corner under 28px) now draws a circle, unless it sets the `chat-send-button` radius. Butter, Chocolate, Gothic, Matcha, Neutral and Stone set `--radius-chat: 28px`, and Butter keeps its 16px send-button corner, so they look the same; Y2K sets `--radius-chat: 0px` and stays square. A theme that extends one of them keeps that chat radius. To keep the 28px chat corners in another theme, add `--radius-chat: 28px` to its tokens. Set the token in the theme rather than on an ancestor such as `:root`: a theme scope that declares it now replaces an inherited value.
`ChatToolCalls` inside a `ChatMessage` now truncates a long target with an ellipsis on a narrow screen, instead of running past the message column.

The chat composer's @-mention and slash-command menu resolves its default "No results" message through the locale catalog, so a translation supplied to `InternationalizationProvider` replaces it. Before, it was a fixed English string. A trigger's own `emptySearchText` still wins.

ChatComposerDrawer rounds its top corners and its tuck under the composer with the composer corner, so a theme that sets `chat-composer` borderRadius moves the drawer with the composer. Outside a ChatComposer the drawer still uses `--radius-chat`. Shipped themes look the same.

CheckboxInput runs its disabled-message tooltip only while that message can show (the checkbox is disabled and has a `disabledMessage`), so a page of many checkboxes renders faster. A disabled checkbox's reason now also describes it in the server-rendered HTML, before the page hydrates.
CheckboxListItem and ListItem docs say that a string `description` shows on one line with an ellipsis, and that a node such as `<Text type="supporting">` shows the full text on more lines.

A required `CheckboxInput` is no longer announced as invalid before anyone touches it. Chromium reported an unchecked required checkbox as invalid from its first render, so a screen reader said "invalid" on every required checkbox of a fresh form. The invalid state now follows `status`, as on `Switch`, and native validation still blocks a form submitted with the box unchecked.

A theme sets the room between a checkbox or a switch and its label with `gap` on the `checkbox-input` or `switch-field` target, for example `components: {'checkbox-input': {base: {gap: '3px'}}}`. Before, that gap sat on an inner row no target reaches, so the only way to change it was the `--spacing-2` token, which also changed the status message's padding. The default room stays 8px, and a hidden label still keeps no gap.

The checkout wizard template fits a 320 px phone again: the order summary, the step strip, the promo code row and the Continue buttons stay inside the page's side padding instead of running about 18 px into it, and the promo code's Apply button keeps its full label while the field gives up the room. Wider screens look the same.

Citation: a label citation with a source icon no longer rides above the line inside a sentence; it now sits centred on the line, as a label without an icon already did. A paragraph that contains an icon citation can be 2 px taller. A number citation stays a superscript.
In development, `Citation` throws an error that names the `source` prop and shows the fix, instead of a TypeError from inside the component. Production output is unchanged.
Internal: the technical documentation template's Copy prompt button uses Core's useClipboard instead of calling the clipboard API directly. Pages look and behave the same.
Internal: the editor template sizes its sidebar with LayoutPanel's width prop instead of an inline style. Pages look the same.
Internal: the shell-nav template registers its Cmd+K and Ctrl+K shortcuts with Core's useHotkeys instead of a hand-written key listener. Pages look and behave the same.

Bases, first step: a run resolves one base. The new global `--base <package>` picks it; otherwise, in an integration package, the base it is or builds on; else the project's Core; else its one installed base; else Core. A package becomes a base by declaring `base` in its integration manifest. Commands and options that need a platform step the base does not serve (theme build, add, use, remove, targets, and template; `template --skeleton` and `--cdn`; `integration add theme`; `experimental render`) are hidden from help and refused with `ERR_BASE_CAPABILITY`. Commands do not call base adapters yet, so a base other than Core serves no platform step. In a run on another base, component, hook, swizzle, template, docs, search, and codemod reads leave out Core's items and answer from the integrations that build on the base (an empty list or an unknown name). There, `build` names no Core frame or foundation components; the `hook --list` and `swizzle --list` envelopes name the active base as their package; `upgrade --from` targets the active base's installed version, runs only the codemods of integrations that build on that base (even when `astryx.config` does not list the base), checks no copied ShadCN composition (with `--registry` too), and keeps the agent-docs version `init` writes; and `doctor` checks that the active base is installed instead of reporting Core and Core's theme packages as missing. `component --list --detail compact|full` lists no integration's components, so on another base that view is empty (the base's own components appear in the default list). A project with no base-declaring integration gets the same command output as before, except that root help gains the `--base` option; the "Component style overrides" lines of theme help, and the `--json` unknown-subcommand suggestions of `theme` and `experimental`, start with an integration's `cliCommand` when one is declared, as every other printed command does; and `astryx manifest --json` gains `base`, `available` on each command and each command option, and `requires` where a command, option, or argument declares steps.
changesets.body: `--base` is a global option, so `experimental theme editor new <name> --base <theme>` reads it as the base library and refuses with `ERR_BASE_NOT_FOUND`; the refusal suggests the same run with `--like <theme>`, which stays the editor's base-theme option.

changesets.headline: The bundled chocolate theme's light category text reads at 4.5:1 on a card.
The bundled official themes export `colorModes`, the modes each draws: gothic `['dark']`, the others `['light', 'dark']`.
The bundled gothic theme template matches the gothic error-toast fix.
The bundled matcha theme's dark menus, popovers and muted fills take its near-black neutral like its cards.

The official themes that `astryx theme eject` scaffolds carry the theme packages' text contrast fixes: text, links, category and status text, and code text meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) on the surfaces the theme packages now check.
The neutral and y2k themes that `astryx theme eject` scaffolds show Skeleton placeholders on their light page: their `--color-skeleton` takes a darker neutral stop, as the theme packages do.
When Node already uses a compile cache (`NODE_COMPILE_CACHE`), the CLI leaves it as it is and no longer makes an empty `node-compile-cache-<uid>` folder in the temp folder.

The contact-form template no longer scrolls sideways on a phone. Its section takes the full width up to 800px instead of its content's width, so a long field placeholder no longer sets the page's minimum width. On its own, the page looks the same at 768px and wider. Inside a padded layout region narrower than 800px, the section now stays within the padding where it used to run into it.

`astryx docs --list` lists every docs topic: the same list that `astryx docs` prints with no topic, in text and as `docs.list` with `--json`. It used to fail with `unknown option '--list'`, while `component --list`, `template --list` and `hook --list` each list their catalog. Every other docs flag reads with `--list` as it reads with no topic; a topic or section beside `--list` is refused with `ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. `docs()` takes the same `list` option.

`astryx docs <name>` points to the right command when the name is a component, hook or template rather than a docs topic. The read still fails with `ERR_UNKNOWN_TOPIC`, and its first suggestion is now the command that reads that entry, such as `astryx component Button`, `astryx hook useHotkeys` or `astryx template ai-chat`. Only an exact name counts, in any case and with or without spaces and hyphens (`docs text-input` points to `astryx component TextInput`); a hook also answers to its name without `use`. The suggestion keeps the usual `{name, reason}` shape and takes the last suggestion's place, so the list does not grow. When no docs topic shares a word with the name, it is the only suggestion, instead of the whole topic list. The check reads file names first and loads no docs for other names, so a docs miss stays fast. Docs routes and docs typos get the same suggestions as before. `doctor`'s cache row names the docs not-found hint's name summaries.

The `theme` row of the bare `astryx docs` list says what the topic is in one sentence; the theme editor's how-to lines (make or change a theme, look after each change, a denser or roomier app, one kind of part, a starter app with no app yet) are now the first sections of the `theme` topic, each shown whole where `astryx docs theme` opens.

`astryx doctor` text used to print each check as a block of `id:`, `status:`, `label:`, `message:` and `fix:` lines, with the summary counts on four lines. It now prints each check as one record: its status (`[ok]`, `[warn]`, `[fail]`, `[info]`) in a column, then its id, label, message and `fix`. A legend under the heading names each field by its `--json` key, and the summary prints its counts on one line. Every field still prints, so the answer reads the same in less space: about 10% less on a small app checked with `--built`. The JSON output does not change.

CLI errors name a run to try. An option a command does not take now names the options the command takes, and the command as meant when the option points at one of them: `component Table --format json` names `component Table --json`, `--full` names `--detail full`, `--props-only` names `--props`, and `theme --list` names `theme list`. A word the CLI has no command for names the command the words point at: a whole command passed as one word, a command's plural, an option some commands take (`list` names `component --list`), a command deeper in the tree (`verify` names `integration verify`; `eject` names `theme eject --help`, since it needs a theme), or a name another command reads (`info Text` names `component Text`); with no such command, it names near command names by Commander's own rule (at most three edits, and more than 40% of the name the same), so `info Text` names `component Text` where it used to name `init`. `doctor` given a path names `doctor --built <path>`, and several paths in the project name the folder that holds them. `upgrade --from <version> --list` names `upgrade --list` and the migration from that version, `template` with `--skeleton` or `--list` and other words names each run alone, and an option given without its value prints the command's usage with that option in it. Every named run parses, and a call that does not itself name the `experimental` group gets no experimental command in its answer. A word that names no command followed by an unknown option (`astryx describe Table --format json`) now reports `ERR_UNKNOWN_COMMAND`, as the same call without the option does, instead of `ERR_INVALID_OPTION`; every other error code, and every exit code, is unchanged.

`astryx doctor integration validate` (and so `integration check`) lists each component example that is not `kind: 'setup'` but cannot run on its own, the way a docs page or catalog card runs it as a live preview: code that does not compile, such as a top-level `return` or code that stops partway (`example_does_not_compile`); code that renders nothing (`example_renders_nothing`); a name the example never defines or imports (`example_undefined_name`); an import of code that runs only on a server, an async server component it renders, or a read of `process.env` (`example_server_only`); and an import of a relative path or of a package the package does not declare (`example_import_unresolvable`). Each is a note with its fix that fails `integration check --strict --next` now and `--strict` from the next minor release, so no build that passed before fails. An example may use without importing the components its package documents, the components and hooks Core documents, React's exports, and browser globals. `previewableExample(example, scope)` from `@astryxdesign/cli/authoring` is the same rule for a tool that shows examples as live previews: it returns the module to bundle, or why the example cannot run. `integrationExampleScope(pkg)` from `@astryxdesign/cli/api` returns the scope Doctor reads a package's examples with, as JSON, so a catalog can store it and a preview tool read each example exactly as Doctor does. `showcase_not_standalone` now reads the same packages: a Node built-in name such as `events` that only `devDependencies` installs counts as server-only, because an app that installs the package does not get it.

`astryx component`, `astryx hook` and `astryx template` now point to the right command when a name they do not find is an entry another lookup command reads, as `astryx docs` already did. One rule serves all four commands. An entry's name is its full id: a component, hook or template id, or a docs route. A name matches the typed name at one of four tiers, best first: exact (the whole name, in any case); folded (the whole name without spaces and hyphens, and a hook with or without `use`); last segment (only the last segment of a path id or docs route, exact or folded); words (the name carries every typed word). When the typed name matches another command's entry at one of the first three tiers, that command joins the suggestions by the entry's full id, such as `astryx hook useHotkeys` for `component use-hotkeys`, `astryx component Button` for `template Button`, or `astryx docs typography/font-setup` for `hook font-setup`. A better tier wins; inside a tier, a component comes before a hook, a hook before a template, and a template before a docs route; among docs routes, the route with the fewest segments comes first, then the first in tree order. The hint goes right after the command's own suggestions that match at its tier or a better one, so it is first only when none does. The list never grows: the last suggestion drops, and a hint that would come last is left out; when a command had no suggestion, the hint is the only one. Every hint names an entry the hinted command reads: a template only when `astryx template` lists it, and any route of the docs tree, namespaces included. The error code and the `{name, reason}` shape stay. Docs keeps its rule that the hint stands alone when no topic shares a word with the name, and `component` keeps its example-block message, which already names `astryx template`. Names that resolve still resolve as before, and a miss stays fast: file names and doc text say first which components, hooks, templates and docs routes can match, so only those are read.

For AI tools that cannot run commands, `astryx mcp` serves every astryx command as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool, over standard input and output; agents that can run commands keep using the CLI. Each command that answers with `--json` is one tool, named by its words (`theme build` is `theme_build`), with the command's arguments and options as its inputs under their CLI names, and every root option except `--json` and `--version`; an input a tool does not list is refused. A tool call runs that command with `--json` in the project folder, or in a folder inside it that the call names, and answers with the command's output unchanged; a command that exits non-zero answers as an error. The tools come from the same command definitions as `--help` and the manifest, so a new command or option is a tool input at once. When the project has no agent docs yet, the server gives the agent the text `astryx init` writes. `astryx mcp --docs-only` serves only the commands that read the docs (`search`, `build`, `component`, `hook`, `docs`, `template`, `discover`, `theme list` and `theme targets`), one message at a time, without the inputs that name a folder, a file to write or a package to read (`cwd`, `path`, `cdn`, `overwrite`, `package` and `base`); the docs site's MCP server is this command. `astryx mcp --json` exits 1 with `ERR_INVALID_OPTION`, because standard output carries the protocol. `astryx docs working-with-ai` shows the client entries.

A theme module that throws from a microtask while it loads is a refused theme load (`ERR_THEME_LOAD`, naming the error) on every supported Node. Before, Node before 24 answered `ERR_UNKNOWN`, and a theme loaded through the CLI's own Core (no Core in its folder, and each member of a `--family` build) could build with the exception dropped. `astryx theme build` and the theme editor still need Node 22.15 or later, or 23.5 or later, to load a theme that imports a stylesheet or an asset, and so does a recorded theme that imports an asset, or a stylesheet that a module in another folder imports by a relative path. On an older Node those loads are now refused with a message that names the file and the Node versions that load it, and says that nothing was written, in place of Node's "Unknown file extension" or "Unexpected token" error. A recorded theme's other stylesheets still load there.

`astryx theme palette generate` refuses a palette config made with a newer Astryx CLI, whose recipe this CLI does not know yet, with the recipe it uses, the recipes this CLI knows, and the update step that fits where the CLI runs. The refusal keeps its error code.
The Order Detail template writes the discount with a true minus sign held to its amount (`− $15.00`), not an en dash and a space that a narrow row could break between.

A long answer piped to a slow reader arrives whole. When a command ended in an error with an answer longer than 64 KiB, such as `astryx template <name> --json` with many suggestions, a reader like `$(…)` or `| (sleep 1; wc -c)` got only the first 64 KiB, so `--json` callers got invalid JSON. Every command now writes piped output in full before it exits; short answers are as fast as before.

The theme authoring doc shows `defineTheme({palette})` with `themePalette()` from `@astryxdesign/core/palette`. `astryx theme palette generate` and the theme editor's colors give the same output as before: the CLI now runs a copy of the palette engine and its token mapping generated from Core's source.

On a phone, the payment-form template's order summary keeps each price inside its card. An item's name and badge wrap onto two lines, and when even that does not fit beside the price, the price moves under them at the end of the line. Desktop is unchanged.

Component docs: `playground.mobile` holds the props of a second render at a phone viewport, merged over `defaults`, for a component whose layout changes at phone width; the theme editor's part census renders it too. AppShell declares its mobile layout there (the menu button in the top bar, the open drawer); its playground defaults are unchanged.

A command doc's option can declare `pointers`: parts of its description that help leaves out when the run's base does not serve what they name. On a base other than Core, `astryx template --help` no longer names `--skeleton` in the `--list` text or suggests `--package @astryxdesign/core`, and `astryx mcp --help` no longer names `theme targets` in the `--docs-only` text.
`CodeBlock`'s and `Timestamp`'s copy buttons no longer update after they unmount: a clipboard write that finishes once the control is gone sets no state, starts no timer and announces nothing.

Copy works inside a frame that does not allow the async Clipboard API, such as a sandboxed artifact viewer or an embed. There `useClipboard`, and so the copy buttons of `CodeBlock`, `Timestamp` and Markdown heading links, copy with the browser's copy command inside the reader's click or key press, also in an open modal dialog or a hover card, without moving focus. Before, those buttons copied nothing there (`CodeBlock` and `Timestamp` showed a failed copy), and the browser logged a permissions-policy violation for each press. Where the async Clipboard API is allowed, nothing changes.

CodeBlock's run-time highlight stylesheet now sits in the `astryx-base` cascade layer, like the rest of Core's CSS. A theme's syntax colours and an app's own `--color-syntax-*` or `::highlight()` rules now win over CodeBlock's defaults in any load order, also for a CodeBlock in a portal under a root Theme.
In development, `CodeBlock` throws an error that names the `code` prop and shows the fix, instead of a TypeError from inside the component. Production output is unchanged.

On right-to-left pages, CodeBlock and Code keep code in its own direction: punctuation stays where it was written, a long left-to-right line starts at the visible edge and scrolls toward its end, and inline code inside right-to-left text reads in source order. Each code line takes its direction from its first letter, on any page, so a line that starts with an Arabic or Hebrew letter reads right to left from the line's end (when it is wider than an unwrapped block, its start sits at the far end of the scroll); other code looks the same on left-to-right pages. CodeBlock's line-number gutter, header and controls still follow the page.

`CodeBlock` scrolls a long line, or code past `maxHeight`, before script runs and in a page that runs none, such as a file made with `astryx experimental render`. Until now the code was cut off at the edge of the block until script measured it, and in a static page it stayed cut off. The code viewport still becomes a Tab stop only while its code overflows.

`upgrade` skips a codemod for a file that holds a backslash when the file's escapes spell none of the codemod's words, as it already did for files with no backslash. Before, any backslash anywhere in a file (a `\n` in a string, a `\d` in a regular expression) sent the file through every codemod's parse, so a scan of a typical app parsed about a quarter of its files several more times than needed. An upgrade from 0.6.8 answered 24% to 55% sooner across the apps measured; ranges that run mostly older codemods gain less, because those codemods still run on every file. Output and written files are unchanged.

`upgrade` binds jscodeshift to each parser once per codemod instead of once per file, which built a new copy of jscodeshift's helpers for every file. An upgrade over a 240-file app runs about 150 ms faster. Output does not change.

Core's compact StyleX media key matched at exactly the `md` width point (768px) and at exactly 500px tall, because StyleX rewrites `(width < 768px)` to a length the browser rounds up to 768px. The key now matches only below those edges, as the compact definition says, and Core spells every range-syntax width and height edge through one set of helpers. No component uses the key yet, so nothing changes on screen.

The CLI orders names the same way on every machine. Build, search, discovery and the CLI's lists (such as `astryx component --list`) broke ties with the host's locale, so a machine set to another language could pick a different template or print lists in a different order. They now use one fixed text order, and a lint rule keeps locale-dependent comparisons out of the CLI.

`astryx component` and `astryx discover <package>/<Component>` print the commands a component doc writes (with a `{@command …}` token, a `{@link …}`, or a bare `astryx …` code span) with the project's command, as `astryx docs` does, instead of a bare `astryx …` that may not run in the project. `--json` keeps the bare command.
`astryx component VStack --detail full` and `astryx component HStack --detail full` print the props list once, under Props, instead of again under Components. The JSON is unchanged.

`astryx component <hook>` prints the hook's parameters, which `astryx hook <hook>` also prints: one line each in the default answer (name, type, default, required, and the description's first sentence) and the whole table at `--detail full`. The JSON is unchanged.

`astryx component <hook>` prints what the hook returns, as `astryx hook <hook>` does: a Returns section at the default and full detail, and the returned fields in the brief signature. The JSON is unchanged.

`astryx component <name>` no longer opens a component through one of its keywords. A keyword is a word to find a component by, not another name for it. A name that is clearly one component's keyword now gives the usual not-found error, with that component as the first suggestion. Exact names, names in another case, and file names open as before. The component doc type and the single-component authoring guide now define keywords the same way, and the guide has a section on choosing them.

`astryx component <Name>` names a family's sub-components that have their own doc on one line, with the command that reads each, instead of a heading and a "see" line per sub-component. A sub-component with its own description or props keeps its section.

`astryx component <Name>` prints a short answer by default: what the component is, its import, a usage line, every prop as one line (name, type, default, required, and its description's first sentence), its accessibility requirements, its pieces with one command that reads them all, and the commands that print the rest (`--props` for each prop's whole description, `--detail full` for anatomy, best practices, examples and theming). The same answer is `--detail compact`; `--detail full` prints the whole doc as before, and `--json` is unchanged. Every part comes from fields each component doc already has, so an integration's component gets the same answer.

`astryx component <Name>` with a name that is not a component now suggests the components of your project's integrations, not only Core's. A typo of an integration component's name (`ZorbletCrd` for `ZorbletCard`), or its name without its package's prefix, gets that component as a suggestion, matched by the same rule as a Core component: name, keywords and description. Two adjacent letters swapped in a name (`Butotn`) now count as one slip, as a one-letter typo does, and so does one slip in a name typed as words (`hover crad` or `hover-crd` for `HoverCard`): that name comes before a component that only has the words as a keyword. A component whose name is part of the typed name now comes before a component that only has one of the typed words as a keyword, from any package (`MetricCard` suggests Card, not InfoTip). Among names that hold every typed word, the one with the fewest extra words comes first (`time` lists TimeInput before Timestamp). Only a Core component still resolves by a close match, and the suggestion count rules are unchanged. `astryx component tag-list` no longer opens OverflowList: the name is also one slip from TabList, so the lookup lists OverflowList first, then TabList.

The Astryx skill the CLI writes for agents on the computer, and the Claude Code and Codex plugin skill made from it, now say to start a page with `astryx build "<what the page is for>"`, and to start anything else with `astryx search`.

The computer-level agent text adds Astryx to a new project, or to an existing app only when the user asks for Astryx; an existing app that doesn't use Astryx keeps its current UI stack. Before, it told agents to add Astryx to any project without it, so an agent asked for one page in a plain React app could rewrite the app with Astryx.

The Astryx skill the CLI writes for agents on the computer, and the Claude Code and Codex plugin skill made from it, now say to pin `@astryxdesign/cli` exactly when the project pins `@astryxdesign/core` exactly. Before, agents added the CLI at Core's version with a `^` range beside an exactly pinned Core.

The computer-level agent text says that inside a project with its own Astryx text (an `astryx-project` skill, or an Astryx block in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md), an agent follows that text, which knows the project's version and setup. Asked a vague question about a project, agents loaded the generic computer text and missed the project's own facts.

An option that answers a question in other tools (`--yes`, `-y`, `--assume-yes`, `--non-interactive`, `--no-interactive`, `--no-input`) now gets a direct answer: no Astryx command asks a question, so the error says the option is not needed and names the same command without it (`Run: npx astryx init`). On `upgrade`, which writes only with `--apply`, it names the `--apply` run first and the preview run second (a `--list` run keeps the plain answer). Before, `astryx init --yes` listed init's options and pointed at `init --help`, so an agent spent a step reading help before it ran plain `init`.

The `useContainerReveal` usage block says the actions stay visible under a coarse primary pointer (a phone or tablet), not on any touch device, matching the hook's behavior on a touchscreen laptop used with a mouse.

Two content page templates now ask for confirmation before a destructive action: Refund on the detail page and Delete in each attachment's menu on the work item page. After you confirm, a demo message says what would happen; Cancel does nothing.

The order detail, work item detail and component documentation page templates read correctly when they are shared as a file that runs no script. Their first paint is the narrow layout at every width, instead of a desktop side rail that squeezed the page into a narrow column on a phone; once script runs, wide screens still get the side rail. On a narrow screen the order and work item details now follow the main column instead of opening in a full-screen dialog, and the component documentation's section links stay on top as links instead of a picker.

The documentation, technical documentation, design documentation, order detail, work item detail and library page templates now list keywords in the words their users use for those pages, so `astryx search` and `astryx build` find them for more ideas. The template authoring guide now asks authors to describe each page that way.

The content page templates now give their dead buttons and menu items a behavior: in `course-detail`, `documentation`, `documentation-technical`, `detail-page` and `work-item-detail`, the buttons, cards and menu items that did nothing now either work or show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"), the documentation banner's Get started is a link, and toasts that claimed an action had happened now say it would happen. Refund on `detail-page` and Delete in `work-item-detail`'s attachment menus are left unwired, because an irreversible action needs a confirm step. No layout or styling changes.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the part data now knows the context menu (and its dividers): each part is right-clicked when a press opens nothing and it holds a layer, as one drawn in its own place is, so `how` reads what a context menu draws instead of saying it is unknown.

A pointer `ContextMenu` (the default presentation, and every Table cell menu) no longer carries the touch sheet's action list: `ContextMenu` now shares `DropdownMenu`'s sheet module, which loads the sheet only for the sheet presentation. A page with a Table that has cell actions, or with a `ContextMenu`, loads about 57 KB less JavaScript before first paint (about 20 KB gzip). A menu with `presentation="bottom-sheet"`, or `adaptive` on a compact touch screen, still loads its sheet after mount and opens it as before.

ContextMenu: in a bottom sheet, a data sub-menu whose label is not a plain string (for example emphasized text) now names the sheet after that label's text while its level shows, as DropdownMenu does. Back returns the root name.
The agent workflow copy that Core ships says to read a block example for a part the template lacks, not to insert a block, matching `astryx build`.

Banner gives themes two more parts: `banner-message` (the title and description together) and `banner-title`. The default status icon no longer sits in an extra box, so a theme that hides `banner-icon` leaves no empty gap before the message. A theme can now draw a one-line alert with no icon; one space separates the title and the description in every banner, so the gap between them is the same on one line. The four built-in statuses look the same. A status with no default glyph and no `icon` loses the empty 8px space before its message.

A CodeBlock title or language label too long for its header wraps before Copy and any caller controls, at a space or anywhere in a long file name, instead of running under them on a narrow block or with a wide code font.

`defineTheme({palette})`: a theme can take its color tokens from a few seeds. `themePalette({accent, neutral, success, warning, danger, info, vibrancy, recipe})` from the new `@astryxdesign/core/palette` entry generates the palette and maps it to the color tokens the CLI theme editor sets for the same color settings (surfaces, text, borders, icons, the accent and the status colors); explicit `tokens` and `components` still win, one by one. A palette that names no recipe runs `astryx-oklch-v1`. With a `neutral` seed, a pinned recipe keeps the generated shades across upgrades. Without one, the surfaces are Core's defaults, so shades picked by contrast against them follow the installed Core, as does secondary text lifted on a tinted part. Only apps that import `@astryxdesign/core/palette` ship the generator. The entry also exports `generateTonalPalette()` and its types.

`defineTheme` names a token map that holds itself ("tokens refers to itself: the value of self holds an object it sits in …") instead of recursing until the call stack overflows, when the theme extends one with adaptations. Themes whose tokens hold no such loop build as before.

A Dialog's and a Drawer's header row now contains its title, close button and end content. A theme that paints the header row (a title bar) no longer sees the title spill above and below it. Every slot stays where it was, so a theme that leaves the row unpainted draws the same pixels.

Text that sets no color of its own (such as a selected nav row) in an open MobileNav, Dialog, Drawer or BottomSheet now draws in the theme's text color. Before, it took the browser's dialog default, which ignores the theme and drew black on dark panels. A Toast's text takes the side that reads best on its card, and the default top-layer viewport passes the page's text color down instead of the browser's. A dark-mode error toast now reaches 4.5:1. Before, it read about 4:1 in an in-place viewport.

The docs of four components list props they already take and left out: ComplexSelector's `isLabelHidden`, `description`, `labelTooltip`, `isOptional` and `isRequired`; Selector's `changeAction`, `labelTooltip`, `placement` and `isDefaultOpen`; Toast's `isExiting`; and ContextMenuItem's `onClick`, `href`, `target`, `rel`, `isDisabled`, `hasCloseOnSelect`, `variant` and `ref`, which it takes as the DropdownMenuItem it re-exports.

`defineTheme({extends})` refuses a base written as a plain theme object (a name and tokens, not built by `defineTheme()`) with the named "`extends` must be a theme from defineTheme()" error. Before, it merged the object's raw values, so a light/dark pair was written as `#fff,#000`. A base from `defineTheme()` or a built theme module merges as before.

A toast shown from inside a `Theme` with no `LayerProvider` draws under that Theme and its mode, and follows it while the Theme is mounted, so its text reads even when the host page rewrites `<html data-astryx-theme>` (an artifact viewer that themes its own frame). A toast shown with no Theme around it still follows `<html>`. A toast that replaces another by `uniqueID`, one shown with a Theme and the other without, keeps drawing as the first one did, so the card stays in place.

Text inside a `Theme` that sets no line height of its own now uses the theme's body leading (`--text-body-leading`), as Core's own body text does, instead of the reset's 1.5. Plain text in a Card or Stack and a Blockquote's quote follow the theme's line height and move when a theme changes it. Core parts that set a text role's size now also set that role's leading, so none of them draws on an inherited line height (inline `Code` keeps the line of the text around it, and a few parts keep a fixed line height they are measured or aligned to: the Selector trigger, the Stepper step description and the chat composer): Table cells, header cells and row index numbers, Calendar month heading, day, weekday and week-number text, the touch date and time fields' titles, weekdays and wheels, Stepper step text, Pagination, Collapsible titles, Command Palette items, Dropdown and nav menu items, Selector and MultiSelector items and empty states, the MultiSelector trigger's overflow count, the PowerSearch nested editor's root label, the Typeahead empty state, the chat trigger menu's empty and loading states, the chat system message and pasted-text details, Code Block sizes, Empty State compact text, Segmented Control and Token small sizes, the Switch description, the top nav menu's item descriptions, the chevron in a breadcrumb item's menu trigger, the Avatar Group overflow count, the skip link, Tokenizer and Slider labels. With the default theme, 14px text moves from 21px to 20px lines; 12px text in these parts moves to 20px lines (the supporting leading), from 18px or about 17px; 12px text that only inherits moves from 18px to about 17px; 17px text such as Collapsible titles moves from 25.5px to 24px; the Avatar Group overflow count's line grows inside its fixed circle. Inherited text outside a Theme is unchanged; the listed parts take their role's leading wherever they render, also outside a Theme.
changesets.body: To keep the old lines: for inherited text, set a line-height on your own container inside the Theme, or set `--text-body-leading` in your theme (which also sets Core's own body text). The listed parts follow their role's leading token instead (`--text-body-leading`, `--text-label-leading`, `--text-supporting-leading`, `--text-large-leading` or `--text-code-leading`): set that token in your theme, or style the part through its theming target.

changesets.headline: Text inside a `Theme` that sets no size of its own now uses the theme's body size, 14px by default instead of the browser's 16px. Plain text in a Card or Stack, a Blockquote's quote and `Text type="inherit"` follow the theme's `--text-body-size`, as Core's own body text does, and move when a theme changes its text size. Text outside a Theme, and a host app's own styles, are unchanged: `reset.css` sets no font size. To keep 16px inside a Theme, set a font-size on your own container inside it, or set `--text-body-size` in your theme (which also sizes Core's own body text).

`doctor`'s fix for a missing Core, and `theme build`'s hint to install Core, now name Core at the same release as the theme hints. That is the Core release the project already names, in its dependencies or peer dependencies, or, when it names no Core at all, the release of the CLI that answers. Before, they named the newest Core. A project that followed both hints could get a Core that its theme's exact Core peer does not accept.
Internal: Core's internal touch entry re-exports its group press tracking and group-item mark for Lab's Rating, and the catalog gains two Rating messages. Apps import nothing new.

LayoutContent names the container it sits in (`data-container="dialog"`, `"card"` or `"bottom-sheet"`), as LayoutHeader and LayoutFooter do, so a theme can style a dialog's body apart from its header and footer through `layout-content` with `container:dialog`, for a full-bleed title bar over a padded body and a footer bar. The Dialog's own LayoutContent takes it, an AlertDialog's body included.
Adds two English catalog messages for the Lab media player's visible time readouts (elapsed and total, and remaining time), so a locale can translate them.

MobileNav's painted drawer panel carries its own theme target, `mobile-nav-drawer`, with the resolved `side`, so a theme can give the panel a surface and text colors without painting the full-screen overlay behind it. The default look does not change.

defineTheme: a typography weight that reaches Core as a number (from a theme written in JavaScript or read from JSON, such as `heading: {weight: 700}`) is written as its text (`700`) everywhere it is read. A theme that extends a base with adaptation rules now builds instead of failing with "adaptations.rules[0]… must resolve to a concrete CSS string". The `FontWeight` type does not change.

The active option of a select, multi-select and typeahead list (the one the keyboard or pointer is on, named by `aria-activedescendant`) carries a `highlighted` theme state on its row target, as Item and CommandPaletteItem rows do: `selector-option-row`, `multi-selector-option`, and the typeahead's option row, which gets its own target, `typeahead-option` (with `size` and `selected`). A theme can style the highlighted option without a structural selector.

Themes can draw Pagination's controls as one joined strip. The control row carries `pagination-list`, each of its Button controls carries `pagination-item` (the current page's reflects `data-selected`), and the ellipsis carries `pagination-ellipsis`. On the cells, `pagination-item` competes with the theme's `button` entries: its base rule loses to a `button` entry keyed on variant, size or elevation, and its hover and selected rules weigh the same as a one-key `button` rule, so the later one in the theme wins. The default look does not change.
Themes can reach parts that painted with no target of their own. The default look does not change.
changesets.body:
- Each key badge in Kbd carries `kbd-key`.
- The Typeahead result popup carries `typeahead-popup`.
- Calendar's range band and hover-preview band carry `calendar-range` and `calendar-range-preview`, with `start` and `end` on the first and last day.
- BottomSheet's grab bar carries `bottom-sheet-handle`.
- AlertDialog's title and description carry `alert-dialog-title` and `alert-dialog-description`, and a theme's `heading` and `text` rules no longer reach them. A theme that styled them through `heading` or `text` keeps that look by repeating those rules on `alert-dialog-title` and `alert-dialog-description`.
- LayoutHeader and LayoutFooter reflect `container` (`card`, `dialog` or `bottom-sheet`), so a theme can style a dialog's header without a card's.
- ToggleButton reflects `grouped` inside a ToggleButtonGroup.
- An accent Link's hover color reads `--link-hover-color` when a container or theme sets it.

changesets.headline: The radio's circle (RadioList, the menu radio, and every host of the shared radio indicator), its dot and its pressed layer are drawn at a 50% radius instead of the `--radius-full` pill token, so a theme that squares its pills keeps round radios. A theme that wants square radios overrides the radio component.

The README's setup box now shows how to install the CLI at the version of `@astryxdesign/core` you have, saved exactly when `package.json` pins Core exactly, and its link to the Astryx CLI section now works. A second box tells agents to ask the Astryx CLI before they write code, with three commands that work with or without the install: `build`, `component` and `doctor --built .`. Before, the setup box's command installed the newest CLI with a `^` range.

The README's stylesheet setup boxes (Next.js, Next.js + Tailwind, Next.js + StyleX) now import the theme's `fonts.css`, as `astryx theme add` does. It holds `@font-face` rules for the font files the theme package ships, so the page requests nothing outside the app. Before, a page set up from those boxes loaded no theme font and fell back to the system font stack.

`Theme`'s runtime style injection hint no longer names a package or an import made up from the theme's name (`@astryxdesign/theme-canvas-editor/built`, `canvas-editorTheme`). It gives the build step, `astryx theme build` on the file that defines the theme with `--detail full`, whose printed import lines bring in the built .js and .css; a theme from an Astryx theme package ships both built.

Core's install note no longer tells a project that keeps its Astryx guidance as a project skill (`astryx init --to skills`, or a folder in the project) to run `init`: the setup check also counts the Astryx project skill in `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, or a project folder astryx.config saves (`astryx init --to ./<folder>`), read from the config's text without running it.

The switch thumb is drawn at a 50% radius instead of the `--radius-full` pill token, so a theme that squares its pills squares the switch track and keeps a round thumb. A theme that wants a square thumb sets the radius on `switch-thumb`.
Themes can reach four more parts. The default look does not change.
changesets.body:
- A theme's `spinner` indicator replaces the ring a Spinner turns.
- A theme's `tree-disclosure` indicator replaces a TreeList row's rotating chevron with a mark for each state.
- NumberInput's stepper buttons carry `number-input-stepper` with `direction` (`increment` or `decrement`).
- The close buttons of Toast and Banner carry `toast-close` and `banner-close`, so a theme can style them apart from other buttons. Toast's close button draws in the toast's text color; Banner's keeps its status text color.

changesets.headline: A theme value left `undefined` in a part's style block, a color-mode block (`@light`, `@dark`), a pseudo-class block, an `onDark`/`onLight` surface or an adaptation rule's parts is now not set, and so is a component, style key or color-mode block left `undefined`, or one whose every value is, as a page token left `undefined` already was: the stylesheet writes nothing for it. In a style key or a color-mode block, the value the theme inherits for that property stays. A restated pseudo-class block still replaces the inherited one whole, even when every value in it is `undefined`: it stays, empty, and its component counts as themed. Before, the stylesheet held the text `undefined` (`padding: undefined;`), which the browser drops, and the inherited value was lost too; in an adaptation rule, `defineTheme` refused the theme. A `null` value keeps its meaning: it replaces an inherited value and is written as it is, and an adaptation rule still refuses it.

`defineTheme` treats a local token left `undefined` (in the theme or in an adaptation rule's `localTokens`) as not set, as a token, or a value in a part, surface or adaptation rule, left `undefined` already is: the theme builds and the stylesheet writes nothing for it. Before, it was refused as no CSS string, so a conditional spread or an unset environment value failed the theme. An adaptation rule that writes a local token name no theme in the lineage declares still fails with its name. `localTokens: undefined` at the root is refused by name ("localTokens is undefined: omit the field or pass an object"), as `extends: undefined` is: a root `localTokens` or `extends` left undefined is almost always a failed import.

defineTheme: a theme's own token map that holds itself is named as the theme's `tokens`, not as one of the adaptation rules of the theme it extends; and an adaptation rule's value or condition that holds itself is refused by its path (`adaptations.rules[0].value.tokens.self …`) instead of overflowing the stack.

A toast's card draws on the right side from the first paint on a system-mode page. Before a script ran, a reader in dark mode saw the info toast with light text on its light card (about 1.1:1). The toast now renders its light-page side and names its dark-page side beside it, and the theme draws that side on a dark page. Themes whose toast surfaces keep one side in both modes write no extra CSS.

Toast: before the surface is measured (a server render, a static page), the Toast's text side comes from the theme's own resolved inverted surface color, by the same rule the measurement uses, instead of assuming the surface is dark in light mode. This applies when the inverted surface is an opaque hex, `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `black` or `white` value and the on-dark and on-light colors are hex, `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `black` or `white` values; any other value (such as a translucent surface, `oklch()`, `hsl()` or another named color) still starts from the color mode until the measurement runs. A theme whose inverted surface is a light hex or `rgb()` color in light mode no longer renders a Toast with white text on a white bar until the page runs its script.

TopNavHeading carries `data-mode="drawer"` when TopNav draws it as the phone menu's title, as TopNavItem already does, so a theme keys the menu's title with `mode:drawer` (for example a heading colored for a dark top bar, kept readable on the menu's own surface). In the bar it carries no `mode`; nothing else changes.

The typography docs say what Core builds, in one rule: a heading with no `family` takes the body's whole font list; with its own `family`, only its own `fallbacks`; `fallbacks` with no `family` build nothing. `TypographyConfig`, its `heading` field, `defineTheme`'s `typography`, the `fonts-and-assets` doc page and the theme template say it; the `font-setup` page says a heading with no family uses the body's and points to `fonts-and-assets` for the rest.

In dark mode, secondary text on a neutral fill (an unselected SegmentedControl label, AvatarGroup's "+N" count) now meets 4.5:1 contrast on the default surface and on a Card. The default dark `--color-text-secondary` is a little lighter: `#B0B5BB`, was `#AAAFB5`.

The dashboard page templates give screen readers clearer structure: each page marks its content area (`LayoutContent`) as the main landmark, has exactly one level-1 heading, and has a heading outline with no skipped levels (set with `accessibilityLevel`, so the look is unchanged). `dashboard` gains a visually hidden "Dashboard" title, and `dashboard-comparison`'s decorative sparklines no longer take keyboard focus inside hidden content. No visual change.

Controls that did nothing in six dashboard page templates now respond with a demo message that says what would happen: Reload and both View more buttons on the analytics dashboard, Export on the comparison, scorecard and funnel dashboards, Export status on the program dashboard, and View more on the portfolio dashboard.
Under Reduced Motion, releasing a mouse drag on a date or time wheel lands on the nearest row at once instead of gliding to it.
In development, `DateRangeInput` throws an error that names the `value` prop and shows the fix, instead of a TypeError from inside the component. Production output is unchanged.
The debug event's `project.integrationCount` is documented as what it counts: the integrations the project's astryx.config names, not integrations loaded from dependencies the config does not name.

On Linux, in a project whose integration takes the CLI's debug record, every command finishes about 11 to 17 ms sooner. The record names the locale and time zone the process's Intl uses, and asking Intl for them first loads ICU's data at the end of the run. The answer is now kept beside the kept gathers while the environment values, the Node and ICU versions and the time zone files it comes from are unchanged. Elsewhere, and on other systems, it is asked as before. The record's values do not change.

`astryx component <name>` keeps a suggested component whose keywords or synonyms are the typed name ahead of another command's hint for a near spelling, and leaves the hint out when such components fill the list (`astryx component Combobox` lists Typeahead, Selector and Tokenizer, not `astryx hook useCombobox`).

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a role color too dark to stand out on the dark page still draws dark mode at the documented shade 70, and the set result now offers the shade nearest it that passes as a one-line dark-mode choice. `how` for a deeper or darker role color includes a dark-mode line that stands out on the dark page, so dark mode goes the way the color asked instead of turning paler.

The text wrapping, word break, truncation, heading truncation, overflow list, context menu, bottom sheet menu and direction hook examples draw their demo frames and targets with theme colors instead of fixed grays, so they follow the app's theme and dark mode.

Dialog: opening a dialog no longer moves focus to a `data-autofocus` field (such as a `TextInput` with `hasAutoFocus`) inside a closed dialog nested in it. A nested dialog's focus request belongs to that dialog alone. Before, a closed nested dialog whose box was still laid out (for example through a display utility class) could take the caret into a field nobody could see.
Dialog's guidance now names its one nesting exception: an AlertDialog that confirms a destructive action may open from a dialog. It asks one question, and Escape closes only the alert.

Dialog: a DialogHeader that mounts after the dialog opens now names the dialog, and the name goes away when the header unmounts. A dialog's own `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` wins, and an `aria-label` that arrives while the header is mounted now names the dialog instead of losing to the header title.

`useSpeechRecognition` and `ChatDictationButton`: a page rendered on the server no longer has a hydration mismatch. The server and the render that hydrates its markup both report `isSupported: false`, so they draw the same tree; the dictation button appears in the next render when the browser supports speech recognition.

`astryx discover` names an installed integration's docs the way `astryx docs` opens them: a doc that adds sections to a topic by that topic's name, and a guide by its route. It listed each doc by the name on its file, so a doc such as a theme package's guide, which adds its sections to `theme`, printed a name `astryx docs` did not know.

`astryx discover` names the sections an installed integration adds to a doc another package owns, so a reader can open its own section straight away: the list prints the read beside the doc, `docs: theme (read: astryx docs theme install-and-apply)`, the JSON entry gains `docSections` (each name's section keys, each opening with `astryx docs <name> <key>`), and the doc's item page gains `sections` and prints the same reads.

`astryx discover` lists the icon sets your discover sources offer even where icon features are off (no icon-set package installed and no `experimental.iconSet`), so an app can compare packs before it picks one. A pack shows in the Available list (`iconSets`), in a search, and on its `discover <package>/<set>` page, with the catalog's display name, description, license and icon count. When the catalog lists the set's definitions, the page's text says how many of the CLI's icon definitions it maps (`definitions: 152/180`, as `experimental icon --list` prints it); the definitions themselves are listed only where icon features are on. Each listed set is marked `[experimental]` in text and carries `experimental: true` in JSON (a package entry names its experimental `iconSets` in `experimentalFields`). The page gives the project's install command, then `astryx experimental icon use <package>/<set>`. Installed sets, their pages and `--type icon-set` still need icon features on, `astryx search`'s discover line never points at an icon set while they are off, icon-set fields on other kinds are ignored, and a catalog with no icon set gives the same output as before. Discover catalogs may give an icon set's `license`.
