`astryx discover <package>/<set>` names an icon set's default look by its variant in text (`default: outline`) instead of printing `[object Object]`, and leaves the line out when the default names no variant. `astryx experimental icon --list` no longer prints an empty `default:` line for such a default. The JSON is unchanged.

`astryx discover` shows an installed integration's package.json `description`, as it already did for a package a source lists: on the list's Installed side and on the package page (`discover <package>`). Text shows its first sentence; `--json` carries the whole description as the entry's `description`. Terminal escape codes and control characters are removed, and a blank description is left out. Search (`discover <words>`), which already matches package descriptions, now also finds an installed package by a word in its description.

`astryx discover` with no query asks the project's discover sources for their catalogs while it reads the installed packages, instead of after. With a large integration whose source asks a remote catalog, the list came back about 0.4 seconds sooner. Output does not change.

`astryx discover <words>` matches word by word, as `astryx search` does: every word is part of the query, and an item matches by the words of its name (camelCase split), title, summary, and keywords, with its package's description adding words. So `discover chart categories` finds a `BarChart` whose summary says "Compare values across categories", which the old whole-phrase match missed. When an item matches every word, only such items are listed; matches rank by how many words they match. When nothing matches, the error suggests the Core component or hook `astryx search` gives first for the query, such as `astryx component AlertDialog` for `discover modal`, when search matches it by name or keyword. `astryx search` now prints its "More in packages you could add" line only when the `discover` command it names would list a match: discover's own search, run over the saved copy of a discover catalog, decides. With `--type <kind>`, the line names `discover <query> --type <kind>`. With no saved copy, the line prints as before. Search reads only the saved copy and never calls a discover source.

A command that keeps catalogs keeps the parse of each shipped doc it reads, by the doc's text, so a later read of that doc does not parse it again. The doc parsers build their schemas only when they first parse, not when the CLI loads them. Output is unchanged.
Text's `as` docs list `h1`, `h2` and `h3`, and PowerSearch's `statusVariant` docs list `tooltip`, as their types already allow; the `tooltip` text says what PowerSearch shows for it.

A section an integration adds to a topic, or to a guide by its route, now stays when another integration, configured later, replaces that topic or guide: whether it showed used to depend on configured order alone. A topic read also names, at its top, the sections other packages add to it, since an added section joins the end of a topic that can be long.
`astryx docs use-a-theme` now says how to make dark mode the default: pass `mode="dark"` to the root `Theme`. A server-rendered app also sets `<html data-theme="dark">`, so the first paint is dark.
Internal: the docs namespace view and the `astryx docs --depth` list share one rule for the [experimental] mark. Output is the same.
`astryx docs --help` shows `astryx docs skills` and `astryx docs skills/astryx` among its examples, and the `docs` command reference says what `skills` and `skills/<name>` read.

`astryx docs` now names Core, the CLI, and the packages Astryx releases with Core such as themes, at the Core release your project uses, as `theme add` and `doctor` do. In a project that pins Core 0.7.10, the step to add a theme shows `npm install -E @astryxdesign/theme-neutral@0.7.10`. Before, it named no version, so npm picked the newest theme, which needs a newer Core than the project has, and the install failed. In a folder with no Core, on the docs site's pages, and in a step that first moves to another folder, the commands still name the packages with no version. The docs site's MCP endpoint names the Core release it documents.

Two packages that add a section with one title to the same docs topic or guide both keep it. Across packages, a section replaces another only when one carries an authored `id` that is the other's key or a title query the other's title answers. When one package's section holds the key another package's later section derives from its title, the later one is read by a key that starts with its package's provider id (its package name unless it sets one), such as `acme-dune-theme-install`, so `astryx docs`, `--index`, namespace reads and search show both. This includes titles that differ only in letter case: the later of two packages' `Install` and `INSTALL` was read as `install-2` and is now read by its provider key. Every other key collision keeps its numeric suffix. Sections of the topic itself still take a replacement from any package, the last configured winning.

The documentation page templates fit a phone: the overview page's hero gives its title the card's width, so in the default theme the title no longer breaks inside a word, and the design page's example actions and button previews wrap instead of running past their card. Wide screens look the same as before.

`astryx docs <topic>` prints the topic whole, as `--json` already did, so a guide's first read carries its rules and examples. A topic whose own text is over 16 KB still lists its sections, and a whole read ends with the commands that open one section or the section list. `--index` lists the sections of any topic, and `--full` prints any topic whole.

The stored docs routes, and so the build id, are the same on every machine that packs the same files. How the machine's Node resolves module imports no longer changes which folders the stored routes list.

`astryx docs cli/skill-places` says where to keep the Astryx guidance for AI agents: the AGENTS.md block in a project (the default, read by every agent), a project skills folder when a team keeps its guidance as skills, and the computer skill for agents outside a project, with the `init --to` command, file, and saved record for each place and how each is kept current. `astryx init --help` links to it.
The technical documentation page template's "Next steps" items wrap on a narrow screen instead of cutting off after one line, so a phone reader sees each item in full. Wide screens are unchanged.

The technical documentation page template reads correctly when it is shared as a file that runs no script. Its first paint is one column with the section links on top at every width, instead of a desktop side rail that squeezed the article into a narrow column on a phone; once script runs, wide screens still get the side rail. Copy buttons appear only once the page runs, so a static copy shows no buttons that do nothing. On a phone the section links stay on top as links instead of a picker.

The `theme` topic has a section on publishing a theme so other teams can use it (ship it in a package; another team runs `theme add <name> --package <package>`), in English, dense and Chinese, and its summary no longer calls its steps "sections", so a search for a section or a scoped section theme finds Section and MediaTheme first again.

`astryx docs <topic>` opens a page typed in another spelling of its route: spaces, hyphens, slashes, dots and underscores all separate words, and word order does not count (`docs tokens.tokens-color` opens `tokens/tokens-color`). When the typed words only name a page and no other command's entry matches, the miss suggests the pages whose title or declared keywords carry them, closest first (`docs theming` suggests the Theming topic first), keeps a route the typed words name first, and never lists more than before; a namespace's children are ordered the same way.

`docs` keeps the CLI's own docs tree between runs, while every file it was read from is unchanged. In a project where an integration can load, `docs` and its topics start about 30 to 65 ms sooner. Where none can load, `docs` keeps nothing and nothing changes. `doctor` still checks the tree's files themselves. Output does not change, except that `doctor`'s row for the per-user cache now names the docs tree among the entries it holds.
`astryx docs` with a mistyped topic or namespace (`tokns`, `colr`) now lists the one a slip or two away first, ahead of the other topics and namespaces.

`astryx theme build` and `astryx doctor` no longer offer to install a package named after a project folder, such as `src`, for an import the project's `baseUrl` maps to a TypeScript file written with a `.js` extension (`src/rows.js` for `src/rows.ts`). They now read such an import as the project's own file, as TypeScript does.

`doctor --built <path>` now reads doctor's kept checks back as `doctor` does, once the per-user cache folder exists: the CLI took the path after `--built` for a subcommand, so those runs checked the docs again every time. In a project whose integrations add docs, a warm `doctor --built` is about 200 ms faster; in a Core-only project the difference is within noise. The build itself is still checked on every run. Check results do not change; the cache row counts the kept checks.

`doctor --built` reads source files faster: it parses each file without attaching comments to syntax nodes, blanks comments in one pass, and walks a file's syntax tree for `require()` and `import()` calls only when its text can hold one. On a 240-file app the source scan takes about a third less time. Output does not change.

`astryx doctor` warns about a Core button that does nothing when pressed (`button-actions`): a `Button` or `IconButton` from `@astryxdesign/core` with no `onClick`, `clickAction`, `href`, or `submit` or `reset` type, or with an empty handler or a link that goes nowhere (`#`, unless the app routes by the URL hash), where nothing around it acts on a press. The warning names each button's file, line and label. Doctor reads the app's own source as syntax trees and leaves out test, story and fixture files. It does not report a button it cannot judge: one with props spread in, a ref, a tooltip, or a disabled or loading state, or one inside a link, a trigger prop, a custom element, a `Provider` read off a namespace import of the app's own module, or a component it does not know, or one that holds an HTML control, a custom element, another package's component other than an icon, or content doctor cannot read (`{children}` a wrapper passes in). It does not judge a workspace member's buttons when the app imports the member by its package name. When doctor cannot follow a linked folder, it treats no component as a page. When the app's own code listens for a press through the DOM (`addEventListener('click', …)`, an `addEventListener` whose event a variable names, a library's `.on('click', …)`, or an `onclick` property), doctor judges no button and reports the check as not run. Nor does it judge a component that a module may load by a path doctor cannot read (a computed `import()` or `require()`, `import.meta.glob` or `require.context`, in a module, an MDX or Astro page, or a module that does not parse), or that an MDX or Astro page names. The check never fails `doctor`.

Once the per-user catalogs folder exists, `astryx doctor` keeps what its `button-actions` check finds while every folder the check listed, every file it read and every package it looked up are unchanged. A warm `doctor` in a project that has not changed then skips that check's scan: it no longer parses the project's pages for buttons again. Every answer is unchanged.

Outside a project, `astryx doctor` now warns about an integration installed for the computer that has issues in its own files, and names them. Before, commands such as `astryx search` and `astryx discover` warned about the integration and said to run `astryx doctor`, but `doctor` passed and named no issue. Issues that need a comparison with Core components are still not named there, because `doctor` reads no Core outside a project.

Once the per-user catalogs folder exists, `astryx doctor` keeps what its `core-props` check finds while every folder the check listed, every file it read, and the TypeScript, Core and project config it used are unchanged. A warm `doctor` in a project that has not changed then skips that check's scan: the check no longer parses the project's pages or reads Core's types again. The check also loads its parts only when they are needed, so a project without TypeScript no longer loads the component reader. Every answer is unchanged.

`astryx doctor` warns about a prop the app gives a Core component that the component does not take (`core-props`), such as `selectedID` on `TabList` or `labelHidden` on `CheckboxInput`. Such a prop does nothing, and unless the build type-checks, no build step reports it. The warning names up to eight props, each with its file, line and component and a documented prop with the same words when there is one, and counts the rest: "src/App.tsx:6 CheckboxInput has no `labelHidden` (did you mean `isLabelHidden`?)". A prop is reported only when Core's docs for the component leave it out and Core's own types, read with the project's TypeScript as its pages see them, do not take it either. The name of an HTML, SVG, DOM or ARIA attribute, which a component can pass on to what it renders, is never reported, and neither is a name with a hyphen (such as `data-` or `hx-` attributes), which JSX never checks against a props type, a prop that JSX gives every component (such as a `css` prop the project's own types declare), a prop of a component from outside Core or of a generic component, or a prop in a module compiled with another JSX runtime. Doctor reads the app's own source as syntax trees and leaves out test, story and fixture files. Without TypeScript, or in a project whose TypeScript or build config compiles JSX with another runtime, the check says it did not run. The check never fails `doctor`.

`doctor` now says when an app does not load Core's component styles, `@astryxdesign/core/astryx.css`. In an app that uses Core's prebuilt styles, components render unstyled without them. Before, nothing caught it: the build, `doctor` and `doctor --built` all passed. Plain `doctor` warns when no project stylesheet or module imports them and no page links them. `doctor --built` warns when the output uses Astryx but no built stylesheet or page carries them. An app that compiles Core's styles from source with `@astryxdesign/build` is not checked.

`astryx doctor` reads its kept docs checks back after an edit to the app's source. They run before the scans that read the app's source (its theme wiring and, in a project that names an icon set, its placeholder icons), so what they keep no longer depends on the app's files. Right after an edit, `doctor` in a project with an app finished about 230 ms sooner. Output does not change.

`astryx doctor` no longer reports a theme as wired because a theme source or a generated theme file imports it: the theme editor's settings module, a theme build's output, or a theme source that imports a package theme only to extend it. Before, an editor theme built on an installed theme package (`--like <theme>`) turned the "no theme appears wired" warning into a pass while the app rendered no theme; now only the app's own imports of a theme, or a theme it passes to `Theme`, count.

`astryx doctor`'s theme font check now accepts a Google Fonts or Bunny Fonts stylesheet `<link>` in the app's page head as loading the families it names: in `index.html`, `public/index.html`, `src/index.html`, or a Next.js root layout or `_document` (`.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.js`, `.mjs` or `.ts`, under `app/`, `pages/` or `src/`). An app that loads a theme's fonts that way no longer gets the warning. A link inside a comment, one whose `rel` is not `stylesheet`, or one from another host does not count. When a package theme ships no font stylesheet, the fix names the page file whose `<head>` the link goes in.

`doctor`'s theme font check now counts a family as loaded when a `family` parameter of a font service URL in the theme's font stylesheet names it. The Google Fonts import in every Astryx theme's font stylesheet does this. Before, an app set up correctly with the neutral theme got a warning it could not act on: "External font imports prevent proof for neutral: Figtree." A family that no `family` parameter names still gets that warning, as does a font service URL that names its families another way.

`doctor`'s theme font check now counts a family as loaded when any font stylesheet that the generated theme module imports loads it. A local theme built on neutral, such as one whose source extends neutral or a copy that `theme eject` makes, names neutral's fonts but ships no font stylesheet of its own. Before, `doctor` warned "Added themes name font families but import no font stylesheet (<theme>: Figtree (font stylesheet is not imported))", even when the app also added neutral and the module imported neutral's font stylesheet. A family that no imported font stylesheet loads still gets that warning.

With no update check recorded, `astryx doctor`'s `newest-release` check no longer says the check runs once a day after a command, which is true only for a copy installed for the computer. It now says that only that copy checks, that a project's own copy changes only when the project upgrades it, and that a tool that runs its own copy chooses its release.

Doctor's new `icon-imports` check names each icon import that no longer matches the app's icon sets after the list changes or a set is uninstalled: an icon from a set the list leaves out, or from a backup when an earlier set draws the same meaning, warns with the icon of the list that replaces it; an icon import or re-export of an npm package that is not installed, not declared, and not mapped by a `paths` or `baseUrl` entry in the app's tsconfig or jsconfig fails, since it breaks the build, even when that package is the main set itself. The check runs where icon features are on and a main set is decided.

`astryx doctor integration <check> <package>` run in the folder of that package now says the package is the one in this folder, not one the project installs, and names `astryx integration check` for checking the package you are making. Before, it said only that the package was not installed and to install it first.

`astryx doctor` prints a short kept-cache row. Before, the `gather-cache` row printed a paragraph of about 2 KB: every kind of kept result, when each is used, the size limit, the transpile cache, and "deleting the folder clears it". Now the row prints only the folder, its entry count and size, the command that lists every kept item and the size limits (`astryx doctor --json`), and the exact command that clears the caches, such as `rm -rf ~/.cache/astryx/catalogs`. That command also names the transpile cache folder when it exists. The JSON check keeps its whole `message` and adds an optional `brief` field with the short form, which text prints in the message's place; the legend then reads `message (or brief)`. Ids, statuses and exit codes do not change.

`astryx doctor --built`'s purity check no longer flags the stylesheets the app's registered themes load. It reads them from the theme module the CLI writes (`theme add` and the theme editor), so an editor-made theme starts with no "imports the stylesheet" findings. Any other stylesheet import is still flagged.

`astryx doctor --built` no longer flags the setup stylesheet as page styling. A stylesheet that only imports Astryx packages' CSS (`reset.css`, `astryx.css`, a theme's CSS), as the getting-started steps write it, is read as wiring. A stylesheet with rules of its own, or an import from another package, is still flagged.

With no update check recorded, `astryx doctor`'s `newest-release` row reads "Newest release unknown: no update check recorded here. Only a copy installed for the computer checks, daily in the background after a command; a project's copy changes only when the project upgrades it; a tool running its own copy picks its release." The `gather-cache` row keeps its list of what is kept, and states the CLI's build id, the lookup commands' not-found path and the size limit in short clauses. Check ids, statuses, fields, the JSON shape and exit codes do not change.

`astryx doctor` no longer fails its private theme variables check in a Yarn Plug'n'Play project. For a built-in theme that the app installs as a package, the check now reads that package's own theme source, which is the copy the app uses, instead of the CLI's copy, whose icon import Yarn refuses to resolve.

`doctor`'s private theme variables check now loads each theme input with the Core the project installed when the CLI is installed for the computer. Before, in an app with Core and a theme package but no CLI in the project, the check failed for every theme input that imports `@astryxdesign/core`, as every Astryx theme package does. That CLI has no Core of its own: "Added theme inputs set private --_* variables directly (…: input could not be inspected …)". When the project's Core isn't installed yet, as in a fresh clone, the check now says that it did not inspect the theme inputs. Before, it failed for each input that imports `@astryxdesign/core`.

`astryx doctor` warns when a setting of an added local theme does not show as written (a later shorthand resets it, a more specific rule of the theme it extends wins, or cascade order decides), naming the theme, the setting with its line, and the fix, from the same check `astryx theme build` runs. It is a warning, never a failure: the theme builds as before.

A `DropdownMenu` whose layer opens after its trigger becomes a valid anchor now takes focus as it opens, and fires `onClick` once. A menu in a native `<dialog>` that the page displays closed opens one commit after the press. The menu read that open as refused, so focus stayed on the trigger and `onClick` never fired.
DropdownMenu: a mouse press opens a menu whose trigger sits in a same-origin iframe or another window, and the menu stays open through that press's release

DropdownMenu: in a bottom sheet opened from the keyboard, focus stays on the row a person moved to when the menu re-renders with a new `items` array, such as after a choice that updates the app's state. It moved back to the first row before. The sheet still focuses its first row when it opens, and its heading when a sub-menu is entered or left.
changesets.body: Reported by duytbp.

changesets.headline: A DropdownMenu sub-menu whose `label` is not a string, such as emphasized text or a translated message component, is now named correctly: a drilled-in view is named by the label alone, not by the whole row with its description; a view nested in it names its Back row "Back to" that label; and in a bottom-sheet data menu the sheet takes that label's text as its name while its level shows. Sub-menus with string labels do not change.

The editor template's transactions table keeps names readable on a phone. Each column now has a floor (name 180px, date and amount 120px, actions 60px), and its share of the width matches that floor. The table needs at least 480px; in anything narrower, such as a phone, it scrolls sideways instead of squeezing names to a letter or two per line. Desktop windows that give the table 480px or more do not scroll; the name column takes a larger share and the actions column a smaller one.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> --color-border <color>`: the emphasized border (input and selector frames) follows a border only where that makes it stronger on the surface, never fainter, and the result now says it follows; `show` names it as following your `--color-border`, not as a change in the theme's own source.

In a project that pins `@astryxdesign/core` to one version, as Astryx starters do, the commands the CLI prints to add or upgrade Astryx packages (the once-a-day hint, `doctor`'s fixes, the setup reminder, and the upgrade notice) save the new versions exactly too, such as `npm install -E @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.16`. Before, with npm, following them replaced the project's exact pins with ranges such as `^0.7.16`, so a later install could bring a CLI from another release than the project's Core.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: secondary text set exactly for the whole theme (in one mode or both) no longer turns off the readable shade on the parts that lift it (selected items and rows, a dropzone, numbered citations). Where the exact color reads on what those parts sit on it is used as written; where it does not, they take the gray nearest it that does, or, with no color dial, the base theme's own lift.

A kept value from an exact codec is stored as the JSON text its exactness check already read, so storing it no longer writes, parses and compares the value a second time. A run that keeps template discovery stores it about 15 ms sooner. A value that does not read back exactly is still never kept. Output does not change.

A layer's exit copy, which a touch close plays on, keeps the padding, border and colors of the element it copies. Before, the browser's popover style padded, bordered and painted it, so a surface with no padding of its own drew its content inset during the close.

A run of one `astryx experimental` command loads only that command, as `astryx <command>` already does. `astryx experimental export` and `astryx experimental import` no longer load the theme editor first, so each run starts about 0.2 seconds sooner. `astryx experimental` alone, its help, and an unknown word still load every command, so they print the same answers.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> accent <color>` keeps the color you gave as the link and accent text color wherever it reads at 4.5:1 on what that text sits on, in each mode its fill is your exact color; only where it does not do links move, to the nearest shade that reads, and the result says so with the ratio. Text on the fill stays white or near-black by contrast (button and badge labels are normal-size text, which needs 4.5:1, so white on iOS blue #007aff, at 4.02:1, is not picked), and the note now names how to keep the other one exactly.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads every way an amount is said ("a quarter bigger", "half again", "2x", "×2", "x0", "4 times", "by a factor of 2", "+50%", "-25%", "50 percent", "½") as a factor of what is there now, never as a length and never with an extra dial step; keeps fractions of a pixel; scales a part's line height and opacity the asked way ("50% more transparent" lowers the opacity and leaves the fill); answers whole-theme radius and border width amounts with exact token values (a whole-theme spacing or text amount it can only step says so); says when a part has no width to scale instead of giving a fixed cap; scales an own side padding with the rest; keeps the state and variant of a "2px rounder on hover" move and of a padding step; reads a corner percent with an amount ("50% of now", "20% bigger") as an exact radius, never a CSS percent; says when a corner amount can only step; and reads "no inner spacing", "zero padding" and "no gap" as zero of that thing, in the state asked.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: amounts read the way they are said. Zero, none and no set that property to 0 or none in any position ("card corners zero", "zero border", "opacity zero", "no letter spacing", "remove the top padding"), and a padding side reads its own value now. One amount reader takes "up 20%", "increase by 50%", "2/3", "two thirds", "three quarters", "twice as small", "a third again" and a lone "½" as a share of now; a bare percent radius is refused with the command that scales the radius instead. "Two steps bigger" gives two dial steps, "2 spacing units" is twice the spacing unit token, a size such as "24x16px" on padding is that exact padding, and "+4px", "-2px" or "4px more" on padding, gap, radius or text size is the value now plus or minus that length. See-through amounts set opacity ("half transparent", "10% transparent", "50% opacity"), "more opaque" raises it, and "5% gray" is gray at 5% alpha. Color amounts apply to text and hover colors; warmer and cooler move the hue, not the lightness; lighter and darker change the color of borders, dividers and links, and keep the alpha of rgb(), hsl() and oklch() colors. Small, secondary and supporting text and fine print change the supporting text size; "h1 800" is a weight; "h2 through h4" changes each level; "h1 800 and the other headings 600" sets every other level; "h1 twice as big as body text" and "h3 the same size as h2" take the other size times the amount; "and the active one blue" keeps that state. Thinner text is a lighter weight, a sharper shadow halves the blur of the part's shadow and a softer one doubles it, a thinner scrollbar says there is no scrollbar part, the overlay's lighter or darker changes only its alpha, and wider no longer sets a made-up 720px width. `how paddingLeft`, `how borderRadius` and other camelCase names look up that property.

`astryx experimental theme compile`: `--check` of an editor theme also checks its app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/` and fails with `ERR_THEME_STALE`, saying why, when the copy is kept back, missing a file, gone, or not the current build. Each theme's copy follows its own build, so a later theme failing no longer leaves an earlier one's copy behind. The copy's files are not theme sources: compiling its descriptor, a copy build file or `src/astryx-themes.ts` names the theme to compile, the copy's source from a subfolder names the app root, and an `--out` into the copy folder is refused. A copy left with only its build outputs is still the editor's, a copy file that is gone is written back by the next `set`, and a folder the copy could not be made in is named. The compile help says it writes and checks the app copy.

`astryx experimental theme compile`: a successful compile of an editor theme always writes its app copy from what it just built, a hand edit of `<theme>.theme.ts` included, with the copy's font stylesheet from the fonts the theme loads now (a font package installed or removed since; a `set` that changes nothing refreshes it too). `--check` reads the copy as a checkout writes it (CRLF line endings pass), compares it only once the theme's outputs are current (a hand-edited theme output is named by the outputs check), and a stale copy keeps the documented check result: `upToDate: false`, code `ERR_THEME_STALE` and `appCopyStale` saying why. The copy's source and folder are no compile targets, an `--out` at the copy folder (any case, with or without a slash) is refused and suggests the same compile without `--out`, and a refused compile writes no copy. The help says so.

`astryx experimental theme`: every command that builds or checks an editor theme says when its app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/` is behind: `compile` warns, `compile --check` fails while the copy is kept back or gone, and a `set` that changes nothing still carries `appCopyStale`. A link or a folder of yours at a copy file name stops the copy like a file of yours does, and a copy that cannot be written says why (not writable, disk full, a file where the folder goes). A copy whose descriptor was deleted is still the editor's and is written back. Compiling the copy's source takes the theme's lock and writes the copy again; with the copy gone it names `editor show`. Fonts the copy's font stylesheet loads are not called unloaded. The editor and compile help say the copy rule.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/` is written around a file of yours at another name (a note, a swap file); only a file of yours at one of the copy's names, or a link on the way to it, stops it, and then every change's result and `wiring` say the copy was not updated and why. The copy's `<theme>.fonts.css` is always there (a comment only when the theme loads no font stylesheet), so the app theme module's import of it holds when fonts or the base change; `compile` writes the whole copy, that file included. `new` refuses a name the theme commands skip (`a--b`, `b-`) and suggests the cleaned one. The package commands give true answers for an editor theme: `eject` says its source is yours already, and a path (`themes/<theme>`) is answered with the command by name.

The in-app theme preview's top bar draws the theme's name with Core's `TopNavHeading`, as an app's top bar does, so a setting on the header (such as its text color) shows in the preview as it does in the app.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: asks that name parts by reference or in two states read as Core draws them. "The disabled one" after an element in a place ("the hovered item of menus … and the disabled one") is that element; "the others" are the part's other variants, or the part not in the state named; states said together read by their kind, a condition among them (checked, selected, disabled) meaning all at once and moment states alone (hovered, pressed) meaning each, with the other reading offered as a second line; a selected table row hovered sets the selected wash's token for hover; a switch's "on color" is its checked look; tighter table rows lower the cells' block padding one spacing step. A border asked of a list inside an overlay's surface (a typeahead's) points to the overlay's edge, and `set` refuses a border's color or width on a part that draws no border (a divider), offering the token its line reads.

`astryx experimental theme editor`'s pictures and contrast checks take a toast's text side by Core's own rule for the fill the toast draws: the theme's text where it reads at 3:1, else the on-color that reads better; a see-through fill is composited onto the page first, and a gradient falls back from the inverted surface, as the app does. A problem there comes with a `color` line on the toast, which set takes. A transparent part on a lightbox's dark island is measured on that island. Parts drawn open keep the custom properties their inline styles set (a dialog's maximum size, a popover's gap to its trigger), and a plain element in a doc example (the Overlay's media) draws.

`astryx experimental theme editor set … surfaces`: a panel whose outer frame paints nothing (the banner) gets the dial's line and shadow on the part inside that paints its rounded fill, so `surfaces outlined` no longer draws a square border around the banner's rounded corners, and a border setting on the banner reaches that line. `how` never reads "Windows" named with a version ("Windows 11 accent #0067c0") as the containers.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the "thick borders on everything" answer and a whole-theme `--border-width` also reach a framed control (a segmented control), the parts that draw a box only when selected (nav items, segments), on that state, and the indicator lines (a tab's underline), at the border width.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a size ask with a bound that the part is already past the way the words ask ("rounder but at most 16px" on 42px corners) writes nothing and says so, never a move the other way; a direction beside a bound on a property with no scale of the theme's own (height) goes to the bound; "the body text … but at most 16px" is the base text size. A theme color with a way ("the accent color but lighter") is that color made that way in each mode. "The page color" as a gradient stop is the color the page is painted with, and the page is not changed. A role color made darker or lighter on a dark-only theme moves each of its tokens that way, its text included. "The same as" after a color property compares that color. "What color is the page" gives the page's color in each mode, and its pointer is the token that paints it.

`astryx experimental theme editor` names words the sample page's pictures break across two lines inside the word (a table word at a larger text size, "roadma" then "p"), measured in the page by the browser that takes the picture, as it names text cut short: a note, and a problem with the line that keeps the word whole when the browser measured one, else none.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a light-only or dark-only theme's build exports its one mode beside the theme (`export const colorModes = ["light"];`), and its app copy re-exports it, so `theme add` wires the theme in that mode. Older CLIs and Core ignore the extra export.

`astryx experimental theme`: every build names the pictures it removed, so `editor show` and the preview commands say so too when they build a theme again. A picture run whose browser fails part way says which pictures it took and which it did not. A render that fails on two copies of React points at the package manager's listing of them instead of `doctor`. `show --section` offers a section only within a typo of what was typed, else the whole sheet; `preview add --top` offers the typed number read exactly or brought into range, else the default; `preview add --template` offers a default page (overview, components, colors) within a typo. A base theme whose fonts come from a remote stylesheet (Google Fonts) gets a note that the previews and their pictures show the next font, and how to install a copy they load. The sheet's template pages render (they bind their file's default export), and a part Core re-exports under a name of its own (ContextMenuItem) gets its module and a cell; a component no Core module exports gets no empty cell.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: one built-value check for a theme's own token values runs before every build (`set`, `undo`, `show`, the preview) and in `compile`, so a value one refuses the other never writes. A `[light, dark]` pair on a token that is not a color is refused however the file gives it (an import, a const, a spread), naming the file and line that hold it. Typography weights are judged as the tokens they build. A private variable (`--_*`) and a key that is no token name (`color`) are refused with their line. A pair in the theme file is shown by its light and dark values in notes. `undo` of a token the theme's own source sets names that file and line.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `new` reads a built-in theme typed with another word (`theme neutral`, `neutral stone`) as the base, never as the neutral color dial, and a base or setting typed with its own quotes (`'base neutral'`, `"accent" red`, `'"base": "neutral"'`, `'padding: 8px'`) as that setting, never as words of the name. A setting `new` takes no option for points at the parts it is written on (`how '8px padding'`), in place of a `set` line `set` itself refuses. `undo` by a held value with a scope typed ranks the settings by how much of that scope they share, so `undo t red --on toggle-button` leads with a toggle-button setting rather than a whole-theme one.

`astryx experimental theme editor` contrast-checks the button style (`buttons soft` and `outline`) like any other change: the primary button's text on the fill it draws, or on the page and surface where it draws none, in each mode, with the nearest readable color as its line, instead of a "not checked" note.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> padding '5px 0' --on dropdown-menu` (or any part whose padding Core reads inside `calc()`, where one length is all that works) now offers the sides it means. Before, it offered a pointer to `how` for two lengths, and for three or four lengths (or two variables) one line with the first value only, such as `padding 2px`, which dropped the other lengths. Now it offers `padding-block 5px` and `padding-inline 0` for two lengths, `padding-top`, `padding-inline` and `padding-bottom` for three, and each side for four, each with the length you typed for it. A repair gate fix lets such a refusal offer three or four side lines together.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the cached part data is keyed by a fingerprint of the code that builds it (the census source and every file it imports), beside the installed Core, so any change to that code builds it again; there is no version number to bump by hand.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- The part data reads overlays drawn open: a tooltip, a popover, a hover card, and the lists a menu's button or a selector's field opens, which render on the server as markers alone, so `how tooltip` names what it paints and the menus group is checked.
- A fill set on a part says which fills Core gives its variants and states it now covers (a checked box's accent, a primary button's), with the line that changes only the fill at rest and the lines that fill one variant or state; a later color change says where the part's own fill keeps it from reaching.
- `corners more` from round steps to half as round again before pill, and `corners less` from pill back.
- A border color the theme sets is held to 3:1 against what it sits on in each mode.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor` names more of what a change leaves unchecked or unreached: a part's text color for a state (a selected nav item's) is measured on the fill the part draws in that state, with the nearest readable color as its line; a color the base theme writes as its own accent rather than the accent token (butter's blue links and outline buttons) is listed under missed once the accent moves, with a line that points it at the accent; and a fill made from a status token the theme's status color does not reach (an error toast's red after the danger color is set) is listed, with a line that gives it the theme's status color.

A change lists every custom property whose built value moved, in the JSON and the text: `changedTokens` keeps the theme's own tokens, the page included, and a new `changedPartTokens` lists the tokens the built stylesheet sets on parts (a readable text color on a selected row), each by its rule and mode, read from the stylesheet before and after the change. A dial that moves many tokens at once (vibrancy, a font) lists them all.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: one check for the token values a theme's own source gives, run by `show`, `set`, `undo` and `compile`, each refusing with the same message and writing nothing. A `[light, dark]` pair holds exactly two values in quotes (one, none or three is refused). Values from an imported module or written as an expression (`'ban' + 'ana'`, a template) are checked as a build evaluates them, naming the line. A second `tokens` key is refused, naming both lines (JavaScript keeps only the last). A family list in one pair of quotes is refused in the file as `set` refuses it (the browser reads it as one family by that whole name). The `typography` fields are checked: a family is one family name (the rest go in `fallbacks`), the scale's ratio is above 1 and at most 4, its base a positive size.
`astryx experimental theme`:
changesets.body:
- Custom properties that read each other are refused at their line: a token and a local token reading one another, and a part's own custom property reading itself.
- A pseudo-class after `::search-text` (`:current`) or `::scroll-marker-group` is accepted. A pseudo-element inside `:is()`, `:where()`, `:not()` or `:has()`, a pseudo-class after `::highlight()`, and `:window-inactive` after any highlight but `::selection` are refused. A pseudo-element near a known one (`::befor`) is refused as that one misspelled; one missing from the CLI's selector data and near none (`::column`, `::scroll-button()`) is noted as possibly newer than the CLI, and built.
- A misspelled vendor property (`-webkit-line-clmap`, `WebkitApperance`) is refused, with the vendor property it is near.
- A value read from another file through array or nested destructuring (`const [first] = arr`, `const {a: {b}} = cs`) is blamed on that file and line.
- A null value is warned at its line and the theme keeps working, while a boolean, NaN, an object or an array, which mean nothing in CSS, are refused. The warning says what it builds: a null property leaves the base theme's value; a null token is kept by the browser as the token's value, so most properties that read it act as if they were not set (text keeps the surrounding color, a background goes transparent) and a font family reading it falls back to the browser's default font.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a color dial made lighter or darker steps from the color it grows its shades from, its saved color, else its token where that is a color of its own. "make the neutral color darker" no longer offers `neutral '#000000'` (a gray seed grows the same shades, so it changed nothing) nor an exact `--color-neutral` that turned every see-through neutral fill opaque; it says why and what to name instead. An exact-token alternative keeps the token's own strength.

`astryx experimental theme editor set`: a color set with no `--mode` in a one-mode theme (`dark-only`) is saved for that mode, as it is built, so setting the theme back to both modes keeps it in its mode instead of painting the other mode with it, and a color saved for the other mode (the half a toast or a lightbox reads) is kept. An undo with no `--mode` removes that color.

`astryx experimental theme compile`: the app copy guard reads paths as the build does, so an `--out` written with backslashes or through a link into an editor theme's copy is refused, and a copy file named with backslashes is answered with the theme to compile. A file of yours in the copy folder, without the editor's mark, compiles like any theme source. Refusals run from a subfolder suggest the compile from the app root. The note on fonts named but not loaded follows the font stylesheet this compile writes, and the copy's font file no longer says the system has a font no package loads. A check held up by a file of yours names it and never sends you to a command that does not move it.

`astryx experimental theme`: the editor reads which theme a source defines from the export a build of it loads, so a helper theme exported beside the real one is refused before anything is written, and a name given by a const or a `//` inside a string no longer counts as damage. Font notes, the previews and the app copy load fonts for the families the theme builds, from one list. `compile` refuses an `--out` in the theme's own folder (other than its default stylesheet) before writing anything; an `--out` elsewhere says that the theme's folder and its app copy were not written or checked (`appCopySkipped`). A pointer to compile from the app root leaves off an `--out` the root cannot reach, and a family refusal from a subfolder suggests a compile that runs. Suggested commands stay bare in JSON (`astryx …`), as the text output starts them the way the project runs the CLI. The compile doc says what compiles.

`astryx experimental theme`: the editor judges a theme's source by the theme a build of it loads, its name and the theme it extends after every spread and repeated key, so a spread or a second `extends` that replaces the settings is refused, a spread const or a namespace import of the settings is accepted, and a helper theme read first is named with how to make the build read the theme. `compile` takes an `--out` as the theme's default stylesheet only when it is that same file, refusing a name that differs only in case on a case-sensitive disk and a folder form of the stylesheet before anything is written; builds a source named through a folder link under its own path; says in JSON what the app copy write did (`appCopy`, `appCopyStale`); names the Fontsource package for an editor theme's fonts. Every suggested compile passes the same checks before it is shown. Fonts follow every family the build writes, a part's own font included. A module that imports a file beside the theme keeps the app copy as it was and says why. A change of mode on a theme the app lists names `theme add`.

`astryx experimental theme compile`: a compile or `--check` of an editor theme whose source no longer imports or extends its settings, or names another theme, is refused with the same message `set` gives, so it never writes another theme's files or drops every setting. The app copy's font stylesheet imports the installed `@fontsource` package of every family the built theme uses, the theme's own source included, and compile's note on fonts named but not loaded follows it. A theme build counts the families the theme's own font stylesheet beside its source loads (the app copy's), so a build of the copy's source no longer names them as unloaded. A blank or whitespace-only `--out` is refused.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a part word matches only as a word of its own, never as one half of a hyphenated compound, so "field-service app: large bold text, thick borders" is the whole theme's ask, not the inputs'.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: the contrast check reads gradients, and `how` reads side nav section headings as the sections.
changesets.body:
- Text on a gradient background is measured against each of its color stops, the worst one counting; a background with an image, or a stop with no fixed color, is listed as not checked.
- `how` reads "sidebar section headings" as the side nav's sections, whose title is drawn inside them, and says which inner parts an inherited text property also reaches.
- `how <part>` says what the part is, from its component's doc.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: the contrast check measures what draws the text. A toast's text on Core's media surface reads the on-dark or on-light color, so a low one is a problem with a fix that sets it; a color given as a theme token (`var(--token)`) is measured as that token's value in each mode; and text on different parts is a problem for each part, so following one fix line no longer turns up the others as new.

`astryx experimental theme editor` fixes contrast problems at their source: a whole-theme text color too faint in many places gets one line on that token, the nearest color that reads everywhere it was too faint, instead of one line per part; a pale status or accent fill gets the nearest darker color that stands out from the page as its line; and a failure the base theme draws itself is said by `show`, not after every change.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: every contrast problem is listed in the JSON (`newProblems`, `openProblems`, `problems`); the text shows the first eight and counts the rest. A change's new problems are the ones the settings before it, read as the change reads them, did not have, so a base or part saved in other letters no longer loses the check or lists old problems as new. A fix line sets what draws the text: a plain `color` that wins over a token, else the text token, scoped to the variant the text is drawn in, so following it clears the problem; text written straight in a part with its own `color` is measured against the part's fill. `show` says a saved base in other letters reads as the base; an entry with a thing and no value gets its `undo` line; a dial name in other letters (`Corners`, `MODE`) is the dial; a theme typo on a step back with nothing to undo offers `show`; and `new`'s set repair for a theme it did not make follows its `new` line as the next step.
`astryx experimental theme editor` contrast checks judge what the page draws, and every fix line fixes its problem without making another:
changesets.body:
- A fix line keeps the scope of the change it answers: after a setting with `--only`, its line carries `--only`, so following it changes the part named alone.
- The text typed in an input (its value, or its placeholder) is measured on the input's fill like any other text, with a fix line.
- Text that sits on a part whose variants draw different grounds (a heading on the app's header) is measured on each variant's ground, and its fix line names that variant, so a fix for one leaves the others readable. A new problem on another ground is named as new.
- A base theme's own text color on a part (butter's nav item) is what is measured, before a text token set on the part around it; a line that would change nothing on the page is not offered, and a problem no single line can fix (the same text on grounds that need opposite colors) shows with no line.
- `show`'s `missed` list offers only lines set takes: a part whose filled variants set cannot name is left out, never given a question.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: the source, descriptor and font stylesheet of a theme's app copy (`src/themes/<theme>/`) name the exact command that writes them in their first comment, `astryx experimental theme editor show <theme>`, so a missing or stale copy is fixed with that command; the built `.css`, `.js` and `.d.ts` keep the build's header.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> corners <value>` now gives `--radius-chat` back to the container radius (`var(--radius-container)`, Core's own default), so chat surfaces (the composer, its drawer, message bubbles) follow the theme's corners instead of keeping the chat radius the base theme pins (28px on most bundled themes).

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `corners rounded` is offered the `round` rung first, as the English word says, then Tailwind's 4px: on most bases 4px alone is sharper than the corners already are.

`astryx experimental theme`: a font family name is read as CSS reads it, so an escaped name (`Gill\ Sans`, `"\5FAE\8F6F\96C5\9ED1"`) is a family, never a font file. A family the theme holds in its own property and reads with `var()` counts as a family it builds: the app copy loads its installed package and compile names it until then. `compile` gives the note `show` gives when the theme's own type tokens do not show on phones, and that note's fix for a weight is a rule for the same screens, which keeps it. The full report of an editor theme wires its app copy (`theme add`), not its editor folder.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the sample card's buttons wrap to a second row when a theme's buttons are wider than the card (butter's and matcha's padding, a bolder weight, roomier spacing or a larger text size), so the preview never cuts their labels short. With `--png`, text the sample page's pictures still draw cut short (a label that ends in an ellipsis or runs past the edge of a box that clips it, such as badges at a large text size) is measured in the page by the browser that takes the picture and named in `set`'s and `show`'s results, as a note and as a problem. The problem's fix line is `flex-shrink 0` on the part, offered only when the browser measured it drawing every label whole; otherwise it says that line does not. A theme whose pictures cut nothing short says nothing.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a settings entry whose mode is written in other words (`Dark`, `night`, `Light`, `day`) is read as dark or light, and one whose source is written in other letters (`Dial`) or missing is read from the thing (a dial, a `--` token, a part property). A note says how each was read, and the next change saves it that way, so no command is blocked. An entry whose mode or source means nothing is refused with the undo that removes only that entry first, and the step back, which loses the last change, second. When a theme name is typed as a path (`./t`, `themes/t`), the `set`, `undo` and `compile` with the theme's name is checked by that command before it is offered, with every repair in the one line; an `--out` outside the working folder is dropped, and the reason says why.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: "the today date in the date picker" says why nothing is written in one line (the date picker's calendar is the plain Calendar, drawn in the layer it opens, so a change there reaches every calendar) and names the line that changes every calendar's today day instead. `set` with a CSS property and no `--on`, given a value labeled with a part (`'card: #eeeeee'`), offers that value on that part.

The agent block and the theme docs send a denser or roomier app to the theme (`astryx experimental theme editor set <name> spacing tight`, or `roomy`), as they send colors, instead of gap and padding changes page by page.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: heading colors, the page background, gradients per mode, and background values with many variables.
changesets.body:
- `color … --on heading` (also per level with `--when level:N`) is written as the text color tokens the heading's color prop reads, on headings only, so it shows; `how` answers "headings in the accent color" with it.
- The page behind your parts is painted by `app-shell`: `--on page` (or `body`) is refused with the `app-shell` command, and `how "page background"` offers `--color-background-body` for a color and `background … --on app-shell` for a color or a gradient. Setting `--color-background-body` no longer says it changes nothing where Core's own page styles read it.
- A gradient background can differ between light and dark: `background '<gradient>' --mode dark` paints each of its colors in that mode only, beside the other mode's layers.
- A background value with more than three variables (`color-mix()` with `var()` and a stop position, layered dots) is read as CSS, as the same value with plain colors is.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor` notes a destructive button a person cannot tell from the primary one (a pastel pink accent beside the soft salmon destructive fill: their fills close in OKLab), with the line that draws the destructive button in the theme's danger color. It is a note, not a problem: it fails no contrast.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: what it is given is read as meant and checked.
changesets.body:
- A dial typed as a flag (`set <theme> --corners round`) is refused as a dial typed with dashes and offered as the dial (`set <theme> corners round`), never an empty token list.
- A token value your `<theme>.theme.ts` gives that `set` refuses (`'--radius-page': 'banana'`) is checked by the same rules: `show`, `set` and `compile` refuse it, naming the token and its line, before anything is built.
- The theme typed as its module name (`brandTheme`) is the theme `brand`, never a second theme.
- A light and a dark color on a part's color (`background 'light: #fff; dark: #000' --on card`) is written as that property's `light-dark()` pair.
- A JSON object of settings passed to `set` gives one set line per entry.
- A font stack with escaped quotes (`\"Inter\", sans-serif`) is read as the stack.
- A state a part lists in camelCase (toggle-button's `isPressed`) is taken in any spelling, and `pressed` suggests it.
- A `mode` or `base` entry inside the settings list is named by `show` as doing nothing there, with the `undo` that removes it.
- A pasted line with two declarations (`accent: red; text-size: 18`) sets the first and says the second was not set, with its own set line.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a dial whose number is in pixels takes that number typed with its unit, in any letters and with a space before it, so `set t text-size 24px` sets 24 as `set t text-size 24` does; undo, `new --text-size` and a saved `20px` read it the same way. A size past the dial's range is refused naming the value as typed.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the part data records what a divider's line paints (its color per variant and its thickness) as the divider's own, so `how` makes a divider fainter, thinner or darker through the color and width its line reads, and thinner or thicker steps from the thickness it shows now.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: an icon read as the element of a place ("the chevron in selects", "the close icon in dialogs") takes its color, never a box behind it; a part said right before its separators ("the dropdown separators", "the context menu separators") owns them; an element after, before or next to a part's text ("the icon after the button text") is that part's.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- An element named in, of or after a part ("the checked indicator in checkboxes", "the indicator in selects", "the knob of switches", "the tabs' indicator", "the hovered item in menus in cards", "today's date in the calendar", "the highlighted option in the selector") is the part that place draws it as: the place itself by its name, a part named after it, a lexicon phrase said owner first, a part drawn inside it, or the one whose own state the words name, never the place or every element in it. "The buttons' icons" are the icon tokens on the buttons.
- An element its place has no part of its own for ("the close button of toasts", "the hovered item in the context menu", "the today date in the date picker", whose calendar the part data draws closed) writes nothing, and the answer says why.
- A state read from the part and not said ("the dot in radios") is let go when the element has none.
- "The checked and disabled checkbox" is the box in both states at once, in the part's own order; `--state isPressed+hover` on a toggle button is taken (Core marks isPressed with aria-pressed); "highlighted" names the highlighted state.
- What a line inside a part draws is each part on its element (a dropdown menu's own divider draws its separators), and a part whose paint is a line takes the divider answers: "the menu separators red" is `--color-border` on the menu's own divider, those separators only. PART_DATA_VERSION 24.
- A token a variant never reads is refused with a line that keeps the state and the mode asked.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: the input cleanup follows through. Quotes are mapped only where they delimit a value (curly quotes of one kind in any shape, such as „Inter“ or ‚Inter‘, «», ‹›, full-width quotes and backticks around a font name become straight ones, and a curly quote left unpaired is the straight one it stands for), and a quoted CSS string keeps what it holds, curly quotes, no-break spaces and a `;` included; a saved value is checked the same way, and quotes around a value are named as such. An entry pasted from JSON (`"accent": "#e11d48"`, `{"accent": "#e11d48"}`) or with copy debris (a trailing comma, a stray quote or bracket, a leading `=` or `:`, a second declaration after a `;` outside quotes) is read as the value; a quoted dial value suggests that value; a dash-like character inside a token name is its hyphen; `textSize` and `text_size` are text-size. A font stack is read as families: a trailing comma is dropped, a stack wrapped in one more pair of quotes is unwrapped, and an empty family is refused. `--mode` is cleaned like a value, and a near typo keeps `--mode` in the suggestion. A saved dial value with stray spaces, quotes, other letters or a pasted `corners: pill` is offered cleaned, read by the same input cleanup as typed values; a theme folder holding only empty folders counts as empty for `new`; a mistyped theme name in set or undo (`T`, `themes/t`, `./t`) suggests the same command with the theme's name.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: an exact amount ("half", "double", "a quarter", "a third", "3 times", "25% bigger") of a part's font size, line height, letter spacing, opacity, width or border width is that factor of what the part has now, never a fixed step; "3 times bigger" is an amount, never a 3px value; "double the border width" doubles it (no double-line style, no width cap); "half as round" scales the radius there now; a quarter of a padding or gap with nothing to read is a step down, said to be a step; a group's own name ("checks") is read as that group; an amount with a state ("on hover") scales that state's value and keeps the state; a dialog's header is the dialog header, not the app's top bar (likewise a card's or a dialog's footer); and the part "everything except cards" leaves out keeps the value it has now.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: input readers keep what was typed.
changesets.body:
- A family the editor does not know that is near a generic or a preset (`Inder`, `Monaspace`, `Serifa`) is offered the near name and the family as typed in quotes, which keeps it as written; never only another font.
- A comma between two bare numbers that a property pairs with a slash (`aspect-ratio 16,9`) separates them: `16 / 9`, never `16.9`.
- A saved entry whose thing differs in case or spacing, or whose value is a number, and a saved font value set repairs (`Inter 16px`), are offered set's repair beside the undo.
- A base reads in any of its names (`neutral-theme`, `neutralTheme`, `neutral theme`, its package) in set, new and the settings file alike.
- A list item that is only weight, style or size words (`Inter, bold`) is no family: refused with the families and the weight or size line.
- A JSON entry's string quotes are JSON's, for a font list too (`{"font": "Inter, serif"}`).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor` and `compile`: the families a part's `font` shorthand in your `<theme>.theme.ts` names last get the family check `fontFamily` gets (a comma missing before a generic family, a quoted generic), refused with the file and line.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a weight word at the end of a font family's name is part of the name (`Arial Black`, `Archivo Black`, `Segoe UI Semibold` are taken as typed) unless the whole name is no family the editor knows and the name without the word is (`Inter ExtraBold` is Inter and a weight); a weight number (`Inter 600`) is never part of a name. The Segoe UI weights Windows ships as families of their own are on the system font list.
`astryx experimental theme …`: settings reach the build, and fonts load as the theme shows them.
changesets.body:
- A theme source that spreads the `defineTheme` result and replaces its `components` (`{...defineTheme(…), components: {}}`) is refused by name, as one that replaces its tokens is: a part setting would be saved and never built. Give your own components inside `defineTheme({…, components: {…}})` instead.
- Italic text (`font-style: italic`, or `italic` in a `font` shorthand) loads the installed package's italic stylesheets beside the upright ones (`400-italic.css`, a variable package's `wght-italic.css`), so the browser no longer draws a slanted copy.
- Noto Sans, Noto Serif and Noto Sans Mono are named system fonts of Android, ChromeOS and Linux, and Cantarell, Ubuntu and Ubuntu Mono system fonts of Linux, so a system font stack that names them is not told it needs a package.
- A heading weight given with no type scale is offered `editor set <theme> headings <weight>`, which changes only the heading weight. The hint no longer says to add a type scale, which would also resize all text. A weight number outside 1 to 1000 is no longer echoed as the example.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme …`: the settings file and pasted forms are read as typed input. A saved setting whose `on`, `when` or `state` is not text (`"when": 5`, `"on": {}`), or whose part is empty, no longer makes every command fail: it is refused as a damaged setting with an undo line that removes it. A set of headings replaces a saved headings entry whose axis names no half, so later commands work. A saved base written `None` (in any letters) is no base, and the file's own field names in other letters (`Like`, `Settings`, `Mode`) are those fields. A pasted entry's field spelled as its flag (`"--on": "card"`) is that field, and a pasted change line with the `→` arrow, a label before its colon, or a label and colon with no old value keeps the label as the mode. An empty pasted object points to the dials and the help. `undo t 'accent red'` reads the setting and its value as set does. A swapped setting and value whose setting is misspelled (`set t pill cornres`) gets the swap line.

`astryx experimental theme editor …`: for a setting the settings file lists twice by hand, undo accepts either value it holds (`undo t accent red` or `blue`), removes every entry, and its result names each value removed (`alsoRemoved` in `--json`); a value it does not hold is refused naming the one the build reads. `show` notes a field the settings file writes twice (`like` and `Like`), as a change does. A token name whose word is a part the editor knows (`--color-text-link`) is no longer repaired by spelling to another token (`--color-text-pink`).

`astryx experimental theme editor …`: a saved twin of a setting in other letters (`accent` and `Accent`, `--color-accent` and `--Color-Accent`, `background-color` and `Background-Color` on a part) is that setting listed twice, which a set or undo of it fixes, instead of a refusal saying `Accent` is no dial. A field a saved setting writes several ways, none of them the editor's (`On` and `--on`, `thing` and `setting`), is read once from the first, with a note, and the next change writes it once. A saved field the editor does not read (`modes`) is named, with the field it is a typo of. An entry pasted in the saved form without a value (`undo t '{"thing":"padding","on":"card"}'`) is read by its thing.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a radio's circle (a part with a checked state, a square box and corners at 50%) is no corner. The corners dial on its group leaves it, in the build as in `show`; the dial on the radio alone is refused (it changes nothing you see) with the line that does set its shape (`set <theme> border-radius 0 --on radio-indicator --only`); `how` offers that line for "make radios square" and answers "rounder checkboxes" with the checkbox alone.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: "focus ring color like the links" (or "the same as", "match") sets the focus ring's color from that part's own color token, theme-wide unless a part is named before it, instead of a ring width on that part. An amount of padding on a part with no padding to take it of says the answer is one step, not an exact amount.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a family whose last word the editor knows as itself (`Inter Tight`) is no weight typo and is kept; a misspelled style word (`Inter Bold Itallic`) is answered as the exact words are; any weight number after a known family (`Inter 650`, `Inter 6OO`) is read as a weight; and a value holding `NaN` or `undefined` is refused at set, naming the value, never left to fail the build.

`astryx experimental theme editor set … font`: a number after a family the editor knows is read as CSS reads it, a weight from 1 to 1000 (`Inter 450.5`, `Inter 50`) and any other number no family (`Inter 1500`), never saved as a family of that name; a word with another first letter is no typo of a weight word (`Inter Night`, `Inter Right` are kept); and a font role in other letters (`--on Body`) is answered as that role, never as the app shell.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> font`: a family no package loads is named with the install line of the Fontsource package its name maps to (such as `@fontsource/press-start-2p` for Press Start 2P); once installed, the previews and the app copy load it like any font package.

`astryx experimental theme editor set … font`: a weight or style word typed with a typo after a family the editor knows (`Georgia Blod`, `Inter semibld`, `Courier New Itallic`) is read as that word and refused with the family and weight lines and the name kept as typed, never saved as a family of that name. A typo of a font preset inside a list (`Robto, sans-serif`) is read as the preset, as it is alone.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the font dial reads every weight or style word after a family, each through the one typo limit (`Inter Bold Itallic`, `Inter Tihn`), and offers the family and headings lines for them as for the exact words. A `new` refused for its name keeps the repair of a font the font readers refuse (`--font roboto` for `--font Robto`). The note on a family near a system font with a weight word (`Arail Bold`) names lines set takes: the family, and the headings weight.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: fonts Apple ships on iPhone and iPad as well as the Mac (Apple Color Emoji, Helvetica Neue, PingFang, Hiragino Sans, Avenir Next, Futura and others), and `-apple-system`, are noted as shipping only on Apple platforms (macOS, iOS and iPadOS), not only on macOS. Mac-only fonts (Monaco, Lucida Grande, Geneva, `BlinkMacSystemFont` and others) are still noted as macOS only.
changesets.body: A comma before three digits on a millisecond time (`transition-duration '1,000ms'`) is a thousands mark, as on a pixel length, so the repair is `1000ms`, not `1.000ms`. On rem, em and seconds it stays a decimal point (`1,125rem` is `1.125rem`).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`: a font family maps to its Fontsource package as Fontsource names it: a `<Name> Variable` family to `@fontsource-variable/<name>`, which loads it once installed, and other characters dropped (`Mrs. Sheppards` is `@fontsource/mrs-sheppards`). No package is suggested for a font a system ships on any platform (such as Microsoft YaHei or PingFang SC) or a name Fontsource cannot publish. An installed font package loads every weight the theme uses (a stylesheet per weight, as Fontsource ships them), in the app copy and the previews. The font dial takes a CSS-escaped family, as tokens do. `compile --check` names a missing output in its check result.
`astryx experimental theme`:
changesets.body:
- `editor show`'s `missed` list frames only what draws a box: a part with no filled box at rest in any variant (a ghost toggle button, a menu row) is borderless on purpose, and with the border width at zero nothing is missed for want of a border.
- `preview app`'s font note names only weight sheets a Fontsource package can have: a weight between two hundreds (650) is drawn from the two around it.
- `preview app` refuses a theme that imports a Sass, Less or Stylus file, which the new app does not build, naming the import, before writing anything.
- `preview app` names an entry called node_modules or a version-control folder as left out whether it is a folder, a file or a link, and the note on a link says to copy what it leads to.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a color or timing function typed with commas and no spaces (`rgb(255,0,0);`, `hsl(210,50%,40%) !important`, `cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1);`) keeps its repair line: a comma is read as a number mark only outside parentheses. `font 'Inter ExtraBold'` offers `font Inter` and `headings heavy`, the rung nearest the weight in any form the weight table reads.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a hand-edited settings entry the editor refuses is offered only commands that unlock the theme. A `headings` value saved with no axis is its weight half, so `set <theme> headings <weight>` or `undo <theme> headings` replaces or removes it; a `mode` or `base` entry put in the settings list is removed by `undo <theme> mode` (or `base`), and no `set` line is offered for it (those set the theme's own mode and base).

`astryx experimental theme editor`: one reader takes every settings file and undo step. A null or other non-object entry gets the file refusal, never a crash, and the step back it names works. A damaged mode or base is read as meant by a change and recorded that way in the undo step, so undo works and the history is kept; `like: "none"` is no base. The folder names the theme: a missing or changed `name` in the file is the folder's. A headings value under the wrong half, an unknown half, or a half on another dial is refused with the undo that works, and a half listed twice offers `set <theme> headings <word>` lines that work. A dial listed twice by hand: set names every entry it replaces. A part in other letters or misspelt with `--only` gets the command on that part, `--only` kept. A did-you-mean follows the one typo rule (nothing for one to three letters). The theme-name rule, dashes included, is stated from one text in every refusal and in `new`'s help. `more` or `less` at a dial's last step is refused with the other way. A built-in theme that is not installed is offered with its install line first. A value saved in another form (corners in rem, a fractional text-size) leaves the build current for `compile --check`. `preview <word>` leads with a subcommand the word is a typo of, and offers a theme's pages only for a theme here.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: text of a part that sits in the app's top bar is checked over the header's background. A part with a see-through background of its own (a segmented control's track, a ghost button, a top nav item) shows the header through it, so a dark header now warns when those labels do not read on it, including the light/dark/system switch the in-app preview puts in its top bar, which looks the same in an app.
`astryx experimental theme editor how` holds its answers to what the theme shows now:

An experimental theme command with more than three examples opens its `--help` with "Start here:" and its first three examples, before the options, so the first step is visible without reading every option. The full "Examples:" section stays after the options, as in every command's help.
`astryx experimental theme editor how` now reads these asks the way they are said:
changesets.body:
- **Amounts with a softening word go the right way:** "three times as soft" is a third of now and "half as soft" is twice as strong. "Corners half as small" makes them twice the size.
- **"Exactly 36px high"** is a height of 36px.
- **"…and the text bigger"** changes the theme's text, not the part named before it.
- **A border color on a part** keeps only the colors Core gives a status or focus. It no longer pins every variant back to its old color, so the new color shows on every variant.
- **A part made more transparent or fainter** moves from what it shows now: a disabled button's 0.5 opacity goes lower, never higher. Each variant's fill fades from its own color, in the state asked, and the part never gets a line it does not draw.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` checks every command it suggests against the question: the command must make the kind of change the words ask for (a color for a color ask, a radius for a corner ask, padding or a size for a size ask, a border width, a weight, an opacity or a shadow), move the way they say from the value there now, and reach none or 0 for a removal. A command that does not is left out, and the answer says plainly what it could not work out; a value you typed is always taken as given.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` says what it writes. The words an answer repeats no longer end on a bare "when" once a state is read, and part names take their plural ("switches", never "switchs"); a keep said first ("keep the switches and the background …") ends at a whole verb. A color said as how something looks now ("too bright blue", "is still gray") is never written as the value, and a color said against the one it replaces ("navy, not bright blue") is one ask with no line about the other. Two parts listed with a word describing the second ("the info banner and draft badge") share the ask. A near color off a pure one ("never pure white") takes the theme's own neutral. A one-line look keeps its page, text and font ("green text on black, monospace"), and "text on black" reads the color under the text as the page.
`astryx experimental theme editor how`:
changesets.body:
- An app's own pasted CSS variables (`--brand-primary`, `--brand-bg`…) are read by the role their name ends in. "<color> text on a <color> page" sets the text and the page separately.
- "luxury fashion brand: black and ivory" no longer reads black as the accent. On a dark-only theme, the page color takes no mode.
