A typo of a family with a weight or style word after it is read by the same font rule as the typo alone: `Georiga Bold` is refused with georgia and `headings bold`; `Arail Black`, near a font a system ships only, is kept as typed with the note.

`astryx experimental theme editor` measures a button color that also paints the toast's close button on the toast's own fill, and says plainly that no setting keeps the toast's buttons apart, with the nearest button color that reads on every toast fill and on the page when one does. Text on a pane the theme painted (a side nav's fill) is measured on that pane, and the same text shown on another pane that holds it unpainted (the mobile nav drawer) is fixed by painting that pane like the other, not by recoloring the text everywhere. Text drawn on a fill its part draws only in a state (a selected item) is fixed with a line for that state, which `set` accepts and which ends the problem. An inverted surface whose theme counterpart looks the same as the base's (the same side, nearly the same lightness) is no longer listed under missed. A radius setting on a part whose radius your own theme source sets now says the source wins there, as a padding setting does. Where the base theme's own border is a hairline, a theme's border token is a problem only when it draws nothing on the page at all.

`astryx experimental theme editor set`: what a whole-theme change leaves out (`leftOut` in JSON) comes right under the status line, each part with its own runnable line. A border width names, and the "thick borders on everything" answer reaches, every part that draws a fixed line of its own (a secondary button's edge) or frames a surface (a banner) beside the containers, menus and overlays; only rules count as dividers, never the edge of a cornered box such as a list row or a button.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a line offered when the theme is left out keeps every option typed (`--on`, `--state`, `--mode`, `--only`, `--like`, `--section`), so following it changes what was asked, never the whole theme. `undo` reads the words after the thing as one value, typed unquoted as `set` takes it (`undo t padding 4px 8px --on card`). With the theme left out, `undo` reads the scope in every spelling it takes with the theme typed (`--state focusVisible`, `--on Card`, `--mode Dark`) and offers the undo on the theme that holds it. A token typed where the theme goes (`show --color-accent`) is never a theme to make. A settings file whose list is written `"Settings"` is a theme that exists to `new`, never made again; written beside `"settings"`, the two are read as one list, the editor's entry winning where both set one thing, and the change says so.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a whole-theme change names the parts it leaves out, with the line that reaches them: `set corners square` names the parts drawn as pills (badge, switch, calendar day…), which `--radius-full 0px` squares; `set --border-width` names the surfaces it does not reach (dialog, popover, menus, tooltip, toast…) and the dividers it thickens. The "thick borders on everything" answer gives a border to every surface the shared border width does not widen, the overlays that draw a fixed line of their own included, and keeps each divider at its own width.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a list value with one item misspelled, for a dial that takes each word alone (`set t headings 'blod tight'`), gets a line for each word, as each word alone does; and `undo` reads three or more bare words as a list of settings only when every word names a setting, so `undo t font Inter Tight` is a setting and its value again.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a setting listed twice by hand now changes the last entry, the one the build reads, so "keep pill" saves and builds pill. A damaged mode or base written in other letters or as a package name (`Dark-Only`, `Neutral`, `@astryxdesign/theme-neutral`) is fixed first by the suggestions, and a change to another setting cleans it to the value meant instead of resetting it. A stored vibrancy of `0.5` is offered as 50. `new` cleans each flag value the way `set` does, so `--font '«Georgia»'` saves `"Georgia"`. `--on "text inputs"` and `--on "dialog header"` name text-input and dialog-header, and `--when Variant:Primary` or `variant=primary` gets the corrected command. An app copy the editor wrote, left without its `themes/<name>/` folder, is named as the editor's with `new <name>` to make it again. Names copied from the app (`tTheme`, `tTheme.ts`, `brand.theme.ts`, `themes//t`, `BrandDark`, `Brand Dark`) reach the theme they name, and `new` says when it is here already. The note after Ctrl-C says what `undo` or `new` saved, with the project's own CLI command. An undo of padding in the other form (a side or the shorthand) suggests the undo that matches what is saved.

`astryx experimental theme`: a font role the theme builds as one family with no fallback at all (headings set to `Lora` alone: an exact font token, or a heading family with no fallbacks of its own in the theme's source, which Core builds as just that family) is noted by `set`, `show` and `compile`: that text has no font while the family loads or if it is missing, with the way to give it a list: the setting run again with a list, or the fallbacks to add in the theme's source.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the pictures to open are named where they are read. A change with `--png` says in its `see` line to open preview.png (the sample page) and sheet-overlays.png (every menu, tooltip, popover and list, drawn open); without `--png` it still names the pages. `show --png` says it on its first line and its last (`look`, also in the JSON), so a head or a tail of the output keeps it.
The response types reference says `astryx experimental theme editor show` leaves `look` out when no picture was taken, as the result does, instead of returning it as null.

`astryx experimental theme editor set`: a page background set on the app shell no longer makes the main content area see-through over a background a setting gives it, whichever was set first. `how`'s page-color line for the main panel now changes what the panel draws.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `new` reads more of what is typed after the name as settings, never name words: the base in the key forms (`like=neutral`, `like: neutral`), a value before its dial (`red accent`), a quoted pair or list (`'accent red, corners pill'`), a dial word with no value, and a word typed after an option's value that no reading takes (`--accent red foo` keeps `--accent red`; `--corners pill padding 8px` keeps `--corners pill` and offers `set … padding 8px`). Settings typed where the name goes (`new 'accent: red'`) stay on the free name offered, and two bases in one `--like` (`neutral,stone`) give the first built-in one. `like`, the word `show` prints for the base, points to `set <theme> base` / `undo <theme> base`. The theme typed as an option (`set --theme t accent red`) gets `set t accent red`, and a line set does not read is never offered as working. A theme with a setting pasted on (`show t=accent`) and a list of values where the theme goes (`show 'Inter, Arial'`) get a look at the theme, never a new one. A whole command pasted as one word (`set 'set t accent red'`) is read as that command. An undo by a held value with a scope typed (`undo t 8px --on cards`) leads with the setting in that scope.
`astryx experimental theme editor how` measures more asks the way they are meant:

`astryx experimental theme editor` contrast checks measure a part with a fill of its own on Core's media surface (a button on an overlay's dark island) with the text color that surface gives it, so a glossy light button whose label turns white there is listed as a problem, with a fix that sets the button's own color (its variant), which reaches it on the surface and reads on its fill everywhere. A label on its part's own fill is measured on the fill its variant draws.

`astryx experimental theme editor`'s lines for text on Core's media surfaces end the problems they name: a part drawn with its default props is measured and fixed as the variant Core draws it as; text on a lightbox's own on-color bar takes that on-color on the lightbox, which `set` accepts; a light overlay that turns the lightbox's text and its bar opposite ways is offered the overlay back; and a text token refused on a lightbox points to the on-color that reaches it. A link of yours at a page's name (the sample page, the sheets) or at the record of pictures is left alone and named, as `show --help` says, instead of refusing the command.

`astryx experimental theme editor`'s contrast checks measure a part inside Core's media surface (a button on a lightbox's dark island) as that surface draws it, in its own scheme whatever the page's mode: an untouched base ships no problem there, and a light-only color on the page's part makes none. A problem there is listed once, and its fix is a color in the surface's scheme, which reaches it; when the part lets the surface's ground through and the same text on the page needs the other color, no line is offered, so following the fixes never cycles.

`astryx experimental theme editor show` draws the parts it shows open as a desktop window of the pictures' own size lays them out: a width or height media query is answered for that window, so AlertDialog's buttons sit side by side in the open states picture instead of in its phone layout.
`astryx experimental theme editor show`'s `missed` list names what keeps the base's look beside the theme's own, and each line changes the built theme:
changesets.body:
- A tooltip or toast still on the base's dark inverted surface once the theme's own surfaces changed (a grey Win98-like theme) is listed, with a line that gives it the theme's surface in each mode the theme draws and readable text on it.
- A soft shadow beside square corners or a theme border (a popover's, a menu's, a dialog's) is listed, with a line that takes its blur away.
- A status fill (a banner's, a badge's status variants) is listed only where its dial builds a color of its own (the theme's vibrancy moved); at the base's vibrancy the dial gives the base's own color back.
- `how`'s answer for a part on that list (`how "make the tooltips match the theme"`) leads with the same line.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor` reports what a theme's own changes did not reach where it applies: `new` with a color or dial counts and names the parts it missed as `set` does (`missed`, `missedParts`, and the new `missedOn` in JSON), every change names the parts it missed rather than only counting them, and a base theme square by design is no longer told its soft shadows sit beside square corners it did not choose. `show --section <family>` pictures that family first, with its parts drawn open after it, not the overlays.

`astryx experimental theme editor` gives a missed part one line where one setting reaches it: a toast's text picks its own side from its fill, so its surface alone is the line. Where a line takes two settings (a tooltip's surface, then its text), the problem the first step leaves says that the next step of that line clears it, and names the step. An error toast's line for the danger color takes the text that reads on the new red where the toast's own pick would not, so following it makes no problem.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- `show` and `set` count the missed list as misses on parts (a part can miss two ways, its border and its shadow), and `show`'s line under the six it lists counts the rest as misses, apart from the parts whose fill or text color is only still the base's. The JSON of a change adds `missedParts`.
- The sheet, the preview and the pictures draw an auto media surface inside a part with a fill of its own (a toast with a light background) on the side the app's measurement picks, so its text reads as it does in the app.
- Text drawn in a disabled color (an inactive segment) is held to no 4.5:1 contrast, and no fix whitens it.
- `set`'s note on a border width offers the frames `show`'s missed list has: only parts that draw a box, scoped to the variants that do, and none at a width of zero.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a mistyped part (`nmber-input`) is read as the whole part name it is a typo of, never a group one word of it names, and a did-you-mean follows the one typo limit (a name that only holds the typed word inside it is none). A boolean option written with a value (`--only=true`, `--png=false`, `--only false`) gets the same reading in set, undo, new, how and show: the option takes no value, with the command that works. A dial and its value in the other order (`set t round corners`) lead with the set in the right order, and a theme typed last is offered first only in a line that works. undo names every entry of a setting listed twice by hand that it removes. A bad entry beside a good one of the same setting is named as listed twice, so its keep line keeps the good one, and a keep line whose value set refuses is not offered. A dial word saved in other letters (`Pill`) is that word, and a headings word saved under the other half is filed under its own. `only` on a setting that is no group member is refused with the undo of that entry. show writes a deleted palette.config.json again. A settings file that cannot be read is made again on the base it was built on, and `new --like` reads a base in any case.

`astryx experimental theme editor set`: a page or text color typed as a CSS property with no part (`set t background '#0f172a'`) is offered for the mode it reads in first (`--color-background-body '#0f172a' --mode dark`), with the both-modes line after it, so the suggestion does not leave the other mode unreadable; a color that reads in both modes is offered once, as before. The words people write for a dial reach it: a name with `-color` or `-colour` after it (`primary-color`, `brand-color`), a plural (`shadows`), and `shadows none` / `dark-mode true` / `light-mode true`, which name the dial and the value that does it (`surfaces flat`, `mode dark-only`).
`astryx experimental theme editor`: a color for one mode on a part is written in the part's block for that mode.
changesets.body:
- In the other mode the theme writes nothing there, so what Core and the base theme give the part in context stays as it was: the current page in Pagination, a text field's error, warning and success borders.
- A one-mode color in a state is accepted on a part that has no color of its own in that state; the other mode keeps Core's.
- A one-mode gradient goes into the part's block for that mode as its image layers (and a color layer as that mode's color), so the other mode keeps Core's own images, such as a button's hover tint.
- A one-mode background on an app shell region leaves the page background painting it in the other mode.
- A one-mode color in a state is accepted on every member of a group, and an exception kept in a state (inputs darker except when focused) keeps that state's own fill in each mode.
- The part data records a background a part inherits (`inherit`) as no paint of its own.
- The result lists each property a change writes inside a mode block, under its path (`@dark :hover`).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- A border in one mode on a part that draws none is a ring at its edge (an inset box-shadow) that takes no room, so the other mode keeps its size; where the part draws a shadow of its own, the answer says why it cannot.
- Outlined buttons in one mode keep the outline dial beside the one-mode colors, and say the dial is the same in both modes.
- A divider's line is reached per variant: its color (the strong divider's own token), its thickness by the amount said, and its removal. A fill on the divider's own element, or a token its variant does not read, is refused with the line that reaches it.
- A token family follows a source written as one `light-dark()` value or a token reference.
- A variant's low-contrast text is listed once, with a fix scoped to that variant.
- A part's border is no longer colored through parts inside it that draw no line (a toast's ghost buttons); a part with no border made thicker takes its own height.
- A state shadow that keeps Core's ring keeps each status's own ring there.
- Pieces named after a part's catalog name ("the checkbox check", "the select arrow") are those parts.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: one-mode colors per variant, the spacing dial around kept steps, and padding amounts from the base theme.
changesets.body:
- A one-mode color on a part whose variants each have their own is written to each variant as the property it names (a card's `border-color` stays a border color), with each variant's own other half: an earlier setting for the other mode or for both modes, else what the variant shows unset. `--mode` on a color longhand such as `background-color` or `border-color` is accepted this way.
- A hover set as `background-color` stays on every variant after a later one-mode `background`, and a one-mode background after a plain one applies to every variant in both modes.
- A whole-part state setting that your own `<theme>.theme.ts` sets on the same state is not repeated on the variants, so it does not show anywhere, as the result says.
- The spacing dial keeps spacing steps in order around an exact step the theme keeps, reads a kept control size written as a token, `clamp()`, `min()` or `max()`, and keeps a part's own exact control size in order under a whole-theme dial.
- `how` padding amounts read the base theme's own block and inline padding on a part ("double the button padding" on butter gives `1rem 2rem`).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: one-mode colors, kept sizes and own padding sides.
changesets.body:
- In a `light-only` or `dark-only` theme, a color you set (a token or a part's color) fills only that mode's half; the other half keeps the base theme's, so a lightbox, an overlay or a toast Core draws in the other mode stays readable. A setting saved for the theme's mode keeps its half when the theme turns one-mode.
- `mode both` after a one-mode theme says to take out a `mode` given to the app's `<Theme>` for it.
- The spacing dial keeps control sizes in order around an exact size the theme keeps (`--size-element-md 34px` with `spacing tight` gives a larger size above 34px).
- A padding your own `<theme>.theme.ts` sets on some sides of a part wins on those sides; the editor's padding still applies on the other sides, on every part, and the result says so. A physical side stays physical and a logical side logical, in each text direction: with your own `paddingLeft`, the editor's left is never written; with your own `paddingInlineStart`, the editor's `padding-left` shows only right to left (where the start is the right). A variant your own source pads wins over an editor padding on the part's plain rule, whatever sides that sets.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a `mode` or `base` entry a hand edit put in the settings list, where it does nothing, is listed by `show` only under a "misplaced" note, never as a setting; every change names it the same way, and every refusal leads with the `undo` that removes it.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: one-mode gradients and tokens keep the other mode, the page background in every AppShell, and heading colors and types.
changesets.body:
- A gradient for one mode is written as background images (typed as `background` too), so the other mode keeps its own background color; each mode's layers are kept by mode as they are written, so a fade to `transparent` is never lost. A gradient holding a `light-dark()` stop takes no `--mode`.
- A token set on a part for one mode (a heading color included, and any color in a one-mode theme) keeps the token's own value in the other mode.
- A one-mode `background` no longer removes the other mode's one-mode `background-color`.
- A background on `app-shell` shows in every AppShell variant: the shell's header and side nav take the same background (they stay opaque when content scrolls under them), its main content area is see-through, and the result says so.
- A heading color that names a text color token (`var(--color-text-secondary)`) is accepted; heading `--when type:` takes Heading's own types (display-1 to display-3).
- `how` offers a gradient for one mode as `background-image … --mode`, and a one-mode color under a part's own gradient says it does not show.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: one-mode colors in a variant or a state, gradient layers with a color, keywords with a mode, and the corners dial on parts with their own radius.
changesets.body:
- A one-mode color in a variant or a state (a heading level, a hover) keeps the theme's own value around it in the other mode: the variant's resting color, then the part's, then the whole theme's, as the theme finally has it. A later brand color reaches the other mode.
- In a one-mode background, a color written beside a gradient (`#f00 linear-gradient(…)`) is that mode's background color, and the gradient its image.
- A CSS-wide keyword (`unset`, `inherit`) takes no `--mode`; the offered command sets it for both modes.
- The corners dial reaches parts whose base theme gives them a radius of their own, and a corners step on a part starts from the radius the part shows.
- A one-mode color on a part says that, in the other mode, it overrides what Core or the base theme gives the part in context.
- `how` lists the margins a part reads among its spacing, as `set` reads them.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a mode word typed with a typo that keeps its letters (`drak`, `darkk`, `ligth`) is that mode wherever a person types one, by one reader: a pasted label in a `how` question (`drak: cards #1c1c1e` changes the dark cards only) or in a `set` value (`'drak: #eeeeee'` offers the `--mode dark` line) and the `--mode` flag. A word of its own (right, tight, bark) is never read as a mode.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a setting for one color mode that reaches the whole theme reads as one scope, "accent = red (whole theme, light mode only)", never "(whole theme) [light only]", which reads as two scopes at odds. A setting on a part keeps its mode mark as before.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: a one-mode write changes only its mode.
changesets.body:
- A token set for one mode keeps its other half as what that mode shows: Core's own reference when the base theme's value follows it (a focus ring that follows the accent), so it keeps following the theme's tokens.
- A one-mode page background on the app shell makes the main content area see-through, and a gradient fixed, in its mode only.
- A one-mode background shorthand replaces longhands set for its mode only; a longhand set for both modes stays.
- A light-only or dark-only theme keeps the other mode's settings for the regions Core draws in that mode (a toast, a lightbox), says so, and takes `--mode` for that mode; its own mode needs no `--mode`.
- A color on a link is refused for the token its color prop reads (`--color-text-accent` for a default link), set on the link.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor set`: defineTheme's motion knobs typed as a setting (`motion`, `tempo`, `character`) say the editor sets motion through the duration and ease tokens, and point to `how "faster motion"` and `how "slower motion"`, the slower first for a tempo above 1.

`astryx experimental theme editor set` and `undo`: `--when` takes several conditions, one per prop (a ghost small button: `--when variant:ghost --when size:sm`, or `--when variant:ghost+size:sm`), written as one rule for parts that have all of them, as Core's `prop:value+prop:value` keys are. Each is checked as one alone is, the same prop twice is refused, and the conditions are saved in one order, so an undo finds them whatever order they were typed in.

`astryx experimental theme editor new` reads a setting typed after the name in the pair form with its key in quotes (`'"like": "neutral"'`, `'"accent": "red"'`) or swapped (`red=accent`, `stone=like`), never as words of the name; the base word is never a value (`neutral=like` is `--like neutral`, never a gray tint). The name typed as an option (`--theme t2`, `--name t2`, `--theme=t2`) is that name, and the refusal says the option is none of new's.

`astryx experimental theme editor undo <theme> <word>` with no setting named never leads with a plain step back, which can take back another change than the one typed: a value one setting holds gets that setting's undo, a value several hold gets each one's, a word nothing holds gets a look at the theme (`show`), and only `all` or `last` offers the step back.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a settings entry's `only` written as text (`"false"`, `"true"`) is read as what it says, with a note, and any other value that is not true is refused with the undo that removes that entry, so `show` and the build never disagree. A theme typed after the setting (`set --color-accent '#123457' t`) is refused with the same `set` or `undo` with the theme first, never a `new` of the setting's name. `undo <theme> vibrancy` says the default vibrancy applies now. `new` with several bad dial flags suggests one command that fixes or drops each of them; `new --base` points to `--like`; `show` names a show that works and its help for an option it does not take. The name rule lists every reserved name it refuses (com0-com9, lpt0-lpt9, and com¹-com³, lpt¹-lpt³). corners takes a rem (saved in px), and a bare number gets the px line. Dial words are read in any case (ROOMY, MORE, BOTH). `set t 'corners pill'` is read as the thing and its value. With no theme named in an app with one theme, show and undo name that theme. The compile line in the result works from the folder the command ran in.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: names, damaged themes and stops.
changesets.body:
- A theme name typed as a path (`themes/brand`, `./t`, `t/`) names the theme it ends in, and says when that theme is here already; a typo of a theme name offers the nearest theme by spelling first (`brand-drak` is `brand-dark`, not `brand`), and a camelCase name is the dashed one (`brandDark` is `brand-dark`, `themePark` is `theme-park`), never a new theme.
- A refusal names a command that works: `undo` on a theme whose settings cannot be read and that has no history names `new <theme>`, not `show`; a damaged mode or base no longer sends each fix to the other (changing or removing a setting puts the field back to its default and says so); a settings entry with no thing or no source is damage `new` keeps aside, as the refusal says.
- A folder holding only `desktop.ini` is empty, like one holding only `Thumbs.db` or `.DS_Store`.
- An `undo` that switches the theme between one mode and both names the app's `<Theme mode>` to add or take out, as `set mode` does; `undo --help` says `--mode` removes a setting saved for one mode in a one-mode theme.
- Stopped (Ctrl-C) while the checks and pictures run after a change, the editor says the change is saved and built and that `show` runs the rest.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor` and `compile` name the real problem and the real place:
`astryx experimental theme editor`: `how` names the same states for a state a part lacks (a selected table row) as `set` and `how <part>` do: the states `set` takes there.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `set` with the theme left out and a value of several words (`set padding '4px 8px' --on card`, `set shadow '0 1px 2px red' --on card`) offers the set on the one theme here when set's check passes it, every option kept, never a theme named after the setting. `undo` never offers to make a theme from the word: a typo of a setting the theme holds (`undo acent`), a value it holds (`undo red`, `undo t red`), or a setting with its value in one word (`undo 'corners pill'`) gets that setting's undo, and a step back says which change it takes back; `show 'corners pill'` looks at the theme. A value with commas typed unquoted, as `set` takes it (`undo t font Inter, Arial`), is that setting's value, never a list. `new` reads a setting typed after the name (`new t2 accent red`, `corners=pill`, `corners: pill; accent: red`, a pasted JSON object) as its option, never part of the name, and a token typed for the name (`new --color-accent`) is never the name offered. An option typed before a nested group (`theme --mode dark editor set …`) goes after the command it names; an option whose value is a subcommand's name keeps it; and options with no subcommand at all (`preview --theme t`) name the subcommands that take them, never their value as a subcommand.

`astryx experimental theme editor undo` of a property the theme sets in another form of the same family on that part names it: `undo t background --on app-shell-header` with `background-color` set says "settings for background: background-color = #111827 on app-shell-header" and offers that undo, as it already did for padding and its sides.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a negated state (`--state unpressed`, `--state 'not pressed'`, `--state unchecked`) is read as the part at rest. The refusal offers the same line with no `--state`, instead of the state the word denies (`--state isPressed`), which saved the pressed look when the rest look was asked for.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a typo of a CSS keyword that starts with no- or not- (`cursor not-alowed`, `background-repeat no-repat`) is offered the keyword, as any typo is; a real negation (`cursor 'not pointer'`) is still never offered the word it negates.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> neutral <color>` now reaches the inverted surface tooltips and toasts draw on. As Core makes it from a neutral scale, it is the card surface of the other mode, from the neutral color's own shades and inside the ramp, so it carries the color in both modes (in dark, the shade next to white rather than white itself). The on-dark and on-light text takes the neutral shades the official theme maps them to. Before, a green-on-black theme kept Core's own pure white tooltip and toast.

`astryx experimental theme editor new` checks its color flags as setting those dials does: a pale accent that does not stand out from the page (or any other contrast check a color dial fails) is listed in its problems.

`astryx experimental theme`: a file, folder or link of yours at the open states page's name (sheet-overlays.html) is never written over by `--png`; the picture is not taken, and `set --png` and `show --png` alike say why. The open states picture shows each overlay at the height of what it holds, up to a window's height, and a dropdown menu's submenu opens with rows. `preview app --theme` refuses a theme image reached through a link that leads out of the theme folder, notes images of this app's public/ folder the new app lacks, adds each package the theme's own source imports at this project's version (refusing one this project does not have), and adds no font package for a fallback face or a family the base's fonts stylesheet already loads. A preview page file that is not a regular file is named so, with what fixes it, and its page stays so the same remove runs again. Beside `--template`, a description is offered only when it relates to a page.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `--png` takes sheet-overlays.png beside preview.png, on `show` and on every change: every menu, tooltip, popover and list drawn open, in each mode the theme has. The sample page shows none open and the full sheet is too tall to read whole, so the result of `new` names it in its look-at-it line. A change without `--png` removes it with the other pictures, and names `show --png`, which takes it again. A typeahead, whose doc requires a search source, is rendered with a sample one in the catalog the part data is read from, so its list (`typeahead-dropdown`) is recorded and `how` reads it.

`astryx experimental theme`: an option typed before a group's real subcommand (`preview --theme t list`, `editor --mode light set t …`) is read as that: the refusal names the option and the subcommand, offers the command with the options the subcommand takes moved after it, and says which options it takes none of. An option's value is never reported as an unknown subcommand, and the line offered is the subcommand typed, never another one.

`astryx experimental theme editor` sets a list's highlighted option through `--state highlighted` on its row (`selector-option-row`, `multi-selector-option`, `typeahead-option`), and reads a value labeled with that state.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: every dash form of an option (a hyphen before a dash, minus signs) is read as the option, never glued into a value. A dial name with a space for its dash (`"text size"`) is the dial. A set with no thing points to the settings it takes. A typo as near two values offers each (`tightr`: tight and tighter). A family spelled near a system font the build knows (`arail`, `Menol`) is kept as typed, with a note naming that font. `undo t headings wdie` removes the half its reading names. show, and undo with no history, on a damaged saved value offer its undo and set's repair beside it; a saved base in other letters or with a typo of a base that is not installed reads as that base, with its install first, in show as in a change. An entry saved in a form set reads when typed (`{"corners": "pill"}`, `"corners pill"`) is read as that setting. An undo names the change now on top, which the next undo takes back.

`astryx experimental theme`: an option or words a command does not take are answered one way by every editor and preview command: the options it takes are named, its help is offered, and the same command without them only where that is safe to run (show; never a preview remove, which would then remove the whole preview). A color set on a part whose color comes from its color prop offers the token of the prop's default as its doc gives it (a link: accent), else the token of each color the part reads (Text's color depends on its type).

`astryx experimental theme editor`: every `new` a refusal offers is checked as `new` checks its options before it is offered (a value never typed, such as a stock font, is not offered; a flag new refuses is left out and named; a line still refused is not offered), and a change of another dial is named for after the theme is made. `new` with no name offers a free name; a built-in theme among the extra words (`new t3 like neutral`, `new neutral t3`) is the base. set, undo, new, how and show read their options one way: in other letters, with one dash or a typed dash, or one slip off (`--On`, `-only`, `--olny`) they are named and the command offered with them. A token typed after its value and `set t neutral base` lead with the set in the right order; a repair never adds a part that was not typed; a swapped line that needs an install leads with the install. A base that reads as nothing is set back to the base the theme was built on, never to none. A font dial word on a part's font-family gives the family stack it stands for. A theme whose settings files are both gone but whose history or source the editor wrote is made again on its base, and undo then steps back. A part saved in other letters or as a one-item list is that part. undo of a misspelt setting leads with the one of the scope typed, and `undo <setting> <theme>` gives the reason with the theme first.

`astryx experimental theme`: an editor theme whose icon registry is a module in its own folder (as compile advises) now loads in the editor's checks, and its app copy carries that module, so `show` and `set` check it and `compile --check` passes. A theme source whose tokens replace the settings' (a spread of `defineTheme`'s result with a `tokens` field of its own) is refused by name instead of every change being saved and never built. A source name cut short (`themes/t/t`, `themes/t/t.theme.`) or a theme folder in other letters is offered the theme source. An empty `--out` is refused like a blank one. A weight given in a part's `font` shorthand is loaded, and weights are judged per family, so no font gets a gap note for a weight only another family uses. The stable `theme build` of an editor theme says it does not write (or check) the theme's app copy, and names the compile that does. A copy's compile with `--out` in the theme's own folder offers only a line compile takes, once.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: the refusal of a theme's own token values no longer ends a reason with two periods.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a padding or gap amount ("50% bigger", "20% smaller", "double", "150%") is an exact value from the one the part has now (its own setting, else its rule or the token it reads, each side of an unequal padding scaled), never a CSS percent padding; and with no amount, a part with an exact padding gets a step of that padding (said to be a step), since the spacing dial does not move an exact padding.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: per-variant colors in one mode, hover on every variant, later longhands, nested cards and kept sizes.
changesets.body:
- A one-mode color (`--mode`, or any color in a `light-only` or `dark-only` theme) on a part whose variants each have their own (a button or card background, a badge's text) goes to each variant's own rule, with the other mode's half exactly what that variant showed there (the base theme's value, else Core's; transparent stays transparent), so the other mode is unchanged for every variant; a variant's own hover still shows.
- A whole-part hover background (`--state hover`) reaches every variant, including ones the base theme gives their own hover or resting color.
- A longhand set after a shorthand wins even where the base theme holds that longhand (`padding-inline` after `padding`, `border-color` after `border`).
- A plain card inside a variant card keeps the card padding the editor gives it, in each text direction, and a variant's own padding (from the settings or your own source) no longer leaks into it; a variant your own source pads keeps its padding after an unequal editor padding on the plain card.
- The spacing dial keeps every exact control size the theme keeps (in px, rem or calc, from your own source, or set on the part) in order, on a part too; a size with no room between two kept ones takes the smaller one's size, and the result says so.
- `--mode` refused on a border names the variant in the per-mode color step; a gradient is offered as written for both modes.
- With your own source setting one corner, the corners note says the dial shows on the other corners after the undo.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a page background on `app-shell` also paints the shell's header and side nav, so they stay opaque when content scrolls under a sticky header; a page gradient is fixed to the viewport on the shell and those regions so they line up. `how` gives the page background one example value per mode, so text stays readable in dark mode.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> --color-background-body <color>` no longer moves the neutral color's other surfaces. A mid-tone page such as teal used to turn cards, popovers, menus and dialogs near-black in light mode (with dark text on them), because the neutral shades followed the written page color instead of the page the base theme's surfaces were made for. The written page color is now that one color, in light-only and two-mode themes alike.

`astryx experimental theme`: the editor knows its pages and pictures by their exact names (and its pictures record), so a file or link of yours named like one (`sheet-mockup.png`, `preview-v.html`) no longer blocks a change; `preview app --theme` copies such a file, and leaves a link out and names it (it never reads through a link). A link at a picture's exact name, to a file or to nothing, is never written through or replaced: only that picture is skipped and named, and the others are taken. `preview add` at a workspace root names the app to run it from, as the other commands do. A `--section` refusal keeps `--png`; an option written last with no value offers the command without it (never a usage line), except where leaving it out would widen a removal; an empty `--template` offers `preview add` itself; a template typo offers only a page that can be added now. `preview app --theme` names an open font it cannot install, with the package that would load it. The sheet says when a template page's charts are drawn in the browser (recharts), so its pictures show their space empty.

`astryx experimental theme editor show` keeps going where a page it draws cannot carry or write something: a theme image over 8 MB is left out of the pages and named in show's notes, rather than stopping the pages, and `show --png` in a theme folder that cannot be written names the folder, rather than refusing on a family page it could not write.

`astryx experimental theme editor set`: when a theme's own source sets the fill of the accent or a status color family to a fixed color or a pair of fixed colors, such as `--color-accent: ['#9333ea', '#d8b4fe']` in `t.theme.ts`, the family's other shades (links, icons, the muted tint) now come from that color, the one on screen. Before, they came from the color setting the source overrides, so links could turn blue beside purple buttons. The note about a hard-to-read source color now names a shade of that same color.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a theme whose palette names a palette recipe this CLI doesn't know is now refused plainly, and the file is left exactly as it is. A recipe a newer CLI made gets the same refusal as `astryx theme palette generate`, with the update step that fits where the CLI runs, instead of asking for the file to be fixed by hand. Any other name is said to be no recipe Astryx makes, and the refusal says to set `recipe` in the file to one of the recipes this CLI knows, naming them.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a panel's text color ("the drawer text red", a bottom sheet's, an alert dialog's, a hover card's) is answered with the text color tokens its heading and text read for their color role, never a color property they paint over; a fill set on inputs lands where each member paints its box, a date and time field's two boxes included.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a part's conditions come from what its theming target declares. The part data records every visual prop and runtime state the part's target declares, and the readers keep a runtime state the target declares (or one written as its own name) as a condition, so a state Core adds needs no change to the editor.

`astryx experimental theme editor show` lists as `unreached` each part whose fill or text color is still its base's (a part counts as reached when both changed, or a setting is on it), the most visible first; the text names ten and how many more, and `--json` lists them all.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- The part data draws every prop that changes a part's look (a toast's type, an avatar's shape), and reads a prop as a condition where it changes a color the part paints, so "the error toast background darker" steps from the error toast's own red.
- A part kept from a corner change pins every corner token its shapes read.
- A select's chevron or caret is its indicator icon, and a piece a part does not have (a date picker's segments) is named; neither writes the whole part.
- "indeterminate checkboxes red" reaches indeterminate boxes only, and "selected" is a toggle button's pressed state.
- A part that draws a line on some sides only (a grouped button's join) is still listed as drawing no border of its own.
- A one-mode hover shadow on inputs keeps their hover ring; "half as visible" is the input ring's alpha; "all focus rings" colors the inputs' rings too; a one-mode border on a part with no line draws one, see-through in the other mode; a radio's dot is its own part; "the progress indicator" is the progress bar's, and a state it does not draw apart (indeterminate) is named.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: more part facts read from Core, color asks answered with colors, and refusals that point to the setting that shows.
changesets.body:
- The part data reads a background a part inherits from the region it sits in (a side nav in an app shell), and the declarations of every target an element carries (an app shell's side nav region, which is a layout panel too).
- `how` answers a lighter or darker background with a color, never a brightness filter, which dims the text and icons too: from the page's color for "darker than the page", from each variant's own fill in a state, and from the part's resting fill otherwise.
- `how` answers striped or no striped rows with the token Core paints every other row with, on the row.
- The focus ring Core draws on a checkbox or radio indicator is read as tokens the indicator reads always: an outline property or a focus state there is refused, pointing to the focus outline token with no state.
- A font size, weight, line height or letter spacing on a part whose text is drawn by elements that set their own from a token (a top nav heading, a side nav heading, a banner) is refused, pointing to that token on the part; `how` answers with it and its current value.
- A border on a part that draws none of its own, whose edges its inner parts draw (a date-time input), is refused, pointing to those parts; `how` reads "date and time input" as that part and answers for its date and time boxes.
- A checkbox's indeterminate look is reachable with `--when checked:indeterminate`, and `how` adds it beside `--state checked`.
- A text property CSS inherits, set on a part, says which parts inside it also take it.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a part that another component places somewhere (the current page's button in a pagination, a pressed toggle) records that place as a condition, so what that component paints it with there is never read as the part's look at rest. A ghost button reads no fill at rest, as Core paints it.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: padding and corners reach the elements Core draws them on.
changesets.body:
- Padding on a table row, which CSS draws no padding on, is refused for its cells, and `how` answers a typed table row padding on the cells.
- Corners on a button group are written as the corner token its first and last buttons read, so the group's outer corners follow.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: part facts read from more of Core, colors that reach a part's inner text, corners that reach the parts drawing them, and results and refusals that say what is true.
changesets.body:
- The part data renders each component with each look flag turned on too (a table's `isStriped`, `hasHover`), so a table row reads its hover fill, and `how` steps that token for a lighter or darker hover instead of a brightness filter.
- `how` and a refusal of a state a part lacks list the same states.
- The focus outline tokens can be set on checkbox and radio indicators, where Core draws the focus ring at focus time.
- Changing one member of a group kept alike (inputs) alone in height says it now differs from the rest, and names `--on <group>`.
- A color on a part whose text is drawn by elements that read a text color token themselves (a top nav heading, a top nav) also goes into those tokens on the part, so the text shows it.
- Corners on a part whose corners are drawn by parts of its own inside it (a date-time input's date and time boxes) round those parts, for the part and its group.
- A whole-theme corners dial moves a part a base pins to a length or to a token the dial never moves (such as `--radius-full` on buttons), keeps a part Core rounds with a fixed token (a pill badge), and never overwrites corners set on a part.
- The result lists every state rule a change writes, including one the base theme already has a state block for.
- A color given beside its own image in one background is never reported as covered by it.
- A keyword with `--mode` on a token offers only the color; on a one-mode theme, a thing that takes no mode is refused with the command that drops `--mode`, never with a change of the theme's mode.
- A one-mode state color on a group names the members that cannot keep the other mode and offers `--only` for the part named.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`:
changesets.body:
- A part key the build cannot write as intended is refused at its line in an editor theme: a vendor property written without its dash (`msOverflowStyle`, `webkit-transform`, with the dashed form offered), a pseudo name in capitals (`':HOVER'`, which Core does not read as `:hover`), something after a pseudo-element (`'::before:hover'`, with `':hover::before'` offered), two pseudo-elements, an escaped pseudo name, the custom property `--`, an empty key, and a block under a key that nests none (`'[data-x'`, a pseudo key inside a pseudo key). A plain theme's `compile` warns them, as `theme build` does.
- A custom property of the theme's own whose value is a `var()` that reads nothing is refused at that property, as the same `var()` is in a part's property.
- A value passed to an imported function (`make('nope')`) is blamed on the line that passes it; a value read through an optional chain (`all?.toks`) or an export that is a property of another block in its file is blamed on the line that holds it.
- NaN and Infinity get no example made from them (no `'NaNpx'`).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: an element named before "in" or "of" a part ("the selected option row in the selector", "the hovered option in the selector", "the checked item in the dropdown menu") is that part's own element, by the rest of its catalog name and the state said, never another component the words seem to name (a table's rows) or the part itself; the last place said is the place ("the text in the hovered menu item of the dropdown" is in the dropdown), which is never written as a part of its own.

`astryx experimental theme editor` measures text on a fill the theme sets on a part the base theme draws with none (every tab painted gray): its text in each state is checked on that fill and named on that part, and each line sets the text on that part, so following them ends the problems.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a part's own state saved in a spelling `set` reads typed (toggle-button's `is-pressed` or `ispressed` for isPressed) is read as that state, with a note, instead of being refused as damage. The next change saves the part's spelling.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a state setting on a part (`font-weight 500 --on tab --state selected`) wins over the build's copy of the plain part's value, which the build no longer writes after it; and `how` keeps a state at the value the part shows in that state (a selected tab's semibold).
changesets.body: A shadow on the resting rule of a part that draws its rings in its box-shadow (a text input's hover and focus rings) is refused with that reason, in both modes or one, since it would replace the rings in every state.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a part's own state written as the part names it (`--state isPressed` on toggle-button) is saved and read back as that state. Before, the next command read the saved `isPressed` as `is-pressed`, a state the part does not have, and refused every change to the theme. A theme already holding such a state is refused with its undo and a `set` line that writes the setting in its place, so the theme loads again.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- A text color on a part whose text sits on Core's media surface inside it (a toast's inverted surface) is refused with the lines that reach it, `--color-on-dark` and `--color-on-light` on the part, and `how` answers with them; the part data records such a surface.
- A resting shadow on a part that rings itself in its box-shadow keeps each of its renders' own rings: a status that draws none while focused gets the shadow alone, a shadow of none leaves the rings in their states, and a state's own shadow for the part wins on every render.
- An input's focus ring is its box-shadow ring: `how` answers a focus ring color there with that ring while focused, and an outline color, width or offset on a part that draws no outline is refused.
- "toggle thumb", "switch knob" and the like are the switch's thumb, never its track.
- A one-mode fill's covers notes keep its mode, in their words and their lines.
- The corners help names the step `more` and `less` take between round and pill.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- A part's text made transparent by an amount ("the button text 50% transparent", "the fainter text in cards 50% transparent") is its text colors at that alpha, never the whole part's opacity.
- A state typed by its prop name or its ARIA attribute (`--state isPressed` or `aria-pressed` on a button, `isSelected` on a tab) is the state of that name.
- Several states at once are taken where the element takes them (a hovered selected tab), saved in one order so either spelling is one setting, and undone in either; `how` carries both states said ("hovered selected tabs").
- A one-mode border on a part that draws a border in that state (a focused input) is that border's color alone; a line drawn as a ring keeps the shadow the part draws in that state.
- A divider's line: "fainter" fades every variant's line, "hide" takes them away, and a thickness for one variant ("subtle dividers thicker") stays on it.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor show` names under `missed` the parts the theme's own changes should have reached and did not, one of each kind first: with the accent changed, an inverted surface (a toast, a tooltip), a disabled part drawn as the accent at reduced opacity, a selected state on the base's fill, a status fill (an info banner); with the corners changed, a pill; with the border width changed, a borderless surface. Each comes with the one line that reaches it, its state named (`--state disabled`, `--state selected`). The text shows six and counts the other parts on the base's look; `--json` lists them all. A part whose only fill is the shared hover or pressed tint (a link, a menu item) is judged by its text, so it is no longer listed as unreached.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: two parts joined by "and" share the ask around them, so "half the corner radius on buttons and cards on hover" gives both parts their own command with the amount and `--state hover` (before, the first lost the state and the second was dropped). "context menu" is Core's context-menu part, not the dropdown menu.

`astryx experimental theme …`: a pasted change line whose label names a part (`background-color (card) -> red`) sets that part instead of reading the label as a mode; a label that is no part name is still read as a mode, its typo included (`(drak)` is dark).

`astryx experimental theme …`: a pasted form is read as the typed one. A var() naming a design token in other letters (`var(--Spacing-4)`) gets the line with that token, though others of its family are one letter away. A pasted entry with its setting and value in the other order (`'pill: corners'`, `'{"red":"background-color","on":"card"}'`) gets the same swapped line as the typed pair. A pasted object of several settings gives each setting's line its scope, from the object's own `on`/`when`/`state`/`mode`/`only` keys and from the flags typed with it, and never offers a scope key as a setting of its own. A pasted change line with a mode label and no old value (`--color-accent [light only] -> #7c3aed`) keeps the label as the mode. A change made when the build does not match the saved settings (after a hand edit) says so and lists its token changes against the saved settings, instead of saying the theme already showed it.

`astryx experimental theme editor set`: a pasted object's keys are read as set reads a typed setting name, so a key with spaces around it (`{"accent ": "#7c3aed"}`) is that setting, alone or beside other entries.

`astryx experimental theme editor` pictures (`--png`) never wait on a network: the picture's browser loads the page's own files only, so a remote stylesheet, font or image a page names (a base theme's Google Fonts import, a template's photo) fails at once instead of holding the picture until the time limit when the machine is offline or has no direct internet.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a Chrome or Chromium that stops at once (no display, a missing library) is named with its own error when `--png` reports the picture was not taken, never with the closed pipe it leaves behind. A typo of a keyword with a dash (`cursor not-alowed`) is offered the keyword again.
The pictures an agent opens show the overlays, and the output keeps what was missed where a cut output still shows it:
changesets.body:
- `preview.png` (the sample page) ends with a strip of a tooltip, a popover, a menu and a select list drawn open, from the overlays the sheet draws.
- `sheet-overlays.png` shows the small overlays first, five to a row, each cell at most 300px tall, and no part of an overlay alone, so it stays under about 1600px.
- A change without `--png` names `show --png` and the two pictures it writes to open.
- A change counts, near its top, the parts the theme's changes did not reach; `show` lists them, with their lines, last before its closing look line.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor show --png` and `--png` on a change take all their pictures with one browser start, a few pages at a time, so a run of many pictures costs about one start. A focus ring at the edge of a sheet cell shows whole, and the sample page shows a link in its text and one in a card.
`astryx experimental theme editor`'s pictures and its `missed` list show what the theme draws:
changesets.body:
- `--png` pictures show overlays drawn open as they look open: each opening animation runs to its end before the picture.
- A change that changes nothing counts the parts the theme still misses, as `show` lists them.
- A base theme's own rule for a state (butter's selected nav item, drawn with no fill) is what the contrast checks and `missed` judge.
- An inverted surface that disappears into the page (a toast, a tooltip) gets a line that makes it stand out again, in each mode it disappears in.
- A border line on a part whose variants differ (a button) frames only the variants that draw a box; the ghost button keeps none.
- With the theme's own corners at a pill, no pill part is listed as missed.
- `show`'s count line under `missed` says what the rest are: parts whose fill or text color is still the base's, and the other missed parts.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme` pictures show what a person sees once the page runs:
changesets.body:
- A calendar on the sheet shows its days: a part whose server render keeps content inert until the browser runs is drawn as the browser mounts it.
- The open states page draws a context menu (right-clicked), a submenu's flyout, a popover that holds a form, a date and time field's time list, a command palette's items and a narrow screen's navigation drawer. Its drawing asks about the pointer as a desktop's mouse does, presses the controls an opened overlay holds, and closes an open popover when it presses outside it, as a browser does.
- A states section draws each control of the sample page at rest, hovered, focused from the keyboard and pressed: the page marks each one with its state, and the render's stylesheet applies that state's rules to it.
- A nav icon gets the icon its doc suggests, and an icon-only button gets an icon, so neither draws empty or spills its name.
- A border set on the inputs lands on a date and time field's two boxes, not the row around them, so it draws once on each box.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: settings typed where the theme goes, as a list or a pasted form (`show corners, accent`, `show corners:pill`, `'{"corners":"pill"}'`), get a look at each theme here, never a theme made of them nor "names more than one theme". `new` reads more settings typed after the name as their options, never as name words: a colon word apart from its value (`accent: red`), a dial typo (`cornres pill`), `base <theme>` as `--like`, a pasted value across words (`font=Inter, Arial`), a dial word after an option's value (`--accent red corners pill`), and a property new takes no option for (`padding 8px`), offered as a `set` after the theme is made; a setting with its value typed as the name (`new 'corners pill'`) is never the name offered. `undo` reads a value with commas typed unquoted when the theme is left out (`undo Inter, Arial`), a value then its setting (`undo t red accent`), and a scope in a spelling set reads (`--on Card`, `cards`, `--mode drak`): the line for that scope's setting leads. An option whose value names another subcommand (`editor --on show set t …`) keeps it. A mode typed with its letters in another order (`--mode kdar`) is that mode. `experimental theme compile` with no file names its usage and help.

`astryx experimental theme editor` checks the loading placeholder (Skeleton): one under 1.2:1 against the page or a surface at its brightest, which a person cannot see, is a problem where the theme's colors make it so, with the nearest placeholder color that shows as its line, and a note where the base theme draws it so itself.
`astryx experimental theme` refuses what a build could not apply, at its place, and names the fonts a theme shows:
changesets.body:
- In an editor theme, null under a style key, a pseudo-class or an at-rule is named once, with a fix that holds no null.
- A pseudo-class or pseudo-element typo anywhere in a selector (`::befor`, `:hover:focus-visble`, `:not(:hovr)`) is refused with the selector corrected; a block under a pseudo-class's bare name (`hover: {…}`) is told to start with a colon.
- A part's variable in the page's `tokens` map, which the part sets on its own element, is refused with the part-scoped line; a typo of one is named.
- A value read from another file is blamed on that file and line, through `export {name}` lists, re-exports, namespace imports, imported part blocks and imported single values.
- A named pipe, a device or a socket where the app copy goes is refused at once, never opened.
- Fonts: Apple Color Emoji and Noto Color Emoji count as the systems' own fonts. Apple's interface faces (SF Pro, SF Mono, New York) are told by the generic that reaches them (`system-ui`, `ui-monospace`, `ui-serif`), since browsers do not reach them by name. An installed font package's missing weights are named, a font service request with another axis before `wght` is read, and a weight between the hundreds (550) is named as the face it shows, as CSS font matching picks it.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`: a stop (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM) during `preview add`, `preview remove` or `preview app` now ends the command as stopped, with one line saying where the change stands, never `[ok]` with exit 0; a browser the editor stops at its 60-second bound is said to have timed out, Chrome's startup warnings are no longer given as the reason a picture failed, and a theme folder that cannot be written is named instead of the browser; Chrome gets a profile folder of its own that is removed however the run ends; the `see` fix for an in-app preview Next does not serve is one that works (`preview remove --path …`, then `preview add`, or "tsx" in pageExtensions); `preview app` from a subfolder prints a folder and `cd` that work from there, and its rule and docs name the project folder as the bound; and from a subfolder, the picture note names every picture with its full path.

`astryx experimental theme`: a change no longer deletes a copy of a picture (such as `preview-before.png`): only pictures the editor recorded taking, unchanged since, are removed. Every browser the editor starts for a picture, Playwright included, runs as its own process with a temp folder of its own (removed however the run ends), one 60-second bound and the same stop; a browser that does not start keeps its real cause in the message, and Chrome is named only when there is one. A theme folder that cannot be written is a write failure naming the folder; pictures asked for but not taken are said; `preview add` finds a preview renamed by hand instead of starting a second one, through the one list of previews `see`, a change's refresh and the preview commands share; a theme the route imports from outside the project folder (a workspace app run from its own folder) is never dropped from the preview; the no-template refusal offers only pages the app can show; a page remove over a theme that does not load names the whole-preview remove; the `add --template <default page>` note says what was added; from a subfolder, the wiring's paths work from there; and the `preview remove` help says what happens to a path outside the folder.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: pictures a plain Chrome took are no longer reported as "--png took no pictures"; the `see` line names `editor show <theme> --png` for pictures, never the command that just ran (an undo run again undoes another change); stopping a change while the browser takes pictures stops the browser and says the change is saved, never a browser failure; a picture's part file left by a stopped run is cleared by the next change and never copied into a new app, and a folder by that name is skipped; an in-app preview route that cannot be written, a damaged preview record and a preview in a folder Next does not serve (`src/app/` under a root `app/`, page extensions without `tsx`) are all said, with no URL that would not load; `preview app` copies none of a theme's pictures or preview pages; and from a subfolder, `preview list` and `remove` take the folder they print, and the picture note and `previewStale` name files the way `see` does (absolute).

`astryx experimental theme`: with Playwright in the project, pictures try Playwright's own browser before the system Chrome, and the advice names only a fix that can help (Playwright's browser only when it is missing); the Chrome lookup passes over a folder or a file that does not run and keeps looking on PATH; a change keeps every in-app preview of the theme in step, including one renamed by hand or whose record was lost, the same previews `see` names; `preview add --path app/<x>` in a src/app project says that a root app/ would stop the whole app in src/app/ from being served; the `preview app` error table names the project folder as the bound; and a stop that lands after a preview command printed its result no longer turns that ok into exit 130.

`astryx experimental theme editor` and `preview`: `preview remove --path` given a file is refused with the preview's folder (it reported an unknown error). Pictures are taken under a part name and moved into place, so a `--png` run stopped while the browser runs leaves nothing the next run reads as a file of yours. The `see` line names `preview add --theme <name>` when the project has several editor themes; gives no URL for a preview moved where Next does not serve it, saying why; says preview.html could not be written when a folder is in the way; says what blocked `--png` when a picture of yours did; names files by paths that work from a subfolder; and says when the in-app preview was changed by hand, as `previewStale` now does with what to move out. The show help says pictures change nothing in the app, except that show first brings the app copy up to date after a hand edit. A dial value labeled with another setting (`accent 'neutral: #64748b'`) is refused with that setting's line. The input cleanup reads corner brackets as quotes, keeps escaped quotes and brackets inside strings, reads a light and a dark color typed as a pair (offering `light-dark()` or two `--mode` lines, or one color for a dial), splits a JSON object of several settings into one line each, reads a JSON-escaped font stack, maps `--mode night` and `day` to dark and light, and reads `vibrancy 0.5` and `"50"` as 50; a saved value with paste debris or `!important` is offered cleaned.

`astryx experimental theme`: pictures taken with a Chrome or Chromium (no Playwright) are whole-page pictures, the same as Playwright's, through the browser's DevTools protocol, never the top 2400 pixels only. Every browser the editor starts runs under one runner: a temp folder of its own (a run with none is refused, never started on the person's own browser profile), one time bound per browser with the next browser tried when one hangs or fails (and not tried again for the next picture of the run), and a stop (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, or the terminal closing) that closes the browser's whole process group and removes its temp folder and the unfinished picture. When a later browser took the picture, the result says why an earlier one did not, with its real error. A picture file of your own (`preview.png` of any size) is never taken over: only pictures the editor recorded or stamped are. `preview add` from a workspace app's folder keeps a theme the route imports from outside it, as `preview remove` does; two starter apps from `preview app` never share a package name; refusals name commands that work when followed (each app's own folder from a workspace root, a free folder for a starter app, a page this app can show); and the note that the app does not import Core's stylesheet reads the layouts' real import statements.

`astryx experimental theme` and `astryx experimental render`: a stop (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, or the terminal closing) while pages render removes the render's temp folders. A page with a root Theme is written with that Theme's attributes on `<html>`, as Core's root Theme sets them in a browser, so root-scoped tokens such as the focus ring's color follow the theme in the preview and the sheet. Every `preview app` command a result names works where it is printed: a folder starting with `-` goes after `--`, a folder is given from the folder the command ran in, a theme a workspace app holds is reached from that app, and a repaired folder name is a free one. A starter app gets every open font the theme builds, installed in this project or not. A change names the pictures it removed (the preview's and the sheet's) and keeps a section sheet's. `preview app --theme` refuses a theme whose own files import a file outside its folder, which the new app would not have. A stop during `preview app` says whether the app was written whole or nothing was written.

`astryx experimental theme`: a theme with both modes gets a sheet and preview that render each part as the app renders it in each mode (a Toast in dark is the app's dark Toast, no longer a blank bar), the page showing the render of the mode it is in. From a workspace root, a folder in a workspace app gets that app's own checks (its routes folder, public/, build folder, themes/, Pages Router, unrouted folders); the pointers to an app below keep every argument (`--theme`, `--template`, `--top`) and use `--path` from a project root; a theme that a workspace app holds is named there, with the command run from that app. Every pointer is one its command takes: `preview add` only where add takes the folder, a starter folder free of any file, dangling link or case twin, a `cd` that a folder starting with `-` does not break, and `editor show <theme> --png` after a stop during the pictures. Starter apps get package names that never collide. A preview moved into a folder with a space or another character no plain URL takes is updated where it is. A second Ctrl-C while the pictures stop kills the browser at once and removes its temp folder.

`astryx experimental theme`: a refused `preview app --theme` or `preview add` writes nothing: a stale theme it builds first is put back when the build fails (a theme source that does not load), so the same command is refused again rather than copying an old build. `preview app --theme` refuses a theme stylesheet url that leads out of the theme folder (the new app would not build), a theme file too large for one read, and one that cannot be read, each by name (a read, never called a write). A named pipe or a device at a file the editor reads (the preview record, a page, a picture, the pictures record) is never opened, so no command hangs on one. Theme image names are URL text (`a%20b.png` is "a b.png"), and a quoted url may hold parentheses; an image that cannot be read is left out of the previews with a note. A section sheet's pictures go with the others when the look changes, and the command that takes them again is named. A starter app names the weights of a font it adds that it does not load. `preview add` reads a typed dash form of its options, and beside a description offers only a `--template` page this app can add; `--top` beside a default page, or alone, offers the command without it; an empty `--theme` offers the preview command with each theme.

`astryx experimental theme preview` reads each preview page once per element when it checks whether the page was changed by hand: a page whose JSX nests deep took time that doubled with each level, so `preview add` and `preview remove` were slow on the generated pages.

`astryx experimental theme`: a preview picture's browser makes no network request of its own (no update, time, sync or metrics checks, no proxy, no host name resolved), on the Chrome and Playwright paths alike. A theme file that is not a regular file (a named pipe, a link to a device) is never read, so `show` cannot hang on it. `show` names the theme images the previews cannot show (loaded from the network, not found, not a regular file, or over the size a preview page carries), and an image too large for a preview is refused with its name and size instead of as a React failure. Extra words to `preview app`, `preview list` and `preview remove` get a command that works and the command's help. `preview app --theme` from a workspace root gives the `cd` to the app. A description longer than the words read is quoted as typed, and a refusal says it was cut. A `--template` typo names only pages this app can add now.
`astryx experimental theme preview` and the starter offer lines that work and name what is in the way:
changesets.body:
- `preview remove` with no preview yet offers `preview add` only where add can work; elsewhere (an app with no root layout) it offers what add itself offers there.
- `preview app --theme` refuses, before anything is written, a theme whose import without its extension (`./helpers`) loads a link inside the theme folder, and one whose `url()` names no file (a wrong-case path); a folder in the theme folder it cannot read is named as a read, not a write.
- A named pipe or a device at `sheet.html` or `preview.html` is left as it is and named, as at the open states page's name, never written over.
- `preview app --theme` given a theme as a path or a list offers `preview app <folder> --theme <theme>`, never a look at the theme.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a change's new problems are the ones the theme did not have before it, compared by what each problem is (the text, what draws it, what it sits on, its variant and mode), not by its printed ratio, so moving a color that leaves the same text low makes no new problem.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a problem a change makes leads its result. The status line counts the new problems, and each follows under it with the command that fixes it: the text token set where the text sits, or the border color, for the mode, to the black or white that reads there. A color that fails its contrast check is a new problem too. `show` ends with `openProblems`, every contrast problem the theme has now with its fix (the JSON lists every one; the text shows the first eight and counts the rest). A text token set on the part the text sits on (card text on the card) now counts for the text inside it, so following that fix clears the problem, and a border set again for one mode is measured as set.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `openProblems` and `newProblems` list every contrast problem in JSON, and a change's new problems are compared against all of them, so following one fix line no longer reports old problems as new. The text shows the first eight and counts the rest.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a progress bar's height ("progress bar 4px tall") is its track's, never a strip of fill over the unchanged track; a date picker's selected day says its calendar is the plain Calendar and names the calendar day's selected state, as its today does, never "date-input has no selected state".

`astryx experimental theme editor …`: a set of a property typed in other letters (`set t Background-Color green --on card`) is that property, so it fixes that property listed twice in the settings file, instead of a refusal that offers a swapped line back and forth. A top-level `base` in the settings file (the editor's word for it) is read as the base, with a note, instead of the theme building on no base, and any other top-level field the editor does not read is named, with the field it is a typo of. A saved setting with no source and its part under a field the editor does not read (`"part"`) names that field and offers the undo that removes it, instead of only a remake.
`astryx experimental theme`:
changesets.body:
- A pseudo-class after a pseudo-element that takes one is accepted: any after `::file-selector-button` and `::details-content`, `:window-inactive` after a highlight such as `::selection`, `:target-current` after `::scroll-marker`. One that does not take it is refused with what it takes.
- Only `:hover` and `:active` written in capitals are refused, the two names Core reads; `::BEFORE` or `:FOCUS` build as written.
- A part property that builds dash-first without a vendor prefix (`Color`, `BACKGROUND`, `-webkit-`) is refused, with the name in lower case.
- A tokens map spread from a defined theme's tokens no longer trips over Core's own private copies in it; another private variable it carries is named as coming with the spread, with the way out.
- A value read from another file is blamed on that file through an array element (`cs[1]`), a template (`` `${c}` ``), a choice (`B.x ? B.x : '#fff'`), a call of a global or a function of the theme file's own (`String(B.x)`), and `await import()`.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`:
changesets.body:
- In an editor theme, a pseudo key that is no single selector is refused at its line: one that leaves a parenthesis, bracket, quote or comment open (`':nth-child(2n'`, with the closed form offered), one no browser reads, and a selector list (`':hover, :focus'`), which is named with one key per member. A plain theme's `compile` warns them, as `theme build` does.
- In an editor theme, a custom property with capitals in a part's block is refused: the build writes a part's property names in kebab case, so `--myColor` would be set as `--my-color` while `var(--myColor)` reads the name as written. A plain theme's `compile` warns it.
- A variable a component sets on its own element is refused in `localTokens` and in another part's block, with the part that sets it. On its own part, `var()` of that variable reads it.
