- `editor set` on a theme whose stylesheet is a named pipe gives the pipe refusal, never a failed module load.
- A value read through an imported object's member (`all.toks`), a destructure of one, an imported function's return, or an imported typography object is blamed on the file that holds it.
- A null value in the theme's own file builds as it is with a warning at its line, as in any theme; a null part or style key is still refused.
- `compile` of a missing file near the theme source (`themes/t/t.theme`, `t.them.ts`) offers that source.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more questions the way they are asked:

`astryx experimental theme editor how` checks its answer against what the question means: a part the question only compares against ("rounder than buttons", "darker than the page") is never changed, and the answer says so; a prohibition ("don't make the cards bigger", "buttons should not be rounder") changes nothing and says what stays; a question about a value ("how much padding do buttons have", "what color is the button") answers with the value now. Comparisons write onto the first part only, with a typed offset ("4px rounder than buttons"), its variant and state, and the property the words name ("button text the same color as the card text", "input border the same color as the button background"); two parts that should match copy one value, or say they already match. "Except" keeps an exact radius change, a text size change, a variant beside a part, small and muted ones, and a state. A side border ("remove the top border"), close icons and header titles, "inputs with errors", a heading level ("red h1"), a part's own radius, text colors for two button variants, an elided second clause ("… and darker when pressed", "… and half on ghost ones") and "buttons inside cards" (the container is kept, and the answer says the part changes everywhere) are read as asked. A theme name typed in another case keeps the question.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: on an installed Core that draws a radio's circle with the pill token (`--radius-full`), squaring the pills ("no rounding anywhere", the square-corners note) keeps the radio marks round with that token at Core's value on them. On a Core that draws the circle at 50%, no pin is written. The "thick borders on everything" answer also frames the label boxes (badges, tokens).
`astryx experimental theme editor`: the cached part data is rebuilt once more, so a calendar's range band is read in a cache built before it was drawn.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the part data draws a component whose look names its value's kind (a calendar's range mode) with a sample of that kind (a range of days), so what Core draws for it, the band behind the days in a range, is read: "the calendar range band blue" sets the token it paints with on the calendar. A shadow or border asked of a part drawn inside an overlay that paints its edge for it (a typeahead's list, in its popover) points to that overlay, saying a change there reaches every one, and writes nothing.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: one reader for each kind of input, on every path.
changesets.body:
- A family list reads each family from its end, on the font dial, a family token and a part's `font-family`: a size, a weight or a style after a family's name (`Inter 16px`, `Inter Italic`) is refused with the family and the size's, weight's or style's own line; a bare number in a list (`Lato, 16`) is a weight only as a whole hundred; a misspelled generic (`sansserif`, `serf`, `system ui`) or, on the font dial, preset (`sytem`) is offered as that name, never saved as a family. A family the editor knows keeps its last word (`Source Sans 3`, `Arial Black 900` is Arial Black and a weight).
- A swapped setting and value is offered only when set takes it as typed, with the scope typed, never a sample command on a part nobody named.
- A property written with `_` or spaces (`font_size`, `"border radius"`) reads as the property, as camel case does, and gets the same answer.
- One yes/no reader for a flag given a value and a saved `only`: the documented spellings of yes and no, or a typo of one; any other word is refused with no line guessing it. The line offered is checked as every repair is.
- `--mode` reads a word that names one mode (`dark-only`, `darkmode`, `dark mode`) as that mode, in set and undo alike.
- A pasted object of one entry gets that entry's repair.
- A saved value that set repairs (`headings "blod"`, `spacing "romy"`, `text-size "16px"`) is offered that repair beside the undo.
- A damaged base or mode is offered the lines that set it again (each installed base, each mode), never a default that drops it; a base written with `theme` (`neutral-theme`) is that base.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a typo of a font preset reads as that preset when the preset and the system family it names both match (`Verdena`, `Segoe IU`); a family near a system font only (`Times New Romna`, `Arail` in a list) is kept as typed, with a note whose line sets that font. `show` and `compile` give set's repair for a damaged saved value beside its undo, as every change does, and an entry saved in a typed form (`corners: pill`, `red --on card`) gets the reading set gives it. The editor's own printed setting line pasted back (`corners = pill (whole theme)`, `opacity = 0.5 on card`) carries its scope. A dial saved for one mode is refused as `set` refuses `--mode` on it, never built for both modes or for none. `set mode night` reads as dark only; `undo` compares colors as colors (`#F00` is the saved `#ff0000`); two headings words (`bold wide`, `bold and wide`) are one `new` line, and set's second line is the next step; a token in another style (`--color_accent`) or with a typo is offered as the token.

`astryx experimental theme editor set` points at a line that works and says what happened. A word that names a dial and its value (`shadows none`, `elevation none`, `dark-mode true`) offers that dial's line (`set t surfaces flat`, `set t mode dark-only`) whatever the theme has now. A state a part does not have names the part drawn inside it that does ("today" on a calendar offers the line `--on calendar-day --state today`). A no-op `mode` or `base` set says nothing was built and no undo step was added, as every other no-op does. A theme with one color mode lists its own mode's token changes first.

Receipts say what happened: `astryx experimental theme editor set` of a value the theme already has reads "font = system (whole theme) was already set; nothing changed" in place of "system -> system"; an `undo` names a setting that still applies where the removed one did ("#fef3c7 in light mode and the base theme's value in dark mode"), never the base value alone; and a theme set to one color mode says `astryx theme add <theme>` records the mode and its wiring passes it, in place of reading as a manual step. A dial already at its last rung names an exact size that goes past the rungs (`set t text-size 18`), beside the step the other way.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a refusal offers `new` to make a theme again only for a settings file `new` itself remakes; a setting listed twice gets its keep and remove lines, and a `lifted` field that is no list of text is dropped (the build writes it again). `new` repairs a value as set does: a line never adds a setting nobody typed (a mode read from a color's words), a did-you-mean reads the whole value typed, `how` is named for a value no reading makes work, and a repaired value (`ff0000` as `#ff0000`) stays in the line. Words of a flag value typed unquoted on `new` (`--font Open Sans`) belong to that value, and the line offered is checked as new checks it. show and the preview commands read their options with the one option reader, so a did-you-mean always matches the command offered. A base that is not installed leads with the install, then the set, and a theme already on a base is not offered no base. A part and its variant written in other letters together get the line that works. A corners size saved in rem is read as the px set saves it as.
`astryx experimental theme editor` offers lines that run and do what they say:
changesets.body:
- A setting and value in the other order beside a mistyped option (`set t red --color-accent --mdoe dark`), or with a spaced name beside a part typo, get one line with both repairs.
- A `var()` naming a token one letter off gets the line with the token repaired, typed and as the repair of a saved entry beside its undo.
- `undo` naming two settings of different scopes (`undo t spacing background-color --on card`) offers one undo for each, never one that drops the other.
- After a plain part fill, the "to fill only one of them" and "to change only its fill at rest" lines start with the undo of that fill.
- `new --base` offers the `--like` line as `new` checks it (an install first, other flags repaired). `new --font Open Sans` with no name reads Sans as part of the font, and offers a free name. `--mode light --mode dark` together read as both modes.
- The editor's own lines pasted back keep their repairs in the arrow form (`accent tomato -> tomatoe`), read a mode label in any case or with `mode`/`only` (`(Dark)`, `[dark only]`), refuse a mode typo with its line, and keep a printed scope in another case (`on Card`, `:Hover`).
- A pasted entry's field keys are read in any case (`{"Thing": …, "Value": …}`, `"On"`).
- The line that drops `--only` keeps every other scope flag.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: lines offered work as the person will run them. A `new` refused for its name keeps each misspelled value as new repairs it for a free name. A word after `--like <base>` is read into the name, never glued onto the base. A damaged saved entry's set line is offered on its own only when it replaces that entry; otherwise it is labelled as the step after the undo. A typo of a built-in base reads as that base, installed or not, with its install first (set, `new --like` and a saved base alike), and an unknown base gets `how base`, never `base none` for a theme on a base. A thousands comma reads as such on a property that takes only whole numbers (`z-index '-1,000'`), and a comma in a ratio is a pair only between whole numbers of 1 or more (`0,75` is 0.75). An undo naming several settings offers one undo each; an undo with only a scope offers a step back only when there is one. A setting pasted in the saved form, or beside its scope keys, is one setting with its scope as flags. A word after a mistyped yes/no option is left out of the line and named. The settings reader reads a saved `only` of 1 or 0, refuses a vibrancy with no color as set does, and a saved step word steps from what applies without it.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a repair's offered value reads the whole typed value, never a subset of its words. A line may carry part of the value only when the refusal's other lines carry the rest (`Inter 600` gives the family and the weight, `italic bold` on a part gives the style and the weight); a part alone (`all` for `all 200`, `bold` for `extra bold`, `5` for `0,5`) is not offered.
changesets.body:
- A comma between digits is a decimal point (`1,5rem` is 1.5rem, `0,5` is 0.5), or before three digits after a whole number a thousands mark (`1,000` on a weight is 1000), never a split into layers.
- Several values of one kind for a property that takes one offer the first as typed, with px only when the property takes no bare number (`line-height 1.5 2` is 1.5), and never one value of a shorthand of several kinds (`transition all 200` gets `how`).
- `headings extra bold` offers heavy (800), and `text-size x-large` offers 24, the size CSS gives it.
- `more` or `less` authorizes a computed value only on a dial with a scale: a token, a part property or a dial's other name given a step gets `how`, never a stock color, weight or size.
- A saved value authorizes only a keep line for its own setting, never the setting being typed, so `base buter` no longer offers the base the theme already has.
- A light and dark pair on a part's color in a one-mode theme gives the half that theme shows, as a token does.
- The note about a second pasted declaration names its line only when `set` takes it, or the line `set` offers for it.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: every value a refusal or a saved-settings repair offers now passes one gate, and each offered line is checked as `set` checks it before it is shown. A value may come only from these sources:
changesets.body:
- What was typed, under exact readings: quotes, labels and copy debris (a trailing `;`, `!important`, a comment) taken off; the same number written another way (full-width digits, a comma decimal, an exponent, rem or pt as px, a percent); CSS color names written as words (`dark red` is `darkred`).
- A documented table: Tailwind's radius classes (`rounded-lg` is 8px), a dial's own words, a weight word, a number read as a dial's nearest rung.
- The theme's own saved values, for a keep or unlock line.
- The setting's documented fallback or other-direction step.
- The correction of a typo of what was typed: one letter off for a word of five letters or fewer, two for a longer one.

Anything else, such as a stock color, a stock shadow or easing, a reset, a default token or a nearest guess, gives `how <thing>`. A scale step (`red-500`) is no bare color.

Also:

- `font 'Inter 600'` offers the family and the weight separately.
- A Google Fonts spec (`Inter:wght@400;600`) offers its family.
- Another property's label on a part property (`padding 'margin: 8px'`) offers that property.
- `--color-danger` offers the error token, and `--color-primary` or `--color-brand` the accent token.
- A CSS property typed for the whole theme leads with its dial or token (`border-radius 8px` → `corners 8px`), never a part that was not named.
- A pasted object's nested values are read, and each of its lines is checked.
- A bare fraction on a size token gets no px guessed.
- A very long input is near nothing.
- `--state 'hover,focus-visible'` gives one line per state.
- A saved light-dark pair for one mode is refused with the half for that mode.
- A CSS-wide keyword on a token offers the undo only when the theme sets the token.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: repairs follow the readers `set` already uses.
changesets.body:
- A saved property name with a space or capitals (`"background color"`) is repaired by `set` in place: the line replaces the broken entry, and the theme loads again.
- A unit typed after a space joins its number for every CSS unit (`50 %`, `50 vw`, `200 ms`, `1,5 rem`), not only px, rem and em.
- A typo in `--when` (`variant:primray`, `siez:lg`) offers the same command with `--when` corrected. A saved one gets the undo, then that line, so the setting is kept.
- `undo <thing> <value>` with no `--mode` is refused when the setting is saved for one mode with another value, and names the saved value and its mode.
- `new --font 'Inter 600'` offers `--font Inter --headings semibold`, as `set` reads the same value.
- A saved entry that names its thing under `setting`, a saved entry with the setting and value the other way round, and a saved mode of `"both"` or `""` are read as `set` reads them typed, with a note, so the theme loads.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: repairs work when followed. A damaged mode or base with a second bad value in the list leads with the fix for that value, which also saves the mode or base as meant, and no repair offers a bare `undo` that would throw away the last change. A stored vibrancy is offered as a set only when a color dial is set, and the no-effect refusal names a token color as one vibrancy does not change. `undo` with a theme name typed in another form (`tTheme`, `T`, `brand_dark`) suggests the same undo with the theme's name. A missing name with a doubled or trailing dash suggests the cleaned name that `new` takes. The tracking half of headings listed twice is undone with `undo <theme> headings tracking`, the form that works. A trailing comma or a typographic dash in `--on` (`text-input,`, `text–input`) names that part, never its whole group. A light and dark color pair on `new` offers the user's own colors per mode, never a stock color. In a one-mode theme, a doubled entry for its own mode is kept with that `--mode`, which now replaces both entries.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a reset value typed with a typo on a part property (`display nnone`, `font-weight normall`) offers that value again (`none`, `normal`), since it is what was typed, corrected.

The response types reference describes the change result of `astryx experimental theme editor set` and `undo` as it is: `missed` counts the misses the change leaves and `missedParts` the parts they are on, and an undo of a setting listed more than once names the other entries it removed (`alsoRemoved`).

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a resting shadow on a part that draws rings in its box-shadow (an input's hover and focus rings, a status's ring) is written, and in each state Core rings it the theme's shadow comes with that ring after it, so the rings keep working; a shadow the theme sets for a state keeps its own. `how "sunken bevel on inputs"` answers with an inset bevel lit from the bottom right.

`astryx experimental theme editor` results say what the theme does: a mode's own setting under one for every mode names the one still drawing the other modes, with its undo; an inverted surface left as the base's is given the theme's own other-mode surface (a warm dark tooltip on a cream theme), or its surface in a one-mode theme; a token set on the top bar reaches the text over its ground, and a fix for that text stays in the top bar; a container's faint border, or a hairline where the base draws one too, is a choice, and a border or secondary text that needs a fix gets the nearest color that reads, not black or white; pills are listed as missed only when the corners go square; the open problems header and the missed count say which lines exist and where each miss is listed.

`astryx experimental theme editor` lists under missed a part where the base theme takes a role color away on its own, once the theme moves that role: the base pointing the role tokens at others there (an info banner drawn in the base's categorical blue), or a variant named for the role drawn in a color of the base's palette written out (an accent progress fill in a pale blue). Each line gives the part the theme's role color there.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: what is pasted is read as meant, and a repair carries the value given.
changesets.body:
- A repair never offers a stock value the input did not hold (a gray, a violet, `inter`, `system`, `1px`): a line that sets the same setting again carries the value typed or saved, cleaned, else `how` for the setting.
- A value labeled with a word that is not the setting's own name is refused with what the word means, never set with it dropped: a mode (`accent 'dark: #2563eb'` offers `--color-accent '#2563eb' --mode dark`), a state (set on a part with `--state`), a kind of screen (not set per screen), a part (`--on <part>`), a heading level (`headings 'h1: bold'` offers `font-weight 700 --on heading --when level:1`), or a word it does not read. The setting's own name before the value is the value (`font 'fontFamily: Inter, serif'`); a camelCase or quoted label of another setting names it.
- A size multiplied by a variable with a number fallback (`calc(0.75rem * var(--x, 1))`) is taken.
- CSS function names in any case are read (`LIGHT-DARK(…)`); a `light-dark()` with another separator offers the comma; a font list missing the comma before its generic family (`Georgia serif`) or with a spaced generic (`sans serif`) offers the list meant.
- A backslash before `#`, a quote or a space is taken off; a JavaScript escape in a `content` string is written as CSS writes it (`\u2022` is `\2022`); JSON arrays and design-token objects (`{"$value": …}`, `{"value": 18, "unit": "px"}`) are read as their value.
- `headings lighter` is the weight light; two headings words give one line each.
- The change receipt names a quote or space mark as its CSS escape, so text and JSON name the same value; a saved value in corner brackets is named as quoted, not as spaces.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: several values of one kind on a property that takes one (`margin-top '-4px -8px'`, `padding-top '1pt 2pt'`) are offered the first again, with its sign and any unit: the repair and the repair gate read "several values of one kind" through one shared reading.

`astryx experimental theme editor …`: a saved setting that writes one field two ways (`value` and `Value`, `on` and `--on`) is read the editor's way with a note naming both, and the next change writes the field once. A pasted declaration whose unquoted value went on past a space (`set t font=Inter, Arial`) is read whole, so the line offered with the theme left out works too.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: a saved font family in French quotes (`« Inter »`, with plain, no-break or narrow no-break spaces) is offered as `"Inter"`, the value set saves, not `" Inter "`.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: names saved in a spelling `--state` or `set` reads typed are read the same way, with a note naming the spelling saved. Before, every command refused the theme. This covers:

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `--only` now means one thing to `set` and to the settings reader. A saved `only` on a part that is styled on its own (as another editor version saved it) no longer stops the theme from opening. It is read and built as without it, which is what it means there, and one note says so; the next change saves it so. Where that puts it at the same place as a later entry of the same setting, the later one, the one the build shows, is kept, and the earlier one is named and left out. `set --only` reads it by the same rule.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a state saved in a spelling the editor reads (`aria-pressed` on toggle-button) is named by the part's own state (`--state isPressed`) in every line the editor offers, even before a change rewrites the saved entry.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: "lighter" or "darker" on a part's fill starts from the fill it shows at rest (its own setting first; never a pressed overlay), uses the amount asked and keeps a see-through color see-through. "except" keeps every excepted part or variant at the value it has now (its own shadow, its own weight) in one answer, says when a part reads none of what changes, and says when an excepted place is not a part. Sub-parts and catalog parts named in words go to that part ("dialog header", "dialog title", "code block header", "text inputs", "date pickers", "toggle buttons", "select boxes", "switches"); a sub-part Core lacks ("card header") is answered for the whole part, and the answer says so. "As round as", "the same padding as" and "match" copy the other part's value onto the first part only (an amount of it with "twice as round as"). Each clause keeps its own variant; a bare size in a list of text changes is the font size; "headings 20% bigger" scales every heading level from its own size; a font stack stays whole on the part; side words write only those padding sides; a part whose name has a state word ("hover card") is the part; "card text lighter" and "dialog text twice as big" get commands; a second part with an ask of its own keeps it; and a theme name near the one typed with `--theme` suggests the same question.

The agent block and the theme docs say a change to one kind of part (the sidebar, its selected item, the gaps in a form) is a theme change too, not props or styles on one page, and that `astryx experimental theme editor how "<ask>"` names the `set … --on <part>` line for it.

`astryx experimental theme editor` contrast-checks a change limited to one state or condition (a selected row's fill, an info banner's fill) like any other: the part's text is measured on its fill there in each mode, and a problem comes with the nearest readable color, set on what draws the text in that state or condition, instead of a "not checked" note.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a part kept to its container ("buttons inside cards", "headings in cards", "the card title", "the button groups' dividers") is answered only with a token the part reads, set on the container, which keeps it there ("headings in cards bigger" and "the card title bigger" set the heading sizes on the card); a part's own setting would reach every one, so then nothing is written, and the answer says why.
`astryx experimental theme editor set` and `new`:
changesets.body:
- A new part setting that writes the same token reference Core already uses there, at rest and in every state, such as `border-radius var(--radius-full) --on badge`, is no longer written, and the result says "[no change]". A setting whose value only matches what the part draws today, such as `corners pill --on badge` on a round badge, is written as the person's own choice, and the result says it matches and holds if that token changes.
- The "missed" line that `new` and `set` print near the top now says what it means: each part it names, with the variant and state (or at rest), still shows the base theme's own look where your changes did not reach. Keep each one, or bring it in line with the line `show` lists for it. The JSON lists the same places as `missedWhere`.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme`: the settings a theme's source extends are the settings module's own export, by identity anywhere up its `extends` chain, so a theme merely named like the settings is refused and one that reaches them through another theme is accepted. A source that stops loading is refused by `show` and never recorded as built. `compile` builds a family in a `font` shorthand like any font, leaves a family the app copy loads out of the full font help family by family, names a theme folder it cannot write with its fix, says in its JSON result the `--out` warnings text prints, and says that an editor theme's next set or show builds it without `--icons-specifier`. `set` and `show` give the install line for every built family nothing loads, a font token's included. A theme or an `extends` written as a helper's call or a conditional is named as what the build cannot follow, not as an inline icon registry.

`astryx experimental theme editor show --png` cuts a family's picture taller than 1600px into pictures of at most that height, in order (`sheet-inputs-1.png`, `-2` …), each cut between parts, so a reader takes each in whole. The pictures show a looping animation (a skeleton, a pulsing dot) at a frame a person sees, a status dot in its color, a vertical divider at a height, each table, code and app shell variant on a row of its own, and a section's sample text; a deprecated part, and a closed overlay the open states draw open (the mobile navigation drawer), are no longer drawn as empty cells.

`astryx experimental theme editor show` draws every part of the sheet and its pictures whole: a cell grows to what it holds instead of cutting variants at its bottom; a table, a code block and an app shell take the whole row; a looping animation (a skeleton, a pulsing dot) is drawn at rest; and a section or a form layout holds sample text instead of nothing.
`astryx experimental theme editor show` shows a look's overlays open and names the parts the look leaves unchanged:
changesets.body:
- The sheet's overlays section draws each tooltip, popover and hover card open beside its trigger, each drawer, bottom sheet and lightbox at its cell's size, and, open, each part another section holds whose control opens a menu or list (a dropdown menu, a selector, a tab menu), in light and dark, so its pictures show how a look styles them.
- `show` names, as `unreached`, the parts with a fill of their own the theme leaves on its base's look: no setting is on them, and their fill or text color is still the base's (for example toast, banner, badge).
- The author-a-theme guide opens with the theme editor, and a search for brand colors finds the theme topic.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a shorthand set for one mode points to commands that change that mode only.
changesets.body:
- A shorthand with a color longhand (`border`, `border-top`, `outline`, `text-decoration`, `background`) set with `--mode` points to its color longhand for that mode and its other words (width, style) for both modes, so following it never repaints the other mode; a named color counts as a color.
- A shadow's color for one mode is offered in the value as `light-dark()`: on a part with no shadow of its own, the other half `transparent`; on a shadow token, each layer's other half kept from what that mode shows, or a true reason when the layers differ.
- `set --help` and `undo --help` say a light-only or dark-only theme takes `--mode` for the other mode, which applies where Core draws that mode.
- A light-only or dark-only theme lists the other mode's token changes it writes.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor show --png` takes the sample page, the open states, and one picture for each family of components the theme sets a part of with `--on`, a group of parts counting as its parts (actions, inputs, selection, navigation, feedback, data or containers; the buttons when it sets none), each cut from the full sheet: `sheet-<family>.png` from the `sheet-<family>.html` it writes beside the sheet. A family taller than 1600px is cut between rows of parts into pictures of about that height, in order (`sheet-<family>-1.png`, `-2` …). The full sheet, every component, is still written as sheet.html but is no longer pictured as sheet.png, which was too tall to read whole. `show --section <family> --png` takes any other family. The result names the family pictures first among the pictures to open.
`astryx experimental theme editor show --theme <name>` (the form `set` and `undo` already repair) offers the show on that theme, saying the theme is show's first word, in place of its help alone.
`astryx experimental theme …`: starter apps, pages and pictures say and write what is true.
changesets.body:
- `preview app` with `--theme` given no value says so and offers only lines that work; with no folder, it offers a free folder name and its help.
- A starter on a variable Fontsource family no longer says it loads weight 400 only: the weights its stylesheet loads are read from the package, and no import of a file the package does not ship is offered.
- A starter leaves the theme folder's version control (`.git`) and installed packages (`node_modules`) out, with a note, and refuses before writing when an image url reaches its file through a link the copy does not follow.
- The overlays picture draws every example of a drawer, a bottom sheet and a lightbox.
- A file of yours at `preview.html`, `sheet.html` or a section's sheet is left alone and named, as one at `sheet-overlays.html` already was.
- `show` on a theme source that does not build offers the build failure's own way on.
- `set --png` names as removed only the pictures it did not take again, and `show --png --section` takes the open states too, as the help says.
- `preview remove` says when nothing was removed.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme preview remove` in an app made by `preview app` takes the starter home page's link to the removed preview, and names a home page changed by hand that still links there, instead of leaving a dead link with no word.
`astryx experimental theme` starters and pictures say and write what is true:
changesets.body:
- A starter's note for a font the CLI does not know names the stylesheet of each weight the theme uses, not the package's index sheet, which loads weight 400 alone.
- `show --png --section overlays` makes, photographs and lists the open states page once.
- A starter leaves out every version-control folder (Sapling, Bazaar, Pijul, CVS, Fossil and darcs beside Git, Mercurial, Subversion and Jujutsu).
- A pipe or a folder at the pictures record is left as it is and named, and no picture is taken; the editor's writer never replaces a pipe, a device or a socket.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme preview app --theme` judges an import written as a template literal with nothing put in it (``await import(`../shared.ts`)``) as the string it holds, so a theme file outside the theme folder, a Sass file or a name the new app cannot type is refused there as it is when quoted. A query or a hash on any module the theme imports (`./x.ts?raw`, `./d.json?raw`) is refused too, since the new app's type check reads it as part of the module's name.

With no app yet, the agent block, the theme docs and `astryx experimental theme --help` point to `astryx experimental theme preview app <dir>`, which makes a starter app that shows the theme, instead of building an app by hand.

`astryx experimental theme preview app --theme` refuses a theme that imports a stylesheet in a language other than CSS by the same list the theme build loads (Stylus, PostCSS and SugarSS beside Sass and Less), and with a query after it (`./brand.scss?inline`), before anything is written. Before, those starters were made and the new app's type check stopped at the import. A refusal that comes after the theme's stale build was made again puts that build back, so the refused command changes nothing, as it says.

`astryx experimental theme preview app --theme` refuses a theme that imports a file only a bundler loads by a name the new app's type check has no declaration for: a CSS file with a query or a hash (`./brand.css?inline`), an upper-case extension (`./brand.CSS`), or a font file (`./brand.woff2`). Before, the new app was made and its type check stopped at that import. The declarations it reads are the new app's own (`*.css`) and the pictures Next declares. A refused command that put back a build it made first now puts back each file's and folder's times too, so a dev server or watcher sees no change.

`astryx experimental theme preview app` refuses a starter whose theme reaches a file outside its folder with `import x = require('…')`, or with a `/// <reference path="…" />` at the top of a file, which the new app's type check reads, as for any import.
`astryx experimental theme editor show`'s `missed` and `unreached` lists name only what was missed, and each fix line works when followed:
changesets.body:
- A state is named only when the part draws it as a look of its own (a selected nav item's fill); a readonly field on its surface and a checked switch's thumb are drawn so on purpose.
- A setting takes a part off a list only when it covers the aspect the list is about (the resting fill or text color, the fill in that state, the corners, the border); a hover fill or a corner radius leaves it listed.
- The disabled button's line covers only the variant drawn as the accent, and recolors its label with its fill.
- A status fill's line generates that status color (`set <theme> info …`), never the accent.
- An inverted surface (a toast) is named only when it no longer stands out from the page, with how's answer for it.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: state settings keep the base theme's other state styles, one-mode halves across the background family and states, and one-mode tokens that are no color.
changesets.body:
- A state setting (a hover text color, say) keeps the base theme's other styles in that state, such as a variant's own hover background, in both modes.
- A one-mode color in a state keeps, in the other mode, what that state shows there: its own value, else the resting color a setting gives the variant or the part, else the base theme's.
- `background` and `background-color` count as one property for one-mode settings: a variant's earlier color is kept as the other half and replaced, and a later both-mode color replaces a one-mode one of the other name.
- A one-mode color in a state is accepted where the base theme gives the part that color.
- In a `light-only` or `dark-only` theme, a token that is no color (a shadow) is written as one value, never as a light and dark pair.
- When `--mode` is refused in a one-mode theme, the offered command keeps `--when` and `--state`, and offers `mode both` first for the mode the theme does not show.
- The spacing dial reads kept sizes in pt, pc, in, cm, mm, Q and em, in any letter case, and keeps a variant's own exact size in order on that variant.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: "the card fill" is the card's own background, never a part inside it; "the text after the checkbox" is its label; "the table's header cells" are the table's header cells; an unknown word before a part's piece ("the card zorp title") is said and nothing is written; a second state a part does not have ("the selected and hovered menu items") is said, never dropped; "the inputs in dialogs" are the inputs, never a command palette's; "the separators of menus" are the menu's own divider; "the card headings" are the card's title, kept to the card.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- `how` keeps a state where another of the part's own states was changed only where both hold: a checked, disabled checkbox keeps Core's fill, and an unchecked one is left alone.
- A long answer is cut only between whole asks; the rest follows as the next runnable sequences.
- "remove the underline from tabs" makes the tab's indicator transparent where it paints.
- An input's focus ring is its box-shadow ring for a color, a width or a removal; in one mode only that mode changes, and status fields, which draw no ring while focused, keep none.
- A resting shadow on ringed parts keeps each render's own focus look, for every variant (selectors included) and for a write scoped to one status.
- A piece of a part Core has no part for ("the popover arrow", "the empty state icon", "sheet titles") is named and nothing is written for the whole part; a sheet is the bottom sheet, and an alert's title is the banner's own text.
- A toast's text color refused in one mode keeps that mode on the lines it offers.
- The corners help lists the step between round and pill among its rungs.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: several states saved joined by `+` with spaces around it (`"selected + hover"`) are read as those states, as `--state` reads them typed, with a note. Before, every command refused the theme.
changesets.body: A part's own state saved by hand in a spelling the editor reads (`is-pressed` on button) no longer leaves `compile` refusing after `show`: the build reads the state, and the settings stay as saved until a change writes the part's spelling.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a `--when` or `--state` typo, or another case, on a group (`--on inputs --when status:eror`, `--on checks --state chekced`) gets the corrected command, read against what the group's members have between them, as the same typo on one part does. A setting's name typed where the theme goes gets a command on the theme here (`show accent` offers `show t`, `set corners pill` offers `set t corners pill`, `undo corners` that no theme holds offers `show t`), never a theme of the setting's name; `undo t accent corners spacing` reads the bare words as a list; and an unknown subcommand followed by an option (`experimental theme preview path --theme t`) is named as the unknown subcommand, with the near ones.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- States Core paints from an ARIA attribute are states `set` names: `current` (a pagination's current page), `pressed` and `expanded` (an open menu button), built as that attribute.
- Several states at once (`--state checked+disabled`) are taken where Core paints them together, and `how` names them that way.

The open states picture shows the states first, and show's result says so; a popover that holds a form is no longer cut at its cell's edge.

`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- `how` colors a table's row lines ("table row dividers red", "table borders red") through the color its cells draw them with, set on the row; never the Divider part, a row fill or a border over the cells.

changesets.body:

- `how "selected table row light blue"` answers `--color-accent-muted <color> --on table-row --state selected`, and a background on a selected table row, which Core's inline wash would hide, is refused with that command.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the text result names a setting with the API's own wording, so an entry saved with no value is removed as "(no value)", never "undefined".

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: an answer that writes a panel's look for every one (a card's) says once that the cards an app places in a carousel, a grid or a stack take it too, and names the place to ask for to keep them apart.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: `how` reads "<part> title" (and header) after any part the census knows, of one word or more ("the empty state title"), as that part's own title part, never as every heading; "bigger" on a part that is only text is its text size, so "the empty state title red and bigger" colors and sizes the title text.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- `how`: a dialog's or drawer's title is colored, made bold or bigger through the text tokens on its title block, never on every heading; a title Core has no part for (a card's) is said so. A weight, size or color set on a part whose text is all in parts inside it that set their own is refused with those tokens.
- `how`: an alpha said of a shadow ("card shadows with 30% alpha", "50% transparent") sets its colors' alpha in every layer the part shows; a part's shadow in a state is read from that state at its default status (an input's own hover ring, never the error ring), never from a hidden layer; a ring with no blur softens through its alpha.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`'s sheet, preview and pictures draw a toast's text on the side the app's own measurement picks for the fill the toast draws, by the rule the contrast checks use: light text on a dark fill, dark text on a light one, in each mode and for each type a fill is set for (an error toast's own fill read apart), so the pictures match the app and the checks.
`astryx experimental theme editor`:
changesets.body:
- A toast's text takes its own `color` on the toast: it goes into the two colors Core's media surface gives the toast's text, on the toast alone, so the lightbox and the scrim keep theirs. A text color token on the toast is refused with that line.
- Text on a one-layer linear or radial gradient is measured on the color under the text (the gradient's middle or center), so a glossy highlight at an edge is not taken for the ground.

A line is offered only where it changes the built theme.
- The inverted-surface line in `missed` gives the inverted surface to the part alone, with its text readable on it, and a variant with a fill of its own (an error toast) keeps readable text.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a setting on toggle-button's own pressed state (`--state isPressed`) is built on the attribute value ToggleButton writes, `[data-is-pressed="true"]`, so it now applies; before, it was built on `[data-is-pressed="isPressed"]`, which never matches. A part's state that names a boolean prop of its component is built as that prop's "true" value; any other state is built as its own name, as before.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the check of a theme's own values judges every block the build writes from. Each adaptation rule's tokens, local tokens and parts are judged, named as the file writes them (`adaptations.rules[0].value…`); a `var()` reads the custom properties the theme sets in `tokens` and `localTokens`; a part's property given as text gets the check `set` gives it, a property that reads a design token of a kind it does not take (`background-color: var(--radius-element)`) is refused in `set` and in the file alike, and a misspelled property is refused with the one meant; and a theme the source defines between the editor's settings and the exported theme is judged too, by its name and line. In typography, a weight with no type scale (which builds nothing) is named with the scale it needs, a weight refusal names the weight field, and a scale field that is no number is named as written (a symbol, `NaN`, `true`), never a crash.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the check of a theme's own token values judges what a build made now writes, through one path for `show`, `set`, `undo` and `compile`. A value from an import, an expression, a spread or a computed key is judged by its built value; only the value a later key keeps counts; a pair is judged as the `light-dark()` it builds. The source is read only to name the file and line that hold each value (an imported file is named, not the theme file) and for what a build erases: a second `tokens` key, and a pair with other than two values. Typography is judged by the values the build was given: a scale base with a unit (which builds `NaNrem`) is refused with the number of pixels it means, a scale with a ratio and no base is named, a family written in quotes or holding `; { } < >` is refused with the working form, and `fallbacks` is checked as part of the family list it builds. A family set through typography no longer gets the phone note.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the check of a theme's own token values judges every token its source gives, a design token or the theme's own custom property, and a part's CSS properties: `null`, a boolean, an object or a number a property does not take bare is refused as no text, with its file and line, in `compile`, `set` and `show` alike. A BigInt or a symbol is named as it is (never a crash), a page token left `undefined` is not set (in a part's rule, where the build writes the text `undefined`, it is named), and a `var()` reads the custom properties the theme itself sets.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the check of a theme's own token values judges the input its source gives `defineTheme()`, evaluated as a build evaluates the module, so a value the build would drop or Core would refuse is named before anything is written. `null` and booleans are refused as no text; a value under a computed key is judged before the build drops it; a typography weight given as a number names its field and the quoted form; and the tokens a part's blocks in `components`, `onDark`, `onLight` and adaptation rules set are judged like page-wide tokens, each named by its scope and line.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a token family follows the token it is made from. A surface the theme sets (`--color-background-surface`) now carries the fills made from it, cards, popovers and menus, the muted fill (table stripes), code blocks and skeletons, at the base theme's lightness step from it; an opaque `--color-border` carries `--color-border-emphasized`, so inputs and selectors frame like cards; and the neutral color now reaches the page (`--color-background-body`, the app shell's header and side nav) at the official theme's step, as it reaches the cards. A token the theme pins, by a setting or its own source, always keeps its value.

`astryx experimental theme editor new` offers a free name for a token's name typed where the theme's name goes, with or without its dashes (`new Color-Accent`, `new --radius-element`), as it already does for a dial's name: the editor reads a token by either spelling, so neither is a theme to make. A name of its own (`new Brand`) still reads as that name.

`astryx experimental theme editor set` says when a token set on a part is read there only under a condition the part is not drawn in by default (a link reads `--color-text-primary` only as `color primary`): it changes nothing in the default look, and the note names the token that look reads (`--color-text-accent`) and the condition that reads this one, each with its line.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a token value your `<theme>.theme.ts` gives is checked entry by entry as written, and `show` and `compile` refuse with one message. A number (`'--radius-page': 12`) is named as not text, as `show` already said; a `--font-family-*` token is checked like `set` checks it (a family list wholly in quotes, as Core returns one, is taken); each half of a `[light, dark]` pair is checked; a computed key that is text (`['--radius-page']`) is read like a literal one, and one the editor cannot read is named as not checked. The refusal names the line that sets the token, never a comment that mentions it.

`astryx experimental theme`: tokens of the theme's own that read each other (`--a1: var(--a2)`, `--a2: var(--a1)`) are refused at their line, as a token that reads itself is. A token in `onDark` or `onLight` is judged against what that surface sets, so a surface token that reads a token the page sets from it is accepted.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the sheet and its pictures show a typeahead's list open. The render loads React DOM's client with a document in place before the page (a part that loads it with the page, such as a toast, loaded it with none, so typing never reached a field's change handler), types as a person types, and opens a typeahead's open look without waiting for its search delay.

`astryx experimental theme`: more typed and pasted forms are read as meant. A part named beside a property's value (`set my padding 'card 8px'`, `'red on buttons'`, `'button:hover: red'`) gets the line on that part and state; the editor's own result line pasted with its head (`[ok] my: corners = pill (whole theme)`) is read; `new`'s settings written as pairs apart at commas (`'like: neutral, corners: pill'`) keep every pair; a base with a stray quote or comma (`--like "neutral'"`) gets its line without a did-you-mean for the same word; and a font family whose last word names a weight (`'Bodoni Moda Bold'`) is kept as typed with the family and weight lines in a note.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: every repair reads a typo of a typed value, setting, part, state or theme or token name the same way: within one letter for a word of five letters or fewer and two for a longer one, two letters swapped counting as one. So `border-style line` is no longer offered `none`, and `display flxe` is offered `flex`, never `flow`; `nnone` and `normall` are still corrected. The words of a `how` question keep their own spelling reading.

`astryx experimental theme editor set`: a part drawn under an invisible native input (a checkbox's or radio's box, a switch), which the part data now records, refuses a hover, press or focus state, which would never apply there, naming the part that holds the input; for a token, the same token with no state, which Core reads when it paints that state from the input, is offered.

`astryx experimental theme editor undo`: the headline names what the undo took back (`[ok] v: undid neutral = #78716c (whole theme)`, or `undid 2 changes: …`), in the text and in the JSON (`undid`), so a tail of the output keeps it. When the last change command was refused, the undo says that command changed nothing, so it took back the change before it (`refusedBefore`).

`astryx experimental theme editor undo`: with no `--mode`, a setting saved for one mode only is removed, and the result names its mode; one saved for each mode gets an undo line per mode instead of a refusal that contradicts itself.

`astryx experimental theme …`: undo and pasted forms are read as typed. `undo t 'cornres pill'` names the setting the typo means, and a setting the theme does not hold gets `show`, never a step back that would remove another change. Bare words for undo that are a held setting's value (`corners pill accent`) are read as that value. A setting's name where the theme goes, in other letters or as a token (`undo Corners`, `undo --color-accent`, `show Corners`), offers the themes to look at, never a new theme of that name. Several lines pasted as one argument give one line each. An empty pasted object with a separator (`{,}`) points to the dials. A pasted label that is a part typo (`(crad)`) is read as that part and a state (`(hover)`) as the state; a label that is no mode is never dropped for a line that changes both modes. A damaged saved entry beside a clean one of the same scope gets only its undo, never a set over the clean entry.

`astryx experimental theme editor set … font`: a family the editor does not know is kept as typed (Corben, Gabriela, Candal are real families, no typos of Corbel, Gabriola, Candara), with a note giving the line that sets the font a system ships spelled near it. A typo of a font preset is refused with the preset, a name listed both as a preset and a system font counted once (`Gerogia` reads as georgia), and the presets are read before the system fonts near it (`Corier` is courier, `Monlo` mono). Arial Narrow and Andale Mono are noted as fonts only macOS ships.
`astryx experimental theme editor` and `compile` name more of what a theme's own source misspells or misplaces, each with its file and line:

`astryx experimental theme editor`: lines the editor offers run as offered. `undo` with a value one mode holds removes that mode's entry, and an undo of one of two settings says what each mode shows now; a theme typed second gets no line for a theme that does not exist; a dial or property name a letter off (`cornres`, `paddng`) gets its set line, with the value and scope kept; saved entries with their field names in other letters (`Thing`, `Value`) are read; a design token with a fallback (`var(--color-error, red)`) is offered as typed; and a setting typed where the theme goes (`undo accent`) gets that theme's undo, never a new theme of the setting's name.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` value questions read the status or state they name: "what is the border of error inputs in dark mode" gives the error border, "…of focused inputs" the focused one and "…of selected cards" the selected one, instead of the plain rule's value; "how thick is the input focus ring" gives the ring's width with how it is drawn.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a value your `<theme>.theme.ts` leaves `undefined` is taken as not set wherever it is (a token on the page, in `onDark`/`onLight` or in an adaptation rule, a part, a style key, a property), now that the theme build writes nothing for it. A part given `null` (or another value that is no block of style keys) is refused at its line, at the root and in `onDark`/`onLight`, instead of failing the build.

`astryx experimental theme`: a token in `onDark` or `onLight` that loops through a token Core sets on that surface itself (`--color-on-dark: var(--color-text-primary)`, while Core's dark surface sets `--color-text-primary: var(--color-on-dark)`) is refused at its line.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a value question ("how thick are dividers", "how round are the cards now?") reads a token set on the part itself (or its group) before the theme's own value, so it answers what the part shows.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a `var()` is read as CSS reads it. Glued after a letter or a digit (`padding '2var(--spacing-4)'`), CSS reads no reference there, so the value is refused instead of written as a value the browser drops. Text glued after it (`'var(--spacing-4)px'`, `'8pxvar(--spacing-4)'`) is refused for the value's grammar, not as the token being the wrong kind, and the refusal no longer offers the same input again.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a `var()` with spaces inside its brackets (`background-color 'var( --color-accent )'`) is read as CSS reads it, the same as `var(--color-accent)`. Before, every color refused it as no color.

`astryx experimental theme editor how` reads three more kinds of words as what they say: a weight word before the text it describes, however many words about the text sit between ("thin elegant headings" is the weight, never a border around every heading); "reader" and "readers", which are no longer corrected to "header", so a book-reader ask changes the theme and not the app shell header; and a CSS custom property pasted from a stylesheet, whose last words name what it sets (`--brand-bg` is a background, `--brand-text` the text color), never the prefix a codebase repeats on every one of them.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: one reading for each kind of word. A mode is read one way everywhere (the `--mode` flag, a mode label in a value, a saved entry's mode and the settings file's mode): light or dark in its written forms, or day, daytime, night or nighttime; black, white, dim and bright are no longer read as modes. A base is read one way by `new`, set and the settings file. A `new` on a base that is not installed leads with the install, then the same `new` on that base, as set does. `how` reads state words from one table. A font file in a family list is found with the one family-list reader.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: "table headers" (plural) are the table's header cells, never its rows; "menus" said plainly is every menu (the menus group); a tab's underline asked for a color or a thickness ("a 2px black underline when selected") is its indicator's fill and height, never a text decoration it has no text for.
`astryx experimental export`: the file drops the web font faces that no character in the page, its stylesheet or its script reaches, so a page with a web font is smaller.
changesets.body:
- A font package ships one face per script (Latin, Latin Extended, Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese) for each weight. A browser loads only the faces its text needs, but the file used to carry all of them. A page that imports a font package and never uses its family now carries none of its faces. An English page that uses two weights of a font package is 10% smaller.
- A face stays when its font family is named outside the faces (in a rule, a token, the markup or the script) and its `unicode-range` covers a character the page can draw: one in the markup, the script or the stylesheet (a `content` string). A character written as an escape (`\u039a` in the script, `\41f` in a stylesheet) counts too, so text that a later view, a menu or a hover shows keeps its face. A family name counts as CSS reads it (`Gill\ Sans` is `'Gill Sans'`), also when the script holds it as escapes. A list or counter style with other letters (`lower-greek`, a `@counter-style`), or a `text-transform` that changes the characters (`full-width`), keeps every face of a named family, whether the stylesheet (directly or in a custom property), the markup or the script sets it. Each character's other cases count too, for `uppercase`.
- The cut runs before the font files are read, so a dropped face is not counted in `images` and gives no missing-file or network warning.
- Some text is not in the file, so no face is kept for it: text a reader types, text the script builds from character codes, and text the browser writes in the reader's or the page's locale (a date field's placeholder, Intl-formatted dates and numbers). Such text in a script that no kept face covers is drawn with the next font in the family list.
- Only the exported file is cut. The theme editor's previews keep every face, so text typed into them draws in its font.

changesets.headline: The export guide says that the exported file's CSS keeps only the web font faces its page, stylesheet or script can use, and that text the file cannot know (typed text, text built from character codes, and dates, numbers and date-field placeholders in the reader's or the page's locale) draws in the next font of its font list.
The export guide's column-floor advice says a table heading wraps like its cells, so a column's floor must fit the longest word of its heading.

`astryx experimental export`: a page whose root theme draws in one mode stays readable in a viewer of the other scheme. Before, the file declared both color schemes, so a dark viewer showed its dark canvas behind a light-only theme's dark text. The export reads the theme module's `colorModes` export when it has one, without running the module. Otherwise it reads the page or text colors the theme's compiled stylesheet, which the page imports (directly or through an `@import` in its own CSS), sets on its root: a light page with dark text draws in light only, and a dark page with light text in dark only. Any color the theme editor reads counts (hex, a named color, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `oklch()` and the other CSS color forms). A theme that sets neither (a fonts-only or accent-only theme), sets a `light-dark()` color (a value for each mode), sets one the export cannot fix (such as a `var()`), or sets any page or text color under a light or dark condition keeps both modes, as before. A one-mode page declares only that scheme and paints the theme's own page color on the document. For a theme passed to `Theme` unbuilt, whose CSS is injected only at run time, only what the page's own stylesheets set on that theme's root counts. A page whose theme draws in both modes, or that has no theme, is written as before.

`astryx experimental export` treats a package that `node_modules` links to a folder inside the project (`npm link`, a `file:` dependency, a workspace package) as a package: the file no longer carries its modules as page files, so `--reverse` gives the page back exactly instead of refusing it. The page looks and runs the same.

`astryx experimental export` reads the page's packages faster. Node looks up the package scope of every module it loads and parses a package's exports map again for each one, so a page that loads hundreds of Core's modules parsed Core's exports map hundreds of times. The export now resolves an import between two files of one installed package by its path, and reads each folder's package.json at most once. Every other import, and every import of the page's own files, resolves as before. Exported files do not change.

`astryx experimental export` compiles the StyleX in a package that ships StyleX source, as an app's build does. A component from such a package, installed or linked in from a workspace, that uses `stylex.keyframes`, `stylex.defineVars`, `stylex.createTheme` or `stylex.firstThatWorks` used to fail with "Unexpected 'stylex.keyframes' call at runtime". Its styles now compile with the page's own class-name prefix, so they never share a class with Core's, and its animations run in the exported file. A file of the package that the page loads lazily carries its styles too. A package that ships compiled StyleX stays as it ships.

`astryx experimental export` loads a page whose modules import a `.tsx` file by its `.js` name (`./parts/Kpi.js` for `Kpi.tsx`), which used to fail with `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`. `--reverse` gives back a page whose modules import any TypeScript file by its JavaScript name (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`), which it used to refuse as damaged. A file in which such an import is relative says render format 3, so an earlier CLI names the CLI that reads it instead of calling it damaged; one through a path alias (`@/lib/rows.js`) keeps format 1.

`astryx experimental export` refuses a page that uses no Astryx components or styles, with `ERR_RENDER_NOT_ASTRYX`, exit 1 and nothing written: "page.tsx uses no Astryx components or styles; `astryx experimental export` only writes pages built with Astryx. Don't add Astryx to this app to export it: share the page with the app's own build instead (for a Vite app, a single-file build); nothing was written." The page's own script decides: a page counts as Astryx when any module its script holds belongs to an Astryx package (imported directly, through a local component or a re-export, or lazily), or when it imports an Astryx stylesheet. The theme editor's previews are unchanged.

`astryx experimental export --reverse`: an image a carried module names with percent-escapes (`/pics/a%20b.png`, `./c%20d.png`) is expected back as the file those escapes name ("a b.png"), the file the export read and carried. Before, `--reverse` restored the file but listed the escaped name as missing and reported the restore as not exact. The export also carries such an image when the page draws it only later (after a click), so it shows from the file. An image the page imports, or loads with `import()` or `require()`, by such a name is carried and followed as written, as before.

Outside a project, `astryx experimental export` loads a subpath that a package from its package set exports only under the `import` condition, as a theme package's `./themes/<name>` often is. Such a page used to fail as if the package were not installed. A subpath the package does not export keeps the answer it had.

`astryx experimental export`: the warning for something the page loads from outside the file says so in the words the Checks section uses, which fit a file beside the page as well as a remote address. The share-a-page guide points to the Checks section the export prints instead of a separate reverse run.

`astryx experimental export` warns when text inside an SVG drawing that scales to its box would show under 10 px on a 375 px phone, because the text shrinks with the drawing. The share-a-page guide says how to keep chart labels readable.

A run that prints its answer and then exits 1 records the code that answer carries in its debug event, as an error that `cliError` prints does. A component batch with a selector that does not resolve records the first unresolved row's code (such as `ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT`); `theme build --check` that finds stale outputs records `ERR_THEME_STALE`; `upgrade` records the code of an error it reports in text mode, and the `errorCode` of a run that stops incomplete (such as `ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED`), in text and in `--json`; `init` that refuses its agent-docs path records `ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL`. Each code is recorded once the answer is printed, so an error that stops the answer first (a recorded theme that does not load) keeps its own code. A `debug` handler saw these runs as `ERR_UNCLASSIFIED_EXIT`. Output and exit codes are unchanged.

Field labels use the primary text colour. A label names its control, so it now reads at full strength, while its description and the Optional or Required marker stay in the secondary colour. Before, the label and its description shared one colour.

Field labels use the semibold weight. Arial, Helvetica, Liberation Sans, and Segoe UI have no medium face, so a medium label drew in their regular face, at the same weight as its description. The label now draws in the next heavier face: semibold in Segoe UI, bold in Arial, Helvetica, and Liberation Sans. With fonts that have a medium face, such as the Apple and Android system fonts and the first-party theme fonts, labels become one step heavier. CheckboxInput and Switch labels use the same label style and change too.

A machine's first `search` or `build` run, and its first `component`, `template`, `theme`, `discover` or `docs` run in a project where an integration can load, now keeps what it gathers, and Node's compile cache is written from the first run. With the CLI installed in the project, the second command on a new machine (most often the same session's next one) reads them instead of gathering again: about 1.7 s faster for `search` and 0.8 s for `component` in a project with an integration. A global copy with no Core beside it starts installing its Core after its first run, which changes what the next run reads, so it reads from its third run, as before. Answers do not change; `doctor`'s "Kept catalog cache" row counts the entries the first run now keeps.

Malformed component icon slot values no longer throw while formatting diagnostics. Invalid fields keep the component fallback without dropping valid sibling fields, and production skips diagnostic formatting.
MultiSelector's caller-rendered trigger exposes its disabled state and blocks caller activation handlers, including when read-only or disabled by InputGroup, while remaining focusable.

`astryx theme use <theme>` opens its receipt with the default it set: "[ok] <theme> is now the app's default theme: themes[defaultThemeSlug] is <theme>.", or "[ok] <theme> was already the app's default theme; nothing changed." when it was the default already. The receipt's fields are unchanged, and the JSON is unchanged.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> surfaces flat`: in a mode where the theme gives a panel a fill of its own (white cards in light mode), the panel shows that fill, so its pieces (a gray badge's pill, the muted fill) stay as they are there instead of being drawn in the card's color and vanishing on it.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> surfaces flat` keeps its tinted panels, and the gray pieces inside a panel drawn in the tint's color (a neutral badge, a progress or switch track) are drawn in the panel's own surface there instead, so they stay visible; colored fills keep their hue, and the emphasized border is stepped inside the panel where it would stand out less from the tint than from the panel's surface.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: under `surfaces flat`, menus, popovers, select lists, hover cards, dialogs and drawers, which float over the page, keep their own fill and get a hairline `--color-border` edge instead of the page's tint with no edge (cards and the banner keep flat's tinted look). A floating panel a theme leaves within 1.1:1 of the page with no border or shadow is now a problem, with a line that adds a 1px border.

An `Item` with its own `onClick` or `href` no longer rings the whole row when a control in its `startContent` or `endContent` takes focus, and a `Token`'s remove button no longer rings the whole token: each of those tab stops shows one focus ring. Rows that delegate to a nested control, and reorderable rows with a handle, keep their ring as before.

Tab moves through a `Popover` or a `DropdownMenu` that opens inside a native `<dialog>` that the page displays closed. Tab and Shift+Tab wrap at the layer's edges, and a `DropdownMenu`'s header and footer are Tab stops again. The focus trap counted every control in a closed dialog as hidden, so it found no Tab stops and held focus in place.
changesets.body: A closed dialog that the page displays has a box, so its controls are Tab stops. A closed dialog with `display: none` has no box, and its controls stay out of the Tab cycle.

changesets.headline: The payment form template's Remove link on each cart line now asks for confirmation first. After you confirm, a demo message says what would happen; Cancel does nothing.

The `form-wizard-vertical` template declares its review banner icon as `review`, which icon sets draw as `info`, the meaning the banner shows, instead of `checkDouble`. A project whose icon set draws template icons by meaning now gets that set's info icon in the banner. A project whose main set wraps `@heroicons/react` keeps the check badge unless it picks a variant, and copies without an icon set are unchanged.
The vertical form wizard's cover buttons keep their full labels on every phone width: the dropzone column moves under the cover before "Preview on device" would be cut.

Buttons in form page templates that did nothing now show a demo message that says what would happen: Cancel in the workspace and audiobook wizards, Create workspace and Submit for review on a finished last step, Place Order on a complete payment form, and Save on the payment form's cart line.

In a fresh clone (a project that lists `@astryxdesign/core` and a theme package, with nothing installed yet), `astryx doctor` now says to install the project's dependencies, such as `npm install`, for a missing Core and a missing theme package. Before, its fixes added Core with no version and the theme package at the latest release, so following them replaced the project's versions with others.

In a fresh clone whose `package.json` lists `@astryxdesign/cli`, the once-a-day hint, `doctor`, and the setup reminder now say to install the project's dependencies (such as `npm install`), not to add the CLI again. Adding it again replaced the exact version the project lists with a range, such as `^0.7.10`.

A mouse drag in a page shown in a sandboxed frame (such as an embed or a viewer) that is released outside the browser window now ends when the pointer comes back over the frame or presses again. Before, a Slider thumb or a pan stayed held and followed the pointer with no button down.

File protection now decodes consecutive octal escapes in quoted `.gitattributes` paths as UTF-8 bytes. Before, a rule such as `"caf\303\251.js" linguist-generated` was treated as separate code points and failed to protect the matching `café.js` file; quoted and literal UTF-8 spellings now classify consistently.

In a Yarn Plug'n'Play project, the `astryx` command installed for the computer hands each run to the project's own CLI: it starts again with the project's runtime, as Yarn starts a command, instead of answering with its own release and telling you to install a CLI the project already has. Commands the CLI prints there start with `yarn astryx`, not with a `yarn dlx` download of the CLI.

Palette recipe `astryx-oklch-v2`: a gray family's color now fades toward white the way a gray scale's does, so a colored gray (a slate `#64748b`, a warm `#78716c`) gives the page and the cards on it only a faint tint instead of a clearly blue or cream page; its darker shades keep their color. v1, and so every shipped palette and existing config, is unchanged. The neutral dial's help says so, and names `--color-background-body` for a clearly tinted page.

Two page templates no longer leave an empty column on wide screens. The product gallery's header (a heading and its intro) now fills two columns instead of three, and the two-column form's contact strip fills three columns instead of four, so it sits centered. Narrower widths are unchanged.

Grid's docs say that `columns={{minWidth}}` alone keeps each column at its track width, so a grid with fewer items than tracks keeps an empty column, and that `repeat: 'fit'`, or a `max` no more than the item count, lets the items grow to fill the row.

Grid: `columns={{minWidth}}` without `max` no longer overflows a container narrower than `minWidth`. A lone column now shrinks to the container width, as it already did with `max`, so a phone no longer scrolls sideways. In a container that takes its width from its content (an inline-block, or a flex item with no width), an uncapped Grid is now as wide as its content instead of `minWidth`, as a capped Grid already was.

Page template headers on a phone: when a page title and its action do not fit one row, the action moves under the title instead of squeezing it, in the service-jobs table and the grouped issues table. Wide screens look the same as before.

A Markdown heading's copy-link button now shows when the clipboard write fails, as CodeBlock's copy button does: the `#` becomes a cross for 1.5 seconds, and the button is named and announces "Failed to copy value to clipboard." It used to fail silently and leave `#` unchanged. The error itself is not shown.

`Heading` without a `level` from 1 to 6 renders as an `h2` and warns in development, instead of failing with "Element type is invalid". A numeric string such as `level="3"` keeps rendering its level, and now warns in development.

`astryx --help` now describes `export` in the `experimental` group as "one self-contained HTML file from a page built with Astryx components (not for other pages)". Agents can now tell from the help what `experimental export` makes and which pages it is for.

The hero and gallery page templates' call-to-action buttons (Get started, Learn more, Explore in `centered-hero`, `gallery-hero`, `product-gallery` and `side-gallery`) are now links to `#`, so they behave as the links they stand in for instead of doing nothing. The Get started arrows in `centered-hero` and `product-gallery` now point toward the end of the line in right-to-left, as in `gallery-hero`; nothing else changes in layout or styling.

Hook docs for `useChatDictation`, so `astryx hook useChatDictation` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useChatDictation — Voice input` example block: a start and stop control that stays off when the browser has no speech recognition.

Hook docs for `useChatPasteAsToken`, so `astryx hook useChatPasteAsToken` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useChatPasteAsToken — Long paste` example block: a composer that uses a threshold of 40 and a Pasted note label.

Hook docs for `useSpeechRecognition`, so `astryx hook useSpeechRecognition` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useSpeechRecognition — Transcript` example block: a headless control that shows whether the browser can listen and the interim transcript.

Hook docs for `useSyntaxTheme`, so `astryx hook useSyntaxTheme` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useSyntaxTheme — Keyword color` example block: the word const painted with the keyword color of the GitHub Light syntax theme.

A run through `@astryxdesign/cli/host` now keeps what it gathers, as a run of the `astryx` bin does, so a tool that carries the CLI answers its second `search` from the kept catalog: about 0.47 s instead of 1.4 s. A kept entry names the package sets, integrations and command name the host passed, so a hosted run and a bin run in the same folder never read each other's answers. Answers do not change.

Reading the locale or direction with `useLocale`, `useDirection` or `useCollator` no longer loads the message parser: `useLocale` alone bundles to 441 bytes gzip instead of 10,250. A page that translates any Astryx string still loads the parser, as before. Translation output, with or without a provider, is unchanged for copies of one Core version.

The internationalization guide says provider `overrides` change Astryx wording across an app, and that a component is reworded through its own prop for that string, such as `placeholder` or `cancelLabel`. The InternationalizationProvider overrides example applies its override to every Selector in the app, and shows one Selector rewording its own placeholder through its prop.
The `InternationalizationProvider` example that changes one Astryx string is titled for a change across the app, not a change to one component.

Built-in text in six components that was fixed English now follows the locale. Through the catalog, so a provider's translation or override replaces it: Tokenizer's `+N more` overflow count, Slider's screen-reader "Required", CodeBlock's `<language> diff` header label, the default label of a token made by `useChatPasteAsToken` (the same message the pasted-text chip uses), and the relative-date choices in PowerSearch's popover editor (the touch sheet already translated them). Through the locale's own unit formatting: Timer's elapsed durations, which read `34s`, `2m 08s` and `1h 05m` in English as before and use the locale's unit names elsewhere (German `2 Min., 08 Sek.`). Other English output is unchanged, except that Tokenizer groups the digits of a count of 1,000 or more; Timer's units are never grouped (`1000h 05m`, as before). Shipped locales show English for the new catalog keys until translators add them.
