An `astryx experimental icon` subcommand typed alone, such as `astryx experimental icon add`, now finds icons for its name when an icon (or, with no icon set installed, an icon definition) matches the whole name, as `astryx experimental icon <words>` does, and names the subcommand's usage on one more line. Otherwise the subcommand keeps its error and names the search. Outside a project, a subcommand that needs one still refuses. A subcommand given an argument or an option runs as before.

Icon definitions: five descriptions now name only the job the icon does. `scale` no longer describes its drawing; `wrench` no longer reads as a second `settings` (it means tools for a technical fix or setup); `cloud` drops weather; `globe` drops language, which has its own definition; and `mail` is about email rather than a message inbox.

Icon definitions: a definition can name its `group`, the family of related meanings it belongs to (for example `notification`, `notificationActive`, and `notificationOff`), and Astryx's definitions now name theirs. A set's own definition may join an Astryx group or name its own. `experimental icon --definitions` shows each definition's group; each finder match gains `relatives`, the other definitions in its group with what each means (the text answer names a few under the first match only); with no set installed, each matching definition gains `group` and `relatives`; and a definition's docs page names its group's other members. Groups are information only: ranking does not change, and stable commands print what they printed before.

Icon definitions can declare `replaces`: the name of an older definition they take the place of. The old name keeps answering, through every later replacement: an icon set's `map` key that uses it maps the new definition, a template's `icons` value and a definition named to `experimental icon map` or `add` mean the new one, and `astryx experimental icon <old name>` finds the icon drawn for the new one. `integration check` warns with each `map` key to rename (`icon_definition_replaced`), the next `experimental icon map` writes the new name, and `astryx doctor` warns when an installed set still uses an old key. `experimental icon --definitions` and the definition's docs page show what it replaces.

Icon definitions: `message` no longer lists `conversation` and `textCase` no longer lists `uppercase` or `lowercase` among its words. Each of those words is another definition's name, so a search for it now lists only that definition.

Where icon features are on (an icon-set package is installed or `experimental.iconSet` is set), the agent block that `astryx init` and `astryx upgrade` write adds one line under the runner line: "Need an icon? Run `astryx experimental icon <what it means>` and paste the import it prints, instead of copying one from a template or other code." Where they are off, the block does not change.

`astryx experimental icon <words>` in a project with no icon set installed says so, lists the icon definitions that match (built-in names first, which Core draws with no set), and says how to get a set, in text and in `--json` (`reason`, `definitions`, `next`). `--list` gives the same next step instead of pointing back at the search, and `experimental icon use <set>` or `--set <set>` with no set installed says how to get one. After `experimental icon use <set> --variant <look>`, the search prints each match's import in that look where the icon has it, and names both looks (`look`) where it does not.

`astryx experimental icon` ranks faster: each search works out every icon set's searchable words once and each query's forms once per pass, so its passes read every icon without rebuilding its words. Answers are unchanged.

Experimental `exportIconIndex()` and `rankIconIndex()` in `@astryxdesign/cli/api`, the icon counterpart of `exportSearchIndex()` and `rankSearchIndex()`. `exportIconIndex({cwd, package?})` returns the icon sets `icon()` searches in a folder as plain JSON, and `rankIconIndex(query, indexes, {set?, limit?})` ranks stored indexes with `icon()`'s own ranking, so a catalog that must not load package code can store each package's index once and answer icon searches exactly as `astryx experimental icon` does. `icon()` ranks through the same function, so its answers are unchanged. An index is ranked only by the CLI version that made it.

`astryx docs cli/experimental/icon-sets` explains icon meaning groups and `replaces` in its overview: a match lists the other meanings of its group as `relatives` without changing which icon comes first, and a replaced meaning's old name keeps answering while `integration check` names the `map` key to rename. The search example now says the set's icon for a meaning answers where the set maps one.

`astryx docs cli/experimental/icon-sets` opens with the icon model in one place: Astryx owns generic meanings (a description and a few words each), a library maps its icons onto them inside its own package or the integration that already ships for it, with no separate add-on, a missing meaning is added in that package with `experimental icon new-definition`, and `astryx experimental icon <words>` puts the set's icon for the matching meaning first while related icons stay findable by their own words.

`Icon` given its glyph as `name` (as other icon libraries call it) renders that glyph and warns in development to use `icon`, instead of failing with "Element type is invalid". `name` does not reach the DOM.
Docs now answer three questions in the first sentence that agents read:
changesets.body:
- Icon props such as TextInput `startIcon`, Selector `startIcon`, Field `labelIcon`, DropdownMenuItem `icon` and SideNavItem `icon` take a semantic icon name such as `'search'` (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element. Their documented type is now `ReactNode | IconType`, as in the code.
- Selector `value` and `onChange` show the `hasClear` types: with `hasClear`, `value` is required and `string | null`, and `onChange` receives `null` when the user clears the selection.
- useTableSelectionState names what it returns: `selectionConfig` and `selectionState` with `selectedKeys`, `selectedCount`, `hasSelection` and `clearSelection`, with a bulk-action example.

No API or behavior changes.

changesets.headline: With no icon set installed, `astryx experimental icon` and `astryx experimental icon --list` now name the discover search that lists icon packs when discover lists one the project could add: Find an icon pack with `astryx discover "icon set"`, install it, then run `astryx experimental icon use <set>`. To make your own set, read `astryx docs cli/experimental/icon-sets`. The finder reads the catalog copies discover saved and calls no discover source, so before the first discover run, and where no catalog lists an icon pack, the step reads as before. The JSON `next` field carries the same sentence; its shape does not change.

Installing an icon-set package turns icon features on, with or without `experimental.iconSet` in astryx.config. A project that installs no icon-set package and sets no `experimental.iconSet` sees no change in any command, apart from the search change for experimental docs below. In a project that installs one, these stable commands now read the installed sets, so their output changes there:
changesets.body:
- `astryx discover`: lists each package's sets, and `--type icon-set` works.
- `astryx doctor`: runs the `icon-sets` check and reports an invalid installed set. It runs the `icon-placeholders` check when a main set is decided: the one `experimental.iconSet` names, or the only installed set. `doctor integration validate <package>` checks an installed package's sets.
- `astryx docs icons`: one section, added in the name of the package that ships your set, says how to find its icons (`astryx experimental icon <words>`). `astryx search` does not return it, and search output does not change.

Copied templates still follow a set only once `experimental.iconSet` names it.

For integration authors: `astryx search` now leaves out the sections that a doc marked `stability: 'experimental'` adds to another topic with `extends`, as it already leaves out an experimental topic. `astryx docs` still shows those sections.

Compatibility: in a project that installs an icon-set package, `astryx discover --type icon-set --json` now lists that package instead of failing as an unknown type, so its answer no longer carries the error fields `discover-type-icon-set.json.code`, `discover-type-icon-set.json.error`, `discover-type-icon-set.json.suggestions`, `discover-type-icon-set.json.suggestions[].name` and `discover-type-icon-set.json.suggestions[].reason`. A script built on 0.7.16 keeps working: a type discover does not know still fails with the same fields, and a project with no icon-set package gets the same error as before.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental icon new-set --from` run again on a set whose library dropped an icon now removes that icon in every look from the generated module and its declarations. Before, the filled (or other variant) export stayed behind and named a library export that no longer exists, so importing the integration package failed.

`astryx experimental icon` and the icons block of `astryx search` leave out the words that only join others (`with`, `and`) when they look for icons that carry a query's words, so `card with an icon of a star` no longer lists an icon only because its name holds `with`. A query that no whole word answers as typed is now read without them, so `user with plus` finds `user-plus` directly.

`astryx experimental icon` names each match's meaning import when its icon set maps the icon for a definition: `meaningImport` imports the icon under the meaning name, such as `import {TrashIcon as DeleteIcon} from '…'`, so app code keeps the name `DeleteIcon` when another icon set draws `delete`.

`astryx experimental icon` answers a query of several words that no icon matches as a whole, such as a glyph named in a phrase with the control around it. Icons that carry some of its words come back as word matches (score 20), the project's set first and, within a set, the icon carrying the rarest words first; a word that names a definition the set maps an icon for counts twice for that icon, and a word no icon carries counts for nothing. Word matches appear only in the search's own answer, and only where nothing answered before. A word written as an export name (`SearchIcon`, `ChevronDownIcon`) is also read as its words; the reading with the better-scoring match answers, so an answered query changes only when the split reading finds a better match.

The icon-sets guide shows how to make a set inside your own app, with no other package to make, install, or publish. When the package's own package.json sets `"private": true`, the `experimental icon new-set` receipt leaves out the publishing steps (peers, the `typecheck` script, the strict check's TypeScript, the placeholder description) and its notes end with the `experimental icon use <set>` step that turns the set on. Every other package gets the notes as before.

Icon sets: the generated icons module marks each adapter call and each theme-map element `/* @__PURE__ */`, so a bundler drops the icons an app does not use. Before, importing one icon from a set also bundled its whole theme map (and, for a set built with an adapter, every adapted icon). Modules written without the marks, or with `/*#__PURE__*/`, read the same; the next `experimental icon add`, `map`, or refresh adds the marks, keeps any mark a statement written by hand already carries, and changes nothing else. Set authors: author and check a set with this release or later. An earlier CLI misreads a module written with the marks: its `experimental icon add` and `map` drop the adapter import, its `new-set --from` refuses, and its `integration check` and `doctor integration validate <set package>` report `icon_generated_types_mismatch`. In an app on an earlier CLI, template copies, icon search and the default `doctor` run read a marked set as before; validating the set package itself fails until the app moves to this release.

Icon definitions: two new definitions, `fullScreen` (show something full screen) and `exitFullScreen` (leave full screen), so an icon set can map its full-screen icons apart from the icons it maps to `expand` and `collapse`. `expand` and `collapse` are unchanged for now, so every set keeps answering full-screen asks with the icons it maps today; sets that map neither new definition keep working, and `experimental icon --definitions` and `integration check` list them as optional.

`astryx experimental icon` breaks a tie between equally scored icons in favor of one whose name the query names in full, so a request for a plus icon to add a row gets `plus` before `folder-plus`. Remaining ties keep id order.
The IDE page template's description now says what its middle pane is: a single read-only code pane, not tabbed documents.

In the Tool: IDE page template, the editor's and terminal's scrollbars no longer sit under the properties panel's resize handle. On desktop the editor and terminal keep a small gap before the handle, so the whole scrollbar scrolls; before, a press on the half of the scrollbar nearest the handle resized the panel. Mobile, where the panel is hidden, is unchanged.

In `RichTextEditor`, a Markdown block marker typed at the start of a list item now re-marks it and keeps its text: `- `, `1. `, or `[ ] ` switches the item's list between bullets, numbers, and tasks, and `# ` or `> ` takes a top-level item out of its list as a heading or a quote, the rest of the list continuing after it. Each change is one undo step, back to the marker as typed.

The incident console page template works on a phone and its buttons act. On a narrow screen its header controls wrap onto their own rows, and choosing an incident opens its details in a bottom sheet instead of doing nothing. The inspector's next-step button ("Mark mitigated", "Resolve", "Reopen") moves the incident to its next status, and "Escalate" and "Declare incident" confirm with a demo toast that marks where to connect the real action. Rows show each incident's start date and time instead of a relative time that grew stale. The template stays unready for now.

The checkbox check and dash and the radio dot are sized as a share of their box, so a theme that sizes the box through the `checkbox-indicator` or `radio-indicator` target's `width` and `height` gets marks in proportion to it: a 13px box draws a 7.6px check and a 5px round dot, where before the 14px check was squeezed into the box's 11px inside, filling it edge to edge, and the 10px dot nearly filled the circle. The dot is rounded to whole pixels so it stays a circle. The shipped 20px and 24px boxes draw the same pixels as before in every official theme. A theme that sets the box's `borderWidth` directly, rather than through `--border-width`, gets marks slightly smaller or larger by that difference.

The slot that holds a checkbox's box or a radio's circle in CheckboxInput and RadioList is as big as the mark itself, instead of a fixed 20 or 24px. A theme that sizes the box (for example 13px) now gets the label right beside it and a pressed layer that fits it, where before the box floated in an empty 24px slot. The hidden input keeps its 20 or 24px hit area (at least 24px on touch screens), centered on the mark, and the focus ring stays on the mark. The shipped look is unchanged. A row is as tall as its mark or its label, whichever is taller: with a 13px box a default-size row goes from 24px to about 20px. A theme with a replacement indicator (`defineTheme({indicators})`) of another size sees its rows tighten: the label moves closer by (24 − size) / 2 px at the default size, the row is as tall as the mark or the label (the probe theme's 16px marks: 24px to about 22px), and the pressed layer matches the mark. A Markdown task item drawn in its list's marker column keeps its checkbox centered on the item's first line at any box size.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> accent <color>`: when the accent is a color far from the hue of the base theme's info, and the theme leaves info unset (a pink theme over a bright blue info), the result says info's banners and badges keep the base's color and offers an info between the two hues, so it sits with the palette and stays apart from the accent.

`astryx init` next steps and the `doctor` theme hint name the project's own install command (`pnpm add`, `yarn add`, `bun add` or `npm install`) instead of `npm install` in every project. An install command the CLI prints no longer adds a `@"*"` range to a package name.

`astryx init --to <places> --once` writes a copy that is saved nowhere, so no later `init`, `upgrade`, or background refresh touches it (a bundle, or a skill to upload elsewhere). `astryx init --remove` removes the Astryx skill from every place the project saved, and with `--to` from the places it names, in the project, a folder outside it, or the computer (`--remove --to user`), and drops each from what is saved; an edited skill file is kept and named. `--remove-agents` is now the same option as `--remove`; in a project that saves nothing it removes the block as before, adding one note when a folder is saved for this computer (kept, with the command that removes it), and its `init.remove` result gains `from`, `skills`, and `user`. `--once` is refused for the AGENTS.md block and for a place already saved, and a skill file Astryx did not write is kept, a linked skill folder's included, while an unedited Astryx file is the place's own through a link too (a folder saved for this computer where every file was kept is not saved; in the project, linked copy folders share one file, written and removed once); the computer-level skill and its links and copies, reached through a saved folder such as `~/.agents/skills` or `~/.claude/skills`, are kept (`astryx init --remove --to user` removes them).

`astryx init` says what it did to each agent-doc file: `[ok] AI agent docs: AGENTS.md updated (Astryx 0.7.15 -> 0.7.16)`, `... created`, `... already current, nothing changed`, or `...: Astryx block removed, another agent file holds it`. The `init.run` receipt adds `docsChanges` (`{path, change, from, to}` per file, in `docsWritten` order); every earlier field keeps its name and value.

`astryx init` in a project whose Astryx agent-docs blocks are all current prints the `build` and `search` commands (and where the setup guide is) instead of the five install steps, since the app is already set up. It judges the files the run writes: the `--agent-docs-path` files, the `--agent` preset's file, or every agent file at the root. A first run, or a run that refreshes an outdated block, still prints the install steps. The `init.run` receipt adds `agentDocsStatus` (`missing` | `stale` | `current`, the agent docs before the run; null when agent docs were not installed or the write failed); `nextSteps` is false when the steps are left out.

`astryx init --help` is about half as long: each option and exit code keeps what an agent needs to run it (what it writes, what it refuses, the error codes), and the rare cases (file deletion on `--remove-agents`, the `--user` link details, the five soft exit-0 cases) move to `astryx docs cli/commands/init`.

`astryx init`'s theme step now names the theme at the project's Core release, as `theme add` and `doctor` already do. In a project that pins Core 0.7.10, it prints `npm install -E @astryxdesign/theme-neutral@0.7.10`. Before, it named no version, so npm picked the newest theme, which needs a newer Core than the project has, and the install failed. `doctor`'s hint for an app with no theme and `theme build`'s hint to install a missing theme follow the same rule.

`astryx init --to <places>` puts the Astryx skill where your agents read it: `agents-md` (the AGENTS.md block, still the default), `skills` (the `astryx-project` skill in `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills` in the project, named apart from the computer's `astryx` skill so neither hides the other), `user` (this computer, the same as `--user`), or a folder written as a path. The choice is saved: in astryx.config `skills.to` for the project, so a later `astryx init` writes the same places, and in the settings file for a folder outside it, whose copy the CLI installed for the computer refreshes after each of its upgrades while it is there (delete the copy to stop it). Moving a project to another place removes the skill from the old one. `astryx init` with no `--to` and nothing saved writes exactly what it wrote before.

`astryx init --user` on a skills folder you cannot write (such as a read-only `~/.agents/skills`) now fails with `ERR_WRITE_FAILED` and a message that names the path, the reason, and what to change, instead of a bare `EACCES` line with `ERR_UNKNOWN`.

Nine page templates fit a 320 px phone without their content scrolling sideways, and a tenth scrolls less. Their responsive grids now pair the minimum column width with a column cap, so a column narrower than the screen shrinks to fit instead of overflowing. The inline form wizard's checkbox descriptions now wrap instead of being cut to one line. Screens up to 1920 px wide look the same as before; above about 2,380 px the library's six category cards fill their row instead of leaving an empty column.

On a phone or tablet, TextInput, TextArea and NumberInput keep themselves above the on-screen keyboard, with nothing to turn on. A field in a page that scrolls is scrolled 10 px above the keyboard as it opens, rising with the keyboard on iOS and at once under Reduce Motion; on a page with nothing to scroll, the browser's own reveal stays. When the keyboard closes, the page or scroll area goes back to where it was, sliding down with the keyboard on iOS, unless the person scrolled it meanwhile. In Firefox for Android on a slow device, Back can sometimes leave the page where the reveal scrolled it. A field in a scrolling area is scrolled 10 px above the keyboard when the area can bring it there; otherwise the page brings it into view. A field in a bar fixed at the bottom of the viewport rides up with the keyboard, the bar's bottom on the keyboard's top, and back down when it closes, even in a bar the app owns. A field inside a fully expanded Tall BottomSheet leaves that to the sheet. In a fixed container the app positions itself, such as a full-viewport dialog, a floating bar or a bar with its own `translate`, a scroller around the field brings it above the keyboard when it can; otherwise the page brings it into view, or the browser's own reveal does. In Firefox for Android, where the page cannot scroll further, a field the page should bring into view can stay under the keyboard. Nothing changes under a mouse or a trackpad.

`astryx docs global/problems` now also explains the "installing CLI release" line outside a project, where the astryx command you started downloads its own Core once. Before, the page said only that a project's own CLI could not start, and told you to install the project's dependencies.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor` name a theme module that `theme build` wrote (`.js`, `.mjs` or `.cjs`) and that imports TypeScript source, as built themes from a CLI before this one do (`built_module_imports_typescript`, a `next` note with the weight of `relative_import_not_shipped`), with the file, the line, and the fix.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` in a package's own folder keep npm's list of the files the package packs. They read it back while the package's folders list the same entries (names, types and where each link points), and package.json, the ignore files npm applies in the package and in each folder above it, any package.json above it, and the npmrc files npm reads are all unchanged. Which files npm packs never depends on what they hold, so a run after an edit inside a file, saved in place or by renaming a new copy over it, skips npm. That took seconds for a large package: each check there finished about 2.6 seconds sooner. A package that bundles dependencies, or has a link in its folders, is asked every time. Output does not change.

`integration check` and `doctor integration validate` ask npm once what a package's own folder packs, instead of once for each check that asks, and the authoring checks inside `integration check` no longer run the shipped-import check, whose notes they never read. In a large package with a `files` field, `integration check` finishes in about 10 seconds instead of 27, and `doctor integration validate` in about 9 instead of 12.5. Output does not change.

An integration can say how its apps add a dependency: `installGuidance` in its manifest, one line where `{packages}` stands for the packages to add. Where the CLI prints a step that adds packages the app lacks (template readiness, `init`'s theme step, `doctor`'s fixes, theme hints and errors, `theme eject`, the theme editor's notes, and `discover`'s add commands), it prints that line instead of the package manager's command; the `template` and `theme eject` receipts carry it as `installGuidance` beside `installCommand`. Steps that move Astryx's own packages to another release, or add `@astryxdesign/cli` at the project's Core release, keep the package manager's command. Without guidance, doctor's Core and peer-dependency fixes, `theme build`'s no-Core message and `render`'s missing-package suggestion now print the project's package manager in place of a fixed `npm install`. Two different lines cancel out, and a new `install-guidance` doctor check warns. An invalid line is ignored with an `invalid_install_guidance` warning.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` now resolve every relative import of the modules a package ships the way an app's bundler does, against the files npm packs (for an installed package, its files on disk). Run in the package's own folder, they used to pass an import such as `./icons` that the tarball leaves out, because the file was on disk there. Each import no shipped file answers is a `relative_import_not_shipped` note marked `next`, naming the importing file, the import, and that the file is not in the package. It fails `integration check --strict --next` now; the next minor release makes it a warning, which fails `--strict`. When npm cannot be asked, an import whose file no `files` entry can reach is still a note, and any other is listed as not checked. `astryx doctor`'s theme owners check now also reads a package theme's stylesheets, whose `@import` and `url()` references it never followed, and warns that the built module loads but names a file the package does not ship. Type-only imports are skipped; `./icons` resolving to `icons/index.js` is fine.

An integration can ship a skill: a doc that sets `skill: {name, description}` becomes a skill of its own in every app that keeps the Astryx skill in a skills folder (`astryx init --to skills`), and the AGENTS.md block gets one line that names it and points to `astryx docs skills/<name>`. `astryx docs skills` lists every skill a folder has (the project skill, the computer skill, and each integration skill), and `astryx docs skills/<name>` reads one. `astryx upgrade --apply` refreshes integration skills and removes one an integration no longer declares, `astryx doctor` checks them, and `astryx discover` lists them. A skill that breaks a rule (its name, a repeated name, its description) is left out with a note, and its doc still loads. `agentDocs.append` keeps working as before, and a project whose integrations declare no skill gets exactly the block it got before.

`astryx theme add`, on the first add, when an installed package names the provider that wires its themes, says so: "This app may already get its theme from <Provider> (from <module>, declared by <package>)", with the props it takes the theme and mode through. When that one provider takes the theme (its manifest's `themeProvider` names `themeProp`), every receipt that shows wiring shows that provider in place of a Theme wrap: the first add passes the generated module's theme to it (`<Provider theme={themes[defaultThemeSlug]}>`, plus `<modeProp>={themeModes[defaultThemeSlug]}` for a theme with one color mode when it names `modeProp`), a later add that first lists `themeModes` passes the mode to it when the manifest names `modeProp`, and `theme remove` of the last theme undoes those props and keeps the provider. With no `themeProp`, or two such providers, the first add names each provider and its trade-off ("Replacing <Provider> applies this theme everywhere but also drops anything else it sets up; a Theme inside it themes only what it wraps.") above the Theme wiring. No receipt reads app source. The JSON carries it as `appProvider`: each provider as `{export, from}` (with `themeProp` and `modeProp`), `wire`, and `themeProp` and `line` when the provider form applies. An integration manifest's `themeProvider` takes an optional `themeProp` and, beside it, an optional `modeProp`. `themeProvider` is a hint and never stops a manifest loading: a part this CLI cannot use (an export that is no component name, a prop that names no prop, a `modeProp` with no `themeProp`) is dropped with an `ignored_manifest_field` warning.

For an app whose theme its integration's provider wires, `astryx doctor` names the theme a stylesheet of the package belongs to: one in that theme's own folder, or one its stylesheet imports. `astryx theme list` says on each such theme's `wiredBy` line that the provider applies when the app renders it, and that `astryx doctor` checks where.

An integration that wires its themes with its own provider component can name it once in its manifest: `themeProvider: {export, from}`. `astryx doctor` then counts the package's theme as wired when the app renders that component (the theme whose stylesheet the app imports, or the package's only theme), instead of warning that no theme is wired, and its CLI-managed-themes check names the theme and its provider instead of offering `theme add`. An import of the provider that is never rendered still does not count. A stylesheet the app imports from the package counts as the theme it is, wherever the package keeps it; doctor names it, and never calls it missing when it cannot match it to one theme. `astryx theme list` shows `wiredBy` beside each of the package's themes, in text and JSON; its added and default marks stay as they are. A CLI that does not know the key, or a key inside it, ignores it with a warning and keeps the rest of the manifest.

On an interactive Item or ListItem row (with onClick, href or a delegated control), the current marker (`aria-current`) is now on the element that takes focus, so a screen reader announces "current" when the row's button or link is focused. Before, it sat on the row's root, so a screen reader did not announce it on the focused button or link (WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2, Name, Role, Value). Rows whose root takes focus, and rows that are not interactive, keep it on the root. A selected row still carries `data-selected` on its root and looks the same at rest; while it slides past other rows, a selected row now keeps its fill whatever its `aria-current` value.

An open swipe-action row on `Item` and `ListItem` closes on a touch tap on its own content, as a UIKit list row does, and that tap no longer activates the row or paints its press. It also closes when the list or the page scrolls, including a scroll that starts on the row itself, unless focus is inside its open panel (the browser may be scrolling a focused entry into view), and it counts as open from the release that opens it, before its spring comes to rest.

Under a finger, a full swipe on an `Item` or `ListItem` swipe-action row works like a UIKit list row's, the same on every touch device. Past the open width the entries ride the row and the outermost action stretches out to the edge. Dragged on past the confirm point, judged on the finger as UIKit does, the row runs ahead and the outermost action covers its place. Letting go there fires it at any speed; backing out undoes that and closes the row. On a side with two or more actions, a full swipe confirms only from the open row. A disabled outermost action never confirms.

Swipe actions on `Item` and `ListItem` run on the gesture system. A row claims a sideways touch at 8 px, before a browser commits to scrolling it. From the claim the row follows the finger one for one, so the part under the finger stays under it. A pen now swipes the row as a finger does. A second finger that lands before the claim leaves the touch to the browser's pinch; once the row has claimed its finger, a second finger no longer cancels the swipe. The click a browser synthesizes after a swipe is cancelled at its source instead of being swallowed by a 400 ms timer.

A trackpad's two-finger swipe moves an `Item` or `ListItem` swipe-action row with the fingers from its first event past 8 px and, when they lift, settles it on the nearest stop at their speed, without stopping first. Within one swipe an open row only closes, and a long fast swipe fires the outermost action where a full swipe may. A mouse wheel's notches never swipe a row.

Under a finger, swipe actions on `Item` and `ListItem` move like a UIKit list row, the same on every touch device. The row stays under the finger, one for one, until the release, and settles on UIKit's own spring from where it is and as fast as it was moving, so a release no longer stops dead and restarts. The settle plays on the compositor, so a busy page cannot hold it back. A flick opens the row or closes it, by its direction. Under Reduce Motion nothing a release starts travels or springs: the row cross-fades to where it lands, as `design:reduced-motion` asks. A finger that lands on a moving row catches it instead of being ignored until the row stops.

The kanban-board page template stacks its lanes top to bottom at the full width below 768px, so a phone shows whole lanes instead of one lane and a cut edge of the next. A swipe that starts on a card now scrolls the board; a finger lifts a card with a long press and carries it to another lane. A mouse drags as before, and the layout at 768px and wider is unchanged.

In development, `Kbd` without a `keys` string (for example with children, or an array) throws an error that names the prop and shows the fix, instead of a TypeError from inside Kbd, such as "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')" or "keys.split is not a function". Production output is unchanged.

`component --list` keeps its list between runs in a project where an integration can load, like template discovery's records, so a repeat list answers sooner there (about 220 ms with a large TypeScript integration). A new, removed or edited component, doc or integration lists again on the very next run.

Which integration component answers to a Core component's name is kept between runs with the component list, so `component` in a project whose integration replaces Core components no longer loads every one of that integration's component docs on each run: about 40 to 60 ms faster per call in a project with a large integration. It is decided again whenever a doc's `replaces`, the package's CLI range, the integration's components folder, its configuration or its manifest changes. Output does not change.

A kept catalog entry now names the kept entries it builds on and stores only the file states they do not hold. A run checks each kept entry once, however many entries build on it, so an entry checks no file that the entries it builds on already checked. A warm `component`, `search` or `template` in a project with a large integration checks about 3,800 fewer files; output does not change.

In a project with an integration, `astryx` commands that read back what they kept (`component`, `search`, `template`, `docs`, `build` and others) finish about 10 ms sooner. A kept gather no longer checks the CLI's own files one by one: as the per-user cache record already says, the CLI's build id stands for them, and now so does the folder the CLI runs from, so a copy installed in another folder, such as a patched one, keeps its own entries. In-place edits to an installed CLI stay unsupported; deleting the per-user `astryx/catalogs` folder clears what was kept. A package in the node_modules folder inside the CLI's is still checked, as before. Output does not change, except `astryx doctor`'s cache row, which now names the folder beside the build id.

A released input hold no longer changes its layer. A closing BottomSheet's hold reads focus a moment after focus leaves the sheet; if the hold was released in between, that late read could leave the sheet inert and hidden from assistive technology. No browser flow is known to hit this today.

`doctor` keeps its scan of how the app wires its themes between runs, like its docs checks, so a repeat `doctor` answers about 20 to 35 ms sooner. An edit to the app's source, a theme or a theme package scans again on the very next run.

Keyboard users can reach two template controls. The kanban board's column info icons use InfoTip, so each is a named button that Tab reaches and Enter opens, where before Tab stopped on a hidden, unnamed icon. In the side-navigation shell, a conversation's options button sits in the row's actions slot and shows while focus is in the row, so Tab reaches it; focus returns to it after its menu or delete confirmation closes, and the conversation link keeps its status in its name.
`astryx` discovery lists the lab's new media players: `VideoPlayer`, `AudioPlayer`, and the `MediaPlayer` root and parts for custom layouts.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx integration verify` handle very large icon libraries (tens of thousands of exports). The check scans every file of the package for contribution metadata instead of stopping after 5,000 files with a warning that failed `--strict`. Verify reads npm's pack list from a file, so a package of any size no longer fails with `ENOBUFS`, and both commands keep a bounded number of parsed modules in memory, so they run in Node's default memory. An icon set that re-exports icons from its own package name (`export {X} from '<own package>'`) is now checked through the package's `exports`, as Node resolves it, instead of being listed as not checked.

Every anchor-positioned layer (Popover, DropdownMenu, Selector, Tooltip, and other `useLayer` surfaces in anchor mode) stays on screen when its trigger runs partly past the viewport edge, such as a control in a panel that scrolls sideways, as long as the layer fits between the viewport gutters. Layers now place themselves with `anchor()` insets against the viewport instead of a position area that grows to include the trigger.

`Popover`, `Tooltip`, `HoverCard` and the other anchored layers open again when their trigger sits in a native `<dialog>` that the page displays closed. Such a dialog never enters the top layer, so its trigger is a valid anchor. The layer waited for the dialog to open, and it never opened.
changesets.body:
A layer still waits for a `Dialog` that displays its element before it calls `showModal()`. `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `Lightbox` and `MobileNav` open their dialog in the Effects of the commit that displays it. A trigger with a box in a closed dialog now waits for one more commit. React runs those Effects before it renders that commit, so a dialog that is still closed then stays closed, and the layer opens at once. For a press, that commit runs before the press's task ends, so the layer and its initial focus land within the press. A closed dialog with `display: none` gives its trigger no box, and the layer still waits for it with no time limit.

A second `show()` while a layer waits for the same trigger keeps that wait. It no longer restarts it.

changesets.headline: Popover and DropdownMenu, in their popover presentation, and Dialog move focus as they close only when the close would strand it (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3, Focus Order). Focus that used to fall to the page body when the opener was gone now goes, in order, to the element focused when the layer opened, its trigger, the control that names the layer in `aria-controls`, the component's own stand-in (a typeahead's input), the anchor or the first control inside it, the opener's former place in its group, the nearest surviving ancestor, the layer that opened this one, then the page's `main` region. A released behavior also changes: a DropdownMenu no longer focuses its trigger at close when focus never entered the menu. The `useFocusTrap` hook shares the trap that Popover uses, so it returns focus the same way. A Drawer keeps its own return at close and gets the shared one only when it is removed while open. There is no option to turn focus return off. To send focus somewhere specific, focus it in `onOpenChange` (Popover, DropdownMenu) or in `usePopover`'s `onHide`; for a Dialog, focus it after the dialog has closed, since the page outside an open dialog is inert. A Popover or DropdownMenu returns focus before the browser's own restore, so its trigger gets a focus ring only after keyboard input.

The theme build loads jiti, which transpiles TypeScript theme sources, through the module loader's lazy CommonJS loader, instead of importing jiti's ES module entry whenever any command loads the theme API. `component` in text and `doctor` no longer load jiti and start about 15 to 30 ms sooner. `theme build` still loads it, but no longer through the ES module entry, which made Node scan jiti's whole CommonJS bundle for export names; it starts about 15 to 30 ms sooner too. Output does not change.

Lightbox: an open caption that ends in a block image wider than the room beside "less" keeps its text lines when the window widens, instead of growing by a line every frame. "less" takes the line below the image. (#11740)

An open Lightbox caption that widens to fewer lines no longer forces a layout in the frame that shrinks it. That holds for a caption of text, inline elements, inline-blocks, images, and paragraphs or other plain blocks with no room under its last line. Anything else takes the exact read, as before: one forced layout. That includes floats, drop caps, flex, grid and clipped blocks, and empty inline-blocks. It includes room under the last line of text, such as bottom padding or a trailing line break. It also includes list markers, text indents, justified last lines, and `::before` or `::after` content outside an inline element's boxes.

In block and inline layout, a Link whose label has no break opportunity, such as a bare URL from `useLinkify`, now wraps inside its line instead of running past it and making the page scroll sideways. The Link stops at its container and its label may shrink, so its text wraps. In a flex row, a Link whose label is wider than the row is now capped at the row's width and wraps. A Link in a line wide enough for its label looks the same. A content-sized grid or table column still grows to the label's longest word.

In development, `TreeList`, `Outline`, `TopNavMenu` throw an error that names a missing required prop and shows the fix, instead of a TypeError from inside the component. Production output is unchanged.

The CLI reads a project's lockfile only for an Astryx package the project has not installed, and reads it once per lookup for all such packages. In an app whose `node_modules` holds the Astryx packages it declares, no command parses the lockfile. With a large lockfile (2 MB in our measurement), that saves about 50 ms per command and about 200 ms per `doctor` run.

Markdown's anatomy now says when its Image part shows alternative text: for an empty image URL, while an unsafe URL renders as source text. Its guidance adds two don'ts: plugins cannot cross a Server Component boundary, and Markdown does not sanitize renderer output. Prop docs now describe `density`, `isStreaming`, `onLinkClick`, and `components`; `inlinePlugins` keeps its own description instead of lending it to `plugins`; `contentWidth` names its 680 default; and the `contentAlign="start"` description now says inline start instead of left. The `onLinkClick` docs say that a custom `link` renderer does not receive the handler.

Markdown bulleted and numbered lists stay inside their column: a list no longer reaches 8px past both edges, so Markdown that fills a phone screen no longer makes the page scroll sideways. Markers and text keep their positions.

Markdown task lists stay inside their column: a list of checkbox items no longer reaches 8px past both edges, so it no longer makes a phone-width page scroll sideways. Checkboxes and text keep their positions.

A bottom-sheet DropdownMenu, MoreMenu or ContextMenu opened before its sheet code has loaded (a press right after the page loads) now shows the sheet together with its actions, instead of an empty sheet for a moment first.

The messaging shell page template, still marked not ready, now works as an app. AppShell owns its side navigation of channels and direct messages, so on a phone the channels open from the navigation toggle. Picking a direct message shows that conversation, sending a message or a thread reply adds it to the page, a message's replies open its thread (in a drawer on narrow screens), and selecting a conversation clears its unread count. The page no longer uses raw elements or a local style object, and the actions without a real destination show a demo toast.

The messaging shell template notes what must hold before it is marked ready: build keeps the default app shell for parts and edits whose words the template does not use, and the page-pick model is retrained to include it.

MetadataListItem's prop docs now list `xstyle`, `className`, `style`, `ref`, and `data-testid`, and say which element each one reaches: the label `dt` when the item is side by side, or the wrapper when it is stacked. The `data-testid` docs say that a side-by-side item puts `-label` and `-value` on its two cells.

`MetadataListItem`: a value no longer breaks an ordinary word or number mid-way when its row is tight, such as an amount beside its description on a phone with a wider font. A word longer than the whole line still wraps.

MobileNav's prop docs now list `label`, `xstyle`, `className`, `style`, `ref`, and `data-testid`, and the `label` docs say what names the drawer when it is not set. MobileNav's Chinese and dense prop text now reaches the docs: it was written where the doc compiler does not read it for a doc with two components, so those docs showed the English text. The Chinese text no longer marks `isOpen` and `onOpenChange` as required; inside AppShell the drawer reads them from context.

MobileNavToggle's docs now say every case where it renders nothing: above the mobile breakpoint, without an AppShell mobile context (AppShell's, or an `AppShellMobileContext` you provide), and when AppShell has no mobile navigation (no side or top nav, `mobileNav={false}`, or a `mobileNav` node).

MobileNav keeps its link to MobileNavToggle when a caller passes `id={undefined}`: the dialog keeps AppShell's drawer id, so the toggle's `aria-controls` still names the drawer. A defined `id` still replaces it.

MobileNav with `side="auto"` opens from the opener's inline edge in right-to-left layouts. When the opener holds focus, that is used. When nothing is focused (such as the first open after a page load), the opener is found through its `aria-controls`, which AppShell's `MobileNavToggle` sets. A custom opener without `aria-controls` that never takes focus still opens from `end`.

MoreMenu's prop docs now list `isMenuOpen` and say that without `size` the trigger takes the surrounding size (from a SizeProvider, ButtonGroup, or Toolbar), else `md`. The Chinese docs gain `isMenuOpen` and `onOpenChange` and the note on where host `data-*` attributes land.

`MultiSelector` with `hasSearch`: the trigger button no longer carries `aria-required`, which ARIA does not allow on a button (WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2, Name, Role, Value). Before, the button carried it, an attribute a button may not have. A required field still says so: the field label's visible marker is part of the trigger's name, or a hidden "Required" description is added when the marker is not shown, and the search box carries `aria-required` while the list is open. This matches `Selector`.

`astryx docs layout` and `astryx docs tokens` carry the core rules on the namespace page itself: layout names the frame, structure, spacing and breakpoint rules with a three-region example, and tokens shows the StyleX import and the tokens most code needs, so one read is enough to start.
Card, Center, Collapsible, Divider and Blockquote examples no longer overflow a narrow column: each keeps its demo width but now shrinks to fit. Wide columns look the same.

TextArea, TextInput, Switch, SegmentedControl and TabList examples no longer overflow a narrow column: each keeps its demo width but now shrinks to fit (and the status-variant columns wrap). Wide columns look the same.
Layout header, footer, content and panel examples and the chat layout examples no longer overflow a narrow column: each keeps its demo width but now shrinks to fit. Wide columns look the same.

Toolbar, TopNav (and its item, menu and mega menu examples), Table, Step and Stepper examples no longer overflow a narrow column: each keeps its demo width but now shrinks to fit, and the custom-content stepper's two side-by-side fields wrap. Wide columns look the same.

The AspectRatio examples other than its showcase, the Avatar, AvatarStatusDot, Grid, GridSpan, the clipboard, hotkeys, streaming text and container reveal hook examples, Markdown, OverflowList, Resizable and ScrollableArea examples no longer overflow a narrow column: each keeps its demo width but now shrinks to fit (and rows of avatars wrap); the Resizable showcase's sidebar can grow to two thirds of its card, so the handle stays inside a narrow card. Wide columns look the same.

NavHeadingMenu's docs now document NavHeadingMenuItem and its props (`label`, `description`, `icon`, `href`, `onClick`, `isDisabled`, `ref`, `xstyle`), add `ref` to the menu, and say that `minWidth` wins over the size's minimum width. New best practices name the WAI-ARIA menu pattern and its keys, say to name a standalone menu, and explain how a disabled row stays reachable.

A `NavHeadingMenu` passed as the `menu` of a `SideNavHeading` or `TopNavHeading` no longer adds a second, unnamed menu inside the heading's menu. Screen readers now meet one menu, named after the heading, that holds the items. A `NavHeadingMenu` used on its own is still a menu, named by the `aria-label` you pass.

Icons, `useIcon`, and component icon slots use the nearest Theme's object, so registering or nesting another theme with the same name does not replace their artwork. Icons outside a provider keep the registered root-theme fallback.

A neutral Badge in a primary or destructive Button now meets 4.5:1 contrast in light and dark mode. It paints the Button's own colour pair inverted: the Button's content colour as the badge fill and its fill colour as the badge text.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> neutral <color>`: a neutral color whose shades are the base theme's own grays (black, white, or a pure gray) now says the page, surfaces, text and borders keep their colors, and how to get dark surfaces, instead of a bare `[ok]`: a gray sets the tint of the grays, not how light or dark the surfaces are.

The payment form and checkout wizard page templates no longer squeeze their form beside the order summary on a narrow screen before script runs: the summary wraps below the form instead. Wide screens look the same.

When `astryx component` or `astryx template` finds no entry, the not-found error also points to a hook the name nearly spells or names by meaning. A `use…` name one or two slips from a hook's name, or one whose every word that hook's name carries (`useTableExpansion` for `useTableRowExpansion`), suggests that hook (`astryx hook <name>`). For `astryx component`, a name of two or more words that are exactly a keyword one hook's doc declares (`CopyButton` for a hook whose doc lists `copy button`) suggests that hook. The hint goes first only when no own suggestion matches as well: a suggestion whose name nearly spells the typed name or carries every typed word, or a component whose doc keywords or search-card synonyms hold the same phrase, stays ahead of it. The list never grows, the lookup still fails, and a name that already matches another command's entry by name keeps that hint.

In a project, the update notice and `doctor`'s matching fixes now upgrade every Astryx package the project lists that is released with Core, such as its themes, beside Core and the CLI. Before, the command upgraded only Core and the CLI, so following it left a theme on the old release; its exact Core peer no longer matched, and `doctor` reported it.

The npm commands that the CLI runs for itself now use npm's own `noproxy` setting. These commands install a release into the CLI's per-user cache and ask the registry for versions. Before, when the shell's `NO_PROXY` named the npm registry but npm's own settings sent the registry through a proxy, npm went straight to the registry. Then the first command that needed the cache, such as `astryx component` outside a project, waited until npm's time limit and failed.
The npm descriptions of `@astryxdesign/core` and `@astryxdesign/cli` name Astryx, so a search for "astryx" on npm lists them with the other Astryx packages.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: text on a role fill (accent, success, warning, danger, info) where neither the theme's white nor its near-black reads at 4.5:1 now uses the end of the gray ramp on the better side (black, or white) when that reads better, so the editor's own pick no longer makes a contrast problem that a darker gray would have solved; an exact fill that then reads keeps its color in dark mode too.

The computer-level skill, the project skill and integration skills render their SKILL.md through one function, so their frontmatter and hash line stay the same shape. The files are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Outline: under reduced motion, following a link lands on the heading at once instead of scrolling there, the active indicator moves at once instead of sliding, and a link's hover and current colors change at once. A caller's `aria-label` now names the navigation, in place of `label` and the default name.

OverflowList: in a theme whose spacing scale differs from the default, or when the root font size changes, the list now fits items with the gap it actually renders, so the last visible item and the overflow indicator are no longer cut off at the list's edge.

`OverflowList`s that mount or change in one render now measure together after it, before the frame paints. When other components write to the page in the same render, each list used to read its size after those writes and force its own layout; now all lists read their sizes first and the page lays out once for them. The first painted frame is the same. `useOverflow` results and `onOverflowChange` arrive one microtask after the render instead of inside it. A test that checks them right after a synchronous render awaits that microtask first, for example with `await act(async () => {})`. With fake timers that also fake `queueMicrotask`, as Jest's modern fake timers do by default, flush the faked microtasks too, for example with `jest.runAllTicks()` or `vi.runAllTicks()`.

In a project with an integration, `astryx` commands that keep what they gather (`component`, `search`, `template`, `docs`, `doctor` and others) load the installed CLI's own modules by their path in its folder, without Node first checking that each file exists and where it really lives, so they finish sooner.

Pagination: page links. Pass `getPageHref` and the page number, previous, next, first and last controls render as real links to each page's URL, so a page opens in a new tab, its address can be copied, and it works before scripts load. `getPageHref(page, pageSize)` returns the URL in the shape your app uses: a query parameter, a path segment, an offset or a cursor. `as` sets the link component, as on Button, and `LinkProvider` applies too. `onChange` still runs when a link is activated: use it for state or analytics, and do not navigate in it, because the link navigates. The dots, the page box and the page-size selector are not links and work as before. A control that stops being a link while it holds focus, at the first or last page or while the pagination is disabled, keeps that focus. A Pagination without `getPageHref` is unchanged.

Pagination's first and last controls in the row reflect `data-first="first"` and `data-last="last"` on their `pagination-item` target, so a theme that joins the controls into one strip can round the outer corners on the end cells and leave out the separator after the last. The default look does not change.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> neutral <color>` says the page background follows the gray too (or keeps a page color the theme sets), as it does, and so does the neutral dial's help; a moved accent text color's note names only the grounds it fails on, with the ratio on each.

Palette generation has a second recipe, `astryx-oklch-v2`, beside `astryx-oklch-v1`: its pale stops, where a vivid seed asks more than the sRGB gamut holds, follow the vibrancy and each seed's own chroma instead of all landing on the gamut's edge, and a dusty seed stays dusty there; the dark side of a ramp, and every pale stop whose gamut holds the most vivid seed at the default vibrancy, are drawn exactly as v1 draws them, so role text and dark fills keep their strength. New palettes name v2: `astryx experimental theme editor` records `"recipe": "astryx-oklch-v2"` in each palette config it makes, and the palette guide's example config names it. A request or config that names no recipe still runs v1, from `generateTonalPalette()` and `astryx theme palette generate` alike, so existing callers, the shipped themes' palettes and any existing config keep their colors; a config keeps the recipe it records, and naming one pins it. A theme the editor saved before keeps the recipe it was made with, and a color change on it says how to move it.
The payment form's promo code "Apply" button keeps its full label on a phone; the promo field gives way instead.

Page templates keep their text on a 320 px phone. The filtered table no longer scrolls sideways on a phone, buttons in three templates (the vertical form wizard's cover, the editor and the composition dashboard) keep their full labels instead of cutting off, the work item's success criteria and the report wizard's option descriptions wrap instead of cutting off after one line, and the canvas editor's document tabs show their full name in a tooltip when a name is cut. Wide screens look the same as before.

Theme editor pictures show responsive charts drawn: each page draws in a window of its own until it is quiet, and its script is held while the whole page is pictured, so a chart no longer starts over and is pictured empty. The page stays laid out for the 1280 × 900 window.

The theme editor's pictures and the render stylesheet cut read a media query's condition the way the browser does: `not` before a condition in parentheses, `or`, and nesting. A rule under `(not ((min-width: 768px) and (min-height: 500px)))` no longer counts as matching in the 1280px picture window.

`usePopover` takes an `anchorRef`: a ref to the element the popover sits on when it is not the control that opens it. Any element with a CSS box works (an HTML element such as a card or a table cell, or an `<svg>` element; a shape inside an `<svg>` warns in development). The trigger keeps its toggle and ARIA, and the anchor gets neither. The ref is read when the popover opens, on each render of your component, and on each `show()`, so a popover with `hasLightDismiss: false` moves between rows without closing when you set `anchorRef.current` and call `show()`. With light dismiss on, the press on the other row closes the popover first, and `show()` opens it again on the new element. A `show()` before the ref holds an element waits, and opens when the ref is next read and holds one. A composition with an anchor and no trigger opens through `show()`. The `Popover` component and its own `anchorRef` are unchanged.

Popover: a closed popover's trigger no longer points at the popup with `aria-controls`, so it no longer references a popup that is not shown. The trigger names the popup only while it is open; `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup` are unchanged. A render-function trigger still receives `aria-controls` in its props.
`usePopover` keeps its focus-return target when `show()` runs again after initial focus has moved inside the popover, so a close returns focus to the element that opened it instead of losing it.

`astryx doctor` starts about 6 to 10 ms sooner, and a first lookup in a project whose integration imports the CLI's API about 15 ms sooner. Doctor's theme checks and the codemods' parser loaded postcss as they loaded, so every importer of the CLI's API loaded it too; they now load it only when they read a stylesheet. Output does not change.

`astryx component` and the `astryx theme` commands start about 5–10 ms sooner again. The theme build module they load loaded postcss at once, through the module that reads a built theme's imports; postcss now loads only when a stylesheet's imports are read. The font stylesheet reader uses the same first-use postcss. Output does not change.

A press no longer scales a trigger whose own layer is open: a Button that opens a menu or a Popover, and a ghost or secondary Selector, MultiSelector or ComplexSelector. Under a mouse or a finger, the open layer stays where an unpressed open puts it. A disclosure button without a popup keeps its press.
The principles doc says settings groups use Section, not Card, matching the Card and Section docs.

What the CLI keeps between runs is checked against what each check it made returned, and no more. A check whether a file is there is checked by whether it is still there, and a real-path lookup by the path it answered. An edit to a file the CLI only checked for, or only resolved, no longer makes the next run work its kept data out again. A file whose content any kept step read is checked by its stamp, as before, and so is an ignore file a check looks for before it asks npm what a package packs. Output does not change.

ProgressBar and CircularProgress fills reach 3:1 against their track (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11, non-text contrast). ProgressBar's status fills take the status text colors, and its neutral fill, like CircularProgress's, takes the secondary text color instead of the disabled one, which is the bar's track color in dark mode in Theme Neutral and Theme Stone and under 3:1 on the bar's track in every bundled theme in light mode. A disabled bar takes the same fill and dims its track and fill to half opacity, as a disabled Slider or Switch track does, and a disabled ring dims as a whole, center content included, so each reads quieter than a neutral one. A mark on any fill but accent takes the surface color; in Theme Butter and Theme Stone, a mark on a status fill takes that status's on-color. CircularProgress draws every variant on the muted background track, ProgressBar's base track, because some themes' status muted colors are the status color itself. In Theme Neutral, Theme Butter and Theme Stone a dark neutral or disabled fill takes a lighter neutral stop, Butter's and Stone's status fills take the theme's status colors, Stone's accent fill takes a blue stop that reaches 3:1, and the CLI's bundled theme templates match.
`astryx doctor integration components` no longer reports a documented string union that leaves out a value the code marks `@deprecated` in every place the type takes it from.

`astryx component <Name>` (and its `--props` view) lists props one per line, ``- `name`: `type` = `default` - description``, with the required and experimental markers after the type, instead of a four-column table. Union types keep their pipes as written, and no field is dropped; `--json` is unchanged.

`astryx component <Name>` prints the first sentence of each prop's description, under one line naming the command that prints them whole: the read's own selector and `--package` scope with `--props`, so it resolves to the same component. A read prints its descriptions whole when that line would cost more than the cut saves. The `--props` view, `--json` and `astryx discover` keep every description whole.

When two installed packages both declare the same provider ID in their manifests, the warning and `astryx doctor`'s fix now say that if they are one integration installed under two names, keep one of the two dependencies, and otherwise change one package's providerId. When a provider ID comes from a package name, the advice is unchanged.

In development, `Markdown`, `SyntaxTheme`, `InternationalizationProvider` throw an error that names a missing required prop and shows the fix, instead of a TypeError from inside the component. Production output is unchanged.
Selector and MultiSelector keep their selection surfaces closed when mounted disabled with `isDefaultOpen`, including when read-only or disabled by an InputGroup.

Tab from any radio in a `RadioList` now leaves the group, also from a radio that the app focused by script. Before, Chromium sent Tab from that radio to the group's checked radio when it came next, so the group took two Tab stops, and in a modal `Dialog` the result depended on where the group sat.

The README's Quick Start now installs the CLI and runs `init` as part of setup, and the note at the top says setup is install, then `init`, run once before writing UI, and says what `init` prints and writes. Before, Quick Start installed only Core, a theme, and StyleX, and the note framed `init` as an extra for AI agents, so agents that followed the README finished setup without the Astryx guide in `AGENTS.md`. The repository README's Getting Started gets the same `init` step.
The not-found hint refreshes its name index after an imported doc dependency changes on the minimum supported Node version.

The install page now says that registry calls use Astryx's own short retry and timeout, not npm's fetch-retry or fetch-timeout settings: one retry after a 2-second wait, and at most 30 seconds per request.

A stop signal sent to the CLI's own process while it installs the release matching a project's Core, such as a time limit's SIGTERM, now stops the run. Before, the run went on once npm returned, answered, and exited 0 to a caller that had already given up: npm runs synchronously, so the signal waited for the install to end, and by then its handler was gone. The handler now stays until the signal is delivered, and the hand-off lets it stop the run before it answers.
A release that failed to install is tried again at once when npm's registry changed since the failure, instead of waiting 2 or 10 minutes, and the reason names the registry npm tried.

Remove six page templates that were never marked ready: not-found, access-denied, error-page, welcome-portal, run-console and review-workspace. Page templates will come from the design team instead. None of them was in a release, and no command offered them as a start.

`astryx experimental render`: a page whose script holds a long run of letters and digits, such as a large string, renders in its usual time again. The pass that finds the script's reads of images from the embedded source started a match at every character of such a run, so a page with a 1 MB string took minutes.

`astryx experimental render` carries the page's own modules and JSON data whose names only look like configuration: `config.ts`, `lib/arc.ts`, `data/chart-config.json`, `data/config.json`. They were left out as tool configuration, so the page came back from `--reverse` with `exact: false` and without them. These names stay refused: `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.*.json`, `jsconfig.json`, any `*.config.json` or `*.config.{js,ts,…}` module, manifests and lockfiles, and dotfiles such as `.eslintrc.js`. A file that carries one says render format 2, so a CLI that reads render formats names the CLI that reads it; 0.7.16 and earlier refuse it as damaged.

`astryx experimental render` carries the `.mts`, `.cts` and `.cjs` modules a page imports, and `--reverse` gives them back and follows their imports. The render loaded them but left them out of the file, so the page came back with `exact: false` and those modules missing. A file that carries one says render format 2, so an earlier CLI that reads render formats names the CLI that reads it instead of calling the file damaged; every other file stays format 1.

`astryx experimental render` carries every image, font and media file a carried module's strings or a carried stylesheet name by a relative path inside the folder that holds the carried files, also when the page did not show it in this render: a branch the page did not take, or a stylesheet rule no element uses. Such files now ship in the rendered file, up to 8 MB each, as a shown image does; a larger one, one whose bytes are not an image, font or media file, or one it cannot read, is left out with a `not-embedded` warning that names the file that names it. A name that climbs above that folder is not the page's file and is not carried, as `--reverse` reads it too. `--reverse` reads the same names with the same scan, so such a page used to come back with `exact: false` and those files missing.

`astryx experimental render` draws a recharts chart sized by its `ResponsiveContainer` at a set of widths, from a narrow table cell to a wide screen, and the file's CSS shows the drawing nearest the width the reader's browser gives the chart, with no script. Before, such a chart was drawn once at a guessed size and stretched to the page's width: its text was about one and a half times its size on a desktop and half its size on a phone, and a chart that filled a box of fixed height ran out of the box. The widths run from 60 to 1920 pixels, each the square root of two times the one before, so the drawing shown scales by at most the fourth root of two either way. The chart now keeps the height the page gives it (a number, the width over `aspect`, or its share of the height that the box it fills states in its own style) and fits that box whole, so its text stays within a fifth of its own size. A box whose height comes from a stylesheet gives no height to read: the chart is drawn 300 pixels high and fits inside the box, scaled down in a shorter box and with empty space above and below in a taller one. Its legend sits inside its picture, where recharts places it, and keeps the rest of its style. Each such chart carries eleven drawings, whose coordinates keep two decimal places, so it takes several times the room in the file that one drawing takes. A chart of fixed size is drawn as before.

`astryx experimental export` checks the file it wrote and says so: whether the file's markup and stylesheets load anything from outside the file (the page's own script is not read), and whether `--reverse` gives back every carried file exactly, naming any that differ (`data.checks` in JSON). When the file stands alone, it names it as the one file to share, with its size.

`astryx experimental export`: a large exported page that repeats an element names each repeated list of the StyleX classes Astryx's packages write (the `x…` classes) by one short class in its first paint, when those repeated lists add up to at least 16 KB; the page's own StyleX classes keep their names, so a large table or list writes a much smaller file: a 10,000-row grid goes from 52 MB to 18 MB. The page looks the same, also where scripts are blocked; its script draws with StyleX's own classes, and `--reverse` gives the page back exactly. The experimental `render()` takes `keepClassNames: true` for a caller that styles the file's markup with its own copy of the StyleX styles.

When a page does not compile, `astryx experimental render` names the file and the line the error points at, also for a module the page imports. When StyleX cannot read a value a style imports, the message names the value and the import, and says what StyleX needs: the value written in the style, or a `.stylex.ts` or `.stylex.js` file that defines it; for a `.stylex` file it cannot find, it says to check that the file or its package is there.

`astryx experimental export` checks its `dropped-children` warning against Core's component docs. A Core component whose docs list no `children` prop is named as the one that dropped the text, even when the text sits inside another component (`<Badge><Text>New</Text></Badge>` names Badge), and the warning points to `astryx component <Name>`. Text that the first paint does not show yet (a collapsed Banner, an inactive tab or route) stops warning only when every component around it is a Core component whose docs list `children`. A text inside a page's own component, or another package's, keeps today's warning. A warning for a text in another of the page's files names that file (`on line 12 of components/Card.tsx`). The warning's code does not change.

`astryx experimental render` names every package the page and its own modules import that is not installed, in one refusal, before it runs the page, with one install line for all of them. An Astryx package (a theme, say) counts as installed outside a project only when the CLI's package set holds it; otherwise it is named with the rest. Before, it named only the first, so a page that needed three packages took three failed renders. The message and the install suggestion name every package. In a TypeScript module, a static import the module uses only as a type, or not at all, does not count, as TypeScript drops it; a re-export, `import()` or `require()` of the same package still counts. A JavaScript module loads every import, so each one counts. A package stylesheet that is missing is still a warning, as before.

`astryx experimental render`: a rendered file now explains itself to whoever opens it next. A note at its top names the CLI version and render format that made it, the page's path, the files it carries and the packages it rendered with, and gives the exact commands that get the source back and render it again; a short note after the embedded source repeats the way back. `--reverse` reports the render format, the CLI version (`renderedBy`), the packages and an explicit `--title` (`title`), and, for files this version renders, whether someone changed the markup after the render (`edited`, read as a browser reads the file, so a copy whose line ends changed on the way is not edited) with each text change (`edits`: what it was, what it is now, and the restored file and line that hold the old text, in a module or the JSON data it imports, also where it wraps across lines). A file in a newer render format than the CLI reads is refused with the new `ERR_RENDER_NEWER_FORMAT`, which names the CLI version that wrote it; a file that names a CLI version that is not a semantic version is refused as damaged, so no printed command carries it, and every path a printed command takes from a received file is quoted. The render format stays 1, so earlier CLIs keep reading the files this version writes, except for a file that carries an `.mts`, `.cts` or `.cjs` module, which says format 2 so that a CLI that reads render formats names the CLI that reads it; 0.7.16 and earlier refuse it as damaged.
`astryx --json experimental export`: the `data.files` description also names the images a page names by a path from the site's root, which the export reads from `public/`.

`astryx experimental render --reverse` finds a rendered file's title, styles and body as a browser does, outside comments and outside the text of the style element, so an untouched file whose stylesheet text looks like HTML, or whose page path looks like a tag, no longer reads as edited.

`astryx experimental render` says why when no answer from the page's process reaches the CLI: the answer was sent but not received, the process ended while it sent it, or the stage it ended in, after how many seconds and with how much memory free. When the page's process cannot send its answer, the error now says so.

`astryx experimental export`: an exported page's script reads from the first paint an image the first paint shows through `src`, `srcset` or `poster` when the page's code names it as a whole string by that exact path or https address. The file holds each such image one time fewer: a page with one 450 KB local photo goes from about 2.05 MB to 1.45 MB, and an https image the page shows through `src`, `srcset` or `poster` is held once (the same photo by an https address: about 1.46 MB to 0.86 MB). The first paint is the same, also where scripts are blocked.

A page rendered with `astryx experimental render` carries one copy fewer of each image a page module imports (`import photo from './photo.png'`) when the file's embedded source carries it. The page's script reads such an image from the embedded source, so the script holds no copy of its own. An image the embedded source leaves out (under a dot-folder or in `node_modules`) keeps its own copy in the script, and an image the page names by a string path keeps its copy too.

New `astryx experimental import <file.html>` turns a file `astryx experimental export` wrote back into its page, the same as `export --reverse`, which keeps working. Help, the share and export guides, the file's own note and the render's suggestions now give the way back as `experimental import`. The JSON answer is unchanged (`render.reverse`). An old `experimental render --reverse` line now points straight to `experimental import`, and an unknown top-level `import`, `back`, `restore`, `unrender` or `reverse` suggests it without running it.

`astryx experimental export`: a link to a place in the page (`<a href="#section">`) keeps working in a viewer that shows the file in a frame given its document inline (`srcdoc`), as many artifact viewers do. There the address resolves against the viewer's own page, so the click navigated the frame away and the page vanished. Now the file moves to that place, as a browser tab does: it scrolls there, sets `:target` for the page's CSS and fires `hashchange` for a page that routes by hash. `#` goes back to the top. This also holds in a viewer that cancels such a link itself on its way down and only scrolls to the place, from a listener its own script adds on the frame's window before the file's script runs, or on the frame's document from a DOMContentLoaded listener its script adds on the frame's document before the file's script runs: tabs and navigation that route on the address switch there too, also for a link inside a card that stops the click. A link the page cancels or handles itself, from any of its own listeners (also one its modules add while they load), one with a target, and a click with a modifier key keep their own way.

`astryx experimental render` now writes the page as a live app in one file: popovers, menus, dialogs, tabs, forms and every other control work as in the app. The file carries the page's own script, inline after the embedded source: the page's modules and the packages they use, bundled for the browser by esbuild. It paints the rendered markup first, then the script draws the live page over it.
