It is still one file, and the render adds no network request and no `eval`, so it works in a sandboxed frame that allows scripts, under a content security policy that allows inline scripts; a frame that blocks scripts shows the markup, and `--reverse` still gives the page back byte for byte. A link out of the file opens in a new tab, and a form submits even in a viewer frame that blocks form submission: the file fires the form's submit event itself. A page whose script cannot be built for the browser (a module it loads needs Node, say) is refused with the new `ERR_RENDER_SCRIPT`, which names the module. esbuild is a new dependency of the CLI, and only `experimental render` loads it, so no other command starts slower. The JSON adds `scriptBytes` and `scriptModules` to a render. When the page's script throws, in its render or in an effect (a frame that blocks storage, say), the file keeps showing its first paint. An image the page names by a path in a string, in `src` or `srcSet`, keeps showing once the script draws the page, and an image named in `srcSet` is carried too. A page file the page loads later (a dynamic import) that does not compile is refused as a static import is, with `ERR_RENDER_COMPILE` naming the file and line.

The experimental command `astryx experimental render` is renamed to `astryx experimental export`. It still writes a page as one self-contained HTML file, and `--reverse` still turns that file back into its page; its options are the same, and its text output says "Export it again:" where it said "Render it again:". The old name is no alias: `astryx experimental render …` fails, exit 1, with `ERR_UNKNOWN_SUBCOMMAND`, and suggests the run with `export` in its place, keeping the options before it (also as a JSON error with `--json`). An unknown top-level `export`, `render`, `share`, `bundle`, `snapshot` or `standalone` suggests `astryx experimental export` and never runs it, unless the next word is a name another command reads (`astryx export Button` still suggests `astryx component Button`) or the active base does not serve the command. The guide `cli/experimental/render-pages` is now `cli/experimental/export-pages`, and the command's reference is `cli/commands/experimental-export`.
changesets.body: JSON fields that carry the command name now say `experimental export`: the command's entry in `astryx manifest --json` and in `astryx --json experimental --help`, and every suggestion's `name` that names the command. The result types stay `render.page` and `render.reverse`, the error codes stay `ERR_RENDER_*`, and the `render()` function keeps its name. A file written before the rename names the old command in its note; `--reverse` reads it as before.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental render` refuses a page that imports a name its module does not export, as a build refuses it, with `ERR_RENDER_COMPILE`: "The page does not compile (src/page.tsx, line 3): @astryxdesign/core has no export Chart". It checks named imports in the page's own modules from those modules (not from a CommonJS one, which a bundler reads by interop), from Astryx packages and from StyleX variables modules (`.stylex`), and an element drawn as `<Name.Member>` whose export has no such member. It counts only names the page uses as values, so a type imported without `type` is fine, and a file the page reads as text (`?raw`) is not checked. The script's build names the file and the module the same way. An import of a package subpath the package does not export (`@astryxdesign/core/Chart`) is refused the same way: "@astryxdesign/core has no export ./Chart". Before, the render named what the missing import broke, not the import: `ERR_RENDER_FAILED` with "Element type is invalid" for a missing component, `ERR_RENDER_FAILED` with "… is not a function" for a missing function the page calls as it loads, `ERR_RENDER_SCRIPT` for a name only the script uses, and a missing `.stylex` value rendered without its style and with no error.

`astryx experimental render`: when a page imports packages that are not installed, the suggested install line now follows the page's own package, and no line is offered where running it would install in the wrong place. The page's package decides the package manager. When its lockfiles disagree, the message names them and suggests no install, where it suggested `npm install`. For a page in another package than the folder you run from, the message names that package and the line to run there, since the line run here would add the packages to this folder's package. In a folder that no `package.json` holds, the message says to install them in the project that uses the page, and suggests no install, since an install there would make the folder a project.

`astryx experimental export`: an exported page's script is a module script when it runs the same in strict mode, so it runs once the file is parsed: a browser paints the page before the script draws it, and on the pages measured a small page shows its first paint about 200 ms sooner on a slow phone, with about the same time until it responds. A page whose script bundles a file that is not an ES module and does not ask for strict mode (CommonJS code, or a side-effect file with no `import` or `export`), or code that reads `document.currentScript`, keeps a classic script.

`astryx experimental export` leaves `autofocus` out of the file's first paint. The page's script owns focus once it draws the page, as the app does, so a field the page focuses still gets focus. A viewer that shows the file in a cross-origin frame no longer logs a blocked-autofocus error.

`astryx experimental export` draws some large chart pages faster: React no longer logs each render's timing while the export draws them. A page of four charts of 50,000 points each took 42 s to render and now takes 29 s; most pages take the same time as before. The file it writes is the same.

`astryx experimental render` names every file the page uses that the rendered file does not carry. A file left out because its name reads as a tool's configuration now gets the warning code `not-carried` instead of `not-embedded`. It says what carries the file: rename a `*.config.json`, such as `chart.config.json` to `chart-data.json`, or move the values the page reads from a tool's own file, such as `package.json`, into a file of its own. The note at the top of the file lists every left-out file on a "Not carried" line, and then no longer says the page comes back exactly. The JSON adds `notCarried`, and the text output shows it, both only when a file is left out.

A page render that draws overlays open waits for React's queued work before it reads them, and no longer compares the page's markup turn after turn: a page whose overlays have settled is read at once, so the theme editor's sample page and sheet render as fast as before while each render stays the same every time. The theme editor's contrast checks reuse each part's token reads within a command.

A page render that draws overlays open (the theme editor's sample page and sheet) reads each overlay once its update has finished. Before, on a busy machine it could read an overlay between two renders, so the same theme could render to different pages: `undo` then left the sample page different from before the change.

`astryx experimental render --out` accepts an absolute path in any folder, such as a folder of files to upload as an artifact. The render still never replaces a file it did not write. A relative `--out` still stays inside the current folder, and its refusal now says that an absolute path works.

`astryx experimental render` outside a project carries the modules a page imports from above its own folder, and the files those modules import, as long as they are inside the current folder. A page restored with its neighbours (`report-restored/app/report/page.tsx` beside `report-restored/components/`) and rendered again by the command its file prints used to leave those modules out, so the new file came back with `exact: false`. Where the render reads the page's `tsconfig.json` and `public/` images does not change.

`astryx experimental render` renders a page outside a project whose StyleX reads Astryx theme variables (`@astryxdesign/core/theme/tokens.stylex`), as many templates do. Such a page stopped with "The page does not compile: Could not resolve the path to the imported file", because the StyleX compiler looked for Core beside the page, where outside a project there is none. The compiler now gets the theme file the page loads from the CLI's own Core, and the page renders the same as it does inside a project.

`astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` read a folder or file whose name begins with two dots (`..x`) as one inside the folder that holds it, where they took it for the folder above. A page in such a folder keeps its own folder as the root of the files it carries, so the file it writes reverses; a file above it stays out, named in a `not-embedded` warning. The note at the top of a page rendered outside a project names the page by its path among the files it lists (`app/x/page.tsx`), where it named only the file (`page.tsx`) and pointed at it as the file to edit.

render: a page's own styles compile with their own class-name prefix, so they never share a class with Core's stylesheet. Core's rules keep their layer on Core's elements (a Table's first and last cells keep their edge padding), and a page's override of a component still wins, as in the app.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the overlays a page opens are drawn one part at a time, so a part's document listeners (a typeahead's or a menu's outside press) hear only presses on its own controls. Every editor command that reads the part data, and every sheet picture, no longer pays for each press on every other part. The part data is the same as before.
`astryx experimental export`: more images named by a path from the site's root (`/pics/shoe.png`) show in the file and come back with `--reverse`.
changesets.body:
- When the project has no `public/` folder, export reads such a path from the nearest `public/` above the page, inside the project. This covers a site folder below a shared package.json. Outside a project, it reads it from the nearest `public/` above the page, inside the folder you run the command from.
- The file now carries each such image with the page's other files, so `--reverse` puts it back in the `public/` folder export read, at the same path.
- An image the page names this way but draws only later (after a click, in the next view) is carried too, and the file's script shows it from the carried data.
- Export reads such a path only from `public/`. A file of that name at the project's or the page's root is no longer read, and a path that leaves `public/` (`/../x.png`) is not read. A path to a file that is not in `public/` gets the missing-image warning, which now names the `public/` folder export searched.
- The experimental theme editor's image notes read a theme's `url(/…)` file the same way: a file at the project's root, not in `public/`, is now reported as missing.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` say that a file they cannot read cannot be read, with the reason (`EACCES: no permission`, a folder or a pipe given as the file), and the new error code `ERR_READ_FAILED`. They used to say the file does not exist, with `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, which a file that is not there keeps.

`astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` read path aliases from the config TypeScript reads for the page: the nearest `tsconfig.json` (else `jsconfig.json`) at or above it, through its `extends` (a path with or without `.json`, a package's config, or a list, the later one winning, with `${configDir}`), and, behind a solution-style `tsconfig.json` (`"files": []` with `references`, as Vite sets up), the referenced project that includes the page. A page whose aliases live in `tsconfig.app.json` or in an extended config used to fail, with `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, or with `ERR_RENDER_MISSING_DEPENDENCY` when the alias looks like a package name (`@data/rows`), although `tsc` and the app's build found its imports.

`astryx experimental export` now fetches each image a page names by an `https` address, once while the page renders, and the file carries it, so the image shows in a viewer that blocks the network. The render sends no cookies or credentials, takes only an image (by its type and its bytes) up to 8 MB, and gives each image 2 seconds to answer and 5 to arrive, and all of them 15, and asks for no more when the network answers none of the first ones. Any failure (no network, no answer in time, not an image, too large, or an address that is not `https`) leaves the address as the page wrote it and warns, naming why; an address the page's code holds that counts as an image only by a name (an object's `src`, `imageUploadUrl`) is listed, and its fetch adds no warning, when its answer is another type. The JSON result lists every address fetched and every one that was not (`remoteImages`); the text names the first ten of each and counts the rest. `--reverse` gives back the page with its addresses. A fetched image travels with the file, so anyone who has the file can see it.

`astryx experimental export`: an https image the page shows only later (after a click, in the next view) is carried too, when the page's own code writes its address whole. That means an address an element shows as an image (an ``'s or an ``'s `src`, an ``'s or a ``'s `srcSet`, a `

`astryx experimental export --reverse` gives back a page that imports through a path alias in a project whose alias leads outside the new folder, instead of refusing it. When the file the alias reaches, and every carried file it imports where the project has it, is byte for byte the page's copy, the page uses the project's files and their copies are not written (`aliased.sameAsProject`), so export, reverse, edit and export again work in the page's own project, again and again. When that file differs or is not there, the page's copy comes back in its own layout inside the new folder, never into a folder that exists, and the answer names the file the alias reaches today and any file it imports that differs (`aliased.differs`), with the `paths` entry that leads the import to the copy. It says that entry applies to the whole project (`projectWide`) and gives the narrower fix: the relative import of the copy for each restored file that makes the import (`instead`). A file from a CLI that recorded no alias imports gets the same `paths` entry, found from the carried file the import's path ends with. `aliased.config` and `aliased.paths` now appear only when `aliased.imports` is not empty.

`astryx experimental render --reverse` gives back a page that imports files through a path alias (`@/components/Header`) in a folder whose project has no alias for those imports, such as an empty folder holding only the HTML file. A render records which carried file each alias import named; where no alias of the receiving project names the import, the file comes back in the page's own layout inside the new folder, byte for byte. The result's `aliased` names each such import with its file, the whole `paths` the page needs to build (the entries the config has now, own or inherited, with every target the imports need), and the tsconfig.json or jsconfig.json it belongs in (the one TypeScript reads for the page, else a new one), and the text prints them. Only an import that cannot be a package name or a package's own subpath import is followed this way (`@/…`, `~/…`), so a received file can never remap a package or the reader's own imports. Such a page used to be refused as carrying "files the page does not import". Where the project's alias points outside the new folder, the restore is still refused; an import that looks like a package name (`@components/Header`), or a file from an older CLI, which records no alias imports, is still refused unless the receiving project has the alias, and the refusal now says so.

`astryx experimental render` names at most 10 files in its text answer, then counts the rest and names the folder they share, such as "... and 190 more in page-restored/images/". A page with many images no longer prints a long line an agent must read. The JSON answer still lists every file.

`astryx experimental render --reverse` finds the embedded source in a file whose script tag a minifier or another tool rewrote: an unquoted `type` (`<script type=application/x-astryx-source>`), or an attribute before `type`. Such a file used to come back as a page rebuilt from its markup (text and layout only) instead of the exact source.

`astryx experimental export --reverse` names every file the render records as not carried as missing, so `exact` is false whenever one is. A rendered file now records the files the render left out, and the reverse adds them to `missing`. This covers a module the page imports through a path alias from outside the carried folder, which the reverse cannot resolve and used to report as exact.

`astryx experimental render --reverse` refuses two kinds of damaged Astryx page with `ERR_RENDER_SOURCE_DAMAGED` and writes nothing, instead of answering with a page that looks fine. A rendered file cut short before its embedded source used to come back rebuilt from the part of the markup that was left; it is now refused as cut short. An Astryx page a merge left with conflict markers used to give back one side's source without a word; it is now refused, naming the conflict, so you keep the whole file from one side or render the merged page again. A file that is not an Astryx page is still refused with `ERR_RENDER_NOT_ASTRYX`, markers or not.

`astryx experimental export` says what the file's size is made of, one line per part (`scriptBytes`, `cssBytes`, `markupBytes`, `sourceBytes`, with a note when the script is most of it), and adds `markupBytes` and `sourceBytes` to its JSON.

`astryx experimental export` keeps a theme's rules for the parts a component draws only after the first paint, such as a Banner's icon, a tab's indicator or a dialog. Core builds those parts' class names while the page runs, so the cut now also keeps, for each name in the page's script, the class Core's naming module makes from it. Before, those parts lost their theme styles in the rendered file.

`astryx experimental export` warns when a page gives a Core component's prop a value it does not have: `unknown-prop-value`, "page.tsx:12: Button has no variant "danger"; its variants are primary, secondary, ghost, destructive." Such a component draws no variant's look and nothing else says why. The check reads Core's own docs for the component in the page's Core (the props `astryx component <Name> --package @astryxdesign/core` shows), so an integration that replaces the component does not change it. Where a theme can add values to a prop (Button's `variant`, Banner's `status`, Link's and Heading's `color`, which take Text's colors), the values the project's themes add count too: the check reads the module augmentations in the project's own TypeScript files (a theme build's `.variants.d.ts` included) and in the declaration files of the theme and integration packages it installs. It checks only string values written in the page, for props whose type is a closed set of strings, on components imported from Core by name or through a namespace import (`<Core.Button>`). A value the page computes, a component that is not Core's, and a prop with no doc entry are not checked.
`astryx experimental render`: a page that saves to storage or copies text keeps working in a viewer's frame that allows scripts but blocks storage or the clipboard (`sandbox="allow-scripts"`).
changesets.body:
- **Storage:** there, touching `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` throws, and the page went dead after its first paint. Now the file gives the page an in-memory storage that acts as the browser's does, methods and properties alike (`localStorage.theme`, `Object.keys(localStorage)`). What it saves lasts until the page closes. A file opened from disk or on a real site keeps its real storage.
- **Clipboard:** a frame can leave `navigator.clipboard` out, refuse it by permissions policy, or refuse the write, so a page's own Copy button failed. Now the write falls back to the browser's copy command where Core's clipboard hook does. It resolves when the text was copied and rejects with `NotAllowedError` when it was not, so the page's own success and error paths run. `readText` rejects with `NotAllowedError`, as a browser does.

The share guide now says what such a frame allows: forms, storage in memory and copying work; a cookie write throws, fullscreen and printing do not work, and a link opens only when the viewer allows pop-ups.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental render` gives a relative or aliased import with `?raw` the file's text, and a `.css` file imported with `?inline` its text (not added to the page), as Vite does by itself, however the import names it. It used to give a JSON file's object for `?raw`, fail on a text file such as `notes.txt?raw`, and refuse a `.css` file with `?inline` as CSS Modules. A package import with `?raw`, and a Sass, Less or package stylesheet with `?inline`, stay as before. Any other query loads the file as it loads without one, as before: an image, font or media file as its address (`?url`, `?inline`, `?w=400`), a module as itself. `--reverse` gives back the files the render carries; a `?raw` file of a kind a render never carries, such as `notes.md`, is named in a `not-embedded` warning.

`astryx experimental export` follows an import written the TypeScript way, such as `./helper.js` for `helper.ts`, to its source when it looks for the files a page uses. A module from outside the carried folder that imports one now gets that file named in `notCarried` too.

`astryx experimental render` warns when the page asks a media query in JavaScript, with Core's `useMediaQuery` (from `@astryxdesign/core` or `@astryxdesign/core/hooks`) or with `matchMedia`. The rendered file runs no script, so readers on every screen got the layout of the answer the page had on the server, with no word why. The new `screen-query` warning names each query and says to fold the layout with CSS: `Grid` with `columns={{minWidth}}`, or a StyleX `@media` or `@container` style.

On Windows, `astryx experimental render` and the experimental theme editor now transform the page's own files. The renderer read every file as outside the project, because the module loader named files with forward slashes while the project path used backslashes, so no file was transformed. A page or theme that imported a stylesheet then failed with `Unknown file extension ".css"`, and StyleX, image and JSON imports were not handled either.

`astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` write in one step. A render writes the HTML file under a temporary name beside it, then gives it its name, so a reader or another run never finds half a file: two renders of one page to one file both succeed, where one could be refused because the file "already exists and was not written by a render". A restore writes its new folder the same way, so restores run at the same time each get a folder of their own, also when they restore with `--out` into folders under one new folder, where some were refused, and a restore stopped part-way leaves no folder behind, so the same command works again. A run stopped between its write and its rename leaves a hidden temporary file or folder, which the next run to the same place, on the same computer and in the same container or sandbox, removes once that run's process is gone. A render still never replaces an HTML file this user cannot write, and the file it replaces keeps its permission bits; it now needs to make a file in the HTML file's folder, so a folder this user cannot write is refused, and the refusal names it. Every copy a restore writes, except the page at its target, lands in the one new folder, including a copy of the page that a path alias places; such a copy outside it is refused with nothing written.

reset.css gives the page the `--font-family-body` font, so text in the page body outside the Theme wrapper, such as a tooltip or a hidden span a chart uses to measure labels, no longer falls back to the browser's serif font. A page where no stylesheet defines the token keeps its current font.

Importing `ResizeHandle` on its own no longer pulls in `useResizable` and its resize controller. The handle reads the hook's collapse, release and maximum details from the resize model instead, so its static import graph drops from 90 to 84 modules. A bundler that tree-shakes already dropped most of that code (25 bytes gzip less); one that keeps whole modules loads the controller only with the hook.

A focused `ResizeHandle` acts only on its own keys: plain arrows, Shift with an arrow, Home, End and Enter. Any other combination, such as Alt, Control or Command with an arrow, Home, End or Enter, or Shift with Home, End or Enter, now passes through to the page, so the browser's own shortcuts on those keys (history navigation, scrolling to the top or bottom) and the app's own shortcuts run.

A command that reuses kept data hands each kept list of what it read to the run's records once, instead of once for every step that reuses it, and works out the CLI-file states a derived value keys on only when one is asked for. In a project with a large integration, `component`, `docs`, `doctor`, `search`, `template` and `theme list` finish 4 to 14 ms sooner. Output does not change.

In RichTextEditor and RichTextView, a code block's language label too long for its header wraps instead of being cut off, and the code starts below the taller header, as in Markdown, so a block is as tall in edit mode as in read mode.

Apps that install the rich text package no longer see "Warning: @astryxdesign/richtext has N integration issue(s)" on `astryx search`, `component`, `template`, `theme`, `discover` and `upgrade`. The editor's internal plugins now live in a folder the CLI does not read as components, so the integration check reports no issues. The public components and imports are unchanged.
Internal: the toolbar's link popover, its URL form, the link address rule, and the toolbar's inline-format helpers move into modules RichText shares internally. Apps see no change.

RichText: the README says that server rendering outputs no document content, because `RichTextView` and `RichTextEditor` fill their blocks on the client, and points server HTML at core `Markdown`, which renders the same Markdown document on the server (affordances only RichText draws appear in their Markdown form), or at `@astryxdesign/richtext/markdown`.

RichText text reads the way it is written, in either document, and the shared first-strong classifier reads three Arabic marks, the Rumi numerals, and the digits of Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil, Thai and other scripts by their bidi class, which changes `Markdown` output too: a line opening `०१ שלום` now reads left-to-right where it read right-to-left before. `Badge`, `Token` and `InputGroupText` read the same strong set to decide whether their own text holds any right-to-left character, so the three Arabic marks — the semicolon, the question mark and tatweel — now count there too, wherever they sit in the label. A paragraph, heading, quote or list item takes the direction of its own text at any depth, so a Hebrew paragraph in an English document flushes right with its caret following the arrow keys instead of walking backwards, and an English paragraph, list item or table cell in a Hebrew document does the mirror. Each line of a fenced code block reads its own way too, so a Hebrew comment reads right-to-left while `const x = 1;` keeps its semicolon at the end. Top-level lists, tables and code blocks keep ordering their contents in the document's direction; a nested list follows the item that holds it. The stored value now drops a `dir` that arrives on them with pasted HTML or an older document.

A line break typed with Shift+Enter at the end of a paragraph, list item or quote no longer saves as a backslash that comes back as a literal `\` the next time the Markdown loads. Markdown has no line break at the end of a block, so the editor leaves it out of the Markdown; a line break inside a block still saves and loads as a line break.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a role color the theme sets (accent, success, warning, danger, info) now reaches the parts where the base theme draws that role on its own: a variant named for the role in a color of the base's palette written out (a success badge or progress fill), a role token the base points at another color on a part (a success banner), and a color the base gives a part as its own accent written as the color itself (nav links, outline buttons). Those parts take the theme's color, the missed list no longer lists them, and a color the theme sets on the part itself stays.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a role's text and icons (warning, danger, success, info, accent) now start from the fill the theme really shows in a mode where it sets the fill token exactly, and the note names that color and calls the text by its role (warning text and icons) instead of the dial's color and "links and accent text".

In right-to-left pages, the settings dialog's Reset buttons, the inbox's Reply action and Send button, and the tree list settings example's Documentation chevron now point the right way: these icons mean back, reply, send or go into, so they mirror. Left-to-right pages look the same.

In right-to-left pages, the canvas editor's artboard no longer goes blank and the progress dashboard's milestone timeline no longer draws its labels over the bars: both keep a left-to-right layout, as a design canvas and a chart should (the same page's scope burndown too). Left-to-right pages look the same.

The dashboard scorecard template's trend charts keep their y-axis labels whole with a small font up to 16 px, wide fonts included: the labels are compact and in the series' own scale ("6M" and "1.4M" for values stored in thousands, matching the heading's "4,350k") instead of 6000 and 1400, and the axis gutter is 52 px instead of 40 px. The tooltip still shows exact values.

The dashboard scorecard template fits a phone screen: its trend charts shrink to a narrow column instead of running past the screen edge, a chart's change line moves under its title when the card is narrow, the header's generated date moves to its own line instead of squeezing into a sliver, and on the narrowest phones Export moves under the period control instead of running past the edge. Tablet and desktop layouts look the same.

On phones and tablets, a Table or CodeBlock that scrolls sideways now fades each edge that hides content. Those browsers show the scrollbar only while scrolling, so the fade shows there is more to see. With a mouse or a trackpad nothing changes. A viewport that fits does not change.

A warm `astryx search` reads back from its kept entry table only the word lists the query names, not every list, so it allocates less and spends less time collecting garbage. Every answer is unchanged.

Search: a family's root now comes before a part of its own family whenever the part adds nothing the query asked for, also when the part's name scores higher. `astryx search "code sample"` lists CodeBlock before Code. The part still comes first when the query is the part's exact name (`astryx search code`), holds a word only the part's name has, or writes the part's name of two or more words as one word, as is or misspelled (`astryx search "breadcrumbitm"` keeps BreadcrumbItem first). The new order changes no match, score or reason. The `search()` doc page now describes this order, so it also matches a few of those words (such as "family" and "root"), and such a query, in `search` or `build`, counts one more match.

Search: a family's root now leads a part of its own family when the part adds nothing the query asked for: `astryx search tabs` lists TabList before Tab. A query that holds a word only the part's name has, in any plural form, such as "item" for ListItem or "statuses" for FieldStatus, keeps the part first. Scores, reasons and match counts are unchanged; only order inside a band moves.

`search` answers sooner: a name or keyword word that starts with another letter than a query word is no longer expanded into its plural and stem forms to compare them, since every form of a word keeps its first letter, and an entry's description words are read only when a spelled-out name needs them. Output is unchanged.

`astryx search` prints the first sentence of each result's description instead of the whole description, so a list of 20 results stays short. Component, hook and doc results' commands print the full doc; `--verbose` and `--json` keep descriptions whole.

`astryx search` no longer lists icons for an `icon` or `icons` right after `with` (only `a`, `an` or `the` between) when its results hold a component or template: `card with an icon` answers the card alone. An icon described after `of` or `for` (`card with an icon of a star`), or named before the word (`button with plus icon`), still lists the icons that answer it.

`astryx search` loads its icon-section code only where icon features are on, so a search in a project without them no longer loads it. Each such search is about 6–8 ms faster, and every answer is unchanged.

With an icon set installed, `astryx search` answers a query that asks for an icon (`trash icon`, `SearchIcon`, or a set's name) with up to three of the installed icons that answer it, after the results: `icons` in the JSON, one line each in the text. The results and their count do not change, a search with `--type` lists no icons, and with no icon set installed every search answers as before.

`astryx search`'s icons block names a set two installed packages ship with its package (`trash (@acme/glyphs/glyphs): …`), as the JSON `name` does, so the two lines no longer read the same. A set no other package ships prints as before.

Every `--json` result that lists or returns a template gives it `isReady`: false for a template whose doc sets `isReady: false`, else true. `discover`, which names a package's templates only by id, carries neither. That covers `search` results, `build`'s start, alternatives, pages and blocks, `template <id>` (shown, `--skeleton`, and copied), and `component <Name> --blocks`; `template --list` already had it. In text, those commands mark an unready template `(not ready)`, and `template --list` says `(not ready)` instead of `(WIP)`. Search still lists an unready template in the same place.

In development, these components throw an error that names the missing prop and shows the fix, instead of a TypeError from inside the component: `Tokenizer` without `value`, `PowerSearch` without `config` or `filters`, `PowerSearchFilterEditor` and `PowerSearchToken` without `config`, `TypeaheadItem` without `item`, and `ComplexSelector` without a `children` function. Production output is unchanged.

Search: a match whose name of two or more words the query writes as one word now comes first, also inside a longer query. `astryx search "TableSortableTable with pagination"`, `astryx search "table-sortable-table with pagination"` and `astryx search "tokens-color for dark mode"` list that block or doc first. Words written apart stay plain words (`astryx search "multiline text input"` keeps its order), and so does a one-word name such as `card`. A name inside a longer name the query holds, such as a block's display name or a doc's title, does not come first. Matches, scores, reasons and counts are unchanged; `build` is unchanged.

`astryx search` reads another entry's name as that entry's evidence. A block no longer ranks above a component only because it uses components that match the query's words. A guide whose title sits in the query no longer takes the title's rank when the query also names a component the guide does not answer: it ranks by the words it matches, so a guide whose title is its only match yields to that component. Two cases keep the guide first: a component word that is also a doc's name (`link`, `icon`, `theme` or `calendar`), which may be asking for the docs, and a guide whose own name is a query word. `build` is unchanged.

Search: when matches of one domain tie for first place on score and on the query words they matched, the one whose own name holds more of the query's words now comes first, instead of the first by name. `astryx search "side navigation sidebar"` lists SideNav first. A first result that matched the whole query, as a name, keyword or title, or whose title the query holds, keeps its place: `astryx search "date picker"` keeps Calendar first, and `astryx search "how do i generate a palette"` keeps the theme authoring guide first. A part of the first result never takes its place this way. Matches, scores, reasons and counts are unchanged; only the order inside one score band moves.

`astryx search` reads a one-identifier query written as a component's, type's or icon's name (PascalCase, such as `ThemeProvider`) as its words also when all it matches is text that mentions it, including a code term or table cell a doc's keywords gather. The entry that mentions it stays in the answer, beside the entries its words find. In the lexical ranking, the entry that mentions it, and an entry one of its words names outright, come before every entry its words only match; search's learned order inside a score band still applies, so `astryx search` can list a words-only match above them. A prop's name (camelCase, such as `autoFocus`) keeps only the entries that mention it, as before, and other queries rank exactly as before.
`astryx search` and `astryx build` use the scores they already worked out for each word of a request when they order the results, so a long request ranks sooner. The results do not change.

`search` lowercases each candidate's names, keywords and prose once per run instead of on every term and synonym, and scores a one-word query once instead of twice, so a warm search answers up to about 20 ms sooner, most for one-word and typo queries. Results are unchanged.

In an Astryx project, and outside any package, `astryx search` finds the experimental guides for sharing a page as one HTML file. A search for words like "share", "single file", "static html", "snapshot" or "artifact" now returns them, one entry per guide, and each says it is experimental; every other experimental doc still stays out of search, and in a package without Astryx search answers as before. A reference doc gains the optional field `searchable: true`, which only these CLI guides may set.

`astryx search` reads a docs namespace page at the reader's grain. A word the page's text shares with a doc beneath it, which that doc answers at least as strongly, is that doc's evidence, so a namespace page that sums up its guides no longer ranks above the components, templates, hooks and guides it summarizes. Words only the page carries, and its name, title, description and declared keywords, still match it. `build` is unchanged.

Secondary text now reads on every palette tint. The default light `--color-text-secondary` is `#445564` (was `#4E606F`), so secondary text on a gray Card or any other `--color-background-<hue>` tint meets 4.5:1 over the surface and the page body. The dark value is unchanged. To keep the previous light colour, a theme can set `--color-text-secondary` to `light-dark(#4E606F, #B0B5BB)`.
SegmentedControl: when a page's own style wraps the segments onto two rows, a tap selects the segment it lands on, not the segment above or below it in the other row.

Selector, MultiSelector, and ComplexSelector: the option list's trigger-width minimum is now clamped by the layer's viewport cap, so a trigger wider than that cap no longer makes the list wider than the cap.

In development, `Selector` and `MultiSelector` without an `options` array (for example with `<option>` children) throw an error that names the prop and shows the fix, instead of "options is not iterable". Production output is unchanged.

When an option grows while a `Selector`'s list is open, and the list is shorter than its height cap, the selected row stays on the trigger. The selected-item overlay measured its place only when the list opened, so a row that grew above the selection left it off the trigger, and a list near the viewport's end grew past it. The overlay now measures again when the open list resizes, before that frame paints. No API changes.

Selector, MultiSelector: focus returns to the trigger again after a mouse pick in a Selector and when a MultiSelector closes after a pick. It also returns after a press on a container around the list that is no Tab stop, such as one with `tabIndex={-1}`. Before, inside such a container, as a dialog's content box can be, focus stayed on the container, so keyboard and screen-reader users lost their place. A press elsewhere still leaves focus where it lands, such as on another field or an unselected tab. So does a press on a container that is a Tab stop, such as a card with `tabIndex={0}`.

Selector and MultiSelector inside an open shadow root: after a press on a container around the list that is no Tab stop, such as one with `tabIndex={-1}`, closing the list returns focus to the trigger, as it does outside a shadow root. Focus stayed on the container, because the close read the shadow root's host as the focused element. A closed shadow root hides its focus from the page, so there focus still stays on the container.

Outside a project, when a tool runs the CLI for you from its own package set, a page can use the other packages that set's `package.json` lists, such as an icon library, as it already uses Astryx, React and StyleX. `render` renders a scaffolded template page with nothing to install, and `template` no longer asks you to install those packages there. Before, `template` printed an `npm install` step for the template's icon library, and `render` stopped until you ran it. In a folder with no `package.json`, `template`, `build` and `theme eject` now name a package that nothing provides as missing, for the project that uses the page, instead of printing an install step that would turn the folder into a project.
The settings dialog template's Delete my account button now asks for confirmation first. After you confirm, a demo message says what would happen; Cancel does nothing.

The settings and settings-sidebar page templates no longer offer nav items that lead nowhere. In settings, choosing an item other than Profile no longer moves the selection while the Profile form stays; in settings-sidebar, Notifications, Taxes, Payments and Travel for work no longer open an empty page. A nav item with a section works as before; an item without one shows a demo message and keeps the current item selected, and the current item is marked as the current page for screen readers. The first screen looks the same.
Settings page template on a phone: the search moves under the title instead of squeezing it until "Settings" breaks mid-word.

Controls that did nothing in two settings page templates now respond with a demo message that says what would happen: the three Save buttons on the settings page, and Professional hosting tools on the sidebar settings page. The sidebar settings page's back arrow and drill-in chevrons now point the right way in right-to-left languages.

The setup reminder (`Next step: run … init …`, shown at most once a day in a project that has not run `init`) now prints on stderr before the command's own output instead of after it. Agents often keep only the start of a long answer (`2>&1 | head`), so a reminder at the end was cut and the day used up without anyone seeing it. It still never prints under CI, in `--json`, or once the project is set up; a command that fails now shows it too.

The setup reminder now says why to run `init` now: "Astryx is not set up in this project yet. Next step: run `npx astryx init` now, before you write Astryx code. It asks no questions, prints the getting-started steps, and saves the Astryx guide to AGENTS.md." Before, it said `init` would "install the Astryx agent prompt", which agents read as a file change the user did not ask for, so they kept working without it. The command it names is unchanged, and so are the places it prints.

A new experimental guide, `astryx docs cli/experimental/share-a-page`, walks through making a shareable page: write it with Astryx components, render it to one HTML file, share or upload that file, and turn the file back into source to change it.

The shareable-page guide (`astryx docs cli/experimental/share-a-page`) names the layouts that go wrong on a phone in a file with no script, and how to write each one: a Badge beside text in an HStack (StackItem `static` and `fill`, as its example now does), a Badge on its own line in a VStack (`<StackItem crossAlignSelf="start">`), a long string ListItem label (pass an element), and a table wider than the screen (the file cannot scroll it sideways: keep it within about 310 px with shares that match the floors or `pixel()` columns, each floor fitting its column's longest word and header, padding included). It also suggests `isWrapped`, which shows long CodeBlock lines whole. `astryx experimental render --help` and its doc now point to the guide.

When an unknown top-level word such as `share` or `export` suggests `astryx experimental export`, the reason now says what the command is for, as its help line does: one self-contained HTML file from a page built with Astryx components. It used to say "a page as one shareable HTML file", which also read as an offer for pages that do not use Astryx. The command's summary in `astryx experimental --help` and `astryx experimental export --help` says the same ("Export a page built with Astryx components as one self-contained HTML file, or turn one back into a page"), and the group's example is "Export an Astryx page as one HTML file".

Delete in two shell page templates now asks for confirmation first: a conversation's menu in the side-navigation shell and a row's menu in the theme showcase. After you confirm, a demo message says what would happen; Cancel does nothing.

Some controls in the app shell page templates did nothing when clicked. Now `shell-nav`'s Run project and Share, `shell-top-nav`'s Search products, Sign in and Checkout, and in `theme-showcase` the chat's Export, Close, Attach and Voice input buttons, Add item, the list and grid view buttons, and the inventory row menu's Edit, Duplicate and Move to each show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"). No layout or styling changes.
`astryx docs layout` and the scaffold guide say that a short form keeps its own 640 column, even when the page starts from a template with a wide frame or a multi-column grid.

Three styles that set a shorthand after another style on the same element set one of its longhands now set the longhands instead: an ordered List with dividers (its row gap), a flexible vertical on-track Stepper connector, and the PowerSearch sheet trigger with tokens. StyleX resolves that order differently in Storybook and in the published CSS, so each state had two computed values. It now has one. Nothing changes on screen in either build. A new lint rule, `@astryx/no-shorthand-longhand-merge`, flags the pattern.

When the docs catalog withdraws an integration's docs because one doc fails its checks (such as a flat topic that sets `aliases`), `init` and `upgrade --apply` keep that package's skill copies until the doc loads instead of removing them as leftovers, and when any of its docs does not load, its skills get one note saying so instead of a `replaces` fix.

A horizontal `Slider` with labelled `marks` now keeps room for the labels: before, the labels hung below the slider's box and the content after it overlapped them; now that content starts below the labels. The labels take the supporting text's line height, so the room no longer depends on the surrounding text. Sliders without mark labels, and vertical sliders, keep their size.

The useTableSortable doc now says in its first sentence that the plugin adds the header sort controls but does not reorder the rows, and shows two ways to sort the data: from the sort state yourself, or with useTableSortableState. It also says a column needs `sortable` to get a control, and gives the correct default of `allowUnsortedState` (`true`). No API or behavior changes.

useTableSortableState no longer throws when a sorted column holds an Invalid Date. The default comparator now treats an Invalid Date like null, undefined and NaN: it sorts last in ascending order and first in descending order.

The useTableSortableState docs say that arrays and plain objects have no sort text, so they need a comparator, and that a Date sorts by its time and an Invalid Date sorts with the missing values. A new useTableSortable example sorts by a status rank and a tags array. Table's `columns` prop says Table has no onRowClick prop: to open a row, put a Link or Button in its main cell's renderCell. No API or behavior changes.

`astryx component Flex` names Stack first. Stack's search card now lists `Flex`, the name Chakra UI and Mantine use for the same row-or-column layout part, so the lookup that misses suggests Stack before Layout.

A field with an error, warning or success status shows keyboard focus again. The status style replaced the whole field shadow, so the focus ring disappeared and a focused field with a status looked the same as an unfocused one. It now keeps the focus ring in TextInput, TextArea, NumberInput, Selector, MultiSelector, the date and time fields, Typeahead, Tokenizer and PowerSearch.

In a Stepper's compact horizontal layout, a disabled Step now tells screen-reader users it is unavailable, with a hidden word after its label, as the expanded layout's disabled button already does. The new translated string is `@astryx.step.status.unavailable`; locales without it fall back to English.

Stepper: the current step's `step`, `step-indicator` and `step-label` targets carry the `selected` theme state, the state tabs, side and top navigation and segmented controls use for their chosen item, so a theme can give the current step a selected look with a `selected` rule on those targets. Screen readers still hear "current step".

A vertical `Stepper` step with separated indicators (the default) keeps its content within the step. Before, a wide field in an expanded step, such as a `Selector`, pushed the step's body past the step, so on a phone the page scrolled sideways, text was cut at the right edge, and a dropdown opened off-screen. Now the body shrinks to the step's width and the content wraps inside it.

The published CLI stores Core's component list and imports at publish, and uses them while the installed Core's files are unchanged, so `component --list` answers about 30 to 60 ms sooner in a project with no integrations. Another Core version, or a change to any Core file or folder the list reads, reads Core live, as before.

The published CLI reads its own shipped docs as already checked against their schema at publish, instead of checking each one on every read, so `docs` answers about 25 ms sooner. A doc that was edited or is not shipped is checked as before. Output is unchanged.
A shipped doc's stored parse is used only when the installed zod release is the one that made it. With another zod release, the CLI parses the doc, so the answer is always what a fresh parse gives.

The published CLI stores search's catalog at publish, and uses it in a project that adds nothing to a catalog while the CLI's and Core's files are unchanged, so a machine's first `search` answers about 350 ms sooner and its first `build` about 290 ms sooner. The catalog is gathered live, as before, in a project with an integration, a package that adds docs or blocks, or a local theme; with another Core version; and after a change to any file or folder the catalog reads. Output is the same.

`astryx docs styling` and `astryx docs typography` state their core rules on the namespace page itself, with one short example each, so one read is enough to start; each page still points to its guides for the details.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the fills that follow a surface the theme sets (cards, popovers, the muted fill) keep their place between the page and the surface, as the base theme keeps them: a dark card that is the base page's shade never turns darker than the page the theme sets.

`astryx upgrade` rewrites the deprecated `swipeActions` and `swipeBehavior` props of `Item` and `ListItem` to `swipe={…}` where each entry is an object literal. It defines each swipe once with `createSwipe`. The definition goes to module scope when every value outside a handler is fixed at import: a literal, a JSX element, an import or a module `const`. It goes into `useMemo` in the enclosing component or hook when the options read its props or state. A function counts as one when it is declared or assigned under a capitalized or `use…` name, directly or through `memo` or `forwardRef`. Each entry with no `id` takes one named after its label or handler, else its side and place, with a TODO. On a `ListItem`, a handler that compares the row's `itemKey` value with `===` or `!==` takes it from `onActivate` instead. Where it cannot define a swipe once, it keeps `createSwipe` on the row and leaves a TODO. That covers options that read a map callback's value, a ref's `current` or a local assigned after its declaration. It covers a local they read at render when code sets, updates or deletes a property read from it. A method called on such a local counts too, and so does passing it to a call, naming it again, storing it or returning it. It also covers options that call or read at render something that is neither fixed nor one of the component's own props, state or locals. The codemod assumes that props, state and hook results are not changed in place, as React's rules and the React Compiler assume. Only an entry's `onActivate` runs when the action fires; any other callback in the options runs at render. On an `Item`, that TODO says an `Item` passes no `itemKey`. It reports, and leaves unchanged, a value whose entries it cannot see and a JSX spread that may carry the props. It migrates a condition only when it can read every id and prove both swipes key alike exactly where the deprecated props did. Otherwise it leaves the condition unchanged, with a TODO.

Swipe actions on `Item` and `ListItem` come from one prop, `swipe`, whose value `createSwipe` makes, from `@astryxdesign/core/Swipe` or the package root: `swipe={createSwipe({leading, trailing, swipeBehavior})}`. Each action has an `id`, and its `onActivate` receives `{id, itemKey}`: the action's `id` and the `ListItem`'s `itemKey`. So one definition at module scope serves every row; one whose handlers need component state goes in `useMemo`. The swipe's type carries the ids, so an id it does not have fails to compile. A new value with the same ids keeps an open row open, and one with other ids closes it. The swipe's code comes with `createSwipe`, so a row given `swipe` is swipeable at its first paint, and an app that never imports it ships none of it. The `swipeActions` and `swipeBehavior` props and the `ItemSwipeAction` and `ItemSwipeActions` types are deprecated (DEP-0017) and are removed in the next minor release. `ItemSwipeActionVariant` and `ItemSwipeBehavior` stay, and the new API uses them. Until then the deprecated ones keep working, with the swipe behavior this release gives every row, and when `swipe` is set too, `swipe` wins. `astryx upgrade` rewrites static uses and gives each action an `id`.

Internal: the swipe hook's and the swipe layer's file headers keep only their tags and the SYNC reminder. The prose that explains each moves, unchanged, into the JSDoc of `useSwipeAction` and `SwipeActionsLayer`. No behavior or type changes, and neither is exported from the package entry point.
Internal: the swipe's shared drag lists the committed options ref that its begin check reads. The ref is stable, so a row keeps one drag for its life. Not exported from the package entry point.

`Switch` no longer measures its track when it mounts. It reads the track's size at the first press instead, so a settings page with hundreds of switches renders without one forced layout per switch. Dragging, right-to-left layouts and a press right after mount work as before. Two small differences: a mouse or pen drag after a toggle now flips at the thumb's current size (up to 4 px different at the medium size), and a theme that resizes the Switch thumb animates its first value change from the default size.

The switch thumb rests as far from the track's end as from its top and bottom, at both ends, with a mouse and under a finger, read from the track's and the thumb's own sizes. A theme that sizes the track (`width` and `height` on `switch`) or the thumb (on `switch-thumb`) now keeps the thumb at the ends, where before it stopped short or ran past the end, and under a finger jumped at release. The control's box now follows the track too: before, it stayed 32 by 20 or 40 by 24 and squeezed a wider track back to that width. To follow that one rule, the small switch's off thumb with a mouse sits 3px from the start (as under a finger), not 2px; and in forced colors (high contrast) every thumb moves up to 1px so it sits as far from its end as from the top: the on thumb with a mouse moves 1px in from the end, so it no longer touches the track's border, and the medium off thumb with a mouse and every thumb under a finger move 1px toward their end. Everything else draws the same pixels in every official theme.

BottomSheetSwitcher: a flow without its scrim (`hasScrim={false}`) that closes with focus inside it now returns focus to the element that opened it, as a standalone sheet without its scrim does, instead of leaving focus on the page body. A switcher with its scrim that is removed while a sheet is open now returns focus to the flow's opener, when the removal lost focus, instead of leaving it on the page body.

`astryx swizzle` without Core says what to do. Outside a project, it says the folder is outside a project and that swizzle copies source into an app project that installs `@astryxdesign/core`; in a project that has not installed Core, it says to install it. It no longer tells you to work inside the design system's own repository. The error code stays `ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND`.

Tab: a label that wraps, through `xstyle`, stays centered in its tab, selected or not. An unselected label could take one line fewer than its selected (semibold) width, and it sat at the top of the tab, so selecting the tab moved it down half a line. A label on one line in a button tab looks the same as before. The one visible change for one-line labels: a link tab's one-line label sits centred in its reserved width, as button tabs already do. It moves sideways, toward the tab's center, by half the extra width its semibold weight takes: 1 to 3 px for a short label, depending on the label and the font.

A Table inside a Stack or another wrapper no longer reaches past its container's top or bottom padding. Before, a Table that was the last item of a Stack inside a Section, Card or Dialog pulled that Stack short, and the content after it overlapped the table's last row. Now a Table reaches a container's top or bottom edge only when it is that container's direct first or last child, the same rule its rounded corners follow. A Table that is a direct child looks the same as before, except when another Table or a bleeding List sits deeper in the same container: then the direct-child Table also keeps the container's padding at that edge, as its rounded corners already did. A Table nested in a Stack keeps the container's padding above and below it. Its sides still reach the container's edges as before.

The dashboard, dashboard-cohort-funnel, dashboard-composition, dashboard-progress and editor page templates, and the Table in Card block, keep their look with the Table bleed fix in Core: each Table is now the card's direct child, so it still reaches the card's top or bottom edge.

A Table column without `renderCell`, the tree column of a tree table included, no longer throws or prints engine text when a cell holds an Invalid Date. The default cell renderer now shows an Invalid Date as an empty cell, as it does for null and undefined. Sorting already treats it as a missing value.

A Table in children mode whose cells wrap (the default) now scrolls inside its own box when it does not fit, as a data-driven Table does, instead of shrinking every column until words break letter by letter and headings are cut. Its columns now follow their content instead of sharing the width equally. A children-mode Table with `textOverflow="truncate"` keeps its columns within its box and lays out as before.

With `useTableColumnsVirtualization`, a horizontal scroll that changes which columns are mounted now renders only the cells of the columns that enter. Before, every mounted cell of every mounted row ran its plugin transforms and rendered again. Each body cell is now its own memoized element, so cells whose inputs stay the same skip both. `useTableStickyColumns` now returns a new plugin object when its pinned keys change, so changing `startKeys` or `endKeys` at runtime pins and unpins body cells together with their header; before, body rows kept their old pinning until they rendered for another reason.
Table: with column windowing, a horizontal scroll that keeps the same columns mounted renders the table once instead of twice.

Delete in two table page templates now asks for confirmation first: the support inbox's row, conversation and bulk Delete, and Delete issue in the grouped table's row menu. After you confirm, a demo message says what would happen; Cancel does nothing.

A Table stays the one scroll region when a page host gives every table's parent `overflow-x: auto`. Before, the box inside the Table scrolled instead, so the Table lost its keyboard stop and focus ring.
Table: in a narrow column, a header's label truncates before its sort indicator and filter button, so those controls stay inside the header cell and can be reached.

A table header cell whose heading is cut short shows the full heading in a tooltip when keyboard focus reaches a sortable header's sort control; a mouse hover shows nothing, as before. Headings that fit show no tooltip, and screen readers hear the heading once.

A data-driven Table's column headings now follow its `textOverflow`, like the body cells. Under the default `wrap`, a heading longer than its column wraps onto more lines instead of ending in an ellipsis, so on a phone each column still says what it holds. Children-mode tables keep each heading on one line and grow its column to fit it, as before. Under `textOverflow="truncate"`, headings stay on one line and end in an ellipsis, as before.
The `table` and `incident-console` page templates are ready, so build can start from them.

Table's docs say how a long token, such as a code identifier or a URL, wraps in a data-driven table: the columns you pass in `columns` are sized from their definitions, not their content, so a token wider than its column breaks inside the token. To keep tokens whole, give the column a floor that fits them with `proportional(1, {minWidth})` or `pixel()`, or compose the table in children mode, whose columns follow their content.

In a Table with sortable and resizable columns, a sortable column's resize line now sits on the column divider, like every other column's, in left-to-right and right-to-left layouts. Before, it sat one cell padding inside the column. A sortable header's right-click menu still opens at the pointer.

A body row of a data-driven `Table` carries the `table-row` target's `parity` (`data-parity="odd"` for the first, third, … row; `"even"` for the others), and every row an `isStriped` table may stripe (body and footer rows, not the header row) carries its `striped` state, so a theme can style either stripe, for example odd-row striping only where the app stripes: `components: {'table-row': {'parity:odd+striped': {backgroundColor: '#f9f9f9'}, 'parity:even+striped': {backgroundColor: 'transparent'}}}` (the second rule clears Core's own even stripe; in a `hasHover` table it also replaces Core's hover color on those rows, so give the stripe rules a `:hover` of their own to keep one). Core's own stripe stays on even rows and the default look is unchanged. Rows a caller places in a `TableBody` (children mode) carry `striped` but no `parity`. A theme's background on `table-row` (a stripe, or a hover) also reaches a pinned column (`useTableStickyColumns`), whose cells replay the row's fill; Core's theme build now lowers a component's pseudo-class blocks (`:hover`) like its resting rule: derived variables, container padding and `replaces`; pseudo-element blocks stay as written.

A table row that `useTableSelection` selects carries the `table-row` target's `selected` theme state, so a theme can style selected rows (`components: {'table-row': {selected: {…}}}`). The selection wash stays as it was; a theme recolors it by setting `--color-accent-muted` in that state.

The markdown tables in `astryx component <Name>`, `astryx hook <name>` and an integration component read through `astryx discover <package>/<Component>` use a three-dash rule under each header cell (`|---|---|`) instead of a rule as wide as the header text. Tables render the same in markdown.

The `table` page template now builds what its description promises: sortable columns, row selection into a bulk-action toolbar, and a per-row overflow menu, with a confirm step before removing members. It stays unlisted (`isReady: false`) for now.

The table page templates give screen readers more structure: seven pages that had no main landmark now mark their content as main, `table-tree`'s sidebar headings follow the page heading without skipping a level, and the icon-only status and actions columns in `table` and `table-grouped` get visually hidden header names. No visual change.
The Table, Table plugin and useToast docs now answer common questions without the package source:
changesets.body:
- Table documents its `emptyState` prop, how to open a row from a link or button in its main cell (Table has no row-click prop), and what a custom `TablePlugin` can change, in which order.
- useTableFiltering documents its required `searchConfig` and shows that you filter the rows yourself, with an empty state for no matches; useTableFilterState names `clearAll`.
- useTableSelection explains how `getIsItemSelectable` (no checkbox) differs from `getIsItemEnabled` (a disabled checkbox) and what select-all does with each.
- useToast lists every `ToastOptions` field with its default, and says it returns the show function itself (`const showToast = useToast()`), not an object.

No API or behavior changes.

changesets.headline: Table tree rows follow the disclosure pattern. Body rows no longer carry `aria-level`, which ARIA allows only in a treegrid; Table has no grid keyboard model, so it keeps table semantics. Each parent row's expand/collapse button keeps `aria-expanded` and its "Expand/Collapse <row>" name, and while expanded it names its child rows with `aria-controls`. Indentation stays visual. No visual change.

The table page templates now give their dead buttons and menu items a behavior: in `table-inbox`, `table-tree`, `table-grouped`, `table-page` and `table-filter`, the buttons and menu items that did nothing now either work or show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"), and toasts that claimed an action had happened now say it would happen. Delete actions are left unwired on purpose, because a destructive action needs a confirm step these templates do not have. Text fields, form inputs and some menus are not part of this change. No layout or styling changes.
In development, `TableSelectionToolbar` without `selection` throws an error that names the prop and shows the fix, instead of a TypeError from inside the component. Production output is unchanged.

`astryx template <name> <path>` and `astryx template --cdn <path>` accept an absolute path inside the project root, also through a symlinked project folder. It is written exactly as its relative path. An absolute path outside the project is still refused with `ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL`. For `astryx template <name> <path>`, the receipt says the path was written as its relative path (`data.givenPath` in `--json`), and the refusal names a command that writes inside the project and the command that prints the source without writing anything. In a Next app whose `pageExtensions` include `tsx` (the default), the named path is one Next builds and serves: a page goes to the App Router folder (`app/<name>`, or `src/app/<name>`, inside the route group with the root layout when that folder has none of its own), or, with only the Pages Router, to the page file `pages/<name>.tsx`; a block goes to `app/components/<name>` with a root `app/` folder, `components/<name>` with only a root `pages/` folder, else `src/components/<name>`. Every other project gets `src/pages/<name>` and `src/components/<name>`. When that path exists or another page already serves its URL, the name becomes `<name>-2`, `<name>-3` and so on. The path is quoted in the command when a shell would read it otherwise, as with a route group folder. Next refuses to build when its `app` and `pages` folders are in different folders, and when two pages serve one URL. For `--cdn`, the receipt is unchanged, and the refusal names `astryx template --cdn cdn.template.html`.
Dashboard templates show every chart label whole: the progress timeline's "Today" label gets room above the plot, and Y axes wide enough for their widest tick no longer clip it.

`astryx template <name> <path>` names the components the written file uses in one line right after `Copied template to ...`: `Read the components it uses in one call: astryx component A B C`, so an agent reads them all in one call instead of one at a time. `astryx template <name>` prints the same line to stderr, so stdout stays the source. The names are the ones `astryx component` answers in the project (Core's and each configured integration's), in the order the file first renders them, each once, and in a project with an integration each is written as `<package>/<Name>` for the package its import names, so the read never opens another package's component; a chart library's parts and the file's own helpers are left out, and nothing prints when none are left. `--json` carries them as `components` on the `template.copy` receipt and as `componentsToRead` on `template.show`; every existing field is unchanged.

`astryx template` works out the components its "Read the components it uses in one call" line names in one pass: a name the component list holds under Core or a configured integration needs no lookup, a chart library's import needs none, and the names it does look up share each folder listing and doc read. In a project with an integration, a template answer is about 0.3–0.7 s faster again. Every answer is unchanged.

Outside a project, when a tool runs the CLI for you, `template`, `build` and `theme eject` no longer name an integration the tool approves and installs as a missing dependency. `render` already gives the page that integration, so the page renders without installing it. Also, `render` now takes an approved integration only from the tool's package set itself. Before, it also took one from a folder above that set.

In a project with no Next route folder, the page path that `astryx build` and `astryx template` name is now the file the copy writes (`src/pages/<id>.tsx`), not a folder holding `page.tsx`; a block's path is now its file (`app/components/<id>.tsx`, `components/<id>.tsx` or `src/components/<id>.tsx`) in every project. An import of the named path, such as `import Page from './pages/settings'`, now resolves, and a name an import already resolves to (a folder's index or a file with another extension) moves to `<id>-2`. Next App Router pages keep their route folder, and Pages Router pages were already files.

A `{@link …}` in a template's description no longer prints as written. `astryx template` (the list, `--skeleton`, and a template read), `astryx build`, `astryx search` and `astryx component <Name> --blocks` resolve it to the command that opens the doc it names, as `astryx docs` does: with the project's command in text, and as the bare `astryx …` command in `--json`. The JSON shape does not change.

A template doc's `{@command …}` and `{@pm …}` tokens no longer print as written. `astryx template` (the list and `--skeleton`), `astryx build` and `astryx search` show the command with the project's command in text, as `astryx docs` does, and as the bare `astryx …` command in `--json`; the JSON shape does not change. `build` and `search` text show every description's commands with the project's command too. A template's source still prints byte for byte.

`astryx template <name> ~/<path>` reads `~/` as the home folder, as a shell does. A caller that passed `~` through unexpanded no longer gets a folder named `~` in the project: a home path outside the project is refused with the commands that work, like any absolute path outside it, and one inside the project is written there. `template --cdn` reads it the same way. To write into a folder that is really named `~` in the project, write it as `./~/<path>`.

Twenty-one new icon meanings let templates that drew their own icon for a meaning keep it when they import icons by meaning: `copyText`, `paste`, `block`, `verified`, `alert`, `create`, `media`, `listView`, `currency`, `checklist`, `channel`, `team`, `schedule`, `help`, `signal`, `house`, `moveToFolder`, `columnSettings`, `halftone`, `groupRows` and `review`. Each falls back to the meaning the template used before, so an icon set that does not map or declare the new meaning draws the same icon as before, and the set's unmapped template meanings leave it out when the set maps its fallback. The template icon table draws `info` as the information circle; the form wizard's review banner keeps its badge through `review`, which icon sets draw as `info`.

`astryx template` writes each icon placeholder a template imports (`DeleteIcon` from `@astryxdesign/template-icons`) as the import of the icon the template icon table names for its variant (a Heroicon, or a Lucide icon for `/lucide`), under the same name. A project with an icon set then maps it like any declared template icon. The component showcase source and build's setup notes do the same.

The CLI ships the template icon table: for each icon meaning a bundled template draws, the Heroicon (or, for the lucide variant, the Lucide icon) that draws it. A private workspace package, `@astryxdesign/template-icons`, is generated from it, so template sources can import icons by meaning (`DeleteIcon`) and previews draw the same icons.
Bundled templates pick each icon by meaning: the template icon test fails on an icon imported straight from an icon library, with the command that moves it. Copies are unchanged.

A copy of the `canvas-editor` page template no longer carries two comments about its icon imports that no longer described them: one on aliasing `File`, one on which Lucide icon draws the rotation angle. The template now names its icons by meaning, and its copy draws the same icons as before.

Twenty-five page templates (ai-chat through kanban-board) import their icons by meaning from the template icon placeholders. Copies draw the same icons as before: the same Heroicons and Lucide icons with no icon set, and the set's icon for each meaning with one. Icon sets' template meaning counts read placeholder imports. The docs site's code view, playground, MCP source and ShadCN registry, and the theme editor's preview sheet, use the same filled source a copy writes.

Twenty-five more page templates (library through work-item-detail) import their icons by meaning from the template icon placeholders. `astryx template` copies draw the same icons as before, with and without an icon set. The template icon table gains a Heroicons drawing for `wallet`, so every variant of the table draws it.

Fifty-one block templates (AlertDialog through MultiSelector) import their icons by meaning from the template icon placeholders. Copies draw the same icons as before, with and without an icon set. The ChatSendButton custom-icon block's send arrow mirrors in right-to-left pages, as other send icons do.

The last forty block templates (NavHeadingMenu through VStack) import their icons by meaning from the template icon placeholders, so every bundled template now does. Copies draw the same icons as before, with and without an icon set.

When `astryx template` keeps an icon imported from a subpath of the library an icon set wraps, its reason names that library too: `it already comes from @heroicons/react/24/solid, part of @heroicons/react, which <set> wraps`, not the subpath alone as if the set wrapped it.

A page template's keyword now means one concept. When build chooses the start and its alternatives, a multi-word keyword counts only as the whole phrase (skipping stopwords and one-letter words inside it), so its single words no longer count for other templates. Core templates' keywords are migrated: lists of words are split into single keywords, terms that mean something different as a whole (such as "getting started" or "reading pane") stay phrases, and keywords that weren't true of their template are removed. The template-doc field reference says how to write keywords.

Four Core page templates no longer list keywords for things their page does not render, so `astryx build` and `astryx search` stop offering them for those ideas. AI Chat Conversation drops "citations", "reasoning" and "playground"; Kanban Board drops "swimlane" and "backlog"; Page Editor drops "drag and drop"; Theme Showcase drops "tokens", "palette" and "typography". The Page Editor and Theme Showcase descriptions now say what the page renders: blocks reorder with move up and move down, and the showcase shows sample product screens in the active theme.

`astryx doctor` warns on a `{@link}` in a template's description that names no doc, and `doctor integration validate` lists it as a `next` note, so `integration check --strict` fails on it only from the next minor release.

`astryx template --list` prints the first sentence of each template's description, so the catalog is about a quarter shorter. `--json` keeps descriptions whole, and `astryx template <id> --skeleton` prints a template's whole description above its layout. The first-sentence rule that `astryx build` shares no longer ends a sentence at a period inside quotes, so a description quoting a date such as "2. Nov. 2026" reads whole there too.

When `astryx template <name> <path>` refuses the destination of a Core template that no integration replaces, outside the project (an absolute path, or one that leaves it through `..`), it also names the command that writes that same destination: a change to the nearest folder of it that exists, then the template command with the path from there, printed with the CLI invocation for that folder. When `--overwrite` was given, that command and the scratch-copy command keep it, so they do not refuse a second time; the suggested place inside the project is another file and never gets it.
