A `..` path used to get the refusal with no command to run; it now gets the same commands as an absolute one. A `..` path that lands in the system temp folder is still not a scratch copy; the refusal names its absolute path, which takes one.

`astryx template <name> <path>` writes a scratch copy to an absolute path in the system temp folder (`os.tmpdir()`, or `/tmp` on a POSIX system), such as `/tmp/dashboard`, instead of refusing it. The receipt names the folder by its whole path (`data.outputDir` in `--json`), and the checks of a write in the project apply: no link carries the copy out of the temp folder, and an existing file is replaced only with `--overwrite`. A temp folder that is a disk's root or holds the home folder is not used. Any other path outside the project is still refused with `ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL`.

`astryx template` keeps what it reads from a template's source to name the components it uses, by the source's text and the parser's release, so a warm answer no longer parses the source to name them. Every template answer is unchanged; `doctor --json`'s kept-catalog message names the new kept value.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` gather the parts of each source file the template walks judge once per check, instead of walking the file's whole syntax tree again for every template that reaches it. For a package with many templates that share helpers, each check finished about 0.4 seconds sooner. Output does not change.

37 page templates (the tool templates other than `incident-console`, the content templates other than `work-item-detail`, the form, gallery and hero, login, settings and AI chat templates, plus `blank` and `theme-showcase`) give screen readers clearer structure: each marks its content area (`LayoutContent`, or the page's `Center` root where it has no content area) as the main landmark, has exactly one level-1 heading in each state it shows (a phone section view, a sign-in step, the signed-in state), and has a heading outline with no skipped levels. Titles keep their look (`accessibilityLevel`, or `Text` rendered as `h1`); pages without a visible title get a visually hidden one. Also: icon-only columns in `editor` and `theme-showcase` get visually hidden header names, and `documentation-design` names each example's tab list. No visual change.

Action buttons that did nothing in four page templates now respond with a confirmation toast: Restock, Fulfill item, Create label, Refund and Send Invoice on the order detail page, the next-step action in the service-jobs detail panel, Dispute this line on the invoice line items page, and Format Document in the IDE workspace.

Action buttons and menu items that did nothing in eleven more page templates now respond with a toast that names the demo action: Add to Cart and Buy it now on the product detail page, Publish in the page editor, the sign-in, plan, export and connected-app actions in the settings dialog, Sign In, Google Pay, PayPal and the promo code's Apply on the payment form, Save & exit, Crop image and Preview on device in the vertical form wizard, the social sign-in buttons on both login pages, Share in the file explorer, the AI chat landing page's settings menu and composer, and Pin, Rename and Archive in the side-nav shell's conversation menu. On the work item page, Add subtask and each attachment's Edit name their demo action, Cancel clears the comment, and Comment confirms it and clears the field. The settings dialog's search-result chevron mirrors in right-to-left layouts.

78 template buttons that did nothing when pressed now say what would happen, as the other template demo actions do: the example toolbar buttons of the `documentation-design` page template, and the buttons with no handler in the Button, ButtonGroup, Center, IconButton, Layout, MediaTheme, Section, Stack, Theme, Toolbar and VisuallyHidden example blocks, show a "Demo: …" toast. A destructive one (delete, archive, or a destructive-variant demo) first asks for confirmation; Cancel does nothing.

More template buttons that did nothing when pressed now show a `Demo:` toast that says what would happen. Archive and Delete ask first with a confirm dialog, then show the toast. Overflow menu items run the same action as their buttons. Upgrade is a link. Fixed blocks: OverflowListShowcase, OverflowListOverflowDropdownActions, OverflowListCollapseFromStartList, OverflowListCappedToolbar, TooltipActionBarTooltips, BannerWithActionButton, BannerSectionVariant, BannerCollapsibleContent, useOverflowHookUsage, useContainerRevealHookUsage, useListFocusHookUsage, TopNavWithLogo, TopNavHoverMenu, TopNavMenuShowcase, TokenizerEndContent, StepContent, useOverlayHookUsage, OverlayShowcase, OverlayHoverReveal, ChatComposerFullFeatured, ChatComposerFooterActions and ChatComposerFlat. No pages change.

The Table Filter template and the Avatar and LinkProvider example blocks show a "Demo: …" toast for their demo actions instead of calling `alert()`, so the click still responds when the page runs in a frame that blocks browser dialogs.

The technical documentation page template now teaches the real setup. Its AI setup prompt no longer asks for a style compiler, which contradicted the article's own precompiled-CSS step, and its theming example uses the real `Theme` component from `@astryxdesign/core/theme` with a theme package instead of a `ThemeProvider` that Astryx does not export. Its prerequisites now name React 19 or later, which Core requires.

Three menu items in two page templates now respond instead of doing nothing. In the grouped issues table, "Edit issue" and "Duplicate" confirm with a demo toast. On the kanban board, "Assign to me" confirms with a demo toast. Each toast handler carries a comment that marks where to connect the real action.

Page templates now have no horizontal overflow on a 390 px phone, with touch or a mouse. In the service-health, data, funnel-and-cohort and program-status dashboards and the kanban board, the header controls now wrap onto a second row instead of widening the page past the screen edge, and on the data dashboard a section heading's hint is no longer squeezed into a narrow column beside the heading. Desktop layouts are unchanged. A check builds every ready page template into an app and runs it in a 390 px phone emulation, with touch and with a mouse, so a template that widens the page past a phone's screen fails before release.

The `dashboard-scorecard` and `dashboard-progress` templates no longer wrap whole page sections in cards, as Card's own guidance says: the scorecard's goal list, and the progress page's summary panels and workstream table, sit in plain page sections under their headings. Repeated items keep their cards: the scorecard's metric tiles, trend charts and commentary notes.
The `dashboard-scorecard` and `dashboard-progress` templates draw their trend lines as straight segments between the measured points, so a line no longer bends between measured points.

With longer, translated labels at phone width, the form wizard, vertical form wizard, technical documentation and table templates keep their buttons in full: their header, footer and toolbar rows wrap instead of cutting labels or pushing controls off screen. The canvas editor's header keeps its save note and Export at full width, and the badge and stack direction examples wrap their rows. In English at 390 and 1280 px only the form wizard's last step changes: Back and "Create workspace", which were cut, now show in full. On narrower phones, English rows that were already tight wrap instead of cutting a label or running past the edge: the technical documentation's AI assistance row from about 375 px (its More options menu button moves to a second line), the vertical form wizard's header from about 330 px (Save & exit moves to a second line), and at 320 px the form wizard's Back and Next (its Cancel moves to a second line just below 320 px). The badge and stack direction examples wrap in columns narrower than about 295 and 335 px.

TextInput (outside an InputGroup) and TextArea: an error status without a message now gives screen readers text: the field is described by a hidden, translated "Invalid value", so assistive technology hears that the value has an error. In development the field also warns that the error has no message. Nothing changes on screen; give `status.message` to show the error in text.

A page whose components bring no tooltip code, such as one that renders only `Text` and `Heading`, loads about 9.6 KB less JavaScript before first paint (about 3.4 KB gzip). The truncation tooltip's tap handling no longer shares a file with the touch trigger code that its lazily loaded tooltip uses, so that code stays with the tooltip. Tapping a truncated text opens its tooltip as before.

Text: a truncation measurement that finds the same result no longer schedules a state update, so a page that mounts many truncating texts at once, such as a wide windowed Table, does less work. `useTruncation` returns the same values as before.

TextInput: a standalone field grows to hold its text line when text is enlarged, instead of the line running across its borders. At the default text size each size keeps its height (28, 32 and 36 px).

`search`, component lookups, `build`, `doctor`, `integration` and `theme list` no longer load Node's zlib module, which they never use; `theme add` loads it only to unpack a shared theme's `.tgz`. Those commands are about 2 ms faster, and every answer is unchanged.

`theme add` and `theme use` wire a theme with one color mode in that mode. When a theme's built module exports `colorModes` (`["light"]` or `["dark"]`; `theme build` writes it when the theme source exports it), the `theme.app` receipt gives that theme a `mode` field and the generated theme module lists it in a `themeModes` export. The first import's wiring passes `mode={themeModes[defaultThemeSlug] ?? 'system'}` to `Theme`, so the selected theme shows its own mode and a theme with both modes follows the system. When a later `theme add` or `theme use` first adds `themeModes` to an app that is already wired, the receipt marks `change.wireModes` and prints the wiring line to use. Once the module has exported `themeModes`, it keeps the export (empty when no theme has one mode), so the wiring keeps compiling after `theme remove`. The mode is read from the file that declares the theme, so a theme module that re-exports the built module (whole or by name) carries it. A project whose themes all have both modes gets the same receipt, module and wiring as before.

`astryx theme add` with a shared theme follows an integration's install guidance: in a project whose integration says how it adds packages, the command installs nothing with the package manager and names that line for the Astryx base packages and any others the theme imports (`data.copy.installGuidance`).

`astryx theme add` installs a theme someone shared in one command: give it the theme's folder, a `.tgz` archive of it, or an https URL to a `.tgz` instead of a slug. It checks that the one theme folder it finds is a complete, built theme, copies it into the app's local themes root (`src/themes/<name>`), installs the Astryx packages the theme imports that the app lacks (its base theme package) with the app's package manager and install scripts off, and records the theme as the app's default, so an app wired to the generated module shows it at once. Nothing of the theme runs during the add. Any other package the theme imports is named with its install command, never installed. The result lists every file written and the record and dependency changed. It never replaces a file it did not write, and adding the same shared theme again replaces its own unchanged copy. `theme remove` undoes the add: it deletes the files the add wrote (keeping any you changed) and uninstalls the packages it installed. `theme add <slug>` is unchanged; the JSON gains `data.copy`, and a remove's gains `data.undo`.

The theme editor no longer loads all of Core when it checks a theme against its base. The check copied the build's module stand-ins with an object spread, and the spread read the lazy `@astryxdesign/core` entry, so each first `new`, `set` or `how` in a process imported Core's whole root entry and React for a theme that imports only `@astryxdesign/core/theme`. The stand-ins are now copied with their getters, so the root loads only for a theme that imports it. Results do not change.

`astryx theme build` names an import through a path alias (`@/lib/c`, `~/lib/c`) as one the theme loader does not map, never as a package to install; expands a quoted glob to the theme sources it matches in its suggestion; and counts the fonts macOS and Windows ship, from one table by platform, as system fonts in its note on fonts named but not loaded.

`astryx theme build` refuses a blank or whitespace-only `--out` (it wrote files named by the spaces alone), and its note on fonts named but not loaded leaves out the families a local theme's own font stylesheet loads (`<slug>.fonts.css` beside the source, the stylesheet `theme add` imports). `astryx theme build` and `astryx doctor` also treat Segoe UI Light, Semilight, Semibold and Black as system fonts, the faces Windows installs as families of their own, so neither reports them as not loaded.

`astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the same output as before, custom properties that read each other (a token with a fallback reading itself, two tokens, a half of a [light, dark] pair, tokens and local tokens, a part's own custom property), a pseudo-element near a known one (as that one misspelled), a pseudo-element missing from the CLI's selector data (as possibly newer than the CLI), a pseudo-element inside `:is()`, `:where()`, `:not()` or `:has()`, a pseudo-class after `::highlight()`, `:window-inactive` after any highlight but `::selection`, a token name that does not start with exactly two dashes, and an empty token value. A pseudo-class after `::search-text` or `::scroll-marker-group` is no longer warned. A child theme's own build names the file and line of a value the theme it extends writes. A null value's warning says what it builds: a null property leaves the base theme's value, while a null token is kept by the browser as the token's value, so most properties that read it act as if they were not set (text keeps the surrounding color, a background goes transparent) and a font family reading it falls back to the browser's default font.

`astryx theme build` counts the fonts macOS and Windows ship for Chinese, Japanese and Korean (such as PingFang SC, Hiragino Sans, Microsoft YaHei and 微软雅黑) as system fonts, so it no longer names them as fonts the theme does not load.

`astryx theme build` warns a `[light, dark]` pair with any half that is no color (a size, a duration, a word that is no color name), not sizes only, since `light-dark()` takes colors only. A value the build cannot place on a line of the theme file is named as computed in it, and the theme it extends is named only when it holds that very value.

`astryx theme build` of a theme with a local TypeScript or JSX module, such as an icon registry, finishes about 200 ms sooner when the module has not changed since the last build. The JavaScript it compiles from the module is kept beside the kept gathers and read back while the source, the compile options, the imports it rewrites and every file of the Babel that compiled it are unchanged, so such a build loads neither `@babel/core` nor its TypeScript and JSX plugins. A first build, and a build after an edit to the module, compile as before. The written files do not change.

`astryx theme build` of a theme whose part styles hold pseudo-class keys (`':hover'`, `'::before'`) or whose tokens hold names without two dashes finishes about 20 to 30 ms sooner on a repeat build. What its css-tree checks of those keys and names find is kept beside the kept gathers and read back while the keys and every file of css-tree's code and data are unchanged, so such a build loads no css-tree. The build's warnings, errors and written files do not change.

`astryx theme build` reads a font family name as CSS reads it (`Gill\ Sans` is Gill Sans), names as not loaded a family the theme holds in its own property and reads with `var()`, and builds a theme bound with `let` or `var` that is never assigned again as it builds a `const` (one assigned again is refused naming that, not as an icon registry it sets).

`astryx theme build`: a doc module given as the theme (`oceanTheme.doc.mjs`, or a file whose default export is a doc such as `{type: 'theme', name, description}`) is refused with `ERR_THEME_LOAD`, naming it as a doc and the theme source beside it to build, and nothing is written.

`theme build` reads each Core component doc at most once per run. A theme whose component overrides name prop values (such as `variant:ghost` or `size:sm`) was checked against up to three views of Core's docs (the theming targets, the known prop values, and the components a new value augments), and each view read and checked every doc again. Such a build now finishes about 50 to 110 ms sooner. A theme with no such overrides reads the docs once, as before. Output does not change.

`theme build` of a missing file in a folder whose files another command generates (their first comment says which command writes them) says the file is generated and names that command, instead of offering a blank theme template. `doctor` still compares such a local theme's outputs with its source, and its fix for a stale or missing one runs the exact command that writes it, never a `theme build`. `doctor`'s fix when the themes folder cannot be read names the theme the message names (for a generated one, its command), never `<slug>`. A font stylesheet's local `@import` (a file beside it, `url(faces.css)`, or a package stylesheet such as `@fontsource/inter/index.css`, resolved from where the stylesheet really is) is followed and its fonts proven; a URL import is an external font service, and a local import doctor cannot follow, or one past the files it follows, is a warning, never a failure. The help and docs say `editor show <name> --png` takes pictures of real components.

`astryx theme build`: building a theme the theme editor made now also says that the build does not write (or, with `--check`, does not check) the theme's app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/`, which the app imports, and names the `astryx experimental theme compile` command that builds the theme and writes the copy.

`astryx theme build`: a plain-object theme with no `tokens`, a name alone (`export default {name: 'p'}`) or a name and component styles, builds as an empty theme over the base instead of ending with "Cannot convert undefined or null to object".

In a project where an integration can load, `theme build` keeps what it checks a theme against in Core's component docs between runs, while every doc and folder they were worked out from is unchanged. It works them out before it reads the theme, so they do not depend on the theme: building a theme again, with or without an edit to it, finishes about 120 to 150 ms sooner. A Core-only project keeps nothing and works out only what a build needs, as before. `doctor`'s row for the per-user cache names the new entry; output does not change otherwise.

`themeBuildFamily` (`astryx theme build --family`) builds each member as it is at that build. Before, a second family build in the same process, such as a tool or a test that builds in process, built a member file changed since the first build from the module the first build had loaded.

`astryx theme build --family`: the family's root may extend a theme the family does not select, such as an installed theme package. Its CSS and export carry that base as the root's standalone build does, and the module imports the package for the icons it inherits. That package is a requirement: the family's receipt names it (`base`) and its text output says which package it requires, and a build fails naming the package and the theme when it is not installed or does not export the base, never building the root without it. A member whose own base is not selected is refused naming that base, and a local base the family does not select that supplies icons is refused naming the base to select.

`astryx theme build` names a misspelled field at the line that writes it when the theme object is a member of a const (`all.a`), an element of an array, a branch of a ternary, an object `Object.assign` merges, or a `defineTheme()` argument written any of those ways. `astryx doctor` names each cause when a theme package's built module both imports TypeScript source and has a stylesheet that names a file the package does not ship.
changesets.body: Plain themes whose bases extend each other in a cycle are refused naming the cycle, instead of a stack overflow or a silent merge. `astryx experimental theme` removes a render folder a killed command left as soon as its maker is known gone (same machine, no such process), not only once it is ten minutes old.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build` no longer sets the page root's color scheme. A built theme stylesheet used to declare `:root { color-scheme: light dark; }`, so a site that loads it without `reset.css`, and sets no scheme of its own, followed the reader's device: for a dark-mode reader its native controls, links and page canvas turned dark around its own light content. A theme now follows the page's scheme; it still pins it where the page or the Theme provider forces a mode (`html[data-theme="light"|"dark"]`), and a `--family` build drops the same rule from each theme's scope. Apps whose page scheme comes only from `reset.css` see no change, while an app that sets its own `color-scheme` on `html` (in its own CSS layer, as the Tailwind setup does) now keeps it. To follow the device with theme CSS alone, add reset.css or `html { color-scheme: light dark }`.

`astryx theme build`: its font notices name the typography recipe, written with the project's own runner in text output, and it compares real paths in the disk's own case, so a theme reached through a differently cased path is not reported as missing or as another file.

`astryx theme build` and `astryx doctor` give each file that says a tool generates it (`@generated`, `@partially-generated` or `Code generated … DO NOT EDIT.` in its leading comments) one note with the count and that tool (`--family` and doctor give one per file, however many themes extend it), instead of a warning per setting it writes that does not show as written: that file is not where the fix goes. The build's note reaches text, `--json`, `--check` and `--family` output, and `settingIssues` still lists each setting; doctor's note names the `theme build --check --json` command that lists them. A hand-written theme that a generated one extends keeps its own warnings.

`astryx theme build` no longer replaces a file it did not write at its default outputs beside the source. A file of your own named like an output (`brand.css` or `brand.js` beside `brand.ts`) used to be silently overwritten; now the build fails with `ERR_FILE_EXISTS`, names the file, and writes nothing. At the default outputs, a file an earlier build wrote is still replaced, an output of the CLI before it was named Astryx included. At a path `--out` names nothing changes: only a file with the current build header is replaced, as before. Beside the source, an output another theme source built there is replaced with a warning naming both sources, as at `--out`. To migrate a project that keeps its own file under an output's name, build to another place with `--out` (for example `--out dist/brand.css`), or move or rename your file. The `--out` refusal no longer suggests building beside the source, which could replace such a file.

`astryx theme build` and `astryx doctor` no longer warn that a theme's font does not load for Noto Sans, Noto Serif and Noto Sans Mono (system fonts of Android, ChromeOS and Linux) or Cantarell, Ubuntu and Ubuntu Mono (system fonts of Linux). A system font stack that names them needs no font package.

`astryx theme build`: the import hint is given only for a load failure that is an unresolved import, and `@fontsource-variable/<name>` is read as loading `<Name> Variable`, the family that package declares, not `<Name>`.

`astryx theme build`: a theme module that throws from a microtask it queues while it loads is a refused load (`ERR_THEME_LOAD`), not a crash; a listener a theme module adds to `process` (`process.on('exit', …)`, `beforeExit`) goes with its load, so it no longer sets the command's exit code, prints after the `--json` envelope, or keeps the command from ending. `--out` naming a stylesheet's source map (`p.css.map`) is refused, and a slip after `.css` (`p.css.bak`) is told the stylesheet name meant (`p.css`, not `p.css.css`).
changesets.body: `astryx experimental theme compile` refuses a theme whose own values throw when read (a `tokens` getter or Proxy) as the build does, with no stack trace or `ERR_UNKNOWN`.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the form that works, more part keys a browser drops or Core misreads: a vendor property written without its dash, a pseudo name in capitals, something after a pseudo-element, two pseudo-elements, an escaped pseudo name, the custom property `--`, an empty key, and a block under a key that nests none. The output is the same as before. A `--family` build with such a key in a member builds, with each warning naming the member's file, where it stopped on an unknown error before. A default export that is a Promise of a theme is named as one, instead of a theme without a name.
`astryx theme build` (and `astryx experimental theme compile`, which builds the same way):
changesets.body:
- A theme that gives null for a part or a style key's block is refused at the line that gives it, never a crash. A null property or token value keeps its meaning (it is written as it is) and is warned at its line.
- A style key no element carries is warned: a value a closed prop never takes (`size:xxl` on Button, which takes sm, md and lg) and a pseudo-class written as a style key (`':hover'`, which goes inside one: `base: {':hover': …}`).
- A named pipe, a device or a socket where an output or `--out` goes is refused at once, never opened.
- `--out out/.css` is told to give the stylesheet a name. An `--out` that starts with an unexpanded `~` is warned: the build writes in the project's `~` folder, as before, and the warning names that folder and the home folder path to give instead.
- A theme with no name is refused as one, at its line.
- Apple Color Emoji and Noto Color Emoji count as the systems' own fonts.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the same output as before, more values a browser drops: a part property that builds dash-first without a vendor prefix (`Color`), a token or part value that is no text (an object, a boolean, NaN, an array in a part), a [light, dark] pair with a missing half or another count, a token that reads itself, and a token's `var()` that no token sets. A pseudo-class after a pseudo-element that takes one (`::file-selector-button:hover`) is no longer warned, and only `:hover` and `:active` in capitals are. A warning about a value the theme takes from the theme it extends no longer gives a line of the file that extends it, and a `--family` build names it once, at the member that writes it. A tokens map spread from a defined theme's tokens no longer trips over Core's own private copies in it.

`astryx theme build` reads a base theme that the same file defines as a const, and that the theme's `extends` names (directly, or through `defineTheme(...)` or a wrapper), as the theme it extends, not as the theme itself: a setting the base's variant beats is named, and the theme's own lookup never reads that base. A base that a call returns (`extends: makeBase()`) or that a helper's object names is still read as the theme's own.

`theme build` through a CLI installed for the computer now writes the same files as a CLI installed beside Core. It reads the component docs and types of the Core it builds with, which is the project's. So a theme that gives a component a custom variant gets its `.variants.d.ts` type declarations. Before, that CLI read them only from a Core beside it, which it does not have. It wrote no variant declarations, and `doctor` and `theme build --check` reported a theme built by another CLI as stale. The built module's doc comment now names `astryx theme build` rather than the command that ran the build, so builds through different package managers or tools write the same module.

`astryx theme build` now writes a built theme module that loads in any bundler and in plain Node. A local module the built module imports (an icon registry, a component icon slot value, or the helpers they import) that is TypeScript or JSX is compiled to JavaScript named after its source (`icons.tsx` → `icons.tsx.js`) in a folder beside the built module named for it (`w98.modules` beside `w98.js`, whatever `--out` names the stylesheet), at the place each source has under the folder that holds the theme and its compiled sources, so every compiled module has a path of its own: `import { icons } from './icons'` with `icons.tsx` beside the theme becomes `import { icons } from './w98.modules/icons.tsx.js'`, and a helper it imports becomes `w98.modules/helper.ts.js`. Each local import names its file with its extension. Before, the built module kept the TypeScript import, so an app whose bundler does not compile TypeScript from `node_modules` (a plain Next.js app) failed to build after it added the theme. The compiled modules carry the build header, `--check` compares them, and a file of your own at a compiled module's path is never replaced (that import stays as written, with a warning saying so). A theme with no local module writes the same outputs as before; package imports stay as they are. `--family` builds compile each member's TypeScript registry the same way, in a folder named for the family key.

`astryx theme build` warns about a component setting of a theme's page rules that the browser does not show as written, for each setting a key of the theme's own file (or a local theme it extends) writes, also through a call, a const or a spread; settings a helper function builds or a module the theme imports writes, its onDark and onLight surfaces and its adaptation rules are not read. It names one a later shorthand resets (a `border` after the block's own `borderTopColor`, or a second key that builds the same rule), one a more specific rule of the theme it extends beats on a variant, and one whose order against such a rule (or the theme's own variant of it) decides what shows where both hold. A rule for a runtime state alone (`:hover`, `selected`) is the look of that state and never counts. Each warning names the setting's line, the rule that wins and the change that makes it show, and the receipt lists them in `settingIssues`. The output is the same as before.
`astryx theme build`: a family build names a file it replaces, and builds that would not load say so.
changesets.body:
- A family build over a file with no build header at the `--family-key` name (an output of a CLI before 0.6.7, or a file of your own) still replaces it, now with a warning naming the file. Another theme's outputs there are replaced with a warning naming that theme.
- A family member whose icon registry is imported without its extension (`import {icons} from './icons'`) builds, as it does on its own.
- An icon registry that imports an asset (`import check from './check.svg'`, a `.png`, a font) builds; the asset loads as its URL, as a bundler gives it.
- With `--out` in another folder, a relative icon registry import that nothing answers to from there is warned, with the `--icons-specifier` that names the registry from there.
- A theme file that exports two named themes and no default warns which theme it builds and which it leaves out.
- An empty or blank `--icons-specifier` is warned (the built module would import from `""`); `astryx experimental theme compile` refuses it, and an empty or blank `--out`, before building. `theme build --out ''` still writes beside the source.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build`: what a theme module leaves running no longer decides the command, and three source layouts build.
changesets.body:
- A callback a theme module leaves running that calls `process.exit` after the module loaded is ignored with a warning; one that sets `process.exitCode` does not set the command's; one that throws is a warning, not a crash after the result.
- A family root may import the family's own stylesheet (`import './k.css'` for `--family-key k`), and a source its own stylesheet with a query (`import './p.css?inline'`): a first build from a clean checkout writes it.
- A project in a folder whose name holds `#`, `?` or `%20` builds a theme that imports a stylesheet.
- What a theme module changes for the whole process while it loads (the working folder, a built-in object such as `JSON` or `Object.prototype`) is put back when the load ends.
- `--out` naming a TypeScript declaration file (`p.css.d.ts`) is refused with the stylesheet name to give, instead of writing CSS into it.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build`:
changesets.body:
- A plain-object theme (`export default {name, tokens}`) goes through `defineTheme` as a `defineTheme(…)` call does: a `[light, dark]` pair is written as `light-dark()`, and Core's media-surface rules are written. One with `extends` and no tokens builds as the empty theme over its base.
- A spread of a package theme (`{...neutralTheme, name}`) is refused naming the spread and the form that builds (`extends: neutralTheme`), not an `icons` field the file does not set.
- A stylesheet the theme source imports (`import './brand.css'`) is named in a warning: the built outputs do not carry it, so the app imports it.
- What a theme module changes while it loads in `console`, a global (`Buffer`) or the file mode mask is put back when the load ends, so the command prints its result and writes readable files.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build`: a theme file is read for its theme, and nothing it does while loading breaks the command.
changesets.body:
- A Sass, Less, Stylus or PostCSS stylesheet a theme module imports loads as an empty module, as a `.css` import does.
- An import that the project's tsconfig `paths` or `baseUrl` maps (`@app/c`, `lib/c`) is named as a path alias, never offered as a package to install.
- With `--out` naming another stylesheet, the built module's usage comment names the stylesheet written.
- When a build of several files stops at a failure, the error says which outputs the files before it wrote, in text and `--json` alike.
- A default export that holds themes (`export default {light, dark}`) is named as such.
- A theme module that calls `process.exit` while loading is refused by name; `--check` never passes without its verdict.
- A value a theme module throws that is not an Error is shown as it is.
- What a theme module prints goes to stderr, so `--json` output stays valid.
- A timer a theme module leaves running no longer keeps `theme build` or `--check` from exiting.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build`:
changesets.body:
- A plain-object theme a theme extends (`const b = {name: 'b', extends: neutralTheme, …}; export default {name: 'p', extends: b}`) is made with `defineTheme` first, so its own base, typography and `[light, dark]` pairs are kept, and one with no tokens builds.
- A misspelled field is named wherever the theme object comes from (a member, an array element, `Object.assign`), without a line where the source does not write it as one.
- The warning for a stylesheet the theme source imports names a package stylesheet by the specifier the source wrote, and is given by the editor's compile too.
- A plain-object theme whose getter throws is a failed load (`ERR_THEME_LOAD`) naming the file and the field, not `ERR_UNKNOWN`.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the form that works, a part key it cannot write as intended: a pseudo key that leaves a parenthesis, bracket, quote or comment open (a browser then drops the rules after it), a pseudo key that is no selector, a selector list such as `':hover, :focus'` (only its first member is scoped to the part), and a custom property with capitals (written in kebab case, so `var()` of the name as written reads nothing). The output is the same as before. A missing input near a theme source in the same folder (a missing extension, a one-letter slip) is offered that source.

An import written as a template literal with nothing put in it (``import(`./icons.ts`)``) is read as the string it holds by these commands: `astryx theme build --watch` follows it, the built theme module carries it, `astryx doctor`'s shipped-import check judges it, and `astryx template` lists a package imported that way in its install line when the project lacks it. Before, such an import was skipped.

`astryx theme build` reads `var()` in any letter case when it warns about a token that reads itself, tokens that read each other, or a `var()` no token sets, and it follows a loop through the token definitions Core sets on the theme's root (`--font-size-2xl: var(--text-heading-1-size)`). A misspelled pseudo-class (`:hovr`) is warned with the one it is near. The output is the same as before.

`theme build` keeps the transpiled code of the theme sources it loads in the transpile cache the CLI already uses for integration manifests and TypeScript docs, so a build of an unchanged theme no longer transpiles it again: about 150 ms faster per build. An edited theme is transpiled again. On systems with user ids, that cache is the per-user one, which now stays within the same size limit as the kept catalogs: once it has grown, a run removes its least recently used transpiled copies, never one written in the last day or read in the last day where the file system records reads. `doctor`'s "Kept catalog cache" row now names that limit. Other output does not change.

`astryx theme build` warns a misspelled field in a theme a `let` is reassigned to or a dynamic import loads, at its line; warns tokens given as a `Map` or `Set`, whose entries it does not read; and stops at the field, with a message, on a token object that has no text form (made with `Object.create(null)`), never with Node's own text. A BigInt in a plain theme's type scale no longer ends the build. `astryx experimental theme` reads a boxed token (`new String('red')`) as the text the build writes.
`astryx theme build`: a theme file is read for its theme, and what its code leaves behind no longer decides the command.
changesets.body:
- A family build over a file at the `--family-key` name lists the replace warning in `--json` too, as the text does.
- A `process.exitCode` a theme module sets is not the command's exit code.
- A theme module importing a `.postcss`, `.stylus` or `.sss` stylesheet loads it as an empty module.
- What a theme module prints after it loaded (a deferred log) goes to stderr, so `--json` stays valid.
- A theme module whose top-level await never settles is refused (`ERR_THEME_LOAD`, naming the file), not ended by Node with exit 13.
- A theme source may import the stylesheet its own build writes, which a first build from a clean checkout now writes; a missing stylesheet it does not write is refused by name.
- Every handle a theme module opens (a timer from `node:timers`, a file watcher, a server, a message port) is let go once it is loaded, so the command exits.
- A promise a theme module leaves rejecting is a warning on stderr, not a crash after the result.
- `astryx experimental theme compile` names a value a theme two `extends` up refuses in the file and line that hold it.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the same output as before, a field `defineTheme()` does not take (`component:`, `tokenz:`, `ondark:`, `onDark.localTokens`, `typography.body.fontFamily`), with the field it is near; and a BigInt, a function or a Date value, naming what it writes. A BigInt no longer ends the build with an unknown error. A surface token that loops through a token Core sets on that surface is warned once, at its line, and Core's own surface token is no longer named as one from the theme it extends.

`astryx theme build` warns a `[light, dark]` pair of sizes (`['4px', '12px']`), which `light-dark()` does not take, and a pair half that reads a token nothing sets, as it warns the same CSS written as text. A var() name with a letter beyond ASCII (`var(--café)`) is read as CSS reads it: no false warning in the build, and no refusal in `astryx experimental theme`.

`astryx theme build` warns a misspelled field that reaches the theme input through a spread (`{...shared}`, `onDark: {...dark}`, an imported object), or in a theme the file imports and then exports, at the line that writes it; a BigInt typography value held in a const is named too; and a `[light, dark]` pair whose half is empty or a number, which `light-dark()` does not take, so the browser drops the value. A boxed primitive in a part (`padding: new String('4px')`) is written as its text, as a token's is, instead of as JSON text with its quotes.

`astryx theme build` warns a misspelled field wherever the theme's sources write its input: an input held in a const, `defineTheme` imported under another name, a theme a file re-exports from another module (named with that module's file and line), and an `onDark`, `onLight` or `typography` block held in a const; a method written as a field (`onLoad() {}`) is warned too, and so is a BigInt typography value. A TypeScript type assertion such as `<any>1` in a `.ts` theme no longer costs every warning its line. A BigInt inside a part's array or nested block no longer ends the build: it is warned by what is written, and a value that holds itself stops the build at its line. A symbol, or a tokens object that holds itself, stops the build at its line instead of with a raw error. A boxed string (`new String('4px')`) is judged by what is written: no warning as a token or a pair half.

`astryx theme build --json` carries in its `warnings` the `--out` warnings the text run prints (a stylesheet name that is not .css, an output of another theme source it replaces, a folder the theme editor made), names a folder it cannot write with its fix instead of a temporary file's error, and names an `extends` written as a helper's call or a conditional as what it cannot follow instead of an inline icon registry. Its note on fonts named but not loaded also names the families of a component's `font` shorthand (`font: '600 14px Lora, serif'`).
changesets.body: [fix] `astryx theme build`'s full font help leaves out, family by family, each family the theme's own `<slug>.fonts.css` loads; before, it printed the whole list unless every family was loaded.

changesets.headline: `astryx theme build --watch` rebuilds when a file a theme brings in with TypeScript's `import x = require('./file')` changes, as it does for any other import.

Muted cards in dark mode draw the theme's own light text on their dark fill, and links on coloured cards take a deeper accent stop. Inside a coloured card, a nested card, a field, inline code, an open menu, a selected segment, an input group addon, a step number, a banner and a striped table row draw the theme's own text again, and a transparent card keeps the card's ink. Secondary text on a selected row, a dropzone or a numbered citation steps to the nearest stop that meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) on the accent tint over the page, a card and the muted fill; inside a coloured card, up to two coloured cards deep, it takes a dark stop like the rest of the card's ink.
The butter theme exports `colorModes`: `['light', 'dark']`.

`theme build --check` and `doctor` no longer call a local theme's outputs stale just because another CLI release built them, or the CLI ran under another command name. Each output's header still names the CLI release that built it, and a built module still names the build command, but those lines no longer have to match. Before, every update of the CLI that answers marked every local theme stale. So did building under one command name and checking under another, although a rebuild changed only those lines. That CLI can be a global install, or a tool that runs the CLI for you.

In light mode, secondary text and icons, links on the cool tinted cards, green, orange, red and yellow category text, and code comments and operators take deeper stops of their own colours, so they meet WCAG AA (4.5:1). Secondary text on the blue, purple, red and teal cards, and in dark mode on the green, teal and yellow cards, takes the next stop, so it also reads on the accent tint of a selected row or a numbered citation there, on the page and on a surface. Each value is a stop of the palette generator's ramp grown from the earlier colour.

Light-mode category text (cyan, green, orange, pink, red, yellow on Badges and Tokens) reads at 4.5:1 (WCAG AA) on its tinted fill over a card, not only over the page: each takes the next deeper shade of its own hue.
The chocolate theme exports `colorModes`: `['light', 'dark']`.

A theme's component overrides can hold `@light` and `@dark` blocks: properties, pseudo-class overrides and pseudo-elements that apply only where the element's color mode is that mode, as `Theme` resolves it from its own `mode`, the system preference, or a `MediaTheme` surface. Inside media surfaces the nearest surface decides, for up to five surfaces of alternating modes nested one in another, so a light `MediaTheme` inside a dark one (a toast over a dark surface) takes only the light block. Where no enclosing mode matches, the block writes nothing, so every other rule applies there as it would without it, and it can be any value, not only a color. Themes without these blocks compile to the same CSS.

The first `theme build` after a CLI upgrade reads back the JavaScript it compiled from a theme's local TypeScript or JSX modules, as long as the upgrade leaves the code that compiles them and Babel's installed files as they are, so it loads no Babel compiler. For a theme with an icon registry, that first build is about 0.15–0.3 s faster, and about 0.4 s when Node's compile cache is empty too. An invalid browserslist setting in the project no longer makes that compile fail. Every other answer is unchanged.

A theme that gives a Card, a Dialog or a menu corners of different radii (`borderRadius: '12px 12px 0 0'` or a corner longhand such as `borderStartStartRadius`) now reaches what those components hand each corner to: a full-bleed Table or a bleeding List in a Card or a Dialog takes each corner as the container draws it, focus ring and row fills included, and the rows of a pointer menu (DropdownMenu's popover and sub-menu flyouts, and ContextMenu), sub-menu rows included, take the menu's shape less its padding; the touch sheet's list rows, and a drilled-in sub-menu view with its own header or footer, keep their own corners. An elliptical corner (`8px / 4px`) reaches a full-bleed Table; a List and menu rows subtract the padding from it, so they keep square corners there. A default Card, Dialog or menu inside a themed one keeps its own corners. Before, these children kept square corners, or took the first corner's radius at every corner when the CLI theme editor wrote the radius. The theme pipeline writes each corner to its own private variable for components whose derived `borderRadius` entry sets the new `corners` flag. A radius of one value draws as before.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a focus-ring change that keeps a status ("make the focus ring on inputs red but keep the invalid ones") keeps that status's ring as Core draws it while focused, on every input the new ring reaches, instead of writing the status's resting shadow.

`astryx experimental theme` reads its cached part data once per change of the cache file instead of parsing it again for every command in a process. The per-user cache of transpiled TypeScript is not read again when it has grown until its oldest copy could be removed, so a large cache no longer slows every theme command's first load.

The theme editor (`astryx experimental theme editor`) reads the families and weights a base theme loads from its font stylesheet's own `@font-face` rules, as the built-in themes now ship them, so it keeps the base's weight notes and does not suggest installing fonts the base already loads.

`astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> font <family>` says when the theme file covers the setting. A `typography` family or a `--font-family-*` token in the theme's own file wins over its settings, so set now names the roles that keep the file's family, the line that gives it, and how to change it, in text output as well as `--json`.

The theme editor reads a pagination's current page as its own cell. "Make the current page in pagination blue" writes `--on pagination-item --state selected`, kept apart from every other button, instead of a `current` state on every button, and `button` no longer lists `current` as a state.

`astryx experimental theme editor show`: a theme image named by a path from the site's root (`url(/pics/paper.png)`) that is not there now says it was looked for in `public/`, the only folder such a path is read from. Before, the note said the image was not found beside the theme.

The theme editor knows Core's calendar range band and keyboard key badge parts. "The calendar range band" is `calendar-range`, and "range" is no longer corrected to "orange". "The key badges" are `kbd-key`; "keyboard keys", "the keyboard shortcut" and "the kbd" still read Kbd. A part that draws none of what is asked hands it to the one piece of its own inside it that draws it at rest, and names it: "make the keyboard keys gray" writes the fill on `kbd-key`. With several such parts, nothing is written and the answer names them. Spacing asked between the parts a holder lays out side by side ("more space between the keys in the keyboard shortcut", "between the tokens in the tokenizer") is that holder's gap. A fill set on `kbd` or on `calendar` was refused, because the key badges and the range band painted over it from a token; they are parts of their own now, so that fill is taken and paints the group's own box.
Internal: a theme-editor source comment names Citation as its example of a title drawn as the part's own text. Consumers see no change.

`astryx experimental theme editor undo` refuses a `themes` that is a file, not a folder, by name on Node 22.13 too ("themes in this app is a file, not a folder …", with `ls -la themes` to see what is there). Before, on the CLI's oldest supported Node, it stopped with a raw "ENOTDIR: not a directory" error instead.
The theme entry loads the theme build, add, eject and targets code on its first call, so a `component` read that only resolves the project's theme no longer loads it. Output is unchanged.

Each built-in theme ships its open-licensed fonts. `fonts.css` loads every face from a woff2 file in the package (licenses in `fonts/`), with `font-display: fallback` (served from the same machine or a fast connection, a face arrives before the text first draws, so there is no fallback flash; a face that takes more than about 3 s leaves that page in the fallback font), instead of a Google Fonts `@import` that held the page until the request answered (chocolate's Fraunces as its variable face, keeping its optical size), so an app or screenshot offline (a sandbox, CI) draws at once and shows the theme's real fonts.

Links on coloured cards take the card's own category ink. Inside a coloured card, a nested card, a field, inline code, an open menu, a selected segment, an input group addon, a step number, a banner and a striped table row draw the theme's own text again, and a transparent card keeps the card's ink, so card text and links meet WCAG AA (4.5:1). Secondary text on default and muted cards takes the next stop, so it reads on the accent tint of a selected row or a numbered citation there.
The gothic theme exports `colorModes` (`['dark']`), from the package and from its built module, so tools judge it in the one mode it draws instead of guessing from the page.
The error toast keeps one deep red in both modes, so its text reads at 4.97:1 in dark mode, where it read at 4.11:1.

When an app adds a theme from a package it has not installed, `theme add` and `doctor` now name the install that works. They use the project's package manager. For a theme package that Astryx releases with Core, they name the project's Core release, saved exactly when the project pins Core. A project with no Core yet gets the release of the CLI that answers. Before, `doctor` named `npm install <theme>@latest`, and `theme add` named the package with no version. Each Astryx theme names Core's exact release as its peer, so in a project on an older release, npm refused the install. `doctor` also no longer adds `--package @astryxdesign/cli` to the theme add command, which named the CLI as the theme's package.

A theme that styles `link` keeps Core's hover tint on a link's color: the rules that hold each link `color` prop's color now hold, on hover, Core's tint of that color, so a link setting of any kind (a color for one mode, or any theme link color) no longer removes the hover tint in that mode. A theme's own hover color for a link color key still wins over the tint.

`astryx theme list` names, for each theme, the owner the app imports it from and whether that owner is installed (`owner`, `installed`). The CLI ships a bundled theme's descriptor and source (for `theme eject`), not the built output the app imports: `theme add` records and the app imports that from the theme's own package (such as `@astryxdesign/theme-neutral`), and refuses to add it until that package is installed; the list now says so instead of naming only the CLI. Existing fields are unchanged.

Text meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) where it fell short: secondary text on coloured and muted cards, including on the accent tint of a selected row or a numbered citation inside them, primary text on that tint inside a dark muted card, and in dark mode on popovers, menus and the muted fill; category text on tokens and badges, status text on its pale status fill, and comments, operators and properties in code. Each moves to the nearest stop of its own colour; no fill changes.
The matcha theme exports `colorModes`: `['light', 'dark']`.
In dark mode, menus, popovers and muted fills take matcha's near-black neutral like its cards, instead of a saturated olive green.

A theme's `@dark` and `@light` component styles under a `system` `Theme` that no Theme around it forces to light or dark now follow the scheme the page root draws in: the root's `color-scheme`, else its `<meta name="color-scheme">` (a `color-scheme` on `body` or a container does not count). On a page that draws in one scheme, such as a page that names no scheme (no `reset.css`, no `color-scheme` on the page root and no `<meta name="color-scheme">`), which draws light, the styles of that scheme apply whatever the reader's device is set to: a reader whose device is set to dark no longer gets the theme's dark component styles on the light page, and gets its light ones. On a page that follows the reader, the styles follow the reader's setting as before. At the first paint of a server-rendered page, before the root `Theme` mounts, they follow the reader's setting.
Secondary text on coloured cards reads in dark mode: those cards step it to the nearest neutral stop that meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) on their fill, and under a hover.
The neutral theme exports `colorModes`: `['light', 'dark']`.
Skeleton placeholders show on the light page: `--color-skeleton` takes a darker neutral stop, so the placeholder reads at its pulse peak against the page and every surface.

`Theme` no longer stops the page when `theme` gets a value that is not a defined theme, such as the mode string `"light"`, a plain object or `undefined`. That Theme applies no theme of its own: its subtree keeps the theme around it, or Core's default tokens at the root, and still takes its `mode`. The server and the browser render the same markup. In development a warning names the value, and for a mode string it points to the `mode` prop.

The Theming section of `astryx component <Name>` (and of an integration component read through `astryx discover <package>/<Component>`) prints its `defineTheme` override example, and its standard-CSS example, on one line each instead of a multi-line code block. The same keys and comments appear; `--json` is unchanged.

`astryx experimental theme preview add <description>` adds a page only when build is sure of its start. When build starts from the app shell, or from a page its page pick gives less than a clear fit (`start.fit` under build's `CLEAR_FIT`), it refuses, says why, and offers the nearest pages this app can show by name (`--template <id>`), then the list of every page. A description that names a page by its id or display name, names an app the preview has pages for, or names a page build's ranking matches by its name or a keyword, still adds it.

`astryx theme remove --help` states its exit codes plainly: removing the only added theme exits 0, removes the generated module and prints the lines the app root must drop; removing the default fails only while other themes are still added, and the line says to choose another default with `theme use` first. Agents read the old line, "is the default while other themes are added", as "the default can never be removed" and added a theme nobody asked for.

`astryx theme remove` can remove the only added theme. Before, it refused and said to add another theme and make it the default first, so removing a theme left the app on a theme nobody chose. Now it deletes the generated theme module when the module is exactly what the CLI wrote, and prints the module import and the `Theme` wrapper the app root must drop. A module with changes the CLI did not write stays, and the command says how to finish by hand. Removing the default while other themes are added still asks for `theme use` first. In `--json`, the `theme.app` result of that removal has no themes, an empty `default`, and `change.moduleRemoved: true` (and `change.themeModes: true` when the deleted module exported `themeModes`).

`astryx theme build` gives one warning, at its line, for a part's variants written as a `variants` map of values to blocks (`variants: {variant: {secondary: {…}}}`), naming the style keys that write them (`'variant:secondary': {…}`), instead of three warnings that never showed the working form. The output is the same as before.
`astryx experimental theme editor how`:
changesets.body:
- A value no page could show, such as a line height of 0 or 99999px of padding, is not written. The answer gives the range that works instead.
- "List items more spacing between them" points to the list's gap, not each item's padding. A visited link gets the "no visited state" answer.
- "selected tab with a 2px underline" gives the tab underline. "the selected date in the date picker" names the calendar day.
- When the page background is part of a longer request, the combined line also paints the frame and main panel, as the page's own answer does.
- White text asked for the header goes to the mode where it can be read, and the answer says how to have it in both modes. Readable-text lines no longer print an empty "()".
- "buttons font weight medium" sets a weight, not the medium size. "semibold instead of bold" is one request.

- `astryx experimental theme editor how` writes nothing for more kinds of messages that don't ask for a change:

- **Tag questions:** "spacing is compact, isn't that so".
- **A question about how the theme looks now, beside a look it names:** "cards no border. is the shadow still there?".
- **A question about what a dial does:** "what does spacing less do". The answer lists the examples in its text instead of offering them to run.
- **Sarcasm shown by emphasis or a "yes because" reply:** "yes because neon green links are SO professional".
- **A past hypothetical:** "had we gone with serif headings".
- **A change timed to a later event:** "after the review, square the buttons".
- **An ask that takes back a setting the theme doesn't have:** "accent red; also undo the corners" with no corners set. The answer says so, and asks for the rest on its own.

Other fixes:

- In a sequence ("make it compact, then make it roomy"), the later step now decides where it ends, instead of the two being offered as a contradiction.
- "badges: no fill" now makes the badge see-through, including every variant the theme fills itself. It no longer takes back those fills, which brought back the base theme's solid fill.
- A screen named by what it shows ("a records table view") no longer counts as that part.
- A real word is no longer read as a typo of another word that differs at its first letter ("stable" is not "table").
- "no shadows" after a part that draws no shadow ("visible focus ring, no shadows") now applies to the whole theme.
- `set … buttons outline` (or `soft`) no longer claims that an exact text color on the button's plain rule wins on the primary button. The primary label is now measured on the fill an exact property gives that variant.

The answer to a list of looks for a part now reads each item as part of that list:

- A subject how doesn't know ("flurbles: subtle gray background") writes nothing and names the word. It never falls back to changing the whole theme.
- Other design systems' names for a part now resolve to that part: a snackbar is a toast, a lozenge is a badge, and form controls are the inputs.
- A length and a color after the part's line ("inputs: 1px border #79747e, 2px #6750a4 when focused") are that line in that state, not a fill.
- A color word with its value after a text ask ("uppercase 12px text, gray #6b7280") is the text color.
- A day in the date picker ("date picker: today's date circled") is the calendar's day, and gets the calendar answer instead of filling the field.
- A state at the end of a with-item ("red background with white text on hover") applies to the whole look, so it no longer contradicts the resting fill.
- A text color for every button keeps per-variant lines when only a hover fill comes with it.
- A part label with padding ("dialogs: no border, 16px padding") writes the padding on that part.
- Corners on some sides ("4px top corners and square bottom corners", "4px corners on top only") change only those corners. A step on some sides asks for a size.
- A color said with a shape ("a #e8def8 pill") is that shape's fill.
- "divided by 1px lines" is no longer read as a change by 1px, and "shadow-sm" is the small shadow.

Real asks said next to a question ("set font to Inter; does that need an import?") still write.

- `astryx experimental theme editor how`:

- Two-word color names ("off-white", "ink blue", "grass green", "safety orange", "slate blue-gray"), tan and paper now resolve through the color table. Off-white is a warm off-white. "pure white" means exactly white. "amber for warnings" sets the warning color. A typed value said with a named color, as in "bold safety orange #ea580c accent", wins.
- "make it calmer" and "a calm dark mode" lower vibrancy. "more cheerful" means more colorful.
- When no command can do the whole request, the text output now says each result explains why, instead of pointing to lines "above" that appear below.
- Tailwind shadow sizes ("shadow-sm") map to the editor's shadow sizes.
- "dividers between list rows" and "table rows divided by 1px lines" give a bottom border. "32px rows in the menu" sets the menu item height.
- "should be a #e8def8 pill" gives that fill with pill corners. "dialogs with a dark overlay behind them" darkens the overlay. "big touch targets" makes buttons and inputs bigger. "a 2px dark border" uses the theme's stronger border color.

- `astryx experimental theme editor set`: a step past a dial's last rung names an exact line only where one setting does it. On a part, spacing goes on in the control height the part reads ("bigger buttons" at the top rung offers `--size-element-md 46px --on button`); the text size offers a size it takes; the whole theme's spacing, which no one setting carries, claims no exact line. A one-mode theme reads its own mode named with `--mode` (`--mode dark` on a dark-only theme) as the same as no `--mode`, in `set` as in `undo`, and says so. A control height offered past the top rung is measured from the base theme's own height, so a base with taller controls offers a taller line.

- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a role color the theme sets now reaches a badge or other part the base theme draws for that role in a color of another family (stone's info badge in its categorical blue): the part takes the role token the base gives that same color, so its look stays and it follows the role.

- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the fix line for a loading placeholder that does not show now offers the theme's own gray nearest the placeholder's color (else a darker or lighter shade of that color), not a plain gray.

changesets.headline: A `theme build` of an unchanged theme reads back what its check of settings that do not show as written parsed last time, and loads no css-tree. A warm build of a theme with component styles is about 46 ms faster. Every answer is unchanged.

The theme showcase template's inventory table keeps product names whole on phones: the Item column's floor grows from 80 px to 160 px, and in a narrow column the name moves under its thumbnail instead of breaking letter by letter. The table scrolls sideways in its own region as before. Wide screens look the same.
Secondary text on muted and coloured cards steps to the nearest neutral stop that meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) on the card's fill, and on the accent tint of a selected row or a numbered citation inside it.
The stone theme exports `colorModes`: `['light', 'dark']`.

`theme build` (with or without `--check` or `--family`), `integration verify` and `doctor` load a theme that extends a base theme whose module imports its own stylesheet, such as a package's `./themes/<slug>` entry that loads the theme's CSS. Node stopped on that import with `Unknown file extension ".css"`. On Node 22.15 and later, a stylesheet that any module of the theme imports now loads as an empty module. Node resolves each stylesheet import from the module that writes it, so a missing stylesheet still fails. On Node 22.13 and 22.14 nothing changes: a theme build (`theme build`, `integration verify`, `doctor`'s freshness check) still stops on any stylesheet import, and a read of a built theme module (`doctor`, `component`) still loads only a stylesheet whose import resolves from that module's folder.

A `Theme` in `system` mode now takes the light or dark scheme of the page around it. A host that draws the page dark, such as an artifact viewer in its dark theme, now gets the dark theme inside the `Theme` too; before, everything inside it followed the device's setting, so a reader on a light device saw dark text on the host's dark page. `useTheme()` and `useSyntaxTheme()` report the same mode, so charts and canvas match: a `system` Theme resolves to the scheme the page root names (light when it names none), else the device's setting, and under a `Theme` that forces light or dark it follows the device. If your app sets the page root's `color-scheme` to `light` or `dark` itself, that setting now decides what a `system` Theme shows. `useSyntaxTheme()` also follows a `Theme` that forces light or dark, as code blocks do. `reset.css` makes the page root follow the device's light or dark setting. Core's stylesheet, prebuilt or from a source build, sets no scheme on the page root. An app that does not load `reset.css` and names no scheme (no `color-scheme` on the page root and no `<meta name="color-scheme">`) stays light, and so do Astryx's tokens and `useTheme()` there; a theme's own `@dark` component styles still follow the device on such a page. To follow the device everywhere, import `@astryxdesign/core/reset.css`, or set `color-scheme: light dark` on `html`. `useTheme()` also reads the page's `<meta name="color-scheme">`, as the browser does.
`astryx theme template` lists the `'@light'` and `'@dark'` block form among a component's style keys, with a commented example: a block that applies only in that color mode.

A page that renders a Button or an Icon but no `Theme` no longer loads the theme-rule generator on first load when its build keeps whole modules or every re-export: Next.js with Turbopack when the app also uses `useTheme` elsewhere (for example through Toast), and hosts that lend each package entry whole to other bundles. A page that renders `Theme` still loads the generator, because `Theme` compiles theme CSS at run time. Token resolution now reads the unset status-role defaults from a small module that the generator also reads, instead of importing the generator. The module that defines `defineTheme` no longer re-exports the CSS generators; `@astryxdesign/core/theme` and `@astryxdesign/core` still export them by the same names. Every resolved token and every generated rule stays the same. No API changes.

Coloured cards keep their pastel fill in dark mode and now draw dark primary text, secondary text and links on it. Inside them, a nested card, a field, inline code, an open menu, a selected segment, an input group addon, a step number, a banner and a striped table row draw the theme's own text again, and a transparent card keeps the card's ink. Secondary text on a selected row or a numbered citation, and code text on the page, step to the nearest stop that meets WCAG AA (4.5:1); inside a coloured card, up to two coloured cards deep, that secondary text takes a dark stop like the rest of the card's ink.
The y2k theme exports `colorModes`: `['light', 'dark']`.
Skeleton placeholders show on the light page: `--color-skeleton` takes a darker neutral stop, so the placeholder reads at its pulse peak against the page and every surface.

A plain table's rows keep the text colour around them in Butter, Y2K and Gothic; only a striped table's even rows take the stripe's text. Inside a coloured card in dark mode, every second row of a plain table read white on the pastel card, at 1.15:1 to 2.12:1. Those themes' striped-row rule now reads the row's `striped` state, in their packages and in the copies the CLI bundles.
Thumbnail: focusing Open now shows one ring, on the image container, instead of a second ring on the button inside it.

A relative `Timestamp` is now named by the words it shows, then the full date: "2 hours ago, March 25, 2026 at 10:00:00 AM Coordinated Universal Time". A button, link, or radio that contains it keeps its visible words in its name, so voice-control users can say what they see (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.3). A caller `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` still names it instead.

A `Toast` rendered on its own, outside a `ToastViewport`, no longer holds a live role, so a screen reader does not read it a second time when its caller announces the message. Its text stays readable in browse mode. Only the viewport announces a toast; a caller that renders a `Toast` on its own owns its announcement.
changesets.body: Reported by:

changesets.headline: The Toast doc now says in its first sentence that `useToast()` needs no provider or mounted ToastViewport. The Table hooks whose config does not mention the row type (useTableSortable, useTablePagination, useTableFiltering, useTableColumnSettings, useTableColumnResize, useTableInfiniteScroll, useTableStickyColumns) now say that `T` is the row type, that TypeScript cannot infer it and falls back to `Record<string, unknown>`, and that you pass it, as in `useTableSortable<Walk>(…)`. Their examples are typed. No API or behavior changes.

ToggleButtonGroup wraps onto more rows when it is wider than its container, instead of shrinking its buttons until their labels are cut. Each row keeps its own button ends and keyboard order is unchanged; only a single button wider than the whole container still shortens its label. A group that fits looks the same as before.

A clickable `Token` passes a caller's `aria-pressed` to its inner button, so a filter chip can expose a pressed toggle to screen readers. Before, `aria-pressed` landed on the outer container, which has no role, and assistive technology ignored it.

Tokenizer: with `tokenOverflowBehavior="unfocusedLayer"`, keyboard users can now Tab to the collapsed field. Its placeholder takes the tab stop and opens the field with focus in the input, even when it holds no tokens. A disabled field keeps that stop, says it is disabled, shows its `disabledMessage`, and opens nothing; no element is natively disabled.
Tokenizer shows the caret in a focused, empty input when the field has no width

An `OverflowList` placed directly in a horizontal `Toolbar`'s `startContent` now folds its actions into its overflow trigger beside `endContent`, instead of pushing the end content past the toolbar's edge. A single-row `OverflowList` in a flex row now unfolds again when the row widens, and never shrinks below its folded width, so a squeezed row keeps its trigger whole. In a flex row its own width is its unfolded items, at most the row's width, so a folded list keeps the width the row gives it and content after it sits after that width. In a block parent it fills the line, as before. A caller's `width`, `max-width`, or flex basis still sets it.

A Toolbar with start and end content wraps when the two do not fit one row: the end content moves to the next line instead of squeezing the start content until its title wraps and its badge is cut. Each side keeps its controls on one line while it fits the toolbar's width, and a toolbar that fits its container looks the same as before. The kanban board template's header now fits a phone.

The tool page templates now give their dead buttons and menu items a behavior: in `canvas-editor`, `file-explorer`, `ide`, `kanban-board` and `editor`, the toolbar buttons, menu items and view switch that did nothing now either work or show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"), and toasts that claimed an action had happened now say it would happen. Text fields, form inputs and some menus are not part of this change. In right-to-left layouts, canvas-editor's Undo and Redo arrows now mirror. No other layout or styling changes.

Tooltip paints the theme's inverted surface (`--color-background-inverted`), the surface Toast paints, instead of the primary text color, so a theme that sets its inverted surface styles tooltips and toasts alike. Its text stays the page surface color. To keep the previous look, a theme can set the `tooltip` target's `backgroundColor` to `var(--color-text-primary)`.

A `Tooltip` no longer opens when an app moves focus by script to its trigger right after a mouse click or a tap that focused nothing, such as a click on page text. The last input was a pointer, so the focus is not keyboard focus. A text-field trigger still opens, as browsers mark a pointer's focus on a text field `:focus-visible`, and focus after a key press still opens the tooltip.

Tokenizer, Typeahead and PowerSearch draw the on-field status icon, as TextInput does. With `statusVariant="tooltip"` the icon is a button that shows the status message on hover, keyboard focus or a tap; before, sighted people saw only the border tint and never the message. In the sheet presentation a tap on the plain icon opens the sheet, as a tap on the tokens does. With `tokenOverflowBehavior="unfocusedLayer"`, the icon shows once the field opens.

`AppShell`: on a phone, when the theme keeps the standard width points, a server-rendered page no longer paints the top navigation's full row of links for a moment while its script loads; the bar shows only its heading and end content. The menu toggle still arrives with the script.
On a phone, TopNav's compact bar keeps a plain-text heading on one line and ends it in an ellipsis, so a long title no longer wraps and makes the bar taller.

TopNavMenu items and TopNavMegaMenuItem take `hasCloseOnSelect` (default true), as DropdownMenuItem does: set it to false to keep the menu open after a pick, for an action that reports its result on the item.

TopNavMenu and TopNavMegaMenu close when you pick an item with the keyboard, a finger or a pen, and return focus to their trigger. Before, the menu or panel stayed open with focus inside it. In a mega menu, following the featured card's link this way closes the panel too. A mouse or trackpad pick leaves the menu open, as before. To keep a menu open after a pick, set the item's `hasCloseOnSelect` to `false`.

On a phone, TopNav's end content is never wider than the bar, so an end item that can narrow, like a search field, narrows and the menu button stays in view. The Shell Nav template's search now narrows on a phone instead of pushing the menu button off screen at 375 px.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a value drawn on a track (a progress bar's fill) that a theme makes vanish on it, below 3:1 at rest, is now a problem with the nearest track color that reads, set on the track alone; a slider's thumb, larger than its track, counts only where it reads neither on the track nor on the page. Before, a black border the track follows and a near-black accent left a progress bar as one black bar with nothing reported.

`astryx experimental theme editor how <part>` names what a token shows where the base theme points it at another one on the part or a part around it (neutral's progress track reads the muted fill, which it points at the emphasized border: `shows: --color-border-emphasized`), and a border the emphasized border follows names the parts the base theme draws from it (the progress bar and switch tracks).

The per-user cache of transpiled TypeScript stays small and fast however many folders load the same files. Copies now live in `astryx/transpiled`, named for each file's text and settings, so the same file in many folders shares one copy, unless its text contains `meta`. Each new copy trims only its own subfolder, so no run reads the whole cache. Before, a machine that ran many projects or tests in fresh folders could fill the old single folder with hundreds of thousands of copies, and the next theme command spent minutes reading it. Project `doctor` now names that old folder and the command that removes it.

A TreeList row with no action (no onClick, href or children) now shows the focus ring when it has keyboard focus. Such a row was already a stop in the tree's arrow-key focus, but it showed no sign of focus.

Type-to-select: a letter typed with AltGr on Windows, such as ł on a Polish keyboard, now selects a matching item, so typing ł in a Selector reaches "Łódź" (`architecture:internationalization` INV17). AltGr reports Control as well, and type-to-select treated it as a Control shortcut and dropped the letter. This covers `useTypeahead` and every collection that uses it (Selector, MultiSelector, DropdownMenu, ContextMenu), a searchable Selector's typed-to-open query, and TreeList. Control and Command shortcuts such as Control+L still do not type-select.
changesets.body: Reported by Rajatendu1.

changesets.headline: Typeahead and Tokenizer: when a search matches more items than `maxMenuItems` shows, the result count announced to screen readers names every match, not only the rows shown.
