Internal: the UIKit values of a swipe-action row (the swipe threshold, the springs a confirmed row runs ahead on and a released row settles with, the touch claim distance the web needs) and the release rule that picks closed, open or fire (a fast release goes the way it moves, a slow one by where it is, and only a confirmed full swipe fires), checked against releases measured on UIKit. Not exported from the package entry point.

An unknown command names the command meant when its words come from another command line. `astryx add theme matcha` names `theme add matcha`, not `integration add theme matcha`; `astryx eject button` names `swizzle Button`, not `theme eject button`; `astryx templates list` names `template --list`, not a template called `list`. A short table of other tools' words names the command that does their job: `migrate --from 0.6.0` names `upgrade --from 0.6.0`, `add button` names `swizzle Button` and `component Button`, `add settings --path <file>` names `template settings <file>`, `props Card` names `component Card --props`, and `browse integrations` names `discover`. A suggestion keeps the options in reach of the command it names, including the program's own (`--json`, `--base`), and names an input the run still needs as a placeholder (`upgrade --from <old-version>`). A suggestion is never run for you.

A manifest key the running CLI does not know is no longer an integration issue. Everyday commands stop printing "has 1 integration issue(s)" for an integration published against a newer CLI, and project `doctor` no longer lists it. `doctor integration validate` and `integration check` list it as an `unknown_manifest_key` note, which fails nothing; a key one letter from a known one is a `next` note with its fix.

`astryx upgrade --apply` refreshes the Astryx skill in every place `astryx init --to` saved (astryx.config `skills.to`), under init's rules: the two copies of the project skills folders are written together or not at all, an edited file is kept, and nothing is written through a folder linked out of the project. The dry run names each file it would write. An Astryx block is still refreshed wherever it is, and a project that keeps its Astryx guidance only as a skill is no longer told to add it. `astryx doctor` adds a `skill-places` check: it passes when each saved skill file matches this release, and warns when one is missing or stale, when the two copies of a place differ, when the block and a project skill copy (in the project skills folders or a saved project folder) are both there without both being saved, or when a project skill is named `astryx`. Doctor's `computer-agent-text` check names the folders outside a project that `init --to` saved. Inside a project, `astryx init --to` naming only places outside it (`user`, or folders outside the project) with no feature beyond the agent docs is answered by the copy that started the run, as `--user` is.

`astryx upgrade --list` prints each codemod on one line, its name and title, under its version, with `(optional)` on the codemods that run only on request and the package named once when every codemod shares it, instead of a five-line record per codemod. The list now grows by one line per new codemod, plus a heading when a codemod starts a new version. `--json` is unchanged.

Outside a project, `astryx upgrade` without `--from` now leads with the reason: the folder is outside a project. It says to run upgrade with `--from <old version>` in the app's folder. Before, it led with "Missing required --from", so adding `--from` in the same folder got a second refusal.

`astryx upgrade` reads a `.ts` file as TypeScript without JSX and a declaration file as declarations, as TypeScript does. A type assertion (`<Item>value`) in a `.ts` file, or a declaration without a value (`export const limit: number;`) in a declaration file (`.d.ts`, `.d.mts`, `.d.cts`, or an arbitrary-extension declaration file such as `styles.d.css.ts`), no longer stops the run with a parse error, and a codemod changes such a file like any other. A `.tsx` file and JavaScript read as before.

The useHotkeys docs no longer recommend `shift+/` for a help overlay. The hook compares the final key against `event.key`, and Shift+/ produces `?` on US layouts, so a `shift+/` registration never fires there. The docs now use `?` and say to register a punctuation key that shift changes as the character it produces. No behavior changes.

Outside a project, `astryx doctor integration validate <package>` now checks the copy of the package that the folder uses, an integration installed for the computer included. Before, it looked only in the `node_modules` at or above the folder and reported `package_not_found`, though `astryx doctor` names this command for an integration installed for the computer that it cannot load. A copy that the other commands skip for its peer ranges is checked too, with a note that says why: `cli_peer_version`, or the new `core_peer_version` when only its `@astryxdesign/core` range excludes this CLI's release.

`astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` parse each of a package's source files once for the walks that follow each template's imports, instead of once for every template that reaches the file. For a package with many templates that share helpers, each check finishes about a second sooner. Output does not change.

In a Vite source build with `astryxStylex()`, importing `@astryxdesign/core/astryx.css`, from a module or with a CSS `@import`, no longer fails the build or the dev server. `reset.css` resolves to its file, and `astryx.css`, the prebuilt stylesheet a source build replaces, loads an empty stylesheet, because StyleX already compiles those rules from source.

The StyleX setup docs name `@stylexjs/unplugin` (`stylex.vite()`) for Vite. Under Vite, `@stylexjs/rollup-plugin` fails on `astryx.css`, so a page template that uses StyleX stayed blank. The note on such a template now points to the setup section.

A warm `astryx component` or `astryx template` lookup that misses in a project with only Core answers about 55–60 ms faster, because template discovery is now kept for those commands. Every answer is unchanged. (#12585)
The work item's subtasks wrap instead of cutting off after a few words on a phone, and each task's due date and assignee move under its title there.
